controls.title: Information Security Integration in Project Management
controls.objective: Ensure that information security is integrated into all project management processes, from initiation to closure, across all types of projects within the organization.
controls.successCriteria:
All projects demonstrate thorough integration of information security measures throughout their life cycle.
Documented evidence that information security risks are considered and treated as part of project management.
Clear definition and allocation of information security roles and responsibilities in all projects.
Compliance with organizational information security policies, regulations, and best practices in project management processes.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain a list of current and recent projects managed by the organization.
Gather project management documentation for each project, including risk assessments, information security requirements, and meeting minutes from steering committee sessions.
Collect records of information security considerations and activities at different project stages.
Obtain documentation of roles and responsibilities related to information security within each project.

Analysis:
Review project documentation to ensure that information security risks are identified and treated early and throughout the project life cycle.
Verify that information security requirements are addressed in the early stages of projects.
Assess if the projects consider and treat information security risks associated with execution, such as secure communication.
Evaluate the periodic review process and effectiveness of the information security risk treatment within projects.
Confirm the appropriateness of information security considerations and activities against predefined stages and criteria.
Check if the responsibilities and authorities for information security are clearly defined and allocated within project roles.

Output:
A report on the integration of information security in project management for each reviewed project.
A compliance matrix indicating how each project aligns with the organization’s information security policies and procedures.
Recommendations for improvement in cases where projects fall short of the required information security integration standards.

title.en: Inventory every current and recent project with its type, stage and project manager

description.en: This control covers all types of project, so the list has to come from wherever projects are actually run — the portfolio tool, steering committee agendas, departmental plans — not only from the IT project register, which is the omission that makes the rest of this control look compliant. Record each project's type, the lifecycle stage it has reached, its project manager and whether it is still open. This list is the population every later task samples, so a project missing here is a project the security stage criteria will never be applied to. Attach the inventory dated at the point it was compiled.

evidenceHint.en: Dated project inventory covering all project types, giving type, current lifecycle stage, project manager and open or closed status per project

text.en: Collect project lists from the portfolio tool, steering committees and departmental plans.
Record each project's type so non-IT projects are visible alongside IT ones.
Record the lifecycle stage each project has reached, from initiation to closure.
Name the project manager accountable for each project's security obligations.
Date the inventory and hold it as the population the later tasks sample from.

title.en: Define the information security criteria each project stage must satisfy from initiation to closure

description.en: Write down, for each stage a project passes through, what information security work has to be complete before it may leave that stage and what artefact evidences it — security requirements at the early stages, a risk assessment and its treatment during execution, and the security check at closure. This control is tested against predefined stages and criteria, so criteria that exist only in a reviewer's head cannot be evidenced. Keep them applicable to every project type in the inventory rather than to software projects alone. Attach the issued stage criteria showing the artefact expected at each gate.

evidenceHint.en: Issued project security stage criteria naming, for each lifecycle stage, the security work required to leave it and the artefact that evidences completion

title.en: Allocate the information security responsibilities and authorities within each project's role definitions

description.en: For every project in the inventory, record which project role carries which information security responsibility and what each is authorised to decide — who accepts a security risk on the project's behalf, and who signs off that the security requirements have been met. Name people against the roles rather than leaving the allocation abstract, because this control is tested on responsibilities and authorities being clearly defined and allocated within project roles, not merely described. Where one person holds several of these on a project, say so explicitly so the concentration is visible. Attach the role allocation for each project.

evidenceHint.en: Per-project security role allocation naming the individual holding each security responsibility and the decisions each is authorised to take

title.en: Record each project's information security risks and the treatment agreed for them

description.en: From initiation onwards, keep a risk entry per project capturing the security risks identified, when each was raised, the treatment agreed and its owner, and revisit it as the project moves between stages rather than only at the start — this control is tested on risks being treated early and throughout, and a register with every entry dated in the project's first week evidences the opposite. Include the risks the execution itself creates, such as the channels the project team uses to move sensitive material. Attach the project risk register extract for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Project risk register extract per project showing each security risk, the date raised, the treatment agreed, its owner and the stage at which it was last reviewed

title.en: Minute the information security items considered at each project steering committee session

description.en: The steering minutes are the artefact showing security was on the agenda rather than documented after the fact, so record in them the security items raised, the decisions taken on them and the actions assigned with owners and dates. Where a session considered no security item, minute that explicitly — a run of silent minutes across a project's execution is the finding the periodic review looks for, and it cannot be seen if silence is simply absence. Attach the minutes for the period covering every project in the inventory that has a steering committee.

evidenceHint.en: Steering committee minutes for the period showing, per session, the security items considered, the decisions taken and the actions assigned with owner and date

title.en: Score each project against the stage criteria and record the shortfalls and their remediation

description.en: Take the inventory and the stage criteria together and produce the compliance matrix this control's output calls for: for each project, which stage criteria were met, which were missed and which are not yet due. Read the project's own documentation for the evidence rather than asking the project manager whether it was done. Against every shortfall write the recommendation and the owner who will close it, so the matrix carries its own disposition. Attach the matrix with the integration report summarising the position across the portfolio.

evidenceHint.en: Project security compliance matrix scoring each project against every stage criterion as met, missed or not yet due, with a recommendation and named owner recorded against each shortfall

text.en: Read each project's documentation for the artefact each stage criterion requires.
Mark every criterion met, missed, or not yet due at the project's current stage.
Record the evidence reference behind each met verdict so the score can be rechecked.
Write a recommendation and a named owner against every missed criterion.
Summarise the portfolio position and the shortfalls recurring across projects.

controls.title: Anomalous Activity Monitoring Control
controls.objective: To ensure continuous monitoring of networks, systems, and applications for anomalous behavior, in alignment with business and information security requirements, and relevant laws and regulations.
controls.successCriteria:
Monitoring tools are configured appropriately and in line with organizational requirements.
All systems and applications are being effectively monitored for anomalies.
Established baseline of normal behavior is consistently applied, and deviations are accurately detected and alerted.
Response procedures to alerts are effective and timely.
No significant gaps in monitoring coverage of networks, systems, and applications.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Retrieve configuration details and settings of monitoring tools (e.g., IDS, IPS, firewalls).
Gather logs from monitoring tools for a defined period.
Obtain documentation outlining the baseline of normal behavior established for the organization.
Collect evidence of alerts generated by monitoring tools and responses to these alerts.
Secure a list of systems and applications under monitoring.

Analysis:
Review the monitoring tools' configurations against organizational requirements and best practices for detecting anomalous activities.
Analyze the collected logs to verify if monitoring is comprehensive (covering aspects like network traffic, access to critical systems, system and network configuration files, etc.).
Compare the monitoring against the established baseline of normal behavior to check for any deviations or anomalies.
Assess the effectiveness of alert generation and response mechanisms.
Cross-verify the list of monitored systems and applications with the organization’s inventory to ensure complete coverage.

Output:
Report detailing the configurations of monitoring tools.
Analysis report of the monitoring logs.
Documentation review report regarding the established baseline and response to alerts.
Compliance matrix indicating coverage of all systems and applications.

title.en: Record every monitored network, system and application in a monitoring coverage register

description.en: Build the register the auditor asks for as the 'list of systems and applications under monitoring'. One row per monitored network segment, system or application, naming the tool watching it (IDS, IPS, firewall, endpoint agent, log collector), the data source or feed it sends, and the team that owns the asset. Source the rows from the tools' own configured feeds rather than from memory, so the register reflects what is actually being watched. Done when the register is populated for every tool in service and attached as an export.

evidenceHint.en: Monitoring coverage register export: asset, monitoring tool, data source or feed, asset owner

title.en: Document the normal-behaviour baseline for each monitored data source

description.en: Write down what 'normal' means for each feed in the coverage register, so a deviation is decidable rather than a judgement call. Cover at least network traffic volumes and destinations, access to critical systems, and changes to system and network configuration files — the three areas the control's log analysis examines. For each metric state the measured normal range, the deviation that constitutes an anomaly, and the severity it raises. Date and version the document so the baseline in force at any point is identifiable, and agree the operational ranges with IT Operations before it is issued.

evidenceHint.en: Dated, versioned baseline document listing each metric, its source feed, normal range, deviation threshold and alert severity

text.en: Derive the observed normal range for each feed from its own historical data.
Set the deviation threshold and the alert severity each metric raises when crossed.
Name the coverage-register row each baseline metric is measured from.
Record any metric for which no feed exists, so the shortfall is visible.

title.en: Set each monitoring tool's detection thresholds and alert destinations to the documented baseline

description.en: Take the baseline document and make each IDS, IPS, firewall and log-collection tool enforce it: enable the rules that detect the listed deviations, set the thresholds to the documented values, and point each rule's alert at a destination a named responder watches. Where a tool cannot express a baseline rule, record the shortfall against that row of the coverage register. Finish by exporting the running configuration of each tool and filing it with its export date, so the configuration can be compared against the baseline without console access. Security engineering specifies the rule content; IT Operations executes the changes on network devices.

evidenceHint.en: Exported running configuration of each monitoring tool (rules, thresholds, alert destinations) with export date, plus the list of baseline rules no tool can express

title.en: Log every monitoring alert raised and the response taken against it

description.en: Maintain one running record of alerts across the monitoring tools. Each entry carries the timestamp, the tool and rule that fired, which baseline deviation triggered it, the triage outcome (true positive, false positive, tuned out), the named responder, when they first acted, and how it was closed. A false positive that led to a rule change must name the change. This log is what demonstrates that alerting and response are working, not just that tools are installed; it is the artifact attached for the evidence period.

evidenceHint.en: Alert and response log for the period: one row per alert with tool, triggering deviation, responder, time of first response and closure

title.en: Check the monitoring logs for the period and record every registered source that reported nothing

description.en: A feed that stops sending produces no alerts and looks identical to a quiet network, so check liveness directly. Query the monitoring platform for the last event received per source and compare that list against the coverage register. Record the timestamp for every source and raise each source that reported nothing during the period as a gap, naming the asset owner who must restore it. The completed check sheet — every register row marked reporting or silent — is the deliverable.

evidenceHint.en: Source-liveness check sheet: every register row with its last-event timestamp, marked reporting or silent, silent rows assigned to an owner

title.en: Reconcile the monitoring coverage register against the asset inventory

description.en: Match the coverage register line by line to the organisation's inventory of systems and applications to find what is in the estate but watched by nothing. Produce a coverage matrix showing every inventory entry against its monitoring source; for each unmatched entry, record whether monitoring is missing, deliberately out of scope with the stated reason, or pending, and name the owner accountable for closing it. Registered sources that no longer appear in the inventory are removed in the same pass, so the register stops carrying decommissioned assets.

evidenceHint.en: Coverage matrix mapping every inventory asset to its monitoring source, with unmonitored assets, the reason, and the remediation owner per gap

controls.title: Privileged Utility Program Management
controls.objective: To ensure the restricted and controlled use of utility programs capable of overriding system and application controls.
controls.successCriteria:
All utility programs are authorized, necessary, and used only by authorized personnel.
Authorization levels and access rights are properly defined, documented, and adhered to.
Ad hoc use of utility programs is adequately controlled and documented.
Effective segregation of utility programs is implemented and maintained.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain a list of all privileged utility programs used within the organization.
Acquire logs of user activities and access related to these utility programs.
Gather documented authorization levels and access rights for each utility program.
Collect records of ad hoc authorization requests for utility program use.
Retrieve evidence of segregation measures implemented for utility programs (e.g., network segregation documentation, application separation configurations).

Analysis:
Verify each privileged utility program against the list of authorized programs to confirm their necessity and authorized status.
Cross-reference user activity and access logs with authorized user lists to ensure only authorized personnel have used the utility programs.
Review the authorization levels and access rights to ensure they align with the documented standards and are properly implemented.
Examine ad hoc authorization requests for compliance with the policy and proper documentation.
Assess segregation measures to confirm logical and, where applicable, physical segregation of utility programs from application software and network traffic.

Output:
A report listing all privileged utility programs and their authorization status.
Spreadsheet or database entries correlating user activities with authorized access lists.
Compiled documentation of authorization levels, access rights, and ad hoc authorizations.
Analysis report on segregation measures and their effectiveness.

title.en: Inventory every privileged utility program and record why each is needed

description.en: Build one row per utility capable of overriding system or application controls — disk and registry editors, database clients with direct table access, packet capture tools, password recovery and account-manipulation utilities, and the utilities shipped inside vendor support agents — naming the host or image it is installed on, the business reason it is present and whether that reason still holds. A program nobody can justify is the finding this task produces, not a row to leave blank. This inventory is the population the authorisation record, the segregation evidence and the log reconciliation all count against. Attach the dated inventory carrying an authorised or remove verdict against every row.

evidenceHint.en: Dated inventory of privileged utility programs, one row per program, with host or image, business justification and an authorised or remove verdict

text.en: Enumerate installed utility software from endpoint and server software inventories and build images.
Add the utilities shipped inside vendor support and remote-assistance agents.
Record the host, the installing owner and the business reason each program is present for.
Mark any program whose justification no longer holds for removal rather than leaving the row blank.
Date the inventory and hold it as the population the later tasks are counted against.

title.en: Record the authorisation level and the named users permitted to run each utility program

description.en: For every program in the inventory, document the authorisation level it sits at and the individual accounts entitled to invoke it — role names alone will not survive the reconciliation, because the activity logs carry account identifiers. State whether each entitlement is standing or granted per use, since that decides whether an invocation with no matching ad hoc request is a deviation. A program with no named entitled user is a removal candidate rather than an open entitlement. Attach the compiled authorisation record covering every inventoried program with no row left blank.

evidenceHint.en: Authorisation record listing, per utility program, its authorisation level and the named accounts entitled to run it, each marked standing or per-use

title.en: Document how utility programs are segregated from application software and network traffic

description.en: Describe and evidence the separation actually in force: which programs run only from an administrative jump host or a separate management VLAN, which are removed from application servers entirely, and which are held in a restricted repository rather than installed anywhere. Attach the supporting configuration — the firewall or VLAN rules, the application allowlist entries, the repository permissions — rather than a narrative asserting that separation exists. Where a program remains co-resident with the application it can override, record it as a known exposure with a named owner instead of omitting it.

evidenceHint.en: Segregation description with the network segregation rules, allowlist entries and repository permissions implementing it, plus the list of co-resident exceptions and their owners

title.en: Record every ad hoc authorisation to run a utility program with its approver and time window

description.en: Each time somebody is granted use of a utility program outside their standing entitlement, capture the requester, the program, the system it will be run against, the reason, the approver and the period the grant covers. Close each request when that period ends and note whether the entitlement was actually withdrawn, because a grant left open is indistinguishable from a standing entitlement nobody authorised. Attach the ad hoc authorisation records for the period under test.

evidenceHint.en: Ad hoc authorisation records for the period showing requester, program, target system, reason, approver, the period the grant covered and whether the entitlement was withdrawn when it ended

title.en: Reconcile utility program activity logs against the standing and ad hoc authorisation lists

description.en: Take the access and activity logs for the period and match every invocation to either a standing entitlement or an ad hoc request covering that account, that program and the period the invocation falls in. Invocations matching neither are the deviations this task exists to surface; record each with the account, the program, the timestamp and the accountable manager, and carry the unexplained ones into the report's conclusion rather than closing them silently. Attach the correlation spreadsheet with a matched or unmatched verdict against every logged invocation.

evidenceHint.en: Correlation spreadsheet mapping each logged utility program invocation to a standing entitlement or an ad hoc request, with every unmatched invocation and its accountable owner listed

text.en: Pull the activity and access logs covering every inventoried utility program.
Match each invocation to the account's standing entitlement for that program.
Where there is no standing entitlement, look for an ad hoc request covering that account, that program and the period of the invocation.
List every invocation matching neither, with its account, timestamp and accountable manager.

controls.title: Retention of Personal Information
controls.objective: To ensure the retention of personal information aligns with the entity's defined objectives related to privacy, including adherence to legal and regulatory requirements.
controls.successCriteria:
Personal information retention practices are in strict adherence to the entity’s defined objectives and policies.
All systems comply with documented retention schedules.
Any changes to retention practices have been properly documented and comply with the privacy objectives.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Compile a list of systems used for storing personal information.
Obtain data retention policies and schedules applicable to each system.
Gather change logs or records indicating any modifications to retention practices since the last audit.

Analysis:
Review the retention policies and schedules to confirm they align with the entity's privacy objectives.
Compare actual data retention practices in each system against the documented policies and schedules.
Examine change logs to validate that any alterations in retention practices have followed the prescribed process and comply with privacy objectives.

Output:
A comprehensive report documenting the retention practices and their compliance with the entity's privacy objectives.
A spreadsheet comparing each system's retention practices against the documented policies and schedules.
A record of any changes in retention practices and the review process followed for these changes.

title.en: List every system storing personal information that the retention schedule must cover

description.en: The auditor's first request is the list of systems used for storing personal information, and this register is the denominator every later task counts against — the schedule must carry a row for each system, and the comparison reads each system's live retention behaviour. Build it from what is actually running rather than from an architecture diagram: production databases, SaaS applications, file shares, exports, backups and archives all hold personal information and all inherit a retention obligation. Record for each system the categories of personal information it holds and the named owner who can produce its retention configuration when asked. Attach the register carrying the date it was compiled; a row with a blank category or a blank owner is not done, because the later comparison has nobody to ask.

evidenceHint.en: Dated register of systems storing personal information, one row per system, with the personal-information categories held and the named system owner

title.en: Set a retention period, trigger and disposal method for each registered system

description.en: Extend the retention schedule so every row of the register carries the event that starts the clock (account closure, contract end, last transaction), the period counted from that event, and how the data is disposed of when it expires. Beside each period cite the source that set it — the named legal or regulatory obligation where one drives it, otherwise the privacy objective it serves — because the control is tested against adherence to legal and regulatory requirements, not against a period alone. Close every gap between register and schedule: a system present in the register but absent from the schedule, or present with a blank period, is exactly the gap this task exists to close. Attach the issued schedule showing full coverage of the register.

evidenceHint.en: Issued retention schedule with one row per registered system giving the retention trigger, the period, the disposal method and the obligation or privacy objective that set the period

text.en: Take each register row and name the event that starts its retention clock.
Set the period counted from that event and the disposal method applied at the end of it.
Cite the legal or regulatory obligation fixing the period, or the internal objective where none does.
Compare the schedule against the register and add a row for every system not yet covered.
Version the issued schedule so the period in force on any given date is identifiable.

title.en: Record every change to a retention period with the review and approval behind it

description.en: Each time a retention period, trigger or disposal method changes, write a record carrying the system affected, the old and new values, who requested the change, the review it went through and who carried that review out, and the date it took effect. Where the change was made in a system's own configuration, export that system's change log rather than re-keying it by hand, and cover separately any change agreed in a meeting that leaves no machine trace. IT Operations supplies the configuration change exports. This record set is what shows an alteration followed the prescribed process rather than being made quietly at a console, and it is what the audit reads when validating changes made since the last audit. Attach the change record for the period under test, or an explicit nil return where nothing changed.

evidenceHint.en: Retention change record for the period: system, old and new retention value, requester, the review carried out and by whom, and the effective date for each change, with the system change-log exports behind them

title.en: Compare each system's actual retention behaviour against its scheduled period

description.en: Take the register row by row and read the retention actually in force from the system itself — its configured deletion rule and the age of the oldest personal-information record it still holds — rather than from its documentation, because documentation that agrees with the schedule while the system does not is precisely the failure this task exists to catch. Produce the comparison spreadsheet the control calls for: one row per system carrying the scheduled period, the observed setting, the oldest record found and a pass or deviation verdict. Against every deviation record the accountable owner and the remediation agreed. Legal/DPO reviews the verdicts. Attach the spreadsheet together with the raw configuration and query output it was derived from.

evidenceHint.en: Per-system comparison spreadsheet showing scheduled retention, observed retention setting, age of the oldest record held, a pass or deviation verdict, and an owner plus remediation for each deviation

text.en: Pull the configured deletion or retention rule from each registered system itself.
Query the age of the oldest personal-information record the system still holds.
Set the observed behaviour against the scheduled period and mark pass or deviation.
Record the accountable owner and the agreed remediation for every deviation found.

title.en: Check each schedule entry against the privacy objectives and the obligation it cites

description.en: Read the retention schedule against the entity's defined privacy objectives and against the legal or regulatory obligation each row cites, and record a verdict per row: consistent, longer than the obligation permits, shorter than it requires, or citing an obligation that no longer applies. This is the analysis the control asks for before any system is looked at — a schedule that has drifted from the objectives makes every system compliant with the wrong number, and the system comparison would report a clean pass. Raise each inconsistent row as a change through the retention change record rather than editing the schedule in place, so the alteration is documented as the control requires. Attach the review with a verdict per row and the changes raised.

evidenceHint.en: Schedule-to-objective review giving a verdict per schedule row against the privacy objective and the cited obligation, plus the change requests raised for every inconsistent row

controls.title: Third-Party Disclosure Consent Verification
controls.objective: To ensure that personal information is disclosed to third parties only with the explicit consent of data subjects.
controls.successCriteria:
All instances of personal information disclosure to third parties are accompanied by pre-obtained explicit consent from data subjects.
Consent forms or logs are complete, accurate, and correspond to the specific instances of disclosure.
Third-party agreements are consistent with the data subjects' consent provisions.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain a list of instances where personal information was disclosed to third parties.
Collect documented consent forms or digital consent logs for these disclosures.
Acquire third-party agreements that specify the conditions of information sharing.

Analysis:
For each instance of disclosure, verify that explicit consent was obtained from the data subject prior to the disclosure.
Review the consent forms or logs to confirm they clearly relate to the specific disclosure instance and are dated prior to the disclosure.
Cross-reference third-party agreements to ensure they align with the consent provided by data subjects.

Output:
A report detailing each instance of personal information disclosure to third parties.
Verification checklist for consent forms or logs.
Analysis of third-party agreements' compliance with explicit consent.

title.en: Record every disclosure of personal information to a third party in a disclosure register

description.en: The auditor asks first for the list of instances where personal information was disclosed to third parties, and that list is the population every later task works from — the consent check runs down it and the agreement analysis covers the recipients it names. Build one row per disclosure instance rather than one per recipient, carrying the date, the recipient, the categories of personal information sent, the purpose and the data subjects covered. Source the rows from what was actually sent — integration and export logs, ticketed one-off transfers, scheduled feeds — rather than from the contract list, because a disclosure made outside any contract is exactly what this register must not miss. Attach the register for the period under test.

evidenceHint.en: Disclosure register for the period: one row per disclosure instance with date, recipient, personal-information categories sent, purpose and the data subjects covered

title.en: Record the sharing conditions each third-party agreement permits

description.en: For every recipient the disclosure register names, pull the current agreement and extract into a register what it actually permits: the categories of personal information that may be shared, the purposes the recipient may use them for, any onward-disclosure right it grants, and any condition it places on consent. A recipient that received personal information with no agreement in force is recorded as such — that gap is a finding this task produces, not a blank cell. Legal/DPO reads the sharing and consent clauses; Procurement holds the contract set and confirms which version is current. Attach the register with the clause extracts it was built from.

evidenceHint.en: Third-party sharing register giving permitted data categories, permitted purposes and onward-disclosure conditions per recipient, the clause extracts behind them, and the list of recipients with no agreement in force

title.en: Capture the consent record reference and its date against every logged disclosure

description.en: Each time personal information is disclosed, write into the register row the reference of the consent record that authorises it, the date that consent was captured and the wording the data subject agreed to. Export the consent log entries covering the period alongside the register, so a reference can be resolved by somebody without access to the consent platform. Where a disclosure was made with no consent reference, flag the row rather than leaving it blank and carry the flag through to the verification checklist — an unreferenced row is the exception this control exists to surface, and a blank one is indistinguishable from a row nobody has filled in yet. Attach the register with consent references populated and the consent form or log export for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Disclosure register with a consent record reference and consent date on every row, plus the consent forms or consent-log export for the period and the list of rows flagged with no consent reference

title.en: Test each sampled disclosure for consent captured before the disclosure date

description.en: Work down the disclosure register and, for each sampled instance, resolve the consent reference to the actual form or log entry and check three things: that it names the data subject whose information was disclosed, that its scope covers this recipient and this purpose, and that its date falls before the disclosure date. Mark pass or fail per instance and name which of the three failed. A consent captured after the disclosure fails even where its wording would have covered it, because the control requires consent to be pre-obtained. Against every fail record the remediation owner and the correction agreed for that disclosure. Attach the completed verification checklist.

evidenceHint.en: Completed consent verification checklist, one row per sampled disclosure, showing the consent reference resolved, subject match, scope match, consent date against disclosure date, and pass or fail with an owner for each fail

text.en: Resolve each sampled disclosure's consent reference to the form or log entry behind it.
Check the consent names the data subject whose information was actually disclosed.
Check its scope covers this recipient and the purpose the disclosure was made for.
Compare the consent date against the disclosure date and fail any consent captured later.
Assign an owner to each fail and record the correction agreed against that disclosure.

title.en: Compare each third-party agreement's sharing conditions against the consent given

description.en: Set the sharing register beside the consent wording data subjects actually agreed to and record, per recipient, whether the agreement stays inside it. The failures to look for are an agreement permitting categories or purposes the consent does not cover, an onward-disclosure right the data subject was never told about, and a recipient bound by no agreement at all. Record a verdict per recipient with the clause text and consent text that produced it, and raise each inconsistency with the accountable owner named and the correction agreed — an amendment bringing the agreement inside the consent given, or consent whose scope covers what the agreement permits. Attach the analysis with the per-recipient verdicts and the wording relied on.

evidenceHint.en: Per-recipient analysis of third-party agreements against consent wording, giving a verdict, the clause and consent text relied on, and the owner plus agreed correction recorded against each inconsistency

controls.title: Access to Personal Information
controls.objective: To ensure that data subjects have the ability to access their stored personal information and receive copies upon request, in accordance with the entity’s privacy objectives.
controls.successCriteria:
Data subjects are able to access their personal information in a timely and secure manner.
The entity's processes for handling access requests are in compliance with privacy objectives and regulatory standards.
All denials of access are appropriately justified and communicated to the data subjects.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain a list of systems used for storing personal data accessible to data subjects.
Gather samples of requests and responses for access to personal information.
Review the entity's procedures for responding to and processing access requests.

Analysis:
Assess the entity's process for authenticating the identity of data subjects making access requests.
Evaluate the timeliness and appropriateness of the entity's responses to access requests.
Verify that data subjects are informed of the reasons for any denial of access to their personal information.

Output:
A report summarizing the evaluation of the entity's response process to data subject access requests.
A compliance checklist verifying the handling of each access request in line with the entity's privacy objectives.
Documentation of instances where access was denied, including reasons and communication with the data subject.

title.en: List every system holding personal data an access request must be answered from

description.en: Compile the list of systems storing personal data accessible to data subjects: one row per system, the categories of personal data it holds about them, the named person who can extract a copy from it, and the format that copy comes out in. Include systems where a data subject can see their own data directly, since the control covers access as well as the supply of copies. This register is what makes a response complete — a system missing from it is a system nobody searches when a request arrives, and its omission surfaces only when the data subject says the copy is short. Attach the register with an extraction contact and an export format populated for every row.

evidenceHint.en: Register of systems holding data-subject personal data, with the categories held, the named extraction contact and the export format available for each system

title.en: Write the access-request procedure covering identity checks, response time and copy format

description.en: Produce the procedure an operator follows when a request arrives, covering the three things the control's analysis examines. First, how the requester's identity is authenticated before any personal data leaves the organisation, naming the evidence accepted and who verifies it. Second, the period within which a response must be issued, counted from receipt, and the standard or regulation that sets it. Third, the format the copy is supplied in and the secure route it travels. State the grounds on which access may be refused, and require every refusal to be put to the data subject in writing with its reason, because the control tests that denials are justified and communicated rather than simply not answered. Attach the issued procedure.

evidenceHint.en: Issued access-request procedure naming the identity-authentication evidence and verifier, the response deadline and its source, the copy format and delivery route, and the refusal grounds with the written-notification requirement

title.en: Log every access request with the identity check performed and the date answered

description.en: Maintain one register of access requests carrying, per request, the date received, the requester, the identity evidence checked and by whom, the systems searched, the date the response was issued and the outcome (copy supplied, partially supplied, refused). Where the identity check was performed in a ticketing or verification tool, cite the ticket so the check can be resolved later by somebody who was not there. This register is what evidences that requests are handled in a timely and secure manner; without it, timeliness is an assertion and the identity check is unprovable. Attach the register for the period under test.

evidenceHint.en: Access-request register for the period: date received, requester, identity evidence checked and verifier, systems searched, date responded and outcome for each request

title.en: Record the reason and the written notification for every access request refused

description.en: For each request refused in whole or in part, file the reason relied on, the ground in the procedure it maps to, who took the decision, and a copy of the communication sent to the data subject stating that reason. A partial refusal counts: record which data was withheld and why it was withheld. This file is requested by the auditor by name and is the only evidence that a denial was justified and communicated rather than quietly dropped. Attach the refusal file for the period, or an explicit nil return where nothing was refused — a nil return that says so is evidence, an empty folder is not.

evidenceHint.en: Refusal file for the period: per refused or partially refused request, the reason and the procedural ground, the decision maker, the data withheld and a copy of the notification sent to the data subject

title.en: Test a sample of access requests against the procedure's identity check and deadline

description.en: Draw a sample from the request register and, for each, verify that the identity evidence recorded meets the standard the procedure sets, that the response was issued within the deadline counted from receipt rather than from triage, and that the copy supplied covered every register system holding that subject's data. Mark pass or fail per request naming the element that failed, and write a remediation owner and target date against each fail. Attach the completed compliance checklist: it is what shows the process runs to standard, where the procedure alone shows only that a standard exists.

evidenceHint.en: Completed compliance checklist per sampled request showing the identity evidence against the standard, days from receipt to response against the deadline, systems covered, pass or fail, and an owner for each fail

text.en: Draw the sample across supplied, partially supplied and refused outcomes alike.
Check the identity evidence recorded meets the standard the procedure sets.
Count the days from receipt to response and compare against the stated deadline.
Confirm the copy supplied covered every register system holding that subject's data.
Write a remediation owner and target date against each request marked fail.

controls.title: Response Team Structure Management
controls.objective: Ensure a well-defined and competent team structure for effective response to disruptions.
controls.successCriteria:
All response teams and their alternates are clearly identified in the organizational chart.
Roles and responsibilities of each team member are documented and align with control requirements.
Procedures guiding team actions are complete, clear, and cover necessary aspects.
Team members have undergone required training and possess the necessary competence.
Communication with relevant parties during disruptions follows documented procedures and is well-documented.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:

Obtain the organizational chart that identifies the response teams and their members.
Collect role descriptions and responsibilities for each team member and their alternates.
Gather documented procedures guiding the actions of each team.
Acquire training records and competency assessments for team members.
Retrieve communication logs showing interactions with relevant parties during disruptions.

Analysis:

Organizational Chart Review:
Verify that all response teams and their members are clearly identified.
Check for the presence of alternates for key roles.

Role and Responsibility Assessment:
Compare role descriptions with the responsibilities listed in section 8.4.2.
Ensure each team’s role and responsibilities align with the control requirements (8.4.2.2 and 8.4.2.4).

Procedure Documentation:
Review the documented procedures for completeness and clarity.
Confirm that procedures cover activation, operation, coordination, and communication (8.4.2.4b).

Competency and Training Verification:
Assess training records to ensure all team members and alternates have received appropriate training.
Verify competency assessments against the required skills and responsibilities.

Communication and Coordination Logs:
Examine logs to ensure communication with relevant parties, authorities, and media was timely and accurate.
Confirm that communication actions align with documented procedures.

Output:

Organizational Chart Analysis:
Annotated organizational chart with identified teams and roles.

Role and Responsibility Matrix:
Spreadsheet detailing roles, responsibilities, and their alignment with control requirements.

Procedure Review Summary:
Document summarizing the review of procedures and any identified gaps.

Training and Competency Report:
Spreadsheet listing team members, training dates, and competency assessments.

Communication Log Analysis:
Report analyzing communication logs and their compliance with documented procedures.

title.en: Identify each response team, its members and the alternate for every key role

description.en: Annotate the organisational chart so every response team appears with its members, and every key role carries a named alternate who can act when the primary is unavailable. Cover every response team the chart identifies, not the incident team alone. A key role with no alternate is the single point of failure this task exists to surface — record it as a gap against the manager who must fill it rather than leaving the box empty. Attach the annotated chart carrying the date it reflects, with the gap list beside it.

evidenceHint.en: Dated annotated organisational chart identifying every response team, its members and the named alternate per key role, with the list of key roles still lacking an alternate

title.en: Record each team member's and alternate's responsibilities in a matrix

description.en: Turn the annotated chart into a matrix carrying one row per person: their team, their role and the responsibilities they hold while a disruption is running. Read each row back against the responsibilities this control requires of the response teams and mark any requirement that no row covers — an unclaimed responsibility is the finding here, and it disappears if the matrix is written team by team instead of person by person. Alternates get their own rows, not a footnote. Attach the matrix with the requirement coverage check appended.

evidenceHint.en: Role and responsibility matrix with one row per team member and alternate giving team, role and disruption responsibilities, plus the check that every control requirement is claimed by a row

text.en: Create one matrix row per team member and one per named alternate.
State the responsibilities each person holds while a disruption is running.
Check that every control requirement is claimed by at least one matrix row.
Record any requirement that no row covers as a gap with a named owner.

title.en: Document the activation, operation, coordination and communication steps each team follows

description.en: Produce the procedure each response team works from, covering all four aspects: how the team is activated and by whom, how it operates once it is running, how it coordinates with the other response teams, and how it communicates with the parties it must reach. Write it so somebody who has not read the plan before can act from it at three in the morning. Then read the finished document back against those four headings and record any left thin or missing — that gap list is the procedure review summary this control asks for. Attach the documented procedures together with the review summary.

evidenceHint.en: Documented response team procedures covering activation, operation, coordination and communication, plus the review summary naming any of the four found incomplete and its owner

title.en: Record the training completed and the competence assessed for every member and alternate

description.en: Keep one row per team member and alternate showing the training completed, the date, and the outcome of the competence assessment against the responsibilities their matrix row carries. Assess competence rather than recording attendance alone: attendance evidences that a session happened, not that the person can perform the role when the plan is invoked. Carry the people who are untrained, or who did not meet the assessment, into a named follow-up list with target dates. Attach the training and competence spreadsheet for the period, covering alternates as well as primaries.

evidenceHint.en: Training and competence spreadsheet listing every team member and alternate with training dates, the competence assessment outcome against their responsibilities, and the follow-up list

title.en: Log the response teams' communications with relevant parties, authorities and media during a disruption

description.en: While a disruption is running, record each communication as it happens: the time, the party it went to or came from, the channel used, what was said or decided, and the team member who handled it. Cover inbound as well as outbound, because a request from an authority that nobody logged is indistinguishable afterwards from one that never arrived. Mark the entries that went to the media so the analysis can read those separately from operational traffic. Attach the communication log for the disruption.

evidenceHint.en: Disruption communication log giving time, party, direction, channel, content or decision and the team member who handled each communication, with media entries marked

title.en: Analyse the last disruption's communication log against the documented procedure

description.en: Take the communication log from the most recent disruption and read each entry against what the procedure required: was the party one the procedure names, was it reached inside the time the procedure sets, and was the content accurate at the point it was sent. Record a verdict per entry, and for each failure say whether the cause was the procedure being wrong or the procedure not being followed — the two have different remedies and the analysis is worth little without that distinction. Attach the communication log analysis with the entries it examined.

evidenceHint.en: Communication log analysis giving a timeliness and accuracy verdict per logged communication and, for each failure, whether the procedure or its execution was at fault

controls.title: Risk Treatment Plan Implementation
controls.objective: To ensure that risk responses are effectively identified, prioritized, and integrated into the Risk Treatment Plan, aligning with the organization's risk appetite and mitigation strategies.
controls.successCriteria:
The Risk Treatment Plan is up-to-date, comprehensive, and aligns with the organization's risk appetite.
All risk response actions are in alignment with the stated strategies in the Risk Treatment Plan.
Risk prioritization decisions are documented, justified, and align with the organization's strategic objectives and risk management framework.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the latest Risk Treatment Plan document.
Gather documentation of risk assessments and risk response actions taken since the last audit.
Collect records of risk review meetings and decision-making processes related to risk prioritization.

Analysis:
Review the Risk Treatment Plan to ensure it includes strategies for eliminating, mitigating, transferring, or accepting each identified risk.
For each risk response action taken, compare it against the Risk Treatment Plan to validate alignment and effectiveness.
Assess the decision-making process for prioritizing risks, ensuring it aligns with the organization's risk appetite and mitigation strategies.

Output:
A detailed report on the alignment of risk response actions with the Risk Treatment Plan.
A compliance matrix comparing each identified risk with its corresponding response action.
Documentation summarizing the effectiveness and appropriateness of the risk prioritization process.

title.en: Record every identified risk in the treatment plan with its eliminate, mitigate, transfer or accept response

description.en: Take the risk register and make the Risk Treatment Plan carry a row for each identified risk with the response chosen for it — eliminate, mitigate, transfer or accept — so the plan's coverage of the register can be read directly rather than inferred. A risk on the register with no row in the plan, or a row with no response type, is the gap this task closes, and both are the first thing the plan's comprehensiveness is judged on. Where the response is accept, that is a decision to record like any other rather than an absence of one. Attach the current plan showing every registered risk present with a response type populated.

evidenceHint.en: Current Risk Treatment Plan with one row per registered risk showing the response type chosen — eliminate, mitigate, transfer or accept — and no registered risk absent

title.en: Document each treatment action, its accountable owner and where it leaves the risk against appetite

description.en: For every plan row, record what will actually be done to deliver the chosen response, who is accountable for doing it, and where the risk is expected to sit against the organisation's stated appetite once that action is complete. The control asks the plan to align with that appetite, so a row that cannot be read against it cannot be assessed at all. An action written as an intention rather than a deliverable cannot be assessed either, so state what will exist when it is complete. Where a risk is accepted, record the justification and who accepted it in the same columns rather than leaving them blank. Attach the plan showing action, owner and expected position against appetite populated on every row.

evidenceHint.en: Risk Treatment Plan extract showing, per risk, the treatment action, the accountable owner, where the risk is expected to sit against the stated appetite once the action is complete, and for accepted risks the justification and acceptor

text.en: Write the deliverable each treatment action produces, not the intention behind it.
Name the individual accountable for the action, confirmed with that person.
Record where the risk is expected to sit once the treatment action lands.
State that expected position in the terms the risk appetite is stated in.
For accepted risks, record the justification and who took the acceptance decision.

title.en: Capture the prioritisation decision and its justification in each risk review record

description.en: At each risk review, record which risks were prioritised, the reasoning behind that ordering, who was present and who decided — against the organisation's risk appetite and strategic objectives, which is what the decision has to be defensible against. Record the risks explicitly deprioritised as well as those advanced, since a decision to leave a risk untreated is the one that most needs its justification written down. Where a prioritisation moved against the appetite, record that and the reason it was accepted. Attach the review records for the period; a minute recording attendance and outcomes but not the reasoning does not evidence this control.

evidenceHint.en: Risk review records for the period showing, per review, the risks prioritised and deprioritised, the justification against risk appetite and objectives, the attendees and the decision maker

title.en: Log each risk response action taken and the plan entry it discharges

description.en: Every response action carried out since the last audit is recorded with the risk it addresses, the plan entry it discharges, what was done, who did it, the completion date and the evidence produced. An action taken outside the plan is logged in the same place and flagged as unplanned rather than being fitted retrospectively into a plan row, because that flag is what the alignment assessment reads. Where an action was started and abandoned, record that and the reason. Attach the action log for the period with the completion evidence it references.

evidenceHint.en: Risk response action log for the period giving, per action, the risk, the plan entry discharged, the work done, the operator, the completion date, the evidence, and the unplanned flag where applicable

title.en: Assess each risk response action taken against the strategy recorded in the plan

description.en: Build the compliance matrix the control calls for: one row per identified risk, showing the response the plan states, the actions actually taken against it, and a verdict on whether those actions deliver the stated strategy. Score three failure shapes separately, because they need different responses — a plan entry with no action taken, an action that does not match the strategy recorded, and an action taken against no plan entry at all. For each, name the accountable owner and the correction agreed, whether that is executing the action or amending the plan. Attach the matrix with the alignment report drawn from it.

evidenceHint.en: Compliance matrix pairing every identified risk with its planned response and the actions taken, carrying an alignment verdict per risk and an owner plus correction for each untreated, misaligned or unplanned entry

text.en: Set each plan entry beside the actions the log records against that risk.
Mark the plan entries for which no action was taken during the period.
Mark the actions whose effect does not deliver the strategy the plan records.
Mark the actions taken against no plan entry and decide whether the plan should carry them.
Name an owner and an agreed correction against every row that is not aligned.

title.en: Verify every risk on the register carries a current treatment and sits within appetite

description.en: Read the plan against the risk register as it stands now and against the stated risk appetite, and report three things: risks on the register absent from the plan, plan rows whose risk assessment has changed since the treatment was chosen, and risks whose position after treatment sits outside the stated appetite. The second is the one an out-of-date plan hides — a treatment that was proportionate at the last assessment and is no longer. Take each out-of-appetite risk back to the accountable decision maker for a fresh treatment or a recorded acceptance rather than closing it in the report. Attach the coverage review with those three lists and their dispositions.

evidenceHint.en: Plan coverage review listing risks absent from the plan, treatments superseded by a changed assessment, and risks whose position after treatment sits outside the stated appetite, each with its disposition and decision maker

controls.title: Secure Area Access and Activity Control
controls.objective: To ensure that access to and activities within secure areas are managed effectively, maintaining confidentiality, integrity, and availability of assets and information.
controls.successCriteria:
All access to secure areas is authorized and monitored.
No unauthorized or unsupervised activities are occurring within secure areas.
Recording and endpoint devices are used in compliance with organizational policies.
Emergency procedures are appropriately posted and accessible in all secure areas.
Information about secure areas is only disclosed on a need-to-know basis.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain a current list of all secure areas within the organization.
Collect recent access logs and surveillance footage (if available) of these secure areas.
Gather policies and procedures related to secure area access and equipment usage.
Acquire records of any authorization forms for recording equipment or endpoint devices in secure areas.
Get copies of posted emergency procedures in each secure area.

Analysis:
Review access logs to verify that access is limited to authorized personnel.
Compare surveillance footage with access logs to check for unsupervised work or unauthorized access.
Assess adherence to policies regarding the use of recording equipment and endpoint devices within secure areas.
Validate that emergency procedures are properly posted and accessible in all secure areas.
Ensure that awareness of the existence of or activities within secure areas is restricted to individuals with a need-to-know basis.

Output:
A report summarizing findings from access log and surveillance footage analysis.
A compliance assessment report regarding the use of recording and endpoint devices.
An evaluation of the visibility and accessibility of emergency procedures in secure areas.

title.en: Register every secure area with its authorised personnel and monitoring coverage

description.en: Produce one row per secure area — the areas the organisation designates as secure, not every lockable room — giving its location, the custodian accountable for it, the personnel authorised to enter, and whether surveillance covers the entrance and the interior. Where an area is covered by no camera, say so in the row rather than leaving the column blank, because a later task compares footage against access records and cannot do so for an area with none. Attach the register with the authorised-personnel list held against each area.

evidenceHint.en: Secure-area register giving, per area, the location, custodian, authorised personnel list and the surveillance coverage of entrance and interior

title.en: Record the authorisation held for every recording and endpoint device permitted in a secure area

description.en: Collect the authorisation forms for cameras, phones, laptops, removable media and any other recording or endpoint device permitted inside a secure area, and build a register from them: the device, its owner, the area it is permitted in, the conditions attached and who authorised it. A device in regular use inside a secure area with no form behind it is the gap this task produces, and this register is what the footage review is read against. Attach the register together with the signed authorisation forms.

evidenceHint.en: Device authorisation register naming each permitted recording or endpoint device, its owner, the secure area, the conditions attached and who authorised it, with the signed forms attached

title.en: Test each secure area's access log against its authorised personnel list

description.en: Pull the access records for every secure area over the period under test and match each entry to that area's authorised personnel list. Record one row per unmatched entry giving the person, the area, the time and the disposition — covered by a temporary authorisation and which one, or an exception referred to the area custodian. Include contractor and visitor entries, which are the ones an area's authorised-personnel list is least likely to name. Attach the access log extract with the dispositioned exception list.

evidenceHint.en: Secure-area access log extract for the period plus an exception list giving each unmatched, contractor or visitor entry with the person, area, time and its disposition

text.en: Pull the access records for every secure area across the period under test.
Match each entry against the area's authorised personnel list from the register.
Record every unmatched entry, and every contractor or visitor entry, as its own row.
Disposition each row against a temporary authorisation or refer it to the custodian.

title.en: Review surveillance footage against the access log for unsupervised work and unauthorised device use

description.en: Sample time windows from the areas the register marks as covered by surveillance and watch the footage against the access records for the same window, looking for three things: presence with no corresponding badge event, work carried out alone where the policy requires a second person, and recording or endpoint devices in use that the device authorisation register does not cover. Record what was reviewed — area, date, window length — so an absence of findings means something, and give each finding a disposition and an owner. Security engineering assesses the device findings. Attach the footage review sheet and retain the relevant clips for as long as the policy allows.

evidenceHint.en: Footage review sheet naming each area, date and window reviewed, with every instance of unbadged presence, unsupervised work or unauthorised device use and its disposition

title.en: Inspect every secure area for posted, current and accessible emergency procedures

description.en: Walk each area in the register and record whether the emergency procedure is posted, whether the copy on the wall is the current version, whether it is legible and lit, and whether it is reachable from inside the area rather than only from the corridor outside. Photograph each posting so the evaluation is evidenced rather than asserted, and raise a replacement item with an owner and a date for every area that fails on any of the four. Attach the inspection sheet with the photographs and copies of the posted procedures.

evidenceHint.en: Inspection sheet with one row per secure area covering posted, current version, legible and reachable, plus a photograph or copy of each posting and a remediation owner for every failure

title.en: Check where each secure area is named or located outside its need-to-know list

description.en: Look for the places the existence, location or activity of a secure area is disclosed to people outside its need-to-know list: door signage naming what is inside, building directories and floor plans, intranet pages and team wikis, calendar invitations giving the room and its purpose, and contractor briefing packs. Record each disclosure found with what it reveals, who can see it, and the remediation agreed with the area custodian. Attach the review naming the sources checked, so a short finding list is read as thorough rather than cursory.

evidenceHint.en: Need-to-know disclosure review listing the sources checked, each disclosure of a secure area's existence, location or activity, its audience and the remediation agreed

controls.title: Secure Development and Testing Control
controls.objective: To ensure that all new information systems, upgrades, and new versions undergo thorough security testing and verification during the development and acceptance processes, in line with established security requirements and best practices.
controls.successCriteria:
All reviewed projects demonstrate comprehensive security testing in accordance with the secure development policy.
Security testing activities cover all critical areas: security functions, secure coding, and secure configurations.
Effective management and security assessment of third-party components are evident.
The existence and effectiveness of WAF implementations and distinct environments for development, testing, and production are confirmed.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the development and deployment documentation for recent projects, including security testing plans and reports.
Gather evidence of security testing activities, such as results from static and dynamic analysis, code reviews, penetration test reports, and security assessments of third-party components.
Collect documentation on the separation of development, testing, and production environments.

Analysis:
Review the security testing documentation to ensure comprehensive coverage of security functions, secure coding, and secure configurations.
Evaluate the adherence to secure development lifecycle processes, including threat modeling, risk-based security requirements, and security testing methodologies.
Assess the effectiveness of the Web Application Firewall (WAF) implementations through its configuration and update history.
Confirm the proper management and security assessment of third-party components.
Verify the implementation of distinct environments for development, testing, and production.

Output:
A report detailing the findings of the security testing documentation review.
A compliance matrix aligning the actual security testing activities with the organization's secure development policy.
An assessment report on the effectiveness of the WAF and third-party component management.

title.en: Inventory the new systems, upgrades and versions released in the period and their acceptance status

description.en: This control covers new information systems, upgrades and new versions alike, so build the list from the deployment record rather than from the project plan — an upgrade shipped outside a project is precisely the release that reaches production untested. Record each release, the system it changed, its release date and whether it has passed acceptance. This list is the denominator the testing coverage is measured against, and a release missing from it is a release nobody will ask for test evidence about. Attach the release inventory for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Release inventory for the period listing every new system, upgrade and version with the system it changed, its release date and its acceptance status

title.en: Set the security test plan covering security functions, secure coding and secure configuration for each release

description.en: For each release in the inventory, record before testing begins what will be tested and how: the security functions to be exercised, the secure coding checks to run against the changed code, and the configuration baseline the deployed system will be measured against. Name the methodology and the risk-based security requirement each test traces to, so coverage can later be read against the secure development policy rather than judged by volume of output. A plan written after the results is not a plan. Attach the test plan recorded against each release before its testing began.

evidenceHint.en: Security test plan per release, recorded before testing begins, naming the security functions, secure coding checks and configuration baseline in scope, and the security requirement each planned test traces to

text.en: List the security functions the release introduces or changes and must exercise.
Name the static and dynamic analysis tools and the code the checks will run over.
State the configuration baseline the deployed system will be measured against.
Trace each planned test to the risk-based security requirement it verifies.
Record the plan against the release before its testing begins.

title.en: Run the static analysis, dynamic analysis, code review and penetration test for each release

description.en: Execute the plan against each release and keep the raw output, not only a summary: the static and dynamic analysis results, the code review record showing who reviewed what, and the penetration test report. Record the date each was run and the build or commit it covered, because a report predating the code it is claimed to cover is the failure this evidence exists to expose. Findings are recorded here with their severity; their closure belongs to the release's acceptance. Attach the test results for every release in the inventory.

evidenceHint.en: Static and dynamic analysis results, code review records and penetration test reports per release, each carrying the date it was run and the build or commit it covered

title.en: Record the security assessment of each third-party component before it enters a release

description.en: For every third-party component a release introduces or updates, record the component and version, the assessment carried out on it, who cleared it and when. Where a component was brought in without assessment, log it as such rather than omitting it — this control is tested on third-party components being effectively managed and assessed, and an incomplete register reads as no components rather than as unassessed ones. Attach the component assessment record covering the releases in the period.

evidenceHint.en: Third-party component assessment record per release giving component and version, the assessment performed, the clearing party and the date, including any component admitted without assessment

title.en: Verify the web application firewall configuration and update history against the rules it is meant to enforce

description.en: Pull the firewall's current rule configuration and its update history for the period, and check both: that the rules deployed are the ones the protected applications actually need, and that the rule set has been maintained rather than left at its installation state. Record which applications sit behind it and which do not, since an application outside its coverage is not protected by a well-maintained configuration. Attach the configuration export and the update history with the effectiveness assessment written against them.

evidenceHint.en: Web application firewall configuration export and update history for the period, with the coverage list showing which applications sit behind it and the effectiveness assessment written against both

title.en: Map each release's completed testing against the secure development policy and report the gaps

description.en: Build the compliance matrix this control asks for: one row per release showing which of the planned security function, secure coding and secure configuration tests were completed and which policy requirement each satisfies. Include the environment separation documentation with it, since the policy's requirement for distinct development, testing and production environments is part of what a release is accepted against. Where a release went to acceptance with a gap, name the gap, the risk accepted and the person who accepted it. Attach the matrix and the findings report.

evidenceHint.en: Compliance matrix mapping each release's completed security testing to the secure development policy requirements, with the environment separation documentation attached and a named acceptor against every gap

text.en: List each release beside the security tests its plan said would be run.
Mark each planned test completed, partially completed or not run at all.
Map every completed test to the secure development policy requirement it satisfies.
Attach the documentation showing development, testing and production remain distinct.
Name the risk accepted and the accepting person for each release with a gap.

controls.title: Engagement with Special Interest Groups
controls.objective: To ensure the organization actively participates in and benefits from engagement with relevant special interest groups and security forums for information security improvement and awareness.
controls.successCriteria:
Active and relevant participation in identified special interest groups and forums.
Regular and effective internal dissemination of information and best practices acquired from these groups.
Demonstrable impact of the information acquired on the organization's information security posture and practices.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain a list of special interest groups and security forums in which the organization is a member.
Gather documentation or electronic records of interactions, such as meeting minutes, emails, and information bulletins received from these groups.
Collect records of internal dissemination of information acquired from these groups, such as emails, newsletters, or presentations to staff.

Analysis:
Verify the relevance and activity level of each group or forum to the organization's information security needs.
Review the documentation or records of interactions to assess the regularity and quality of information exchange.
Assess how the information from these groups is utilized internally to improve information security practices.

Output:
A report detailing the organization's engagement with each group or forum.
An assessment report on the effectiveness of information dissemination within the organization.
Recommendations for improving engagement and information utilization.

title.en: Register every special interest group and security forum the organisation belongs to

description.en: One row per group or forum, carrying whether the membership is current or lapsed, the named person who represents the organisation in it, the access the membership confers — mailing lists, advisories, closed briefings, events — and the specific information security need it serves. That last column is what makes the register usable: a membership nobody can tie to a need is precisely what the later assessment recommends letting lapse. Include informal forums and vendor security communities alongside paid memberships, since the control asks about engagement rather than subscription spend. Attach the dated register.

evidenceHint.en: Dated register of special interest groups and security forums with membership status, the named representative, the access it confers and the information security need it serves

title.en: Collect the interaction record for each group across the period

description.en: For every group on the register, file what the membership actually produced during the period — meeting minutes, advisories and bulletins received, threads the representative took part in, briefings and events attended — against that group's row. A group with no interactions filed is not a recording failure; it is evidence of a dormant membership and is recorded as an explicit nil, because that is the finding the activity assessment needs and an empty folder cannot supply it.
