Attach the interaction file organised by group, with a short note per group of what the membership yielded.

evidenceHint.en: Interaction file per group for the period holding the minutes, bulletins, advisories and attendance records received, with an explicit nil entry recorded against any group that produced nothing

title.en: Record each internal dissemination of information taken from a group

description.en: Whenever material from a group is passed on inside the organisation — an advisory forwarded to engineering, a briefing summarised in a newsletter, a technique presented to the security team — record the source group, the date, the audience it reached and the form it took. The control tests whether the membership benefits the organisation rather than only the individual who holds it, and an advisory received but never disseminated is indistinguishable in effect from one never received. Attach the dissemination record with the newsletters, emails or presentation material behind it.

evidenceHint.en: Internal dissemination record for the period showing per item the source group, the date, the audience reached and the form used, with the newsletters, emails or slides attached

title.en: Trace each change to security practice back to the group information that prompted it

description.en: Keep a short log linking specific intelligence received from a group to what the organisation did about it: the advisory or discussion, the decision taken, the control, configuration or process that changed as a result, the owner and the date. Where the decision was to take no action, record that with the reason — a considered no is evidence of utilisation and an unanswered advisory is not. This log is the only artifact that can demonstrate an effect on the organisation's security posture rather than mere participation, which is what the control's third success criterion asks for. Attach the log for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Impact log linking each item of group intelligence to the resulting change in control, configuration or process, or to the reasoned decision to take none, with an owner and date for each

title.en: Evaluate each membership's activity and dissemination reach, and recommend which to keep, add or lapse

description.en: Work down the register and judge each membership on what it produced this period: interactions filed, material disseminated and changes traced back to it. Score each as active and useful, active but undisseminated, or dormant, and against every dormant or undisseminated membership name the reason — the representative left, the group changed focus, or no route existed to pass the material on. Conclude with the memberships to renew, the coverage gaps that argue for joining another group, and the memberships to let lapse. Attach the engagement report with the dissemination effectiveness assessment.

evidenceHint.en: Engagement report scoring each registered group on interactions, dissemination and traced impact, with a renew, add or lapse recommendation and the reason recorded for each

text.en: Count the interactions filed against each group for the period from the interaction file.
Count the dissemination entries and the traced changes attributable to each group.
Score each membership as active and useful, active but undisseminated, or dormant.
Record the reason behind every dormant and every undisseminated verdict.
Recommend renewal, a new membership or lapse for each row, with the reason stated.

controls.title: Cloud Service Management
controls.objective: To ensure the acquisition, use, management, and exit from cloud services are conducted in alignment with the organization's information security policies and standards.
controls.successCriteria:
All cloud services are in alignment with the organization’s selection criteria and usage policies.
Cloud service acquisition and exit processes comply with the organization's policies and procedures.
Effective management of information security risks associated with cloud services.
Proper handling and response to security incidents in cloud services as per the incident management policy.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain a list of all active cloud services and contracts used by the organization.
Gather documentation on cloud service acquisition and exit processes.
Collect evidence of cloud service management activities, including security reviews, risk assessments, and compliance checks.
Acquire incident management logs related to cloud services.

Analysis:
Review the list of cloud services against approved cloud service selection criteria and scope of usage.
Assess the adequacy of cloud service acquisition and exit processes against established policies and procedures.
Evaluate the effectiveness of cloud service management activities, focusing on how information security risks are identified, managed, and mitigated.
Analyze incident management logs to ensure proper handling and response to security incidents in cloud environments.

Output:
A report detailing each cloud service and its compliance status with selection criteria and usage scope.
A compliance assessment report for cloud service acquisition and exit processes.
An evaluation report of cloud service management activities.
An analysis report of incident management logs related to cloud services.

title.en: Inventory every active cloud service with its contract, owner and approved scope of use

description.en: The auditor's opening request is the list of all active cloud services and contracts in use, and this register is the population every later task runs against — the criteria assessment reads each row, and an exit route has to exist for each row. Build it from what is actually being paid for and connected rather than from an architecture diagram: pull the expense ledger, the SSO application list and the egress or DNS records, and reconcile the three so a service present in only one of them still reaches the register. Capture per service the provider, the contract or order form reference, the internal owner, the information it holds, the business use it serves, and the date the contract ends or renews. Attach the dated register; a row with no named owner is not done.

evidenceHint.en: Dated cloud service register listing provider, contract reference, internal owner, the information held, the business use served and the contract end or renewal date for every active service

text.en: Pull candidate services from the expense ledger, the SSO application list and egress or DNS records.
Reconcile the three sources so a service appearing in only one of them still reaches the register.
Record the provider, the contract or order form reference and the internal owner of each service.
Record the information each service holds and the business use it serves.
Record the contract end or renewal date, which is what makes the exit process reachable in time.

title.en: Record the selection criteria and approved scope of use a cloud service must meet

description.en: The compliance assessment later in this control has nothing to judge a service against until the selection criteria and the approved scope of use exist as stated values rather than as an impression. Write down what a candidate service must satisfy before it is acquired, and the uses it may then be put to, naming the uses that are out of scope as explicitly as the ones that are permitted. State each line so a reviewer can mark a service pass or fail against it — a criterion that can only be scored 'broadly aligned' will produce that verdict for every service, including the ones that should fail. Attach the issued criteria and scope statement carrying its approval.

evidenceHint.en: Issued cloud service selection criteria and approved-scope statement, each requirement written so a service can be marked pass or fail against it and the out-of-scope uses named

title.en: Document the acquisition and exit process for a cloud service, including data return and deletion

description.en: Produce the acquisition and exit process documentation an auditor asks for as its own artifact — an operating instruction somebody follows, not a statement that a process exists. The acquisition half names who assesses a candidate against the selection criteria, what evidence the provider must supply, and who authorises the contract. The exit half is the one usually missing: who triggers exit, how data is returned and in what format, how the provider's remaining copies are deleted and what deletion evidence is accepted, and how the accounts, keys and integrations that outlive the contract are closed. Attach both documents with a responsible role named at every step.

evidenceHint.en: Issued cloud acquisition and exit procedure naming the assessing, authorising and exit-triggering roles, the data return format, the deletion evidence accepted from the provider, and the account and integration closure steps

text.en: Name the role that assesses a candidate service against the selection criteria.
List the security evidence a provider must supply before a contract is authorised.
Name who authorises acquisition and where that authorisation is recorded.
Set out how data is returned at exit, in what format and to whom.
Set out how the provider's remaining copies are deleted and what deletion evidence is accepted.
Cover closing the accounts, keys and integrations that survive the contract itself.

title.en: Record the security review and risk assessment carried out for each cloud service

description.en: For every service in the register, carry out and record the security review and risk assessment this control expects as evidence of management activity: the risks the service introduces, the provider assurance relied on, how each risk is being managed or mitigated, the residual position recorded and the date of the review. Where a service was assessed at acquisition and nothing has changed, record that conclusion and the check that established it rather than leaving the row blank — a blank row is indistinguishable from a service nobody has looked at since it was bought. Attach the review records covering the period.

evidenceHint.en: Cloud service security review and risk assessment records for the period, one per registered service, showing the risks identified, the provider assurance relied on, how each risk is managed or mitigated and the residual position recorded

title.en: Log every security incident raised against a cloud service and how it was resolved

description.en: Keep the cloud incident management record as its own extractable set: which service, what happened, when it was detected and by whom, whether the provider or the organisation handled it, the response taken and the date it closed. Include incidents the provider notified as well as those detected internally, because provider-notified incidents are exactly the ones absent from an internally scoped incident queue and living instead in a vendor support portal. This log is what shows incidents in cloud environments are handled under the incident management policy rather than informally. Attach the log for the period under test.

evidenceHint.en: Cloud incident log for the period showing service, detection date and source, whether the provider or the organisation handled it, the response taken and the closure date

title.en: Assess each registered cloud service against the selection criteria and approved scope

description.en: Take the register row by row and mark each service against the selection criteria and the approved scope of use, producing the per-service compliance report this control calls for. Read the live position rather than the acquisition-time paperwork: the information actually held in the service now, the uses it has been put to, and the integrations added since it was bought. Give each service a pass or deviation verdict and, for every deviation, the accountable owner and the agreed remediation — including services in use that never went through the acquisition process at all, which is the deviation this reconciliation exists to surface. Attach the report.

evidenceHint.en: Cloud compliance report giving a pass or deviation verdict per registered service against the selection criteria and approved scope, with an accountable owner and agreed remediation for each deviation

text.en: Mark every register row against each line of the selection criteria.
Check the information actually held and the uses made of the service against the approved scope.
Flag services found in use that never went through the acquisition process.
Name an accountable owner and an agreed remediation against each deviation.

controls.title: Physical Security Perimeter Audit
controls.objective: To ensure that the physical security measures in place effectively protect the organization's facilities, assets, and proprietary information against unauthorized access or physical threats.
controls.successCriteria:
All physical security perimeters are in good condition and provide adequate protection.
All surveillance and access control systems are functioning as intended, with no unauthorized access or breaches identified.
Regular maintenance and testing of physical security systems are being conducted in compliance with the policy.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain a comprehensive list of all physical security perimeters (e.g., fences, walls, doors, barriers) around the organization's facilities.
Collect records of recent physical security tests and maintenance activities.
Gather footage or logs from surveillance systems (like CCTV) and access control systems for a specified period.

Analysis:
Evaluate the condition and effectiveness of each physical perimeter, checking for any vulnerabilities or breaches.
Review the maintenance and testing records to confirm regular upkeep and functionality of physical security barriers.
Analyze surveillance and access control logs to identify any unauthorized access attempts or security breaches.

Output:
A detailed report on the state and effectiveness of each security perimeter.
A log analysis report highlighting any security incidents or unusual activities.
A maintenance and testing compliance report for physical security systems.

title.en: List every physical security perimeter with the facility and boundary it protects

description.en: Give each perimeter element a row — perimeter fences, external and internal walls, doors, gates, barriers and turnstiles — naming the facility it belongs to, the boundary it forms, its construction, and the custodian accountable for its condition. Include the delivery and plant-room boundaries people forget, since those are where the inspection usually finds a defect. This register is the population the condition inspection, the maintenance schedule and the compliance report all work from. Attach the register carrying the date it was compiled.

evidenceHint.en: Dated register of physical security perimeters listing, per element, the facility, the boundary it forms, its construction type and the accountable custodian

title.en: Record the maintenance and test interval the policy requires for each perimeter and monitoring system

description.en: Read the interval each element is due from the physical security policy and write it against the register row: what the maintenance or functional test consists of, how often it falls due, and who performs it — in-house or a named contractor. Cover the surveillance and access control systems on the same schedule as the physical elements, because the compliance report a later task produces needs one yardstick for both. Where the policy is silent on an element, record that silence rather than inventing an interval, and refer it for a decision. Attach the schedule showing an interval or a recorded gap against every register row.

evidenceHint.en: Maintenance and test schedule with an interval, a test description and a named performer against every perimeter, surveillance and access control element, and the policy gaps recorded explicitly

title.en: Inspect each perimeter and record its condition and any breach point found

description.en: Walk every element in the register and record its condition against what it is supposed to resist: damage and corrosion, gaps beneath and beside it, doors propped or failing to latch, defeated or bypassed barriers, and climbing aids such as stored pallets, bins and vegetation left against a fence. Photograph each defect, give it a severity against what it exposes, and name the owner and target date for putting it right. Attach the inspection sheet with the photographs; it is the state-of-the-perimeter evidence the report is built from.

evidenceHint.en: Perimeter inspection sheet with one row per element giving its condition, each defect found with a photograph, the severity assigned, and the remediation owner and target date

text.en: Walk each element in the register rather than sampling by facility.
Record damage, gaps, corrosion and any door or gate failing to latch.
Note climbing aids and stored material left against a fence or wall.
Photograph every defect and assign it a severity against what it exposes.
Name a remediation owner and target date for each defect recorded.

title.en: Record each maintenance visit and functional test carried out in the period

description.en: Every time maintenance or a functional test is performed on a perimeter element, a camera or an access control system, write a record carrying the element, the activity, the date, who performed it, the outcome and any part replaced or fault left open. Where a contractor issues its own service report, file that rather than re-keying it, and record separately the in-house checks that produce no report of their own. This record set is what the compliance report is measured against, and a visit that produced no record is indistinguishable from a visit that never happened. Attach the maintenance and test records for the period under test.

evidenceHint.en: Maintenance and functional test records for the period, one entry per activity giving element, date, performer, outcome and any fault left open, with contractor service reports attached

title.en: Analyse the surveillance and access control logs for unauthorised access attempts

description.en: Take the CCTV and access control records covering the specified period and work through them for denied badge reads repeated at one door, entries outside a person's normal pattern or hours, doors held or forced open, and cameras offline during the window. Record one row per event with the location, the time, what the footage shows and its disposition — explained, or referred as a suspected breach. Note the periods for which no footage or log exists at all, because a gap is itself a finding. Attach the log analysis report with the extracts it rests on.

evidenceHint.en: Log analysis report listing each unauthorised access attempt, door-forced or held event and camera outage with location, time, what the footage showed and its disposition, plus any period with no records

title.en: Compare the maintenance and test records against the schedule and report the misses

description.en: Put the schedule and the period's records side by side and report, per element, whether the maintenance and functional testing due were actually performed and within the interval. The misses are the finding — an element never tested, a test performed late, a fault raised at the last visit still open — and each carries a cause, an owner and a date. Attach the compliance report with the schedule and the records behind it, so its conclusion can be re-derived rather than taken on trust.

evidenceHint.en: Maintenance and testing compliance report giving, per element, the interval due, the activity actually performed, a within-interval verdict, and a cause and owner for every miss or open fault

controls.title: Information and Asset Use Compliance
controls.objective: To ensure that all individuals accessing or using the organization's information and associated assets adhere to the defined standards of acceptable use, maintaining the integrity, confidentiality, and security of these assets.
controls.successCriteria:
All users comply with the acceptable use standards as per the Acceptable Use Policy.
Effective monitoring mechanisms are in place to detect and report non-compliant activities.
Incidents of policy violations are minimal and appropriately addressed.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the current Inventory of Information and Associated Assets document.
Gather comprehensive details for each asset, including network addresses (if static), hardware addresses, machine names, data asset owner, and department.
Acquire evidence of network connection approvals for each asset, particularly for mobile end-user devices.
Gather ownership assignment records for each listed asset and signed asset return forms for terminated or changed employment cases.
Acquire logs of recent updates or changes made to the asset inventory and records of asset tracking upon employee exit.

Analysis:
Review the inventory document for completeness, accuracy, and inclusion of additional required details such as network and hardware addresses, machine names, data asset owners, departments, and network approval status.
Cross-check ownership records against each asset and returned assets against the Asset Registry.
Analyze change logs and asset tracking logs to verify that inventory updates, including the additional details, and asset returns are consistent, timely, and comply with policy.

Output:
A comprehensive report detailing findings from the inventory review, including the verification of additional asset details.
A spreadsheet or database capturing the alignment of ownership records with the enhanced asset inventory and returned assets.
Summary of discrepancies or gaps identified during the analysis, especially in regards to the newly added asset details.

title.en: Record the network address, hardware address, machine name, owner and department for every asset

description.en: The audit reads the Inventory of Information and Associated Assets for completeness of exactly these fields, so work it row by row and fill them: the static network address where one is assigned, the hardware address, the machine name, the named data asset owner and the owning department. Where an address is dynamic rather than static, record it as dynamic rather than leaving the cell blank — a blank is indistinguishable from a row nobody examined, and the completeness review counts blanks without knowing which kind it found. Attach the inventory export with its date and the count of rows still incomplete.

evidenceHint.en: Dated asset inventory export showing network address, hardware address, machine name, data asset owner and department per row, with the count of rows still carrying a blank in any of those fields

text.en: Work from the live inventory export rather than a copy, so the edits land on the record itself.
Fill the network address where one is statically assigned, and mark dynamic where it is not.
Fill the hardware address and machine name for each asset from the system that manages it.
Name the data asset owner and the owning department on every row of the inventory.
Report the count of rows still carrying a blank in any of these five fields.

title.en: Record the network connection approval held for each asset, mobile end-user devices included

description.en: For every asset in the inventory, capture the approval that permits it to connect: who approved it, on what date, and to which network or segment. The audit calls mobile end-user devices out separately because they connect intermittently and are the class most likely to be on the network with no recorded approval — give each of them its own row rather than covering them as a category. An asset connecting with no approval on file is listed as such, and that list is the finding this task produces. Attach the approval records with the unapproved list beside them.

evidenceHint.en: Network connection approval records per asset showing approver, approval date and the network approved for, together with the list of connected assets holding no approval, mobile end-user devices itemised

title.en: File the signed asset return form for every employee exit and role change

description.en: Whenever employment terminates, or a role changes such that assets must be handed back, complete and file the signed return form naming each asset returned, its inventory identifier, the date of return and who received it. HR supplies the leaver and mover list this is run against, and the two have to be reconciled: a departure on the HR list with no return form is precisely the exception the audit looks for. Where an asset is outstanding, record it as outstanding with a named person chasing it rather than closing the form short. Attach the signed forms for the period with the leaver and mover list behind them.

evidenceHint.en: Signed asset return forms for the period, each naming the assets returned, their inventory identifiers, the return date and the recipient, plus the leaver and mover list they were reconciled against

title.en: Log every asset inventory edit against the issue, return or disposal that prompted it

description.en: Keep a change log for the inventory itself: which row changed, which field, who changed it, when, and the event that prompted it — an asset issued, an owner or department change, a return, a disposal. The audit reviews these logs for timeliness, so the prompting event's date matters as much as the edit's date; the gap between the two is the number that gets read, and an edit with no prompting event recorded cannot be assessed as timely at all. Attach the change log covering the period since the last audit.

evidenceHint.en: Asset inventory change log for the period showing the row and field changed, the editor, the edit date, the prompting event and the date that event occurred

title.en: Reconcile ownership records and returned assets against the asset registry

description.en: Cross-check both directions the audit asks for, and record them in one sheet: every asset in the inventory against the ownership assignment record naming its holder, and every asset recorded as returned against the registry entry that should now show it unassigned or disposed. Give a row per asset with a matched or discrepancy verdict, and against each discrepancy — an asset with no ownership record, an owner who has since left, a return form with no corresponding registry update — name the accountable owner and the correction agreed. Attach the reconciliation sheet with the discrepancy summary drawn from it.

evidenceHint.en: Reconciliation sheet aligning ownership assignment records and returned assets with the asset registry, one row per asset with a matched or discrepancy verdict, and a discrepancy summary naming an owner and correction for each

text.en: List every inventory asset against the ownership assignment record that names its holder.
Check each named holder is still employed and still in the role the assignment assumed.
Take each signed return form and confirm the registry now shows the asset unassigned or disposed.
Mark every row matched or a discrepancy, naming which kind of discrepancy it is.
Name an accountable owner and the agreed correction against each discrepancy found.

title.en: Review the period's acceptable use violations and the action taken on each

description.en: Pull every non-compliant use of information or assets that the monitoring in place reported during the period, and record for each: what was detected, the asset and the person involved, the date, and the action taken to close it. Where the period produced no reports at all, state which monitoring was actually running and over which assets — a nil return that cannot name what was watching is evidence of nothing, and it is the shape a broken detector takes. Attach the violation record with the disposition of every entry.

evidenceHint.en: Acceptable use violation record for the period listing each detected incident, the asset and person involved, the mechanism that detected it and the action taken to close it, or a nil return naming the monitoring that was running

controls.title: Script Allowlisting Control
controls.objective: Ensure that only authorized scripts, such as specific .ps1, .py, etc., files, are allowed to execute on company systems. Unauthorized scripts must be blocked to maintain system integrity and security.
controls.successCriteria:
All script executions match the authorized scripts on the allowlist, with valid digital signatures and correct version control.
No evidence of unauthorized script executions on the systems.
System configurations effectively block unauthorized scripts.
All changes to the script allowlist have been properly authorized, documented, and aligned with the IT Security Policy.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Get the list of IT systems where script execution is relevant.
Retrieve the allowlist of authorized scripts, including details like script names, digital signatures, and version numbers.
Collect system logs showing script execution attempts and outcomes.
Obtain change management records for updates or modifications to the script allowlist.

Analysis:
For each script execution logged, verify against the allowlist to ensure only authorized scripts have been executed.
Examine the digital signatures and version numbers of the executed scripts to ensure they match the authorized versions.
Review system configurations to confirm that controls for blocking unauthorized scripts are operational.
Analyze change management records to validate that updates to the script allowlist have been properly authorized and documented.

Output:
List of all IT systems reviewed.
Spreadsheet or report detailing each script execution against the allowlist.
System configuration snapshots demonstrating script blocking controls.
Compiled change management records related to the script allowlist.

title.en: List the systems where script execution is relevant and the interpreters installed on each

description.en: Identify where scripts can run at all: servers, workstations, build agents and any appliance hosting an interpreter, one row each, naming the interpreters present — PowerShell, Python, shell, and any interpreter bundled inside an application — the operating system build, the owner, and the allowlisting agent enforcing on it. A system carrying an interpreter and no agent is the gap this list exists to reveal, so record it as unenforced rather than omitting it. Attach the list; it is the population every later task is measured against.

evidenceHint.en: List of IT systems where script execution is possible, giving the interpreters installed, the operating system build, the owner, and the enforcement agent or an unenforced marking

title.en: Record every authorised script on the allowlist with its digital signature and version

description.en: Populate the allowlist so an entry identifies one specific artifact rather than a name any file could take: the script name and path, its digital signature or pinned hash, the version, what it does, the owner who maintains it, and the systems it is permitted to run on. A script that cannot be signed is recorded with its hash pinned and the reason it is unsigned, because a name-only rule is exactly what lets a replaced file through. Attach the allowlist export.

evidenceHint.en: Allowlist export with one row per authorised script: name and path, digital signature or pinned hash, version, purpose, owner and the systems it may run on

title.en: Set each system to block scripts that are not on the allowlist and export the running configuration

description.en: Move each system on the list from audit to enforcement: apply the policy that blocks unlisted scripts, confirm signature or hash validation is on rather than name matching alone, and confirm the policy cannot be sidestepped by invoking the interpreter directly. Export the running configuration from each system afterwards with its export date, so enforcement can be evidenced without console access. Against any system that cannot enforce — an unsupported platform, an interpreter the agent does not cover — record the reason and the compensating measure applied. Attach the configuration snapshots.

evidenceHint.en: Dated configuration snapshot per system showing the enforcement mode, the signature validation setting and the block rule, plus the reason and compensating measure recorded for any system that cannot enforce

text.en: Apply the blocking policy on each system rather than leaving it in audit mode.
Confirm signature or hash validation is enforced, not name matching alone.
Run an unlisted script and confirm the attempt is both blocked and logged.
Export the running configuration from each system and stamp it with the export date.
Record the reason and the compensating measure for every system that cannot enforce.

title.en: Log every script execution attempt and its outcome on the systems in scope

description.en: Configure the enforcement agent and the interpreters to record each execution attempt and forward it to a store the reconciliation can read: the host, the user or service account, the script name and path, the signature or hash presented, the version, the timestamp, and whether execution was allowed or blocked. The blocked attempt is the more valuable of the two records, so confirm blocks are logged and not silently discarded. Attach the log export covering the period under review.

evidenceHint.en: Script execution log export for the period showing host, account, script name and path, signature or hash, version, timestamp and allowed or blocked outcome for every attempt

title.en: Raise a change record for every addition to or removal from the script allowlist

description.en: Each allowlist change goes through change management before it is applied: the request names the script, its signature and version, the systems it is being permitted on, the business reason, and the person authorising it, and the record closes with the date the change took effect and the resulting allowlist version. A change applied before its record was raised carries both real dates rather than a back-dated one, so the reconciliation can see the gap. Attach the change records raised in the period.

evidenceHint.en: Change management records for allowlist additions and removals in the period, each showing the script, signature and version, the systems affected, the justification, the approver and the effective date

title.en: Reconcile every logged execution against the allowlist and report the unauthorised ones

description.en: Take the execution log and test each entry against the allowlist as it stood at the time of execution: was the script listed, did the signature and version presented match the authorised entry, and was the host one that entry permits. Record the outcome per execution in a spreadsheet and disposition every mismatch — an unlisted script that ran, a signature that did not match, a version older or newer than the authorised one — as either a legitimate change that bypassed the process or an incident referred for investigation. Cross-check the allowlist entries themselves against the change records, so an entry that appeared with no authorising change is reported too. Attach the spreadsheet with its dispositioned exceptions.

evidenceHint.en: Reconciliation spreadsheet scoring each logged execution against the allowlist entry in force, with every unlisted script, signature mismatch or version mismatch dispositioned, plus any allowlist entry carrying no authorising change record

controls.title: Environment Segregation Control
controls.objective: To ensure that development, testing, and production environments are adequately separated and secured to prevent unauthorized access and changes, and to mitigate the risk of production system disruptions.
controls.successCriteria:
Clear and documented segregation between development, testing, and production environments.
Access controls and change management procedures are in compliance with the segregation policy.
No unauthorized access or changes in the production environment.
Sensitive information in development and testing environments is adequately protected.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain a list of all systems and environments categorized as development, testing, and production.
Gather configuration details and access control lists for each environment.
Collect recent change management logs and deployment records from development to production.

Analysis:
Verify that each environment (development, testing, production) is operating in separate domains or physical/virtual environments.
Check that access controls are in place and align with the segregation policy, ensuring that compilers, editors, and development tools are not accessible from production systems unless necessary.
Review change management logs to confirm that changes to production systems are tested in the testing or staging environment first and that there are no unauthorized changes or tests in the production environment.
Assess if sensitive information is copied into the development and testing system environments and if equivalent controls are in place.

Output:
A report detailing the segregation and security measures of each environment.
A spreadsheet analyzing access controls and compliance with the segregation policy.
A change management review report.

title.en: Inventory every system with its environment classification and the domain or host it runs on

description.en: Record each system once, classified development, testing or production, with the domain, host or virtual infrastructure it actually runs on. The classification alone proves nothing — two environments sharing a host or a domain are not separated whatever the label says, so the infrastructure column is what makes this list evidence. Flag any system whose classification is ambiguous or that serves more than one environment. Attach the inventory as the population the access control analysis and the change review both run against.

evidenceHint.en: Environment inventory listing every system with its development, testing or production classification and the domain, host or virtual infrastructure it runs on

title.en: Record each environment's access control list and flag every account holding access across two of them

description.en: Export the access control list for each environment and build the analysis spreadsheet this control's output calls for: who holds access to each environment, at what privilege, and — the column that matters — which accounts appear in more than one. A named individual with both development and production access is not automatically wrong, but it is the row the segregation policy has to justify explicitly. Record the justification or the removal against each. Attach the spreadsheet with the raw access exports behind it.

evidenceHint.en: Access control analysis spreadsheet per environment with the raw exports behind it, flagging every account holding access to more than one environment and the justification or removal recorded against each

text.en: Export the access control list from each development, testing and production system.
Record each account's privilege level in the environment it holds access to.
Compare the lists and flag every account appearing in more than one environment.
Record the segregation policy justification or the removal decision for each flag.
Hold the raw exports alongside the spreadsheet so the analysis can be re-derived.

title.en: Remove compiler, editor and development tool access from production systems, or record why each remains

description.en: Go through the production systems in the inventory and identify the compilers, editors, debuggers and development utilities present on or reachable from them. Remove each one that has no operational need, and for each that stays, record the production task that makes it necessary on that system. This control is tested on those tools not being accessible from production unless necessary, so the list of what was kept and why is as much the deliverable as the removals themselves. Attach the before-and-after list per production system.

evidenceHint.en: Per production system, the development tools found, those removed, and for each tool retained the production task that makes it necessary there

title.en: Record for every production change the testing or staging environment it was proven in

description.en: Each change reaching production carries, in its change record, the environment it was tested in first and the reference to that test result. Where a change was applied straight to production — an emergency fix, a configuration touch — record it as such with the authority who permitted it, rather than leaving the field blank; a blank is indistinguishable from an untested change and will be read as one. Attach the change management log for the period showing the field populated on every record.

evidenceHint.en: Change management log for the period giving, against each production change, the testing or staging environment it was proven in and the test reference, or the authority who permitted a direct change

title.en: Test the change and deployment records for changes or testing carried out directly in production

description.en: Read the deployment records against the change log for the period and look for the three things this control names: production changes with no prior test, deployments with no change record at all, and testing activity performed in the production environment. Disposition each hit either as authorised — naming the approval or exception covering it — or as an exception referred for investigation. Attach the change management review report with the deployment records it was read against; an empty exception list evidences nothing unless the records show they were examined.

evidenceHint.en: Change management review report for the period listing production changes made without prior testing, deployments with no change record, and testing performed in production, each dispositioned as authorised or referred

text.en: Reconcile the deployment records against the change log for the same period.
List production changes carrying no reference to a prior test in another environment.
List deployments with no matching change record raised for them at all.
Identify any testing activity performed against the production environment itself.
Disposition each hit as authorised, naming the approval covering it, or refer it.

title.en: Assess whether operational data copied into development or testing carries controls equivalent to production

description.en: Identify where operational information has been copied into the development and testing environments in the inventory, and compare the protection applied there against what the same data carries in production — access restriction, encryption, retention. Where the controls are weaker, record the difference and the exposure it creates rather than only the fact of the copy. Together with the environment inventory and the access analysis this produces the segregation report this control's output calls for. Attach the assessment naming each copy, its source system and the control comparison.

evidenceHint.en: Assessment listing each copy of operational data held in a development or testing environment, its source system, and the controls applied there set against those the data carries in production

controls.title: Data Subject Information Request Management
controls.objective: To efficiently manage and respond to data subjects' requests for an accounting of their personal information and disclosures.
controls.successCriteria:
All requests for information are responded to in a timely and accurate manner as per policy.
Responses to data subjects are complete and comply with the organization’s privacy objectives.
The process for handling information requests demonstrates adherence to legal and regulatory requirements.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Collect records of data subject information requests received since the last audit.
Obtain documentation of responses provided to these requests.
Review policies and procedures for managing and responding to data subject requests.

Analysis:
Assess each request and corresponding response to ensure compliance with policies and procedures.
Verify the completeness and accuracy of the information provided to data subjects.
Evaluate the timeliness of responses against policy standards.

Output:
A detailed report on data subject request handling.
Analysis summary of the adequacy and timeliness of responses.
Documentation of any discrepancies or non-compliance in handling requests.

title.en: Set what an accounting response must contain and the deadline it is measured against

description.en: The control scores responses on completeness, accuracy and timeliness, so both standards have to be written down before any request can be scored against them. Record in the procedure what an accounting must list — the personal information held about the data subject and the disclosures made of it, with recipients and dates — and the period within which the response must be issued, citing the legal or regulatory requirement that sets that period where one does. State how the accounting is assembled and how its completeness is checked before it goes out, so that check happens before the response leaves rather than at audit. Attach the issued procedure showing the content standard and the deadline together.

evidenceHint.en: Issued procedure for accounting requests naming the required content of a response, the response deadline and the requirement that sets it, and the completeness check performed before issue

title.en: Log every request for an accounting with its receipt date and the date it was answered

description.en: Record one row per request received since the last audit: the date received, the data subject, what was asked for (information held, disclosures made, or both), the person handling it, the date the response was issued and the elapsed days. Include requests withdrawn or closed without a response, with the reason, since those are otherwise invisible to the timeliness analysis and read as though they never arrived. This register is the population the audit samples from — a request answered but never logged cannot be shown to have been answered at all. Attach the register covering the whole period since the last audit.

evidenceHint.en: Request register covering the period since the last audit: date received, data subject, request type, handler, date responded and elapsed days for each request, including those withdrawn or closed unanswered

title.en: File the response issued to each requester with the accounting it supplied

description.en: For every logged request, keep the response as it was sent together with the accounting attached to it, filed against its register row so the pair can be produced together. The auditor asks for documentation of responses, and a register row marked answered with nothing behind it evidences nothing. Where the accounting was assembled from several systems, keep the extracts it was built from alongside it, so its completeness and accuracy can be tested later without re-running the search — by which time the underlying data has moved on. Attach the response file for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Response file for the period: the issued response and the accounting supplied for each register row, with the source extracts the accounting was assembled from

title.en: Test each logged response against the content standard and the deadline

description.en: Work down the register and score each response on the two things the analysis names: whether it was issued within the procedure's deadline counted from the receipt date, and whether the accounting it carried contained everything the content standard requires and is accurate against the source extracts filed with it. Mark pass or fail per request naming the element that failed, and against every fail record the cause, the remediation owner and the target date, so the discrepancy and its disposition travel together in one sheet. Attach the scored analysis; an empty discrepancy list is evidence only when the sheet shows every request was actually scored.

evidenceHint.en: Scored analysis of every logged request: days to respond against the deadline, content completeness and accuracy against the standard, pass or fail per request, and the cause plus remediation owner for each fail

text.en: Count the elapsed days from receipt to issue for every request on the register.
Check each response against the content standard the procedure sets out.
Verify the accounting supplied against the source extracts filed beside it.
Mark pass or fail and name the element that failed for each request scored.
Record the cause, remediation owner and target date against every fail.

controls.title: Information Security Policy Compliance
controls.objective:
To ensure that the organization's Information Security Policy 

and its topic-specific policies are up-to-date, approved by top management, communicated effectively, and reviewed regularly to reflect changes in business strategy, regulations, information security risks, and the threat environment.
controls.successCriteria:
All Information Security and topic-specific policies are current, reflect organizational needs, and are approved by top management.
Evidence of effective communication and acknowledgment of these policies by relevant personnel.
Regular reviews and updates of policies following changes in business strategy, regulatory environment, and information security landscape.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the latest version of the Information Security Policy and all topic-specific policies (e.g., access control, incident management, asset management).
Gather records of policy reviews, updates, and approvals by top management.
Collect evidence of policy communication and acknowledgment by relevant personnel and interested parties.
Acquire documentation of the latest management reviews and information security audits.

Analysis:
Review the Information Security Policy and topic-specific policies to ensure they are aligned with business strategy, legal requirements, risks, and threats.
Verify that policies have been approved by top management and that any changes are also approved.
Check that the policies have been communicated to and acknowledged by the relevant personnel.
Analyze the results of management reviews and audits to ascertain if they have led to any updates in policies.

Output:
A report verifying the current status and alignment of the Information Security Policy and topic-specific policies.
A compliance checklist for each policy, indicating approval, communication, and acknowledgment status.
Summary of findings from the review of management audits and their impact on policy updates.

title.en: Register the Information Security Policy and every topic-specific policy with its version and owner

description.en: One row per policy — the Information Security Policy itself and each topic-specific policy such as access control, incident management and asset management — carrying the current version number, its issue date, the named owner and the audience it applies to. Build it from what is actually published to staff rather than from the document library's index, because a superseded version still reachable on an intranet page is a live policy for everyone who finds it. This register is the population the approval, acknowledgment and alignment tasks are all counted against. Attach the register with the version and issue date populated on every row.

evidenceHint.en: Policy register listing the Information Security Policy and every topic-specific policy with current version, issue date, named owner and the audience it applies to

title.en: Define the events and the cycle that trigger a review of each registered policy

description.en: Against each policy in the register, record what obliges it to be reviewed: the periodic cycle it sits on, and the events that force an out-of-cycle review — a change in business strategy, a change in the regulatory environment, a material change in the risk or threat picture, or a finding from a management review or security audit. Name who is responsible for noticing each trigger, because a trigger nobody watches for is why policies go stale between scheduled reviews and why a review schedule alone does not satisfy this control. Attach the schedule showing full coverage of the register.

evidenceHint.en: Policy review schedule covering every registered policy with its review cycle, the events that force an out-of-cycle review, and the person responsible for noticing each trigger

title.en: Record top management's approval of each policy version and each subsequent change

description.en: For every version in the register, hold the record showing that top management approved it: the approving body or individual, the date, and the meeting minute, signature or workflow entry that carries it. Changes made after approval need their own approval record — an amended policy carrying only the original approval is the gap this task finds and it is invisible from the document itself. Where a policy is in force with no approval record at all, record it as unapproved rather than omitting the row, and route it for approval with an owner. Attach the approval records mapped one to one against the register's versions.

evidenceHint.en: Approval record per policy version and per subsequent change naming the approver, the date and the minute, signature or workflow entry, mapped one to one against the policy register

title.en: Track communication and acknowledgment of each policy by the personnel it applies to

description.en: For each policy, record how it was communicated to the audience the register names and who has acknowledged it, with dates. Report the applicable population, the acknowledged count and the outstanding names — a percentage alone cannot be followed up, and the named individuals are the only actionable output. Include interested parties outside the employee population where a policy binds them, such as contractors and suppliers. HR supplies joiner and leaver movements so the population is the current one rather than the one captured when the policy was issued. Attach the acknowledgment report per policy.

evidenceHint.en: Acknowledgment report per policy showing the communication method and date, the applicable population, the acknowledged count and the named individuals still outstanding

title.en: Test each policy's content against current business strategy, legal obligations and the threat picture

description.en: Read each registered policy against four things: the organisation's current business strategy, the legal and regulatory obligations binding it today, the current information security risks, and the current threat picture. For each policy record a verdict — aligned, or a statement of what has changed and what the policy now says that is wrong or missing. Legal/DPO supplies the current regulatory position. The output is a per-policy verdict with the specific amendments named and assigned, not a general statement that the policy set remains fit for purpose. Attach the alignment report with each amendment assigned to the policy owner in the register.

evidenceHint.en: Policy alignment report giving a verdict per registered policy against business strategy, legal obligations, risk and threat, with the specific amendments required and an owner named for each

text.en: List the changes in business strategy and organisational structure since the last review.
Record the legal and regulatory changes bearing on the policy set, supplied by Legal.
Read the current information security risk and threat picture for what the policies now miss.
Give each registered policy an aligned or amend verdict and name the specific amendment.
Assign each required amendment to the policy owner named in the register.

title.en: Trace each management review and audit finding to the policy change it produced

description.en: Take the findings from the most recent management reviews and information security audits and map each one to the policy amendment it caused, giving that amendment's version and date, or to an explicit record of why no policy change was needed. Findings falling into neither column are the open residue and are the substance of this task's report. This closes the loop the control's objective describes — reviews and audits are meant to drive the policy set forward, and without this trace there is no evidence that they do. Attach the traceability summary with the unresolved findings listed and owned.

evidenceHint.en: Traceability summary mapping every management review and audit finding to the policy version it changed or to a recorded reason no change was needed, with the unresolved findings listed and owned

controls.title: Network Services Security
controls.objective: Ensure the security mechanisms, service levels, and service requirements of network services are identified, implemented, and regularly monitored.
controls.successCriteria:
All network services meet the identified security measures and service requirements.
Monitoring of network services is regular and in compliance with the established procedures.
Third-party attestations are valid, current, and in line with organizational security standards.
Network and network service usage rules are comprehensive, up-to-date, and effectively enforced.
Network service usage logs align with established authentication and authorization procedures.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain a comprehensive list of all network services used (both internal and external).
Gather documentation or evidence of security measures implementation for each network service (e.g., security features, service levels).
Acquire records of regular monitoring activities and audit rights exercised on network service providers.
Collect third-party attestations from network service providers, if applicable.
Retrieve current rules and policies related to network and network service usage.
Access records or logs of network service usage, including authentication and authorization details.

Analysis:
Cross-reference each network service against its corresponding security measures to ensure compliance.
Verify the regularity and thoroughness of monitoring activities.
Check for the existence and validity of third-party attestations.
Review network usage rules and policies for completeness and relevance.
Analyze network service usage logs for adherence to defined authentication and authorization procedures.

Output:
A report detailing the security measures in place for each network service.
A compliance matrix showing the alignment of each service with its respective security requirements.
Documentation or records of monitoring activities and third-party attestations.
A summary of findings on the review of network usage rules and policies.
An analysis report of network service usage logs.

title.en: Inventory every internal and external network service in use

description.en: List each network service the organisation depends on — internal ones such as DNS, DHCP, directory, remote access and inter-site links, and externally supplied ones such as carrier circuits, internet access, cloud interconnect and managed network services — giving each its provider, the business function it carries and the owner accountable for it. Build it from what the network actually carries rather than from the contracts on file, so a service running with no agreement behind it appears as a row rather than as an absence. This inventory is the population every later task counts against: the security-measures record has to address each row and the compliance matrix reads each row back. Attach the dated inventory with the internal or external marker populated on every row.

evidenceHint.en: Dated network services inventory, one row per service, showing the provider, an internal or external marker, the function it carries and the accountable owner

text.en: Enumerate the internal services the network provides: DNS, DHCP, directory, VPN, remote access and inter-site links.
Add every externally supplied service: carrier circuits, internet access, cloud interconnect and managed network services.
Name the provider for each row, whether an internal team or the supplier holding the agreement.
Record the business function each service carries so its service requirements can be set against it.
Mark each row internal or external and date the inventory as the baseline the later tasks read.

title.en: Record the security measures, service levels and service requirements agreed for each network service

description.en: Work down the inventory and, against every row, write the security mechanisms the service provides or is required to provide (authentication, encryption, filtering, segregation), the service level committed for it, and the security requirements the organisation places on it. Take the values from the agreement, service description or configuration that actually governs the service rather than from what is assumed, and where a row has none, record that gap explicitly — an unstated requirement cannot be monitored or tested later. Procurement supplies the contracted service levels for supplier-provided services. Attach the completed per-service record with no row left carrying neither a security measure nor a stated gap.

evidenceHint.en: Per-service security-measures record covering the security mechanisms, the committed service level and the organisation's security requirements for every inventoried service

title.en: Publish the rules for the use of networks and network services

description.en: Issue the usage rules that say which people and systems may use which network services, the authorisation needed before access is granted, and the conditions attached to each — remote access, third-party connections, use of externally supplied services. Cover every service on the inventory so the rules and the inventory cannot diverge, and state the authentication and authorisation procedure the usage records will later be tested against, since a log can only be judged against a rule that exists. Attach the issued and dated rules together with the record of how they were communicated to the people they bind.

evidenceHint.en: Issued and dated network and network-service usage rules, covering every inventoried service, with the record of how they were communicated

title.en: Record each monitoring activity and exercise of audit rights over network service providers

description.en: For each period, keep the record of the monitoring actually performed over the network services: availability and security-mechanism checks against the agreed service levels, review of provider service reports, and any audit right exercised over a supplier. Every entry names the service, what was checked, the date, who performed it and what was found, so that regularity can be judged rather than asserted. Where an agreement grants an audit right that was not exercised in the period, record that explicitly rather than leaving the service absent from the record; Procurement holds the contractual audit-right clauses. Attach the monitoring record for the period with the provider reports it was built from.

evidenceHint.en: Monitoring record for the period, one entry per service, naming the check performed, the date, the person and the outcome, with the audit rights exercised and the provider reports behind them

title.en: Test a sample of network service usage records against the authentication and authorisation procedure

description.en: Pull the usage records covering the period for the services on the inventory — session, connection and access logs carrying the account, the service reached, the authentication method and the authorisation that permitted it — and sample them against the published usage rules. Mark each sampled session as conforming or as an exception, and for every exception name the rule breached and the owner following it up. Where a service produces no usable usage record, record that as a finding against the service rather than leaving the row blank: an empty exception list is evidence only when the extract shows the records were actually read. Attach the extract with the completed sampling sheet.

evidenceHint.en: Network service usage log extract for the period plus the sampling sheet giving account, service, authentication method, authorisation and a conforming or exception verdict per sampled session

text.en: Pull the usage records for each inventoried service covering the period under test.
Draw a sample that covers internally provided and externally supplied services alike.
Check each sampled session's authentication method against the published usage rules.
Confirm the authorisation that permitted the access was recorded and still valid at the time.
Name the rule breached and an owner against every session marked as an exception.

title.en: Build the compliance matrix aligning each network service with its security requirements

description.en: Take the inventory row by row and set each service's observed state against the security measures and service requirements recorded for it, producing the matrix with a met or deviation verdict per requirement. For every externally supplied service, obtain the provider's current third-party attestation, record its scope and expiry date, and treat an absent or lapsed attestation as a deviation rather than as an unknown. Against each deviation name the accountable owner and the remediation agreed with them. Attach the matrix together with the attestations it cites.

evidenceHint.en: Network services compliance matrix giving a met or deviation verdict per service and requirement, the third-party attestations with their scope and expiry, and an owner plus remediation for each deviation

text.en: Set each service's observed security mechanisms against the requirements recorded for it.
Record a met or deviation verdict for every requirement against every service.
Obtain the current attestation for each externally supplied service and note its scope and expiry.
Treat a missing or lapsed attestation as a deviation and give it an accountable owner.
Carry every unresolved deviation into the conclusion with its agreed remediation date.

controls.title: Correction and Amendment of Personal Information
controls.objective: To ensure the entity efficiently processes data subjects' requests to correct, amend, or append their personal information, and communicates these changes to relevant third parties.
controls.successCriteria:
Efficient and timely processing of data subjects' requests for correction, amendment, or appending of their personal information.
Compliance with established procedures for processing these requests and communicating changes to third parties.
Adequate documentation and tracking of correction/amendment requests and the entity's responses.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Compile a list of systems where personal data subject to correction/amendment requests is stored.
Gather samples of correction/amendment requests and the entity's responses.
Review the entity's procedures for processing and communicating corrections or amendments of personal information.

Analysis:
Assess the process for handling requests for correction or amendment, ensuring it aligns with the entity's privacy objectives.
Evaluate the timeliness and effectiveness of the entity's responses to such requests.
Verify that the entity communicates any corrections or amendments of personal information to third parties who have received this data.

Output:
A report summarizing the assessment of the entity's processes for handling and responding to correction/amendment requests.
A compliance checklist evaluating each request against the entity's procedural standards.
Documentation of instances where corrections/amendments were communicated to third parties.

title.en: List every system holding personal information a correction request must reach

description.en: Compile the list of systems where personal information subject to correction or amendment is stored, recording for each the named person who can apply an edit, whether the edit propagates to downstream copies, and which third parties are fed from it. That last column is not decoration: it is what produces the notification list when a correction is made, so a blank there means a third party goes untold. Include reporting stores, exports and backups, because a correction applied only in the system of record leaves the old value in circulation everywhere else. Attach the register with an edit contact and a downstream-recipient value populated for every row.

evidenceHint.en: Register of systems holding correctable personal information, with the named edit contact, the downstream copies fed from it and the third-party recipients that receive data from each system

text.en: Enumerate the systems holding personal information a correction could have to reach.
Name the person able to apply an edit in each system and the route they use.
Record whether the edit propagates to reporting copies, exports and backups.
List the third parties fed by each system so the notification list falls out of the register.

title.en: Write the correction procedure covering how an amendment is applied and who is notified

description.en: Produce the procedure the control asks for: how a request to correct, amend or append personal information is received and validated, how the change is applied across every system in the register rather than only where the request happened to arrive, the period within which the entity responds to the data subject, and how third parties that already received the information are told of the change. Name what is recorded at each step, so the tracking the control requires falls out of the process rather than being reconstructed from memory at audit. Attach the issued procedure.

evidenceHint.en: Issued correction and amendment procedure naming the validation step, the systems a change must reach, the response period and the third-party notification route

title.en: Log every correction, amendment and append request with the systems changed

description.en: Record one row per request: the date received, the data subject, what they asked to have corrected, the decision taken (applied, applied in part, refused with the reason), each system the change was applied in with the date it was applied, and the date the response went to the data subject. A request applied in one system and not another is recorded as partial rather than complete — that distinction is exactly what the sampling test later reads, and a row marked complete hides it. Attach the tracking register for the period under test.

evidenceHint.en: Correction request register for the period: data subject, requested change, decision taken, each system changed with its date, and the date the data subject was answered

title.en: Record the notification sent to each third party that received the corrected information

description.en: For every correction applied, work down the third-party recipients the register lists for the affected systems, send them the corrected value, and file what was sent, to whom, on what date and by what route. Where a recipient did not need telling — the disclosure predates the corrected data, or the agreement has ended — record that reasoning against the recipient rather than omitting the row, so the omission is a decision somebody took and can be questioned. This file is the evidence the auditor asks for by name. Attach the notification records for the period, or an explicit nil return where no correction reached a third party.

evidenceHint.en: Third-party notification records for the period: per correction, each recipient told, what was sent, the date and route, and the recorded reason against any recipient not told

title.en: Test a sample of correction requests against the procedure's deadline and system coverage

description.en: Draw a sample from the tracking register and check each against the procedure on three points: that the response reached the data subject within the stated period counted from receipt, that the corrected value is actually in force in every system the register lists for that data, and that every third-party recipient was notified or carries a recorded reason. Verify the last two in the systems and the notification file themselves rather than from the tracking sheet, since the sheet is the thing being tested. Mark pass or fail per request naming the failing element, and give each fail a remediation owner and target date. Attach the completed compliance checklist.

evidenceHint.en: Completed checklist per sampled request: days to respond against the procedure, the corrected value confirmed in each affected system, third-party notification confirmed, pass or fail, and an owner per fail

text.en: Draw the sample across applied, partially applied and refused decisions alike.
Count the days from receipt to the response reaching the data subject.
Read the corrected value back from each system the register lists for that data.
Confirm every third-party recipient was notified or carries a recorded reason.
Assign a remediation owner and target date to each request marked fail.

controls.title: Physical Entry Security Control
controls.objective: To ensure secure areas are protected by appropriate entry controls and access points, mitigating the risk of unauthorized physical access.
controls.successCriteria:
All physical access control policies and procedures are up-to-date, comprehensive, and in line with industry best practices.
No instances of unauthorized access are detected in the access logs.
All physical access control systems are operational and properly maintained.
Visitor management is consistent with policy requirements, with all visitors authorized and logged appropriately.
Inspection procedures for personal belongings at entry and exit points comply with legal requirements and are effectively enforced.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Retrieve the current access control policy documentation and any related procedures.
Collect records of access logs from all entry points (e.g., main entrances, delivery and loading areas) for a specified period.
Gather details of physical access control systems in use (e.g., biometric, card readers, PIN systems).
Obtain visitor logs, including visitor identities, entry and exit times, and areas accessed.
Acquire the list and procedures of personal belongings inspections at entry and exit points.

Analysis:
Review access control policies and procedures to ensure they are comprehensive and in line with best practices.
Analyze access logs to identify any unauthorized access or anomalies (e.g., access during odd hours, access by unauthorized personnel).
Examine physical access control systems' configurations and maintenance records to ensure they are functioning as intended.
Cross-check visitor logs against authorized visitor lists to verify all visitors were authorized and appropriately supervised.
Assess the inspection procedures of personal belongings to ensure they comply with local laws and are effectively implemented.

Output:
A report detailing the findings of the policy and procedure review.
A spreadsheet or database of access log analysis highlighting any discrepancies or unauthorized access incidents.
A summary of physical access control systems' status and maintenance checks.
A report on visitor log analysis, indicating compliance with visitor management procedures.
An evaluation report on personal belongings inspection procedures.

title.en: Register every entry point with the access control system that governs it

description.en: List each controlled entry point — main entrances, side and fire doors used for entry, delivery and loading areas, and the doors into secure areas beyond reception — and record against each the type of control on it (biometric reader, card reader, PIN pad, key, staffed desk), the area it admits people to, whether it produces an electronic log, and the custodian accountable for it. A door controlled only by a key or by a person is still a row, because the log analysis has to account for entries it cannot see. Attach the register with the system details for each point.

evidenceHint.en: Entry-point register giving, per point, the access control type in use, the area it admits to, whether it produces an electronic log and the accountable custodian

title.en: Test the access logs from every entry point for out-of-hours and unauthorised entries

description.en: Pull the access records from each entry point in the register for the period under test — main entrances and the delivery and loading areas included, which are the ones usually left out — and work through them for anomalies: entries by people not authorised for the area, entries outside the hours the policy treats as normal for that point, and repeated denied reads at one door followed by a successful entry. Give each anomaly a row with the person, the point, the time and a disposition. Attach the analysis spreadsheet with the raw log extracts it was built from.

evidenceHint.en: Access log analysis spreadsheet with one row per anomaly giving the person, entry point, time, anomaly type and its disposition, attached to the raw log extracts

text.en: Pull access records for every entry point in the register, delivery and loading areas included.
Flag entries by people not authorised for the area they entered.
Flag entries outside the hours the policy treats as normal for that point.
Flag denied reads repeated at one door and then followed by a successful entry.
Disposition each anomaly as explained or refer it to the entry point's custodian.

title.en: Cross-check every visitor log entry against the authorised visitor list and its host

description.en: Take the visitor records for the period and check each one against the list of visitors authorised in advance: is there an authorisation, does the named host match, are the entry and exit times both recorded, and do the areas accessed match what was authorised. Visitors with no sign-out, no host, or access to an area beyond their authorisation are the findings this task produces, and each carries the host's explanation and the action taken. Attach the visitor log analysis with the visitor records and the authorised list behind it.

evidenceHint.en: Visitor log analysis giving, per visitor, the authorisation held, the host, entry and exit times, the areas accessed and an exception verdict with the action taken

title.en: Record each access control system's operational status and last maintenance check

description.en: Go through the systems the register names — biometric readers, card readers, PIN pads and the controllers behind them — and record for each whether it is operating, when it was last serviced or functionally tested, what faults are outstanding, and whether any reader is currently in a failed-open or bypassed state. A reader that is offline or propped into permanent unlock is what makes the access log analysis incomplete, so this task's findings are read alongside it. Attach the status summary with the maintenance records supporting each date.
