evidenceHint.en: Access control systems status summary listing each reader and controller with its operational state, last maintenance or test date, outstanding faults and any failed-open or bypassed condition

title.en: Test the personal-belongings inspection at each entry and exit point against its procedure and local law

description.en: For every point where belongings are inspected, put three things together: the documented inspection procedure, Legal/DPO's confirmation that it is lawful in that jurisdiction — consent, notice, who may perform it and what may be searched — and an observation of inspections actually being performed at that point. Record a verdict per point on both legality and enforcement, since a lawful procedure nobody applies and an applied procedure with no legal basis are different failures with different fixes. Facilities supplies the observation. Attach the evaluation report with the procedures and the legal confirmation behind it.

evidenceHint.en: Evaluation report giving, per inspection point, the documented procedure, the legal confirmation covering it, the practice observed and a verdict on both lawfulness and enforcement

title.en: Compare the access control policy against what each entry point actually enforces

description.en: Read the current access control policy and its procedures against the register, point by point: what the policy requires there — authentication type, visitor escort, delivery-area handling — and what is in force today. Record a row per requirement per point with a met, partially met or not met verdict, and separate the two kinds of gap because they are fixed differently: the point that falls short of the policy, and the point whose practice is sound but which the policy never addresses. Attach the review report naming the policy version reviewed and the date it was read.

evidenceHint.en: Policy and procedure review report naming the policy version reviewed and giving, per entry point, each requirement with a met, partially met or not met verdict and the gaps in the policy itself

controls.title: Secure Development Lifecycle Compliance
controls.objective: Ensure that all software and system development adhere to the organization’s Secure Development Life Cycle (SDLC) policy and guidelines.
controls.successCriteria:
All projects strictly follow the established SDLC steps and guidelines.
Secure coding practices are in line with organizational guidelines.
Third-party components are used in compliance with security assessments and updates.
Developers are adequately trained and demonstrate capability in secure development practices.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain a list of all ongoing and recently completed software and system development projects.
Collect SDLC documentation for each project, including threat models, security requirements, test results, code reviews, and penetration test reports.
Gather secure coding guideline documents and training records for developers.
Retrieve documentation regarding the use of third-party components and their security assessments.

Analysis:
For each project, verify that all stages of the SDLC were followed according to the policy.
Compare secure coding practices in the projects against the organization's guidelines.
Assess the use of third-party components, ensuring they have been cleared by the security team and are regularly updated.
Evaluate the training records to confirm developers’ proficiency in secure development practices.

Output:
A detailed report of SDLC adherence for each project.
A comparison table matching secure coding practices with organizational guidelines.
A summary of third-party component usage and compliance.
A compliance report on developer training and capabilities.

title.en: Inventory the ongoing and recently completed development projects and the lifecycle stage each has reached

description.en: List every software and system development project running or recently closed, with its current lifecycle stage, the team delivering it and the repository or system it produces. The stage matters more than the name: a project's adherence can only be judged against the gates it has actually passed, and scoring an in-flight project against a closure criterion produces a false finding. Attach the inventory dated at compilation as the population the stage-gate testing and the training evaluation both draw on.

evidenceHint.en: Dated inventory of ongoing and recently completed development projects giving the lifecycle stage reached, the delivery team and the repository or system produced

title.en: Record each lifecycle stage's gate and the artefact that evidences it

description.en: Express the policy's lifecycle as a testable table: for every stage, the security work required to leave it and the specific artefact showing it happened — the threat model, the security requirements set, the test results, the code review record, the penetration test report. Naming the artefact is the point; a gate described only as security reviewed can be neither evidenced nor failed. Where the policy leaves a stage's artefact unnamed, decide it here and record the decision. Attach the stage-gate table as issued.

evidenceHint.en: Issued lifecycle stage-gate table naming, for each stage, the security work required to leave it and the named artefact that evidences its completion

title.en: Collect the threat model, security requirements, test results, code review and penetration test report for each project

description.en: As each project passes a stage, file the artefact that stage's gate names against the project record, dated and tied to the version of the system it covers. Collect them as the project runs rather than assembling them for the review — an artefact produced retrospectively evidences the review, not the lifecycle. Where a stage passed without its artefact, record the stage as unevidenced against that project instead of leaving a gap in the file. Attach the artefact set per project for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Per-project lifecycle artefact set holding the threat model, security requirements, test results, code review record and penetration test report, each dated and tied to the version it covers

title.en: Record the security clearance and last update date of every third-party component in use

description.en: Keep a register of the third-party components the inventoried projects depend on, carrying the component and version, the security team's clearance decision and its date, and when the component was last updated. This control tests two things separately — that a component was cleared before use, and that it is being kept current — so a register showing clearance alone leaves half the requirement unevidenced. Flag every component whose installed version is behind the one that was cleared. Attach the register for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Third-party component register giving component and version in use, the security clearance decision and date, the last update applied, and a flag on every component behind its cleared version

text.en: List the third-party components each inventoried project depends on, with versions.
Record the security team's clearance decision and its date for each component.
Record when each component was last updated in the projects that use it.
Flag every component running behind the version that was cleared for use.
Name an owner against each flagged component to bring it current or re-clear it.

title.en: Test each project's artefact set against the stage gates and report the stages that went unevidenced

description.en: Work through the inventory project by project, checking for each stage the project has passed whether the artefact its gate names is present, dated before the stage closed, and covers the version it claims to. Score met, unevidenced or not yet due, and produce the adherence report this control's output calls for. An artefact present but dated after the gate closed is recorded as unevidenced with the reason, because that is the pattern this review exists to detect. Attach the report with the per-project scoring behind it.

evidenceHint.en: Lifecycle adherence report scoring every project against each stage gate as met, unevidenced or not yet due, with the artefact reference and its date recorded against each met verdict

text.en: For each project, list the lifecycle stages it has already passed.
Check that each passed stage holds the artefact its gate names.
Confirm the artefact is dated before the stage closed and covers the right version.
Score each stage met, unevidenced, or not yet due at the project's position.
Summarise the unevidenced stages recurring across the portfolio in the report.

title.en: Evaluate developer training records against the secure development capability each project role requires

description.en: Set the training records held for the developers on the inventoried projects against what their role on the project actually requires them to do, and report where the two do not meet — a developer performing security-relevant work with no completed training, and training completed so long ago it no longer covers the technologies the project uses. HR supplies the completion data; the accountable read of it is the engineering lead's. Report the position per project rather than as an organisation-wide percentage, since a healthy average conceals an untrained team. Attach the compliance report with the records it was built from.

evidenceHint.en: Developer training compliance report giving, per project, each developer's completed secure development training with its date, and the gap against the capability their project role requires

controls.title: Data Storage Integrity
controls.objective: Ensure the integrity and security of stored inputs, in-process items, and outputs in line with system specifications.
controls.successCriteria:
Storage activities for inputs, in-process items, and outputs align with defined specifications.
Effective protection measures are in place for stored data.
Adherence to archiving and data protection protocols.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Retrieve system storage policies and specifications.
Collect records and logs of storage activities for inputs, in-process items, and outputs.
Obtain documentation of data protection measures for stored items.

Analysis:
Compare storage policies with actual storage records to ensure compliance with completeness, accuracy, and timeliness requirements.
Assess data protection measures for effectiveness in preventing theft, corruption, or loss.
Review records for adherence to archiving and protection protocols.

Output:
Compliance report comparing storage activities with policy specifications.
Evaluation of data protection measures.
Summary of adherence to archiving and storage protection standards.

title.en: Record the inputs, in-process items and outputs held in storage and where each is stored

description.en: The control covers three populations that are usually managed separately — data received into the system, items held part-way through processing, and outputs produced — so the register has to carry all three or the compliance report will silently cover only the one somebody remembered. One row per item type: what it is, which of the three categories it falls in, the storage it lives on, the owner, and whether it is live or archived. Build it from the storage actually in use rather than from the system design, since staging areas, interim files and spooled outputs are exactly what a design document omits. Attach the register with a category and an owner populated for every row.

evidenceHint.en: Storage register listing every input, in-process item and output held, with its category, the storage location or system holding it, the owner, and its live or archived state

title.en: Record the completeness, accuracy, timeliness and archiving requirement for each stored item

description.en: Take the system storage policies and specifications and write, against each row of the register, what that item's storage must satisfy: what counts as a complete stored item, the accuracy condition it has to hold, the timeliness requirement for when it is written or made available, and the archiving rule that moves it out of live storage. Where the specification is silent for an item, record the gap rather than inferring a value — an unstated requirement cannot be tested, and the comparison would score it as a pass by default. Attach the specification set mapped row by row onto the register, with the uncovered rows listed.

evidenceHint.en: Storage specification mapped to the register giving, per item, the completeness, accuracy and timeliness requirements and the archiving rule, plus the list of register rows the specification does not cover

text.en: Read the storage specification covering each register row and extract its stated requirements.
Record what a complete stored item means for that row and how completeness is checked.
Record the accuracy condition and the timeliness requirement the item must meet.
Record the archiving rule that moves the item out of live storage, and to where.
List every register row the specification says nothing about rather than inferring a value.

title.en: Record the protection measure applied to each stored item against theft, corruption and loss

description.en: Separately from the storage specification, document what actually protects each stored item, naming for every register row the measure in force against each of the three harms the control names: theft (access control, encryption at rest), corruption (checksums, integrity checks, write protection) and loss (backup, replication, retained copies). Name the measure and where it is configured rather than the intention — a row reading 'encrypted' with no keystore or setting named cannot be tested, and will pass an inspection it should fail. A row with a harm left unaddressed is a finding this task produces, not an empty cell. Attach the protection documentation covering every register row.

evidenceHint.en: Data-protection documentation per stored item naming the measure in force against theft, against corruption and against loss, where each is configured, and the harms left unaddressed

title.en: Log the storage, archiving and deletion activity for inputs, in-process items and outputs

description.en: Retain, for the period under test, the records and logs of storage activity the auditor asks for: items written to storage, items moved to archive, items restored and items deleted, each carrying the item, its category, the timestamp and the process or person that acted. Export the logs from the storage platforms themselves rather than compiling a summary by hand, and cover separately any archiving or deletion done manually, since a manual move leaves no machine trace and is the event most likely to be missing. This log is what the specification is compared against — without it, adherence is an assertion. Attach the activity log for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Storage activity log or platform export for the period covering writes, archive moves, restores and deletions, with the item, its category, the timestamp and the acting process or person for each event

title.en: Compare the logged storage activity against the specification for completeness, accuracy and timeliness

description.en: Set the activity log beside the storage specification and score each register row on the three requirements: whether every expected item reached storage (completeness), whether stored content matches the source it came from (accuracy), and whether writes and availability met their stated timing (timeliness). Sample stored items directly for the accuracy test rather than trusting the log to report on itself. Produce the compliance report the control calls for with a verdict per row, and for every deviation the accountable owner and the remediation agreed. Attach the report with the log extracts and the sampled items it was built from.

evidenceHint.en: Storage compliance report giving each register row a completeness, accuracy and timeliness verdict against the specification, the log extracts and sampled items behind them, and an owner plus remediation for each deviation

text.en: Check the activity log shows every expected item reached storage for each register row.
Sample stored items and compare their content against the source they came from.
Compare write and availability timestamps against the timeliness requirement.
Record a verdict per register row, naming the requirement each deviation missed.
Agree a remediation and an owner for every deviation before the report is issued.

title.en: Test that each recorded protection and archiving measure is in force on the storage it covers

description.en: Take the protection documentation row by row and confirm the measure is actually enforced where the item lives: read the access control and encryption setting from the storage itself, confirm the integrity check runs and reports, and confirm a copy exists wherever loss protection was claimed. In the same pass check archived items against the archiving rule recorded for them — held on the medium and for the period that rule states. Record an observed verdict per measure, and raise every measure that is documented but not in force as a finding with a named owner, since that is the gap between the paper protection and the real one. Attach the evaluation with the configuration output and check results it was read from.

evidenceHint.en: Protection and archiving evaluation with an observed verdict per measure, the configuration output or check result it was read from, and a named owner for every measure documented but not in force

controls.title: POI Device Inspection Compliance
controls.objective: To ensure that the frequency and type of POI device inspections are in accordance with the organization's targeted risk analysis and comply with relevant industry standards.
controls.successCriteria:
The targeted risk analysis for POI devices accurately reflects the required frequency and types of inspections and adheres to industry standards.
Documented results of POI device inspections are consistent with the targeted risk analysis.
Personnel demonstrate adequate understanding and implementation of POI device inspection procedures.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the organization's targeted risk analysis document that specifies the frequency and type of POI device inspections.
Gather documented results of recent POI device inspections.
Collect interviews or statements from personnel involved in POI device inspections.

Analysis:
Review the targeted risk analysis to confirm that it includes all elements specified for POI device inspections and is in line with industry standards.
Compare the documented inspection results with the requirements stated in the targeted risk analysis to verify consistency.
Assess personnel statements to ensure understanding and correct implementation of the inspection procedures.

Output:
A report summarizing the findings of the targeted risk analysis review.
A comparison spreadsheet or document detailing the alignment between the POI device inspection records and the targeted risk analysis.
Summary of personnel interviews or statements with insights on the practical execution of the inspection process.

title.en: Register every POI device in scope with its location, model and inspection owner

description.en: The comparison between inspection records and the targeted risk analysis needs a denominator, and that denominator is a device-level register rather than a count. Capture one row per deployed point-of-interaction device: serial or asset identifier, model, the site and position it is installed at, the date it was deployed, and the named person accountable for inspecting it. Build it from what is physically deployed — a walk of each site, or an export from whatever system manages the terminals — rather than from the purchase record, because a device swapped under warranty keeps the purchase order and changes the serial. Devices held as spares or in storage get their own rows marked uninstalled, since they are not inspected on the deployed cadence but come into scope the moment they are put into service. Attach the register with the date it was compiled; a row with no named inspection owner is not done.

evidenceHint.en: Dated POI device register listing serial or asset id, model, site and installed position, deployment date and named inspection owner for every device, with spares marked uninstalled

text.en: Walk each site, or export from whatever system manages the terminals, to list what is deployed.
Record serial or asset identifier, model and the exact installed position for each device.
Add devices held as spares or in storage, marked as uninstalled rather than omitted.
Name the person accountable for inspecting each device and confirm they know they hold it.
Date the register and hold it as the population the inspection comparison is run against.

title.en: Record the inspection frequency and inspection type per device class in the targeted risk analysis

description.en: The targeted risk analysis is what the inspection records are measured against, so it has to state values an inspector can act on rather than a general expectation. For every class of device in the register, record how often it is inspected, what the inspection consists of, check by check in the order they are performed, and the reasoning that set that frequency, including the site's exposure and the device's own history. Name the industry standard each element derives from, so the review can confirm the analysis is in line with it rather than merely internally consistent. Where a class is inspected more often than the standard requires say why, and where it is inspected less often record the compensating measure. Attach the analysis showing a frequency and inspection-type entry for every device class the register contains.

evidenceHint.en: Targeted risk analysis carrying an inspection frequency and inspection type entry for every device class in the register, each citing the industry standard it derives from

text.en: Group the register's devices into classes that share an exposure and a threat profile.
Set the inspection frequency for each class and record the reasoning that fixed it there.
List the specific checks that make up an inspection for that class, in the order performed.
Cite the industry standard behind each frequency and each check in the class entry.
Record the compensating measure wherever a class is inspected less often than the standard asks.

title.en: Log the result of every POI device inspection as it is performed

description.en: Each inspection produces a record, and that record is the evidence an auditor asks for: the device identifier from the register, the date and time, the inspector's name, each check performed with its outcome, and where anything was found, what was done about it and who was told. Where a check compares the device against a recorded state, carry that record with the entry, so a later claim is testable rather than a matter of recollection. An inspection that found nothing still gets a record — a missing record is indistinguishable from an inspection that never happened, and that gap is exactly what the comparison will report as a frequency failure. Attach the inspection records covering the period under test.

evidenceHint.en: POI device inspection records for the period, one entry per inspection giving device identifier, date, inspector, each check performed and its outcome, and the action taken on every exception

title.en: Measure the inspections performed against the frequency and type the analysis requires

description.en: Work down the device register and, for each device, count the inspections actually recorded in the period against the frequency its class requires, then check that each recorded inspection covered the inspection type the analysis specifies rather than a lighter check somebody had time for. Produce the comparison as a sheet with a row per device carrying the required frequency and type, what was performed, the shortfall, and a verdict — and keep frequency failures separate from type failures, because a device inspected on time but only partly needs different remediation from one not inspected at all. Against every fail write the accountable owner and the corrective action agreed with them. Attach the comparison sheet together with the register version and analysis version it was run against.

evidenceHint.en: Comparison sheet with one row per device showing required frequency and type, inspections actually performed, the frequency and type shortfalls recorded separately, a pass or fail verdict, and an owner against every fail

text.en: Count the inspections recorded in the period for each device in the register.
Compare that count against the frequency its device class requires in the analysis.
Check each recorded inspection covered every check the class entry specifies.
Record frequency shortfalls and inspection-type shortfalls in separate columns.
Name an accountable owner and an agreed corrective action against every failing row.

title.en: Test that the personnel who inspect POI devices can describe the procedure they follow

description.en: Take a sample of the inspection owners named in the register and ask each to describe how they identify the device, what they check, how often, and what they do when something looks wrong. Record what each said against what the targeted risk analysis requires, noting where the description has drifted from the document and where a step is being carried out from memory rather than from the procedure. An inspector who cannot describe a required check produces a named action with an owner and a date, not an observation. Attach the interview or statement summaries with the actions they raised.

evidenceHint.en: Interview or statement summaries for the sampled inspectors, each setting what was described against what the analysis requires, plus the actions raised with an owner and a date

controls.title: Personal Information Collection Control
controls.objective: To ensure that personal information is collected in a manner consistent with the entity's privacy objectives, focusing on necessity, fairness, and lawfulness.
controls.successCriteria:
Personal information collection practices align with the entity's privacy objectives.
Data is collected in a fair, lawful, and minimal manner, consistent with privacy standards and regulations.
Documented evidence of compliance with privacy policies and regulations in all data collection processes.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Collect a list of all systems and processes where personal information is gathered.
Obtain samples of data collection forms and methods used across these systems.
Review policies and procedures related to the collection of personal information.

Analysis:
Evaluate the data collection forms and methods to ensure they align with the entity's stated objectives for privacy.
Assess whether the collection of personal information is limited to what is necessary for the intended purposes.
Verify that the collection methods are fair and lawful, adhering to relevant privacy regulations and standards.

Output:
A detailed report on the evaluation of personal information collection practices.
A compliance matrix assessing each data collection method against privacy objectives and regulatory requirements.
Documentation of policy and procedure reviews pertaining to personal information collection.

title.en: List every system and process that gathers personal information

description.en: Compile the collection inventory the auditor asks for: one row per system or process that gathers personal information, naming the method it uses (web form, paper form, telephone script, import from a third party, observation or tracking), the fields it collects, the purpose it collects them for and the owner accountable for it. Source the rows from what is actually collecting today — live forms, active integrations, current paperwork — rather than from the systems list, because a paper form or a phone script belongs here and appears in no system inventory. Attach the register with a method, a field list and a purpose populated for every row.

evidenceHint.en: Collection register listing every system and process that gathers personal information, with the collection method, the fields collected, the stated purpose and the accountable owner

title.en: Record the purpose requiring each collected field and the basis making it lawful

description.en: Work down the collection register field by field and write against each field the purpose it serves and the basis on which it is lawfully collected. The point is the necessity test this control applies: a field with no purpose requiring it is collected beyond what is necessary, so list those separately as candidates for removal with their register row and owner named, rather than leaving a purpose cell blank where it reads as unfinished work. Where the same field is collected by several processes for different purposes, record each of them, because withdrawing it from one process does not withdraw it from another. Attach the field-level mapping with the excess-field list beside it.

evidenceHint.en: Field-level mapping of every collected field to its purpose and the basis making its collection lawful, with a separate list of fields no recorded purpose requires and the register row and owner for each

text.en: List the fields each collection method actually asks the data subject for.
Write the purpose that requires each field and the basis making it lawful.
Record the same field separately where processes collect it for different purposes.
Move every field with no purpose requiring it onto the excess-collection list.
Name the register row and the owner accountable for each excess field listed.

title.en: Capture the collection form or method as it is presented to the data subject

description.en: For the period under test, take a sample of every collection method as the data subject actually meets it — the rendered web form, the paper form in use, the telephone script, the third-party import specification — and file it against its register row with the date captured and any notice or consent text shown at the point of collection. Capture what is live rather than the design copy held in a document store: forms drift as fields are added by whoever owns the page, and the drift is invisible until the live capture and the mapping are set side by side. Attach the dated sample set for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Dated sample set of collection forms and methods as presented to data subjects, one per register row, including any notice or consent text displayed at the point of collection

title.en: Test the captured forms against the recorded field purposes

description.en: Set each captured form or method beside the field-level mapping and check two directions: that every field the form actually asks for appears in the mapping with a purpose, and that every field the mapping records is still being collected. Raise each field collected without a recorded purpose as an excess-collection finding naming the register row and owner, and each mapped field no longer collected as a mapping correction. This is the check that keeps the necessity assessment tied to what is live rather than to what was written when the mapping was made. Attach the comparison with the findings it raised.

evidenceHint.en: Form-to-mapping comparison per register row listing fields present on the form but absent from the mapping, fields mapped but no longer collected, and the owner assigned to each finding

title.en: Score each collection method against the privacy objectives and the regulation that applies

description.en: Build the compliance matrix the control calls for: one row per collection method, one column per privacy objective and per applicable regulatory requirement, with an assessed verdict in each cell and the evidence relied on named beside it. The fairness and lawfulness assessment belongs here — whether the basis recorded for the collection actually supports it, and whether the method as captured presents the data subject with what the regulation requires. Against every non-compliant cell record the accountable owner and the change agreed, so the matrix carries its own remediation. Attach the matrix with the assessment notes behind each verdict.

evidenceHint.en: Compliance matrix scoring every collection method against each privacy objective and applicable regulatory requirement, with the evidence relied on per cell and an owner plus agreed change for every non-compliant cell

text.en: Set the privacy objectives and applicable regulatory requirements as the matrix columns.
Score each collection method against every column and name the evidence relied on.
Check the recorded basis actually supports the collection as it is carried out.
Check the captured method presents what the applicable regulation requires at collection.
Record an accountable owner and an agreed change for each non-compliant cell.

controls.title: Secure Facility Management
controls.objective: Ensure effective physical security measures are in place to protect offices, rooms, and facilities from unauthorized access and threats.
controls.successCriteria:
The physical security plan comprehensively addresses all identified risks and complies with internal standards.
No unauthorized access or security breaches are evident in the logs and footage.
Recent audits and tests show continuous improvement and alignment with emerging threats.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the current physical security plan detailing measures for each site (including perimeter security, access control systems, CCTV placement, and emergency response plans).
Collect recent security logs from access control systems and CCTV footage.
Retrieve records of recent security audits, tests, and revisions to physical security measures.

Analysis:
Assess the physical security plan for adequacy in addressing identified risks and compliance with internal standards.
Analyze access control logs and CCTV footage for any unauthorized access attempts or security breaches.
Review the outcomes of recent security audits and tests to identify any gaps or areas for improvement.

Output:
A report on the effectiveness of the physical security plan.
A log analysis report highlighting any security incidents.
A summary of findings from the review of recent security audits and tests.
Audit Success Criteria:

title.en: List every office, room and facility in scope with the security measures installed at each

description.en: The plan an auditor asks for details measures for each site, so the site list is the denominator everything else counts against. Walk the estate and record each office, room and facility that holds people or equipment, and against each one what is actually fitted today: the perimeter barrier, which doors are access controlled, the CCTV cameras and the areas they see, and the intruder alarm zones. Record what is absent as absent rather than leaving a blank, because a blank cell reads as unsurveyed and the later coverage review cannot tell the two apart. Attach the site register carrying the date it was compiled and who walked each site.

evidenceHint.en: Dated site register listing every office, room and facility with its perimeter, access control, CCTV and alarm provision recorded as fitted or explicitly absent

text.en: Walk each site and record the perimeter barrier, the gates and every point at which the perimeter is broken.
Record every controlled door and the access control system that reads it.
Record each CCTV camera position and the area its field of view actually covers.
Record the intruder alarm zones and which parts of the site they leave unarmed.
Record who carried out the walk at each site and the date each site was surveyed.

title.en: Set out the perimeter, access, CCTV and emergency response measures for each site in the plan

description.en: The plan is the document the assessment is read against, so it has to state measures site by site rather than as estate-wide principles. For each site in the register record the perimeter arrangement, which doors are access controlled and who may pass them, where CCTV is placed and what it is there to see, and the emergency response: who is called, in what order, and what happens to the building. Where a site's measures differ from the internal standard, state the difference and the risk accepted rather than restating the standard. Attach the issued plan version showing a section per site.

evidenceHint.en: Issued physical security plan version with a per-site section covering perimeter security, access control, CCTV placement and emergency response

title.en: Review the period's access control and CCTV records and log every unauthorised access attempt

description.en: Pull the access control system log and the CCTV footage for the period under test and work through them for door forcing, badge use outside a holder's permitted hours or areas, tailgating captured on camera, and any entry with no corresponding authorised badge. Record each hit with the site, the door, the time, the person where identifiable, and the disposition: authorised after all, an error, or an incident raised. A period with no hits is recorded as an examined nil naming the logs read and the dates covered, not left blank. Attach the log analysis report with the raw extracts it was built from.

evidenceHint.en: Log analysis report for the period listing each unauthorised access attempt with site, door, time and disposition, plus the access control and CCTV extracts examined

title.en: Log each security test carried out on a site's alarms, doors and cameras with its outcome

description.en: Test the measures rather than reading their documentation: trigger the intruder alarm and time the response, present a revoked badge at a controlled door, and confirm each camera is recording and its footage is retrievable. Record every test with the date, the site, what was tested, who performed it, the result, and any revision to the plan it forced. This is the record of tests and revisions the assessment collects, and its value lies in the failures too, since a log of nothing but passes is also what an unexercised schedule produces. Attach the test log for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Security test log for the period giving date, site, measure tested, tester, pass or fail result, and the plan revision raised by each failure

title.en: Compare the physical security plan against each site's identified risks and the internal standard

description.en: Take the risks recorded for each site, its location, what it holds and the threats around it, and read the plan's measures for that site against them, then against the organisation's internal physical security standard. Produce the effectiveness report the control calls for: a verdict per site, the risks the plan leaves unaddressed, and the standard's requirements the site does not meet, each with an accountable owner. State where a measure is adequate on paper but the test log shows it failing, because that disagreement is what the report exists to surface. Attach the report.

evidenceHint.en: Physical security plan effectiveness report with a verdict per site, the unaddressed risks, the internal-standard gaps and an accountable owner against each

text.en: List the risks recorded against each site and the measure in the plan intended to address each one.
Mark every risk with no measure against it and every measure with no risk behind it.
Read each site's measures against the internal physical security standard clause by clause.
Assign an owner and a remediation to each unaddressed risk and each standard gap.

title.en: Track every gap raised by the last security audit or test through to its plan revision

description.en: Take the findings from the most recent security audits and tests and follow each one to what actually changed: the measure installed, the procedure amended, or the plan version reissued. Record each gap with the date raised, the action agreed, the action taken and its date, and mark the ones still open together with the age of the gap. This is what separates a programme that improves from one that re-finds the same gaps each cycle, and the open list is the output. Attach the summary with the audit and test reports it draws on.

evidenceHint.en: Summary of findings from recent security audits and tests, each traced to the plan revision or measure that closed it, with the still-open gaps and their age

controls.title: Clear Desk and Screen Compliance Check
controls.objective: To ensure adherence to the organization's clear desk and clear screen policy, thereby protecting sensitive information and maintaining data privacy.
controls.successCriteria:
Workspaces comply with the clear desk policy (no sensitive information left unattended, secure endpoint devices).
All printers comply with the authentication requirement of the clear screen policy.
System configurations adhere to the automatic logout and screen lock requirements.
Effective dissemination and understanding of the clear desk and clear screen policy across the organization.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence Collection:
Obtain the organization's clear desk and clear screen policy document.
Conduct surprise checks to take photographs of workspaces, including desks, printers, and whiteboards, in various departments.
Retrieve system configuration details to verify automatic logout and screen lock settings.
Collect a list of printers and their configurations (to verify if they have an authentication function).
Gather training records and communication material related to the clear desk and clear screen policy.

Analysis:
For each photographed workspace, verify compliance with the clear desk policy (e.g., no sensitive documents left unattended, no open and unattended endpoint devices).
Assess printer configurations to ensure they align with policy requirements, particularly concerning authentication functions.
Review system configuration details for compliance with automatic logout and screen lock policies.
Evaluate training records and communication materials to ensure adequate dissemination and understanding of the policy.

Output:
A report with photographs of the workspaces assessed.
A spreadsheet or document detailing each printer's configuration and compliance status.
A report on system configurations regarding automatic logout and screen lock features.
A summary of training and communication effectiveness regarding the policy.

title.en: List the workspaces, printers and endpoint builds the compliance check will cover

description.en: Set the population before the first walkthrough: the departments, floors and shared areas whose desks, printers and whiteboards will be checked; every printer and multifunction device with its model and whether that model supports the authentication function; and the endpoint builds or device groups carrying the screen lock and automatic logout settings. Facilities supplies the floor coverage and IT Operations the device and build detail. Attach the list — a printer or a department absent from it will be absent from the check, which is the failure this task exists to prevent.

evidenceHint.en: Scope list naming the departments and shared areas to be walked, every printer and multifunction device with its model and authentication capability, and the endpoint builds carrying lock and logout settings

title.en: Set the screen lock and automatic logout timeouts on every endpoint build and export the settings

description.en: Apply the policy's screen lock and automatic logout values to each endpoint build or device group in scope, and confirm the setting is enforced centrally rather than left to the user to choose. Export the resulting configuration — the group policy, device management profile or equivalent — showing the timeout values and the device groups they apply to, with the export date. Where a build cannot take the setting, record it with the reason and the compensating measure. Attach the exports; they are the system configuration evidence the control asks for.

evidenceHint.en: Dated configuration export per endpoint build showing the enforced screen lock and automatic logout timeout values and the device groups they apply to, plus any build that cannot take the setting

title.en: Turn on the authentication function on every printer capable of it and record the rest

description.en: For each device on the printer list, enable the authentication function the clear screen policy requires and record the setting applied. A device whose model does not support the function is recorded with the mitigation applied instead — relocation to a controlled area, a restriction on what may be sent to it, or a replacement date. Attach the printer spreadsheet showing model, authentication status and, where authentication is absent, the mitigation and its owner.

evidenceHint.en: Printer spreadsheet listing every device with its model, whether the authentication function is enabled, and the mitigation plus owner recorded for each device that cannot support it

title.en: Photograph desks, printers and whiteboards during unannounced walkthroughs and score each against the policy

description.en: Walk the areas on the scope list without notice and outside the times a visit is expected, photographing each desk, printer output tray and whiteboard as found. Score each workspace against the policy's requirements — nothing sensitive left unattended, no unlocked and unattended endpoint device, no uncollected print output, nothing sensitive left on a whiteboard — and record the area, the date and time, and a pass or fail with what was observed behind it. Frame photographs to evidence the finding without identifying an individual where that is not necessary. Attach the walkthrough report with its photographs.

evidenceHint.en: Dated walkthrough report with photographs of the desks, printers and whiteboards inspected, and a pass or fail per workspace naming what was observed

text.en: Schedule the walkthrough without notice and outside the hours a visit is expected.
Photograph each desk, printer output tray and whiteboard exactly as it was found.
Score the workspace against each policy requirement rather than an overall impression.
Record the area, the date and time, and what was observed behind every fail.
Cover every department and shared area on the scope list before closing the round.

title.en: Record the delivery of the clear desk and clear screen policy and the acknowledgements received

description.en: Track who has been told what the policy requires and who has confirmed it: the training or briefing delivered, the date, the audience it reached, the communication material issued, and the completion or acknowledgement recorded per person. Contractors and temporary staff working in the areas walked are included, since a policy reaching only permanent employees will fail at exactly the desks the walkthrough photographs. HR holds the completion records. Attach the training and communication records for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Training and communication records for the clear desk and clear screen policy: material issued, delivery dates, audience reached and the per-person completion or acknowledgement recorded, including contractors and temporary staff

title.en: Consolidate the walkthrough, printer and configuration results into a compliance report with owners

description.en: Bring the three streams of evidence together and state the position: how many workspaces passed and failed, which printers lack the authentication function, and which endpoint builds are not enforcing the lock and logout values. Give every failure a named owner and a date to clear it. Read the workspace failures against the training records as well — failures concentrated in an area whose staff hold no acknowledgement on file is a dissemination finding rather than an individual one, and the two call for different remedies. Attach the report with the walkthrough photographs, printer spreadsheet and configuration exports it draws on.

evidenceHint.en: Consolidated clear desk and clear screen compliance report covering workspace, printer and endpoint results, each failure with a named owner and clearance date, and the dissemination findings read against the training records

controls.title: Sensitive Information Access Management
controls.objective: To ensure that access to sensitive information and associated assets is restricted and managed in accordance with established topic-specific policies.
controls.successCriteria:
All user accounts and their respective access levels conform to the specifications in the Access Matrix.
All change requests related to access permissions are properly documented and executed following established procedures.
No evidence of unauthorized access or improper modification of access levels.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the Access Control List (ACL) or Access Matrix documenting permissions for systems containing sensitive information.
Gather screenshots or system logs showing current user accounts and their access levels on these systems.
Collect recent change requests related to user access or permissions since the last audit.

Analysis:
For each user account on the system, verify that the Access Matrix authorizes their access level.
Review the change requests to confirm they align with the established process for modifying access permissions.
Examine system logs or screenshots to check for any unauthorized access or anomalies in access patterns.

Output:
A report or spreadsheet cross-referencing each user account with the Access Matrix to validate proper access levels.
A detailed review of each change request, confirming adherence to the access modification procedures.
Anomalies or irregularities report highlighting any unauthorized access or deviations from expected access patterns.

title.en: Identify the systems holding sensitive information that the access matrix must cover

description.en: Name every system, application and repository that stores or processes sensitive information, because that set is the scope the Access Control List has to document permissions for. Record against each the categories of sensitive information it holds, its business owner, and where its user account listing can be produced from — the later cross-reference runs per system, so a system that cannot produce an account listing must be identified now rather than discovered mid-review with no way to test it. Attach the dated list; a system holding sensitive information but absent from the matrix is the first finding.

evidenceHint.en: Dated list of systems holding sensitive information with the information categories held, the business owner, and the source each system's user account listing can be produced from

title.en: Record the authorised access level per role for each sensitive system in the access matrix

description.en: Extend the Access Control List so each system on the list carries, per role, the access level that role is authorised to hold — read, write, administrative or none — expressed in the levels the system itself can actually grant, since a matrix written in levels the system does not have cannot be compared against a real account. Cite the topic-specific policy each restriction derives from, so a later challenge to a row has a source to argue with rather than an author to argue with. Attach the issued matrix version showing full coverage of the systems list.

evidenceHint.en: Issued Access Control List or Access Matrix version giving the authorised access level per role for every system on the sensitive systems list, each restriction citing the policy it derives from

title.en: Capture the current user accounts and access levels on each sensitive system

description.en: For each system on the list, produce the account listing the audit asks for: every account, its holder, the access level as the system itself reports it, and the date the extract was taken. Take it from the system — an export or a timestamped screenshot — rather than from the provisioning record, because catching where those two disagree is the entire point of the cross-reference that follows. Include disabled and service accounts, flagged as such, rather than filtering them out. Attach the extracts with the date each was taken.

evidenceHint.en: Dated per-system account extract or screenshot set showing every account, its holder and its access level as reported by the system itself, with disabled and service accounts flagged

title.en: Record each sensitive-system access change request with the approval that authorised it

description.en: Keep, across the whole period, the change request behind every grant, change or removal of access to a sensitive system: what was requested, for whom, on which system, who approved it, and when it was applied. The audit reads these against the established modification process, so the record has to show the sequence — an approval dated after the access was already applied is exactly the departure this evidences, and it is invisible unless both dates are captured. Attach the change requests raised since the last audit.

evidenceHint.en: Access permission change requests for the period, each showing the account and system affected, the level requested, the approver, and the dates of both approval and application

title.en: Cross-reference every sensitive-system account against the access matrix and report the exceptions

description.en: Put each account from the system extracts against the matrix cell its holder's role authorises, and mark it conforming or an exception. Exceptions come in three shapes and the report should say which: an account holding more than its role authorises, an account on a system its role has no cell for at all, and an account whose holder has no current role. Name an owner and a remediation against each, and state which were corrected before the report closed and which remain open. Attach the cross-reference spreadsheet with the report drawn from it.

evidenceHint.en: Account-to-matrix cross-reference spreadsheet with a conforming or exception verdict per account, and a report giving the exception type, owner, remediation and open or corrected status for each exception

text.en: Resolve every account in the system extracts to a named holder and their current role.
Read the matrix cell that role holds for that system and compare it to the access observed.
Mark each account conforming or an exception, naming which of the three exception shapes applies.
Name an owner and the remediation agreed against each exception in the report.
Record which exceptions were corrected before the report closed and which remain open.

title.en: Examine the sensitive systems' access logs for unauthorised access and unrecorded level changes

description.en: Read the logs and extracts for the period against the two questions the control asks separately: was sensitive information reached by an account the matrix does not authorise, and was any account's access level altered outside the change request set. Disposition every hit as explained — naming the change request or business event that covers it — or as an exception referred for investigation. Attach the anomaly report naming the logs and date range examined, so an empty exception list is readable as a result rather than as an absence of looking.

evidenceHint.en: Anomaly report naming the access logs and date range examined, each unauthorised access or unrecorded access level change found, and its disposition as explained or referred for investigation

controls.title: Personal Information Accuracy and Relevance
controls.objective: To ensure the collection and maintenance of personal information is accurate, up-to-date, complete, and relevant.
controls.successCriteria:
Personal information across systems is accurate, up-to-date, complete, and relevant.
Effective processes are in place for regular updates and verification of personal information.
Compliance with policies and regulations regarding the accuracy and relevance of personal data.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain a sample of personal information records from various systems.
Collect documentation of the processes for updating and verifying personal information.
Access logs of recent updates or changes to personal information.

Analysis:
Review the sampled records to assess their accuracy and completeness.
Analyze the processes for maintaining and verifying up-to-date and relevant information.
Examine update logs to evaluate the frequency and effectiveness of data updates.

Output:
A report on the accuracy and completeness of personal information records.
Analysis of the effectiveness of maintenance and verification processes.
Documentation highlighting any identified gaps in data accuracy or relevance.

title.en: Register every system holding personal information with the record types and data elements it holds

description.en: The auditor's first request is a sample of personal information records from various systems, so this register is what makes 'various' answerable and it is the population every later task counts against. Build one row per system — HR, payroll, CRM, support, marketing, and any spreadsheet or supplier-hosted copy — capturing the record types it holds, the data elements inside them, the purpose each element serves, and the person accountable for that system's data being accurate. Work from the systems that actually hold personal information rather than from the ones that were meant to, so a shadow copy of a customer list appears as a row instead of an absence. Attach the register with an owner named on every row and the date it was compiled.

evidenceHint.en: Dated register of systems holding personal information, one row per system, giving record types, data elements, the purpose each element serves and a named accuracy owner

text.en: Enumerate systems from the application inventory, the processing record and the integrations that copy personal data between them.
Add supplier-hosted and end-user copies — reporting extracts, spreadsheets and mailing lists — that hold the same records.
For each system list the record types held and the data elements inside them.
Record against every element the purpose it serves, so elements that no longer have one become visible.
Name the owner accountable for accuracy on each row and confirm the name with that person.

title.en: Document the update route, verification method and cycle for each registered system

description.en: For every row of the register, write down how a record is kept current: which system is the source of truth for each element, the route by which a change reaches it and any downstream copy, who is permitted to make that change, the method used to verify the element is still correct (a source document, a confirmation to the individual, a match against another system), and how often that verification runs. Record separately the route by which a correction reaches the record and every downstream copy of it, and how long that takes. IT Operations supplies the system and integration detail; Legal/DPO confirms the method satisfies the Privacy Policy. Attach the issued procedure with an entry for every registered system and no cell left blank.

evidenceHint.en: Issued update and verification procedure with one entry per registered system giving source of truth, update route, verification method, verification cycle and the correction route

text.en: Name the source of truth for every data element and the systems holding a downstream copy.
Describe the route a change takes from the source to each downstream copy, and its lag.
State the verification method for each element — source document, confirmation to the individual, or a match against another system.
Set how often verification runs for each system and who performs it.
Describe how a correction reaches the record and every downstream copy of it.

title.en: Log every change to a personal information record as it is made

description.en: Each time a personal information record is created, corrected or updated, the log must carry enough to answer the questions asked later: the record identifier, the element changed, the value before and after where the system retains it, the source that justified the change, who made it and when. Where a system emits its own audit trail, export that rather than re-keying it, and cover separately the changes made outside a system — a correction taken by phone and applied by hand is exactly the event the export will not contain. This log is what shows the update process is being run rather than merely documented. Attach the change log extract covering the period under test for every system on the register.

evidenceHint.en: Change log extract per registered system for the period, showing record identifier, element changed, the source of the change, who made it and the date

title.en: Record the outcome of each system's verification cycle in the verification log

description.en: When a system's verification cycle runs under the documented method, record what it covered and what it found: the system, the cycle date, the records or elements checked, how many were confirmed correct, how many were corrected and how many could not be confirmed at all. Where verification depends on a response from the individual, record the non-responses separately rather than counting them as confirmed — an unanswered confirmation is not evidence of accuracy. Every correction raised here carries through to the change log by the route the procedure sets. Attach the verification log for the period showing each registered system's cycles and their outcomes.

evidenceHint.en: Verification log for the period listing each system's cycles with the records checked and the confirmed, corrected and unconfirmed counts

title.en: Test a sample of records from each registered system for accuracy and completeness

description.en: Draw a sample across the register so every system contributes records, and test each one against the source that governs it: are the mandatory elements present, does each element match the source document or the individual's confirmation, and is anything held that the record's purpose no longer needs. Score accurate, incomplete or inaccurate per record with the specific element named on every failure, and give each failure an owner and a correction date. The report this produces is the accuracy and completeness report the control calls for. Attach the sampling sheet together with the report drawn from it.

evidenceHint.en: Accuracy and completeness report with the sampling sheet behind it, scoring each sampled record and naming the element and owner for every failure

text.en: Draw the sample so every system on the register contributes records.
Check each mandatory element is present and each held element still has a purpose.
Compare every element against the source document or confirmation that governs it.
Score each record and name the specific element behind any failure.
Assign each failure an owner and a date by which the record will be corrected.

title.en: Measure update frequency and correction turnaround against the documented cycle and list the gaps

description.en: Read the change and verification logs for the period against the cycles the procedure states: which systems ran their verification when it was due and which did not, how long corrections took to reach the record and its downstream copies, and which systems produced no usable log at all. Set that beside the sample results, so a system with a clean log and failing records shows up as a process problem rather than a record problem. The output is the effectiveness analysis and the documented gaps in accuracy and relevance, each gap carrying an owner and an agreed remediation. Attach the analysis with the log extracts it was derived from.

evidenceHint.en: Effectiveness analysis of the update and verification processes, listing per system the cycles due and run, the correction turnaround, and every gap with its owner and remediation

controls.title: Incident Management Compliance
controls.objective: To ensure that the organization's Incident Management process aligns with established policies and effectively manages information security incidents from identification through to resolution and learning.
controls.successCriteria:
The Incident Management process is fully compliant with the policy and IRP.
All incidents are appropriately categorized, assessed, contained, escalated, and resolved in line with the policy.
Communication and notification procedures are executed effectively and within legal and contractual timeframes.
Post-incident analyses lead to continuous improvements in the incident management process.
Incident response personnel receive adequate and up-to-date training and professional development.
Evidence collection and handling procedures are legally compliant and adhere to internal standards.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the Incident Management Policy documentation, including the Incident Response Plan (IRP).
Collect records of recent information security incidents, including their categorization, assessment, and response documentation.
Gather logs of incident containment, escalation, and coordination activities.
Acquire evidence of incident-related communications to stakeholders and authorities.
Obtain documentation of post-incident analyses and lessons learned.
Secure evidence of training and professional development activities for incident response personnel.
Retrieve audit logs for evidence collection procedures related to information security events.

Analysis:
Review the Incident Management Policy and IRP to verify that they comprehensively cover all aspects of incident management as per your requirements.
Analyze records of recent incidents to ensure they were identified, categorized, contained, escalated, and resolved according to the policy.
Evaluate communication logs to verify timely and appropriate stakeholder notification.
Assess post-incident analysis documents to check for root cause analysis and learning integration into the incident management process.
Review training and development records of incident response personnel to ensure compliance with policy requirements.
Analyze evidence collection procedures to validate adherence to legal and internal standards.

Output:
A comprehensive report assessing the alignment of the Incident Management process with the policy.
A spreadsheet or database documenting the review of recent incidents, including categorization, response, and resolution.
Documentation of communication and notification actions taken during incidents.
Analysis of post-incident reviews and implemented improvements.
Records of training and professional development activities for incident response personnel.
Audit trail of evidence collection and handling procedures.

title.en: Document how evidence is collected, handled and stored for information security events

description.en: Write the procedure an incident responder follows when an event may need evidence preserved: what is captured and in what order, who is authorised to capture it, how the chain of custody is recorded, where the material is stored, and which legal constraints apply to seizing and retaining it. Legal/DPO confirms the legal position on collection and retention so the procedure is defensible rather than merely tidy. The audit trail this procedure produces is itself requested at audit, so name explicitly which system records each collection action. Attach the issued procedure together with the chain-of-custody form it prescribes.

evidenceHint.en: Issued evidence collection and handling procedure with its chain-of-custody form, naming the authorised collectors, the storage location and the system that logs each collection action

title.en: Log each incident's categorisation, containment, escalation and resolution as it is handled

description.en: For every information security incident, hold one record carrying the category and severity assigned at triage, the assessment that set them, the containment actions taken with their times, each escalation with its recipient and its trigger, and the resolution with the date it was closed and who resolved it. This record is read against the Incident Response Plan stage by stage at audit, so a stage that was deliberately skipped is recorded as skipped with the reason rather than left blank — a blank reads as an incomplete record and fails the same test as an omission. Attach the incident record set for the period under test.

evidenceHint.en: Incident record set for the period, one record per incident showing category, severity, the assessment behind them, containment actions with times, escalations and the resolution date

text.en: Assign a category and severity at triage and record the assessment that set them.
Record every containment action with the time it was taken and the person who took it.
Record each escalation with its recipient, the trigger that caused it and the time it was raised.
Record the resolution reached, the date the incident was closed and who resolved it.
Where a stage was skipped, record it as skipped with the reason rather than leaving it blank.

title.en: Record each incident notification against the legal or contractual deadline that applied

description.en: Each time an incident triggers a notification, record the recipient — internal stakeholder, customer, regulator or law enforcement — the obligation that required it, the deadline that obligation set, the time the notification was actually sent, and the channel used. This control is tested on timeliness against legal and contractual timeframes, so the deadline has to sit beside the send time in the same record or the comparison cannot be made from the evidence alone. Legal/DPO owns the reading of which obligation applies to which incident. Where a notification was judged not required, record that judgement and who made it. Attach the notification record with the underlying communications.

evidenceHint.en: Notification record for the period showing per notification the recipient, the obligation relied on, its deadline, the actual send time, the channel and the communication itself

title.en: Record the root cause and the resulting improvement for each closed incident

description.en: After an incident closes, run the post-incident analysis and write down three things: the root cause reached rather than the symptom observed, the specific change agreed as a result — to the process, the Incident Response Plan, a control or a configuration — and the owner and target date for that change. An analysis naming a cause but no change is exactly the shape this control tests for, because it produces documents without producing improvement. Carry the agreed changes onto a list that is re-read at the next incident to confirm they were actually made. Attach the post-incident analysis records and the improvement list for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Post-incident analysis record per closed incident giving the root cause, the agreed improvement, its owner and target date, plus the improvement list showing which have been completed

title.en: Track the training and professional development each incident responder has completed

description.en: Hold one row per named member of the incident response team recording the training and professional development they have completed, when, and what it covered, so the currency of the team's capability can be read rather than assumed. Include external qualifications and exercise participation as well as internal courses, since the control asks for professional development and not only attendance. Where the roster has changed, the newly added responders are what this record exists to surface, so list them with their outstanding items and a date. Attach the record covering the whole current roster rather than a sample of it.

evidenceHint.en: Incident responder training record covering the current roster, showing per responder the training and professional development completed, its date and subject, and any outstanding items with dates

title.en: Test a sample of closed incidents against the policy's categorisation, containment and escalation requirements

description.en: Draw a sample of incidents closed in the period and read each against the Incident Management Policy and the Incident Response Plan: was it categorised by the policy's own criteria, was it contained by the actions the policy directs for that category, was it escalated to the roles the plan names, and was it resolved and closed as the policy requires. Mark a pass or fail per requirement per incident, and against every fail record the accountable owner and the corrective action agreed. The result is the compliance report this control produces. Attach the report with the sampled incident records behind it.

evidenceHint.en: Incident management compliance report showing each sampled incident scored per policy requirement, with a pass or fail per requirement and an owner and corrective action recorded against each fail

text.en: Draw a sample of incidents closed in the period spanning the severity categories in use.
Read each sampled incident against the policy's categorisation criteria and mark pass or fail.
Check the containment actions, escalation recipients and resolution against what the plan directs.
Record an accountable owner and a corrective action against every requirement marked fail.

controls.title: Management Responsibilities Compliance
controls.objective: To ensure that management and staff comply with information security policies, and management supports and enforces these policies effectively.
controls.successCriteria:
Management Support Verification: Clear evidence of management's active support and endorsement of information security policies.
Training Completion: All staff have undergone regular information security awareness training relevant to their roles.
Effective Reporting Channels: Confidential reporting channels are functional, accessible, and well-documented.
Comprehensive Staff Guidelines and Briefings: All staff have received appropriate guidelines and briefings on their information security roles and responsibilities.
Adequate Resource Allocation: Sufficient resources and planning time are allocated for implementing security-related processes and controls.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Management Communications: Collect recent communications (e.g., emails, memos) from management endorsing information security policies.
Training Records: Obtain records of information security awareness training and professional education programs.
Reporting Channel Documentation: Get documentation on the confidential reporting channels provided for information security policy violations.
Staff Guidelines and Briefing Records: Gather records showing guidelines provided to staff regarding information security expectations and briefings on their roles and responsibilities.
Resource Allocation Records: Access records demonstrating resources and time allocated for implementing security-related processes and controls.

Analysis:
Review of Management Communications: Examine management communications for evidence of active support and endorsement of information security policies.
Training Records Examination: Check training records to ensure staff are regularly trained and aware of their information security responsibilities.
Evaluation of Reporting Channels: Assess the functionality and accessibility of the confidential reporting channels.
Staff Guidelines and Briefing Compliance: Verify that staff members have received appropriate guidelines and briefings on their information security roles and responsibilities.
Resource Allocation Assessment: Evaluate the adequacy of resources and time allocated for security-related processes and controls.

Output:
Report on Management Communications: Summarize findings from the review of management's support for information security policies.
Training Compliance Spreadsheet: List of staff members with corresponding records of completed training sessions.
Reporting Channel Evaluation Report: Assessment of the confidentiality, accessibility, and effectiveness of the reporting channels.
Staff Guidelines and Briefing Compliance Report: Documentation showing compliance with the provision of guidelines and briefings to staff.
Resource Allocation Evaluation Report: Assessment of resources and time allocation for security processes and controls.

title.en: Document the confidential reporting channel for information security policy violations

description.en: Write down and publish how a member of staff reports a suspected information security policy violation in confidence: the routes available, who receives a report, what protection the reporter has, what happens after a report is made, and how the reporter learns the outcome. Then evidence that the channel actually works, because a documented mailbox nobody monitors is not a channel and the control asks for one that is functional and accessible as well as documented. Record where the documentation is published and how staff who do not read the intranet find it. HR advises on the confidentiality protections. Attach the documentation with a walkthrough showing a test report reaching its recipient.

evidenceHint.en: Confidential reporting channel documentation naming the routes, the recipient, the reporter protections and the handling process, with the walkthrough record showing a test report reaching its recipient

title.en: Publish the guidelines stating each role's information security responsibilities

description.en: Produce the guidance staff are actually given about what is expected of them, broken down so a person can find their own role in it rather than reading a policy written for the organisation as a whole. Cover the general expectations that apply to everyone and the additional responsibilities carried by roles with privileged access, people-management duties or bulk data handling. The briefing recorded in the next task is delivered against this document, so it has to exist in issued form before a briefing record means anything. Attach the issued guidelines showing the role breakdown and the date they were published.

evidenceHint.en: Issued staff information security guidelines with responsibilities set out per role, covering general expectations and the additional duties of privileged, managerial and data-handling roles

title.en: Record the briefing each member of staff received on their information security responsibilities

description.en: Keep the record showing which members of staff have been briefed against the guidelines, when, by whom, and which role-specific content they received. Joiners and movers are the population this record exists to catch: a person who moved into a privileged role without the corresponding briefing disappears inside a headline completion figure and is visible only here. HR supplies the joiner and mover movements for the period so the denominator is the current staff list. Attach the briefing record covering that list, with the outstanding individuals named rather than counted.
