evidenceHint.en: Briefing record covering the current staff list, showing per person the briefing date, who delivered it and the role-specific content received, with the outstanding individuals named

title.en: Collect every management communication endorsing the information security policies

description.en: File the communications in which management actually endorses and enforces the information security policies — all-staff emails, memos, town hall material, statements recorded in team meeting minutes — with the date, the sender, the audience reached and what was said. Undated or unattributed material is not usable as evidence of active support, so capture the header alongside the body. A period with no such communication is recorded as an explicit nil return, because that absence is precisely what this control tests for and an empty folder does not distinguish it from a filing failure. Attach the file of communications for the period.

evidenceHint.en: File of management communications endorsing the information security policies for the period, each carrying date, sender, audience and content, or an explicit nil return with its reason

title.en: Track security awareness training completion for every member of staff against their role

description.en: Hold one row per member of staff showing which information security awareness training they have completed, when, and whether the material matched the responsibilities their role carries — the control asks for training relevant to the role, so a single generic course recorded against everyone does not satisfy it and this record is what surfaces the mismatch. Export completion from the training platform rather than re-keying it, and reconcile the population against the current staff list so leavers and joiners do not distort the figure. Attach the training compliance spreadsheet with the outstanding staff named.

evidenceHint.en: Training compliance spreadsheet listing every member of staff with the awareness training completed, its date, the role-relevant content it covered and the named staff still outstanding

title.en: Evaluate the resources and planning time allocated to each security process against what it required

description.en: For each security process or control implemented or maintained in the period, set the resource and planning time that was allocated beside what the work actually took, and record the shortfall where there was one together with its consequence — a control delivered late, delivered partially, or never started. The records showing what resource and planning time was allocated are the source, in whatever form they are kept. The output is a stated position on whether the allocation was adequate, with the under-resourced items named and escalated to management, rather than a general assurance that resourcing is sufficient. Attach the evaluation with its escalation list.

evidenceHint.en: Resource allocation evaluation setting allocated resource and planning time against actual for each security process, naming the shortfalls, their consequence and the items escalated to management

controls.title: Personnel Screening and Verification Control
controls.objective: To ensure thorough and ongoing background verification checks are carried out for all personnel before and during their tenure, in compliance with relevant laws and proportionate to their roles and risks.
controls.successCriteria:
All personnel have undergone the required level of screening before and during their employment.
Screening processes are in line with legal, ethical, and business requirements.
Continuous suitability of personnel is periodically reassessed, especially for those in critical roles.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain a list of all personnel (full-time, part-time, temporary, and contractors) hired since the last audit.
Gather all background verification reports and relevant screening documents for these personnel.
Collect documentation on any ongoing screening processes for existing employees.
Retrieve copies of contractual agreements with suppliers, specifically clauses related to screening requirements.

Analysis:
Review the background verification reports and screening documents for completeness and compliance with organizational policy and legal requirements.
Verify the implementation of screening processes, including checks for references, academic and professional qualifications, and identity verification.
For personnel in critical roles, ensure additional verifications like credit reviews or criminal record checks have been conducted.
Examine supplier contracts to confirm inclusion and adherence to screening requirements.
Assess procedures and criteria for periodic re-verification of personnel suitability.

Output:
A report detailing the compliance status of each personnel’s background verification.
A compliance matrix comparing screening requirements against actual checks performed.
An analysis of supplier contracts regarding screening clauses.

title.en: List everyone engaged since the last audit with their engagement type and role criticality

description.en: Build the population the screening evidence is tested against: every full-time and part-time employee, temporary worker and contractor engaged since the last audit, one row each, carrying the start date, the role, whether they were engaged directly or through a supplier, and a criticality flag for roles holding access to sensitive information or systems. The criticality flag is not decoration — it decides whether the additional checks apply, so a blank there blocks the later scoring, and the supplier column is what produces the population for the contract task. Attach the list with the date it was drawn.

evidenceHint.en: Dated joiner list covering employees, temporary workers and contractors engaged since the last audit, each with start date, role, engagement route and role-criticality flag

title.en: Record the screening checks required for each role level and the re-verification interval

description.en: Write the screening standard the population is scored against: for each role level, which checks are mandatory — identity verification, employment references, academic and professional qualifications — and which additional checks apply to critical roles, such as criminal record and credit reviews. State the acceptable evidence for each check, and state the interval and the trigger at which the suitability of people already in post is reassessed. Legal/DPO confirms each check is lawful and proportionate in every jurisdiction the entity hires in and records where a check is prohibited, so that exception is documented rather than showing later as a gap. Attach the issued standard.

evidenceHint.en: Issued personnel screening standard mapping each role level to its mandatory and additional checks, the acceptable evidence for each, the re-verification interval, and any jurisdiction where a check is prohibited

text.en: Set the checks every engagement requires: identity, references and qualifications.
Name the additional checks for critical roles, such as criminal record and credit review.
State the evidence that satisfies each check and who is competent to verify it.
Set the interval and the trigger for reassessing people already in post.
Have Legal/DPO confirm each check is lawful in every hiring jurisdiction and record exceptions.

title.en: Record the screening clause each supplier of personnel is contractually held to

description.en: For every supplier that places contractors or temporary staff, pull the current agreement and extract into a register what screening the supplier must perform and what evidence of it they must supply to the entity. An agreement silent on screening is flagged as silent rather than assumed compliant — that flag list is the finding this task produces and what Procurement carries into the next renewal. Attach the register with the contract clause extracts it was built from.

evidenceHint.en: Supplier screening register with the contractual clause extract per supplier, the evidence they must provide, and the list of agreements carrying no screening requirement

title.en: File the completed verification report for each person before they take up the role

description.en: For every engagement, complete the checks the screening standard requires and file their results before the person starts work. Each file carries the check performed, the date it completed, the provider or person who verified it, and the outcome, with the completion date set against the start date so a check that closed after the person began work is visible rather than buried in the file. A contractor screened by a supplier is covered by the supplier's certificate filed against the same row. Attach the screening files for the period, or the register export that indexes them.

evidenceHint.en: Screening file or register export for every engagement in the period, showing each required check, its date, its verifier and its outcome, each completion date set against the person's start date

title.en: Re-verify personnel in critical roles at the interval set in the screening standard

description.en: Run the reassessment the standard requires for people already in post: repeat the checks it names for critical roles, record the date, the outcome, and any change in circumstances declared since the last review, and record separately any result bearing on the person's continued suitability for the role they hold rather than closing it inside the reassessment record. Where someone has moved into a critical role since the last audit, their reassessment is what closes the gap between the screening they were hired against and the screening their current role requires. Attach the re-verification records for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Re-verification records for the period listing each person reassessed, their role, the checks repeated, the date and the outcome, plus any case where continued suitability was called into question

title.en: Score every engagement's screening file against the required checks in a compliance matrix

description.en: Take the joiner list and, row by row, mark which required checks are actually evidenced in the file, giving each engagement a pass or exception verdict. An exception is any check missing, completed after the person started work, or evidenced only by an assertion rather than a document. Test the contractor rows against the supplier register as well, since a supplier's contractual obligation is met only if the certificate is on file. Write a remediation owner and a target date against every exception in the same sheet. Attach the completed matrix.

evidenceHint.en: Screening compliance matrix with one row per engagement, a column per required check, a pass or exception verdict, and a named owner and date against every exception

controls.title: PII Privacy Compliance
controls.objective: To ensure that the organization's handling of PII aligns with its privacy policy, applicable laws, and contractual requirements.
controls.successCriteria:
All systems and processes comply with the organization's Privacy Policy.
PII handling procedures are effectively implemented and align with regulatory requirements.
Privacy incidents and complaints are managed promptly and effectively, with measures in place to prevent recurrence.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Retrieve the organization’s Privacy Policy document.
Obtain a list of all systems and processes that handle PII.
Gather evidence of PII handling procedures, such as process documentation, training records, or system configuration settings.
Collect records of any recent privacy-related incidents or complaints.

Analysis:
Review the Privacy Policy to ensure it covers all aspects of PII handling as per legal and contractual requirements.
Cross-reference the list of systems and processes with the policy to ensure all PII handling methods are accounted for and compliant.
Examine evidence of PII handling procedures to verify that they are implemented as per the policy and meet regulatory standards.
Assess incident and complaint records to evaluate how privacy breaches are managed and resolved.

Output:
A report detailing the compliance of each system and process with the Privacy Policy.
A summary of the effectiveness of PII handling procedures.
An analysis of incident and complaint handling related to PII.

title.en: List every system and process that handles PII with the law or contract clause that governs it

description.en: The compliance report this control produces is scored per system and per process, so this list is the population it is scored against. Capture one row per system or process: the PII categories it handles, what it does with them (collect, store, use, share, dispose), whether a supplier or processor is involved, and the specific legal or contractual obligation that governs that handling — the regulation and article, or the customer contract and clause. Build it from the systems that actually touch PII rather than from the ones in the processing record, so a process running outside the record appears as a row instead of an absence. Attach the list with the governing obligation populated on every row.

evidenceHint.en: List of systems and processes handling PII, each with its PII categories, handling activities, supplier involvement and the governing legal or contractual obligation

text.en: Enumerate systems and processes from the processing record, the application inventory and the supplier register.
Add handling carried out outside those records — manual processes, reporting extracts and shared files.
Record the PII categories and the handling activities each system or process performs.
Name any supplier or processor involved and the agreement under which they act.
Cite the regulation, article or contract clause that governs each row.

title.en: Close the Privacy Policy's gaps against the legal and contractual PII obligations on the list

description.en: Read the issued Privacy Policy against the obligations column of the list and record, obligation by obligation, whether the policy addresses it, addresses it partially, or is silent. Silence is the finding: where the policy does not cover an aspect of PII handling that a regulation or a customer contract requires, draft the wording that closes it and put that wording through the policy's own approval route. Legal/DPO owns both the reading and the drafting. Attach the gap analysis alongside the issued policy version that resolved the gaps it identified, and where a gap remains open, the owner and the date it is due.

evidenceHint.en: Gap analysis of the Privacy Policy against each legal and contractual PII obligation, with the issued policy version that closed the gaps and an owner and due date for any still open

title.en: Map the procedure, training and system setting that implements the policy for each system on the list

description.en: For every row of the list, name what makes the policy true there rather than merely applicable: the process documentation the handlers follow, the training those handlers have completed with the date, and the system configuration setting that enforces the policy requirement — retention period, access restriction, encryption, consent flag. Where a row has none of these for a requirement that applies to it, that blank cell is the implementation gap this task exists to surface, and it carries an owner. Security engineering supplies the configuration detail and HR the training records; Legal/DPO owns the mapping. Attach the mapping with a document, a training record or a setting cited in every applicable cell.

evidenceHint.en: Implementation mapping citing the process document, training record and system setting behind each policy requirement per system, with an owner against every blank cell

text.en: Take each policy requirement that applies to a row and ask what makes it true there.
Cite the process documentation the handlers of that system actually follow.
Cite the training completion records for the people who handle that PII.
Cite the configuration setting that enforces the requirement in the system itself.
Record an owner against every requirement with no document, record or setting behind it.

title.en: Record every privacy incident and complaint with its resolution and the measure taken to prevent recurrence

description.en: Each privacy incident or complaint is entered in the register when it is received and its entry completed as it is handled: what happened and which systems and PII categories it involved, the dates it was received, contained and resolved, the resolution reached, and the specific measure put in place so the same cause does not recur — a configuration change, a procedure change or a retraining, each named with an owner. An incident closed without a recurrence measure is recorded as such rather than left blank, because that is the case the review looks for. Attach the privacy incident and complaint register covering the period.

evidenceHint.en: Privacy incident and complaint register for the period, each entry showing the systems and PII involved, the receipt and resolution dates, the resolution and the recurrence-prevention measure with its owner

title.en: Score each system and process on the list against the Privacy Policy in a compliance report

description.en: Work down the list and test each system and process against the policy requirements that apply to it, taking the implementation mapping as the starting point and the system itself as the check — a documented control the configuration contradicts is scored on the configuration. Give each row a compliant, partially compliant or non-compliant verdict, describe every exception in enough detail that somebody else could reproduce the finding, and name the accountable owner and the agreed remediation date against each. Attach the compliance report with the configuration output and document references it was built from.

evidenceHint.en: Privacy Policy compliance report scoring every system and process, with each exception described and carrying an owner and a remediation date

title.en: Test the recorded incidents and complaints for resolution time and recurrence

description.en: Take the register entries for the period and measure each against the handling procedure: the elapsed time from receipt to containment and from receipt to resolution, whether the handling steps the procedure requires were performed and evidenced, whether a recurrence-prevention measure was defined, and whether that measure was actually implemented by its owner. Group the entries by cause and flag any cause that recurred after its measure was closed — a repeat is evidence the measure did not work, which is the point of the test. Attach the analysis summary with the case-by-case working behind it.

evidenceHint.en: Analysis of privacy incident and complaint handling giving per-case elapsed times, the procedure steps evidenced and recurrence-measure status, with repeated causes flagged

controls.title: CVV Retention Prevention
controls.objective: Ensure that the card verification code (CVV) is not stored in any systems post-authorization to comply with PCI DSS requirements and protect sensitive cardholder data.
controls.successCriteria:
No evidence of CVV storage post-authorization in any of the Banking & Accounting systems.
Compliance with PCI DSS requirements regarding sensitive cardholder data protection.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain a list of systems classified under "Banking & Accounting" from the Access Matrix.
Acquire screenshots of payment processing interfaces in these systems.
Gather logs or records of transactions processed since the last audit, with a focus on data retention practices.

Analysis:
For each transaction record, verify that no CVV data is stored post-authorization.
Examine payment processing interfaces in screenshots to ensure there is no functionality or field for storing CVVs.
Cross-reference transaction logs with system capabilities to ensure compliance with CVV retention policies.

Output:
Compiled list of audited systems with annotations on CVV handling.
Screenshots of payment processing interfaces.
Analysis report of transaction logs and data retention practices.

title.en: Extract the Banking and Accounting systems from the Access Matrix and annotate CVV handling

description.en: The audit population for this control is the set of systems the Access Matrix classifies as Banking and Accounting, so take that classification as the source rather than assembling a list of payment systems from memory. Against each system record whether it captures the card verification code, transmits it, or has any capability at all to store it, and name the person who can produce transaction records and interface screenshots from that system when the later tasks need them. A system that touches no card data is recorded as such rather than dropped, so the annotated list accounts for the whole classification rather than a subset somebody chose. Attach the annotated list with the date it was extracted from the Access Matrix.

evidenceHint.en: Annotated list of Banking and Accounting systems extracted from the Access Matrix on a stated date, each row saying whether the system captures, transmits or can store CVV, with the evidence contact named

title.en: Record where each system writes card data and the setting that keeps CVV out of it

description.en: For every system on the annotated list that touches card data, document the stores the authorisation flow writes to — database tables, application and web server logs, message queues, temporary files and any export the system produces — and, against each, the setting, schema constraint or code path that prevents the card verification code being written there. This is the system capability the control cross-references the transaction logs against; without it, a search that found nothing cannot be distinguished from a search that looked in the wrong places. Attach the record with the configuration extracts it cites, dated, so it evidences the period rather than the day it was written.

evidenceHint.en: Per-system record of every store the authorisation flow writes to, naming the setting, schema constraint or code path that prevents CVV persisting in each, backed by dated configuration extracts

text.en: Trace the authorisation flow from capture to response and list every store it writes to.
Include application and web server logs, message queues and temporary files, not only databases.
Name the setting, schema constraint or code path that keeps CVV out of each store.
Attach the dated configuration extract showing each named setting in its current state.

title.en: Capture a dated screenshot of every payment processing interface showing no CVV retained

description.en: For each system on the list, screenshot the payment processing interface at the point after authorisation and, where the system has one, the stored-card or transaction detail view, showing that no card verification code is displayed or held in a field. Put the system name and the capture date in the image or its filename so a screenshot cannot be silently carried over into a later period. Where an interface does offer a field capable of holding a card verification code, capture that screen too and raise it as an exception rather than omitting it from the set. Attach the screenshots with an index naming the system and the screen each image shows.

evidenceHint.en: Dated screenshot set covering every payment processing interface on the list, indexed by system and screen, showing no CVV field or value retained after authorisation

title.en: Search each system's transaction records for card verification codes held after authorisation

description.en: Run a search across the stores named in the capability record — tables, logs, temporary files and exports — for values shaped like a card verification code, over the transactions processed since the last audit. Record per system which stores were searched, the pattern used, the volume of records examined and the number of hits, and state a nil result explicitly, because an omitted line and a clean search read identically otherwise. Capture every hit with its location and record identifier and pass it to the review task before anything is deleted, since the location is what identifies which control failed. Attach the search output for every system on the list, including those that returned nothing.

evidenceHint.en: Search output per system over the transaction records since the last audit, naming the stores searched, the pattern used, the volume examined and every hit with its location, with nil results stated explicitly

title.en: Cross-reference the search results against each system's recorded capability and report

description.en: Bring the three artifacts together — the annotated system list, the capability record and the search output — and produce the analysis report the control calls for. A hit in a system whose record says it cannot store the code is a documentation failure as well as a data failure, and the report says which of the two it is; a clean search on a system whose capability record shows an unconstrained store is a result the report qualifies rather than passes. Give every exception an owner, an agreed remediation and a date, and state per system whether the evidence supports the conclusion that no card verification code is retained after authorisation. Attach the report with the artifacts it draws on.

evidenceHint.en: Analysis report giving, per Banking and Accounting system, the search result set read against its recorded storage capability, a retention verdict, and an owner, remediation and date for every exception

controls.title: DHCP Inventory Update
controls.objective: Ensure that DHCP logging is effectively used to maintain an accurate and up-to-date enterprise asset inventory.
controls.successCriteria:
The enterprise asset inventory is updated at least weekly, incorporating new and changed assets identified in DHCP logs.
The updated asset inventory accurately reflects the current state of enterprise assets as determined from DHCP logs.
Asset inventory update processes are consistently followed and documented.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Retrieve DHCP logs from all DHCP servers or IP address management tools.
Obtain the current enterprise asset inventory list.
Gather records of asset inventory updates for the last month.

Analysis:
Analyze DHCP logs to identify new or changed assets within the network.
Compare the identified assets from DHCP logs with the current enterprise asset inventory to verify updates.
Review the frequency and comprehensiveness of asset inventory updates.

Output:
Compiled list of assets identified from DHCP logs.
Comparison report between DHCP identified assets and enterprise asset inventory.
Documentation of asset inventory update records.

title.en: Inventory the DHCP servers and IP address management tools whose logs feed the asset inventory

description.en: List every DHCP server and IP address management tool operating on the enterprise network, with the scopes or subnets each serves, how long it retains its logs, and how that log is retrieved. A source nobody listed is a blind spot that never announces itself: assets on its scopes simply never reach the inventory, and the weekly comparison cannot report a gap in data it was never given. Record also the subnets served by no DHCP service at all, because statically addressed hosts there will appear in no log and have to be covered another way. Attach the dated source list.

evidenceHint.en: Dated list of DHCP servers and IP address management tools with the scopes each serves, its log retention period and retrieval route, plus the subnets served by no DHCP service

text.en: List the DHCP servers in operation, including any running on network appliances or firewalls.
Add the IP address management tools holding lease history the servers themselves do not retain.
Record the scopes or subnets each source serves and how long it retains its logs.
Record the retrieval route for each source — export, syslog feed or console download.
Identify the subnets served by no DHCP service, where static hosts will never appear.

title.en: Document the weekly procedure that turns DHCP log entries into inventory updates

description.en: Write down the process the control expects to be consistently followed: who runs it, on which day of the week, how each source's logs are pulled, the fields carried across to the inventory — hardware address, address issued, hostname, lease timestamps — the rule that decides whether a lease record is a new asset or an existing one reappearing, and how the resulting update is recorded. Both the comparison and the cadence review read this document as the standard, and an undocumented process cannot be found to have been departed from. Attach the issued procedure.

evidenceHint.en: Issued weekly DHCP-to-inventory update procedure naming the owner, the run day, the sources pulled, the fields carried across, the new-versus-existing asset rule, and how each update is recorded

title.en: Compile the week's new and changed assets from the DHCP logs

description.en: Pull the week's logs from every source on the list and produce the compiled asset list the audit asks for: one row per hardware address seen, with the address issued, the hostname reported, the first and last lease timestamps within the week, and the source it came from. Mark each row as new to the inventory or as an existing asset whose address, hostname or subnet has changed, because those are the two populations the update acts on and an unmarked row is one nobody applies. Attach the compiled list naming the week it covers.

evidenceHint.en: Compiled weekly list of assets seen in the DHCP logs, one row per hardware address giving the address issued, hostname, first and last lease timestamps, source server, and a new or changed marking

title.en: Update the enterprise asset inventory from the compiled DHCP list each week

description.en: Apply the week's compiled list to the inventory: add the assets marked new, correct the address, hostname or subnet of those marked changed, and record against each edit the date it was made and the log row that prompted it. Where a row cannot be applied — a hardware address resolving to no identifiable asset, a device attributable to no owner — hold it on an exceptions list with a named owner rather than dropping it, because a dropped row is how the inventory becomes quietly wrong while the update record still looks complete. Attach the week's update record.

evidenceHint.en: Weekly asset inventory update record showing each row added or corrected, the DHCP log entry that prompted it and the date applied, plus the exceptions list of rows that could not be applied and their owners

title.en: Compare the DHCP-identified assets against the inventory and report what is missing

description.en: Set the compiled DHCP asset list against the current enterprise asset inventory and produce the comparison report: assets seen in the logs but absent from the inventory, inventory entries whose recorded address or hostname disagrees with what the logs observed, and inventory entries not seen in the logs at all. The third group is not automatically stale — a statically addressed host will never appear in a DHCP log — so report it alongside the subnets recorded as having no DHCP coverage. Name an owner against each discrepancy. Attach the comparison report.

evidenceHint.en: Comparison report between the compiled DHCP asset list and the enterprise asset inventory, listing assets missing from the inventory, entries whose details disagree and entries not seen at all, each with a named owner

text.en: Match the compiled DHCP list to the inventory on hardware address rather than on machine name.
List the assets seen in the logs that hold no inventory entry at all.
List the inventory entries whose recorded address or hostname disagrees with the logs.
List entries not seen in the logs, noting the subnets recorded as having no DHCP coverage.
Name an accountable owner against each discrepancy and the correction agreed with them.

title.en: Review the last month's DHCP inventory update records against the weekly cadence

description.en: Take the update records for the last month and test the cadence the control sets: that an update was made in every week, that each drew on all the DHCP sources on the list rather than a convenient subset, and that the documented procedure was the one actually followed. Record a per-week result carrying the date the update was made and the sources it covered; where a week has no update, or only a partial one, record the reason and the catch-up that was performed. Attach the review with the update records it reads.

evidenceHint.en: Cadence review over the last month with a per-week result showing the update date, the DHCP sources covered, and the reason plus catch-up for any week missed or only partially covered

controls.title: Stakeholder Coordination in Incident Response
controls.objective: Ensure effective coordination with internal and external stakeholders, including law enforcement, during incident response activities. This includes establishing protocols for voluntary information sharing with external stakeholders to enhance broader cybersecurity situational awareness.
controls.successCriteria:
The IRP explicitly includes protocols for coordination with internal and external stakeholders, including practices for voluntary information sharing.
Incident records show consistent and effective engagement with stakeholders and demonstrate information sharing activities as per the IRP.
Communication logs and records demonstrate clear, timely, and appropriate coordination and information sharing efforts.
Existing agreements or protocols with external entities, like law enforcement agencies, are adhered to during incident response, including aspects of voluntary information sharing.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the Incident Response Plan (IRP) document.
Gather a record of recent security incidents and their corresponding response activities.
Collect communication logs or records showing coordination efforts with internal and external stakeholders (emails, meeting minutes, joint task force reports, etc.).
Acquire documentation of any agreements or protocols established with law enforcement agencies or other external entities for information sharing.
Obtain records of voluntary information sharing instances with external stakeholders for cybersecurity situational awareness.

Analysis:
Review the IRP to confirm the inclusion of protocols for stakeholder coordination, focusing on roles, responsibilities, and procedures for engaging with internal and external entities, including voluntary information sharing practices.
For each recorded incident, assess whether coordination with stakeholders and information sharing activities were executed as per the IRP.
Examine communication logs or records to verify actual engagement and information sharing with stakeholders, ensuring alignment with the IRP and any established agreements or protocols.
Evaluate the efficiency and effectiveness of the coordination and information sharing efforts in terms of response time, communication clarity, stakeholder involvement, and contribution to broader cybersecurity situational awareness.

Output:
A compliance report detailing how each incident was managed concerning stakeholder coordination and information sharing.
An evaluation report of communication logs, coordination efforts, and information sharing instances.
An assessment of the IRP's current stakeholder coordination and information sharing protocols.

title.en: Register every internal and external stakeholder the Incident Response Plan engages

description.en: Build one row per stakeholder the plan calls on during an incident — internal functions such as legal, communications and the executive, and external parties such as law enforcement, the sector CERT, the regulator, key customers and suppliers. Each row carries the trigger that brings them in, the contact route, the named internal owner of the relationship, and a reference to any agreement or protocol governing the engagement. This register is the population the coordination log is later read against, so a party engaged during an incident but absent here is a gap in the register rather than in the log. Attach the dated register.

evidenceHint.en: Dated stakeholder register listing each internal and external party, the trigger that engages them, the contact route, the internal relationship owner and the governing agreement reference

title.en: Document the coordination and voluntary information-sharing protocols in the Incident Response Plan

description.en: Extend the plan so it states, for coordination, who holds the relationship with each stakeholder class, who is authorised to make contact, at what point in an incident, and what they are permitted to say. For voluntary information sharing, state separately what may be shared for broader situational awareness — indicators, techniques, sector warnings — what may never be shared, who authorises a share, and where each share is recorded. Voluntary sharing is the half most often left implicit, and a plan silent on it cannot be tested for it however consistently it is practised. Attach the issued plan version showing both sections.

evidenceHint.en: Issued Incident Response Plan version containing the stakeholder coordination section and a distinct voluntary information-sharing section naming what may be shared, by whom and under whose authorisation

text.en: Name the relationship owner and the authorised contact for each stakeholder class.
State at what point in an incident each stakeholder class is engaged and by which route.
State what may be disclosed to each class and what is withheld pending authorisation.
Write the voluntary information-sharing rules as their own section rather than as an aside.
Name who authorises a voluntary share and where each share has to be recorded.

title.en: Record what each external agreement permits to be shared, with whom and under what conditions

description.en: For every law enforcement agency, CERT or other external entity the register names as holding an agreement or protocol, extract the operative terms into a form the incident commander can read under pressure: the categories of information the agreement permits or requires be shared, any condition or approval attaching to a disclosure, and the committed contact route. An agreement silent on one of those is recorded as silent rather than assumed permissive, and that silence list is the finding this task produces. Legal/DPO reads the disclosure terms. Attach the register with the agreement extracts behind it.

evidenceHint.en: External agreement register giving per entity the information categories permitted or required to be shared, the attached conditions and the contact route, plus the list of agreements silent on any of these

title.en: Log the coordination activity for each incident against the stakeholders the plan names

description.en: For every incident, keep the record of who was actually engaged and when: the stakeholder, the time contact was made, the route used, what was communicated and what came back. Meeting minutes, joint task force notes and email threads are the raw material and belong filed against the incident rather than left in individual mailboxes, because the test compares this record against what the plan required for that incident's category. Where a stakeholder the plan names was deliberately not engaged, record that decision and who took it, so a deliberate omission is distinguishable from a missed one. Attach the coordination log with its supporting communications for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Per-incident coordination log for the period showing each stakeholder engaged, the contact time and route, what was communicated and the response, with the filed emails, minutes and task force notes

title.en: Record each voluntary information-sharing instance and what was disclosed

description.en: Keep one entry per voluntary share made to an external party for broader cybersecurity situational awareness: the recipient, the date, the substance shared, the authorisation relied on, and anything withheld or redacted before sending. This record is separately requested at audit and is the only evidence that the sharing protocol is used rather than merely written, so a period with no shares is recorded as an explicit nil return carrying the reason rather than left as an empty file — an empty file and a period of no sharing are indistinguishable to a reader. Attach the sharing log for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Voluntary information-sharing log for the period showing recipient, date, substance shared, the authorisation relied on and any redaction, or an explicit nil return carrying its reason

title.en: Assess each incident's stakeholder coordination against the plan and the external agreements

description.en: Take the incidents handled in the period and read the coordination log against what the plan required and what each external agreement committed the organisation to: was every stakeholder the plan names for that incident category actually engaged, was contact made through the agreed route, was it timely, and was the message clear enough that the recipient acted on it. Score each incident per stakeholder and record deviations with an owner. Conclude with the changes the plan's own coordination and sharing sections need, since gaps found here are as often plan defects as execution failures. Attach the assessment report.

evidenceHint.en: Coordination compliance report scoring each incident per stakeholder against the plan and the external agreements, with deviations and owners, and the resulting changes required to the plan itself

text.en: List, per incident, the stakeholders the plan required for that incident's category.
Match each required stakeholder to an entry in the coordination log and mark engaged or missed.
Check the contact route and timing against the agreement or protocol governing that party.
Record a deviation with a named owner for every missed, late or off-route engagement.
Write the changes the plan's coordination and sharing sections need as a result.

controls.title: Post-Termination Information Security Responsibilities
controls.objective: To ensure that information security responsibilities and duties of personnel are adhered to and enforced even after the termination or change of their employment.
controls.successCriteria:
All termination/change of employment agreements include required clauses on post-employment information security responsibilities.
Documented evidence shows that departing employees were made aware of their ongoing information security responsibilities.
The compliance matrix demonstrates full alignment of agreement clauses with policy standards.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain a list of recent employment terminations and role changes from the HR department.
Collect copies of exit interview documentation and termination/change of employment agreements.
Retrieve relevant sections from the employee handbook or policies that outline post-termination duties and responsibilities.

Analysis:
Review termination/change of employment agreements to ensure they include clauses related to post-employment information security responsibilities.
Compare the outlined responsibilities in the agreements with the policy standards to verify alignment and completeness.
Assess the exit interview documentation to confirm that information security responsibilities were communicated and understood by the departing employees.

Output:
A report detailing the review of termination/change of employment agreements.
A compliance matrix comparing agreement clauses against policy standards.
Summary of findings from exit interview document reviews.

title.en: Extract the post-employment security duties from the Human Resources Security Policy into a clause checklist

description.en: Read the Human Resources Security Policy and the employee handbook sections that describe duties continuing after termination or a change of role, and transcribe each duty into a checklist with one row per duty, quoting the policy or handbook section it comes from. Do not paraphrase duties into new obligations — a row exists only where the policy or handbook states one, and related duties stay in separate rows rather than being merged. This checklist is the policy standard that agreements and exit interview records are compared against in the later tasks. Attach the completed checklist with the source policy version recorded on it.

evidenceHint.en: Clause checklist listing every post-employment security duty with the Human Resources Security Policy or handbook section each is taken from, and the policy version reviewed

text.en: Retrieve the current Human Resources Security Policy and the handbook sections covering termination and change of role.
Transcribe each stated post-employment duty as its own checklist row, quoting the source clause verbatim.
Record whether each duty applies to terminations, to role changes, or to both.
Number each row so agreements and exit interview forms can cite it in the compliance matrix.

title.en: Add the post-employment security clauses to the termination and role-change agreement templates

description.en: Amend the standard termination agreement and the change-of-employment agreement templates so that every duty on the clause checklist appears in the signed document, and annotate each clause with the checklist row number it satisfies so the mapping can be audited later. Confirm with HR which agreement templates are actually issued for terminations and for role changes, and hand HR the amended versions to replace the ones in use, so no variant is left on the old wording. Attach the amended templates with their version numbers and effective date.

evidenceHint.en: Versioned termination and change-of-employment agreement templates showing the post-employment security clauses, with each clause annotated against its checklist row number

title.en: Add a security responsibilities section with a signature block to the exit interview and role-change briefing form

description.en: Amend the exit interview form, and the equivalent briefing form used when someone changes role, so the interviewer walks through the duties on the clause checklist and the departing or moving employee signs to confirm they were explained. The section records which checklist rows were covered, the date, and the names of both the interviewer and the employee, so the completed form evidences that the responsibilities were communicated and understood rather than merely listed. HR issues and files these forms. Attach the amended forms and note where completed copies are filed.

evidenceHint.en: Amended exit interview and role-change briefing templates containing the post-employment security responsibilities section, the covered-checklist-row fields, and the employee signature block

title.en: Capture a signed post-employment acknowledgement at every exit interview and role-change briefing

description.en: For each termination and each change of role, run the security responsibilities section of the briefing, obtain the employee's signature, file the completed form against their personnel record, and enter the acknowledgement reference in the leaver and role-change list HR keeps, so the population and the evidence can be tied together. Where an employee leaves without an exit interview, record the reason against their row rather than leaving it blank. Attach the signed acknowledgements for the period together with the list export covering the same period.

evidenceHint.en: Signed post-employment acknowledgement forms for the period, plus the HR leaver and role-change list export showing an acknowledgement reference or a recorded reason for each person

title.en: Compare each executed termination and role-change agreement against the clause checklist in a compliance matrix

description.en: Take the terminations and role changes HR recorded for the period, pull the executed agreement for each one, and build a matrix with agreements down one axis and the clause checklist rows across the other, marking each cell present, absent, or reworded. Every absent or reworded cell is a finding and needs the agreement version and the person's record identified so HR can reissue or remediate. Attach the completed matrix and a report naming the agreements reviewed and the gaps found.

evidenceHint.en: Compliance matrix mapping every executed termination and change-of-employment agreement for the period to the clause checklist rows, with gaps marked, and the accompanying findings report

text.en: Draw the population of terminations and role changes for the period from the HR list.
Retrieve the executed agreement for each person in the population.
Mark each clause checklist row present, absent, or reworded for every agreement.
Record the agreement template version used, so gaps can be traced to a superseded template.
List each gap as a finding with the person's record reference and pass it to HR for remediation.

title.en: Produce the exit interview review summary naming every termination and role change with no signed acknowledgement on file

description.en: Work through the same period's terminations and role changes and, for each person, confirm a completed and signed security responsibilities section is on file and that the checklist rows it records match the clause checklist. Give every person one of three statuses — acknowledgement on file and complete, on file but covering fewer duties than the checklist, or absent — and for each absent one quote the reason held against their row. Where the duties covered are narrower than the checklist, name the missing row numbers so the briefing form or the interviewer's script can be corrected. Attach the summary listing every person checked with their status.

evidenceHint.en: Exit interview review summary naming each termination and role change checked for the period, its acknowledgement status, and the clause checklist rows missing from any incomplete acknowledgement

controls.title: Disciplinary Process Compliance
controls.objective: To ensure adherence to the formal disciplinary process for information security policy violations.
controls.successCriteria:
The disciplinary process for each reported violation aligns with the Information Security Policy.
Actions taken in response to violations are appropriate based on the nature and severity of the breach, as well as the training and intent of the violator.
Consistent application of the disciplinary process across all cases.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain a record of all reported information security policy violations.
Collect documentation detailing the initiation and conclusion of each disciplinary process.
Retrieve training records of the individuals involved in the violations.

Analysis:
Review each reported violation to confirm if the disciplinary process was initiated as per policy.
For each disciplinary action, assess whether the response was graduated based on the nature and gravity of the breach, the intention behind the offense, and the training status of the violator.
Compare the actions taken against policy violators with the guidelines set in the Information Security Policy to ensure consistency and fairness.

Output:
A report summarizing each violation and the corresponding disciplinary action.
A comparison matrix showing the alignment between each case's specifics and the response as per the policy.
A summary of discrepancies, if any, between the policy and its implementation.

title.en: Register every reported information security policy violation for the period

description.en: Pull the period's reported violations from the records in which they are raised and give each one a row carrying the reference, the date it was reported, the policy clause breached, the individual or role involved, and the severity assigned. This register is the population every later task counts against: the case files, the training and intent evidence and the comparison matrix are all one row per entry here, so a violation missing from it is a case nobody tests. Where a report was assessed and found not to be a policy violation, keep the row and record that disposition rather than deleting it. Attach the register with the date it was compiled.

evidenceHint.en: Dated register of reported information security policy violations with reference, report date, policy clause breached, person or role involved and assessed severity

text.en: Gather every reported policy violation raised during the period under test.
Give each report a reference and record the date it was first reported.
Record the policy clause breached and the individual or role the report concerns.
Record the severity assigned to the violation at the point it was reported.
Keep reports assessed as not a violation, marked with that disposition.

title.en: Record the graduated disciplinary responses the Information Security Policy prescribes

description.en: Read the Information Security Policy and set out, as a table an assessor can apply, what response it calls for at each combination of breach nature and gravity, the intent behind the offence, and the training the individual had received. This table is the yardstick the case comparison runs against, so a factor the policy names but the table omits will never be tested. Where the policy gives a range rather than a single outcome, record the range and the discretion it grants rather than collapsing it to one value, and flag any factor the policy leaves silent — that silence is itself a finding for the discrepancy summary. Attach the table with the policy version and clause references it was drawn from.

evidenceHint.en: Graduated response table keyed by breach nature and gravity, intent and training status, cross-referenced to the Information Security Policy clauses it derives from

title.en: Document the initiation and conclusion of each disciplinary case

description.en: For every violation in the register that entered the disciplinary process, hold a case file recording the date the process was initiated, who initiated it, the steps taken, the outcome decided and the date it concluded. Where a violation did not enter the process, record the reason it did not, since an absent case file is otherwise indistinguishable from a process that was never started. Both dates matter: initiation evidences the process began as the policy requires, and conclusion is what lets timeliness be read. Attach the case documentation for the period, one file per case.

evidenceHint.en: Disciplinary case files for the period showing initiation date and initiator, steps taken, outcome and conclusion date, plus a recorded reason for every violation that did not enter the process

title.en: Capture the training status and intent finding behind each disciplinary case

description.en: The policy's response is graduated on the offender's training and intent, so each case needs both recorded as evidence rather than as assertion. Attach the individual's information security training record showing what was completed and when, set against the date of the violation, and record the intent finding the investigation reached and the basis on which it was reached. A case where training could not be evidenced is recorded as such, because that gap changes which row of the graduated response table applies to it. Attach the training extracts and the intent findings alongside the case files.

evidenceHint.en: Per-case training record extract showing completion dates against the violation date, and the recorded intent finding with the evidence it rests on

title.en: Map each disciplinary action to the response its case specifics call for

description.en: Build the comparison matrix the control calls for: one row per case, carrying the breach nature and gravity, the intent finding, the training status, the response the graduated table prescribes for that combination, and the action actually taken. Mark each row aligned or discrepant, and for every discrepancy record why the difference arose and whether the discretion the policy grants covers it. The discrepant rows are the discrepancy summary this control outputs — carry them forward with a named owner rather than leaving them buried in the matrix. Attach the completed matrix with the case references behind each row.

evidenceHint.en: Case-by-case comparison matrix showing prescribed versus actual response with an aligned or discrepant verdict per case, and the discrepancy summary drawn from it

text.en: List one row per case with its breach nature, gravity, intent and training status.
Read the prescribed response for that combination from the graduated response table.
Record the action actually taken and mark the row aligned or discrepant.
For each discrepancy, record whether the policy's discretion covers the difference.
Carry the unresolved discrepancies into the summary with a named owner.

title.en: Test outcome consistency across cases with comparable severity, intent and training

description.en: Group the period's cases by the combination of factors the graduated table keys on and compare the outcomes within each group. Cases that share a row of the table but received materially different responses are the inconsistency this test exists to surface, and each one needs either a documented reason that distinguishes the cases or a finding raised against it. Where a group holds only one case there is nothing to compare — record that rather than reporting a pass, so the coverage of the test is visible to whoever reads it. Attach the grouped comparison and the findings it produced.

evidenceHint.en: Grouped comparison of case outcomes by breach factors, naming each group with divergent outcomes and either the distinguishing reason or the finding raised

controls.title: Business Continuity Exercise Programme
controls.objective: To validate the effectiveness of business continuity strategies and solutions through regular and comprehensive exercising and testing.
controls.successCriteria:
All exercises are conducted as per the planned schedule and following significant changes.
Scenarios used are relevant and aligned with business continuity objectives.
Exercises effectively develop the required skills and knowledge in participants.
Post-exercise reports are comprehensive and actionable.
Documented improvements and changes are implemented based on exercise findings.
Continuous improvement is evident through periodic reviews and updates to the exercise programme.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:

Obtain the exercise and testing schedule for the current year.
Gather the list of scenarios used for each exercise.
Collect pre-exercise plans, including aims and objectives.
Retrieve post-exercise reports, including outcomes, recommendations, and actions.
Obtain records of changes implemented based on exercise outcomes.
Review team feedback and competence assessments post-exercise.

Analysis:

Verify that exercises are conducted according to the schedule and any significant organizational changes.
Assess if the scenarios used are appropriate and align with business continuity objectives.
Check if exercises develop teamwork, competence, confidence, and knowledge for relevant roles.
Ensure post-exercise reports are formalized and include outcomes, recommendations, and actions.
Review if exercises validate business continuity strategies and solutions over time.
Confirm that results are reviewed and lead to continual improvements.

Output:

Schedule and attendance records for each exercise.
Documentation of exercise scenarios and plans.
Post-exercise reports with detailed outcomes, recommendations, and actions.
Records of changes implemented following exercise findings.
Team feedback and competence assessment results.

title.en: Schedule the year's continuity exercises and the changes that trigger an extra one

description.en: Set out, per exercise, the date, the continuity strategy or solution it is meant to validate and the teams taking part. Beside the calendar, write down the significant organisational changes that oblige an exercise outside it, because this control expects exercising after significant change as well as to schedule, and without that list the calendar becomes the only obligation anybody tracks. Attach the exercise and testing schedule for the current year with the trigger list beside it.

evidenceHint.en: Exercise and testing schedule for the current year giving the date, the continuity strategy or solution under test and the participating teams per exercise, with the significant-change trigger list

title.en: Document the aim, objectives and scenario for each exercise before it runs

description.en: For every scheduled exercise write the plan that participants and observers work from: the scenario, the aim, the specific objectives the exercise must demonstrate, and what is and is not in play. Tie the scenario back to the business continuity objective it exercises, so a scenario chosen for convenience is visible as one. Objectives written after the exercise cannot fail, which is why this is a pre-exercise deliverable and why the issue date matters. Attach the exercise plan showing an issue date ahead of the exercise date.

evidenceHint.en: Pre-exercise plan per exercise giving the scenario, the aim, the specific objectives and what is in and out of play, issued and dated before the exercise ran

text.en: Choose a scenario that exercises a stated business continuity objective.
Write the aim and the specific objectives the exercise must demonstrate.
State what is in scope and what is deliberately excluded from play.
Issue the plan to participants and observers before the exercise date.

title.en: Record attendance, participant feedback and the competence assessed at each exercise

description.en: Take attendance for every exercise against the roles that were meant to take part, collect participant feedback while the exercise is still fresh, and record the competence assessment for the roles the exercise was meant to develop — the programme exists to build teamwork, confidence and knowledge, and only the assessment evidences that it did. Roles that were scheduled but absent are recorded as absent rather than dropped from the sheet, because the repeated absence of one role is the pattern that matters. Attach the attendance sheet, the feedback returns and the competence results for each exercise.

evidenceHint.en: Per-exercise attendance sheet set against the scheduled roles, the participant feedback returns and the competence assessment results, including roles scheduled but absent

title.en: Issue a post-exercise report with outcomes, recommendations and assigned actions

description.en: After each exercise write up what happened against the objectives set in its plan: which objectives were met, which were not, what was observed and what participants reported. Turn each observation into a recommendation, and each accepted recommendation into an action with a named owner and a target date. A report that closes with recommendations and no owners cannot be tracked, and that is the point at which an exercise programme stops improving anything. Attach the issued report for every exercise held in the period.

evidenceHint.en: Post-exercise report per exercise stating the outcome against each planned objective, the recommendations made, and the actions raised with a named owner and target date

title.en: Record the change made against each action raised by an exercise

description.en: Track every action from the post-exercise reports through to the change it actually produced: the plan, procedure, contact list, technical configuration or resource that was amended, the date of the amendment and the person who made it. An action closed with no recorded change is closed on assertion, and this control asks for documented improvements rather than documented intentions. Actions still open at period end stay listed with their target dates. Attach the action tracker showing the change and closure date behind every closed row.

evidenceHint.en: Exercise action tracker linking each action to the plan, procedure or configuration change it produced, with the amendment date, the person who made it and the closure date

title.en: Review the exercise programme against the year's outcomes and record the updates made

description.en: At the end of the cycle read the schedule, the reports and the action tracker together and judge the programme rather than the individual exercises: were the scheduled exercises actually held, did the scenarios cover the continuity strategies that matter, did the same finding recur across several exercises, and were the year's significant changes exercised at all. Record the resulting changes to next cycle's scenarios, frequency and participants, and for any exercise not held, the reason. Attach the programme review with the updated schedule it produced.

evidenceHint.en: Exercise programme review covering exercises held against those scheduled, scenario coverage of the continuity strategies, findings that recurred, and the updated schedule it produced

controls.title: Internal Responsibility Accountability
controls.objective: To ensure individuals are held accountable for their internal control responsibilities in pursuit of organizational objectives.
controls.successCriteria:
All roles and responsibilities within the organization are clearly defined and aligned with internal control objectives.
Performance evaluations effectively measure compliance with internal control responsibilities.
Incentives and rewards are appropriately aligned with internal control compliance and the achievement of organizational objectives.
Disciplinary actions are effectively enforced in cases of policy violations or incidents, demonstrating an effective accountability mechanism.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the organizational structure chart highlighting individual roles and responsibilities.
Collect performance evaluation reports focusing on internal control responsibilities.
Gather documentation of incentives, rewards, and disciplinary actions related to internal control compliance.
Retrieve records of any privacy policy violations or related incidents.

Analysis:
Review the organizational chart to verify the clarity of internal control responsibilities across different roles.
Analyze performance reports to assess whether internal control responsibilities are being evaluated effectively.
Examine incentives and rewards to ensure they align with internal control compliance and organizational objectives.
Investigate any instances of policy violations or incidents to evaluate the effectiveness of the disciplinary process.

Output:
A report summarizing the alignment of roles and responsibilities with internal control objectives.
A spreadsheet or document analyzing the effectiveness of performance evaluations in internal control compliance.
A summary of the incentives and disciplinary actions, highlighting their effectiveness and alignment with internal control objectives.

title.en: Map each role on the organisation chart to the internal control responsibilities it carries

description.en: Work down the organisation structure and, for every role, write the internal control responsibilities it holds and the organisational objective each supports — approving, performing, reviewing or monitoring — naming the person currently in the role beside it. Where two roles claim the same responsibility, or none claims it, record that as a finding rather than resolving it silently: ambiguous ownership is precisely what this control exists to surface. Attach the annotated structure with every control responsibility allocated to a named role.

evidenceHint.en: Organisation structure annotated with the internal control responsibilities each role holds, the objective each supports, the current holder, and the list of responsibilities that are unallocated or duplicated

title.en: Write the internal control responsibilities into the performance evaluation criteria for each role

description.en: Amend the evaluation framework so a person's internal control responsibilities are a scored item rather than an implicit expectation: for each role the criteria name the responsibilities taken from the map, state what acceptable performance against them looks like, and give the evaluator somewhere to record the evidence they relied on. HR owns the framework; Management supplies the standard of performance for each role. Attach the issued evaluation criteria or template showing the internal control section and the roles it applies to.

evidenceHint.en: Issued performance evaluation template or criteria document showing internal control responsibilities as a scored section, with the standard of performance defined per role

title.en: Record an internal control assessment in every completed performance evaluation

description.en: As each evaluation is completed, the evaluator scores the person against the internal control responsibilities their role carries and records the evidence behind the score — not a rating alone, but what was observed. Where performance against a control responsibility fell short, the evaluation carries the action agreed and the date it is to be met. Attach the completed evaluations for the period, or an extract of their internal control sections where the full documents are restricted.

evidenceHint.en: Completed performance evaluations for the period, or an extract of their internal control sections, showing the score, the supporting evidence and any agreed action per person

title.en: Log every policy violation and the disciplinary action taken against it

description.en: Maintain one register of violations and incidents attributable to a person's conduct, privacy policy breaches included, carrying the date, what was breached, who investigated, the action taken, the date it was taken, and who decided it. A case closed with no action is recorded with the reason, because an unexplained no-action entry is exactly the pattern the later review looks for. HR holds the register and Legal/DPO records the privacy cases. Attach the register covering the period.

evidenceHint.en: Violation and disciplinary register for the period: date, policy breached, investigator, action taken, decision date, decision maker, and the reason recorded wherever no action followed

title.en: Test whether the completed evaluations actually measured internal control responsibilities

description.en: Sample the evaluations completed in the period and, for each, check that the internal control section was filled in, that it addresses the responsibilities the map allocates to that role rather than generic conduct, and that the score cites evidence. Record pass or fail per evaluation with the shortfall described, and count how many roles carrying control responsibilities were evaluated on them at all. Attach the analysis: a framework that names control responsibilities but is left blank in practice is the failure this task exists to detect.

evidenceHint.en: Analysis spreadsheet scoring sampled evaluations on whether the internal control section was completed, addressed the role's allocated responsibilities and cited evidence, with the shortfall described per fail

text.en: Draw the sample so every part of the structure carrying control responsibilities is represented.
Check the internal control section was completed rather than left blank or marked not applicable.
Read the responsibilities scored against those the map allocates to that role.
Record whether each score cites observed evidence or is an unsupported rating.

title.en: Assess the incentives, rewards and disciplinary actions against the internal control objectives

description.en: Collect the incentive and reward schemes in force and the disciplinary actions taken in the period, and read them together: does anything the entity pays for pull against a control responsibility, is compliance with control responsibilities reflected in what is rewarded, and were comparable violations treated consistently. Name each scheme, the measure it pays on, and the control objective it supports or works against; name each violation and the action it drew, flagging where similar breaches drew materially different outcomes. Attach the summary with the scheme documents and case records it was built from.

evidenceHint.en: Summary of incentive and reward schemes and of disciplinary actions taken, each set against the internal control objective it supports or undermines, flagging inconsistent outcomes for comparable violations

controls.title: Passive Asset Discovery and Inventory Update
controls.objective: To ensure all assets connected to the enterprise's network are identified and the asset inventory is updated at least weekly using a passive discovery tool.
controls.successCriteria:
The passive asset discovery tool is configured and functioning to scan the network at least weekly.
All assets identified in the scans are accurately reflected in the updated asset inventory.
Asset inventory updates are consistently logged and align with the scans conducted by the tool.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the latest asset inventory report generated by the passive asset discovery tool.
Get the configuration settings or logs from the passive asset discovery tool to confirm scan frequency.
Collect change logs or update records of the asset inventory for the period since the last audit.

Analysis:
Verify that the passive asset discovery tool is configured to scan the network at least weekly.
Compare the assets identified in the latest scan with the updated asset inventory to ensure all new or changed assets are accurately reflected.
Review the change logs or update records to confirm that the asset inventory is updated following each scan.

Output:
Latest asset inventory report.
Configuration settings or logs from the passive asset discovery tool.
Change logs or update records of the asset inventory.

title.en: Record the network segments the passive discovery tool observes and those it does not

description.en: A passive tool sees only the traffic that reaches it, so document its placement: which subnets, VLANs and span or tap points it observes, and — the part that carries the risk — which parts of the enterprise network it does not. A segment nobody is listening on produces no assets and no alert about their absence, so it reads exactly like a clean segment, and the comparison against the inventory cannot be read correctly without knowing which segments a scan could never have covered. Attach the coverage map with the date it reflects.

evidenceHint.en: Dated coverage map of the passive discovery tool showing its monitoring points, the subnets whose traffic reaches each of them, and the enterprise segments observed by no monitoring point at all

text.en: Record the span ports, taps or mirrors the tool actually receives traffic from.
Map those monitoring points to the subnets and VLANs whose traffic reaches them.
List the enterprise segments whose traffic reaches no monitoring point at all.
Date the map and reissue it whenever the tool moves or a segment is added.

title.en: Configure the passive discovery tool to scan at least weekly and capture the setting

description.en: Set the tool's schedule to run no less often than weekly, and capture the configuration itself as the evidence — the schedule setting exported or screenshotted with a date, not a statement that it is configured. Record alongside it the fields the tool reports per discovered asset, since those are what an inventory update can carry across, and any asset class or address range the configuration excludes, since an exclusion is indistinguishable from an absence in the results. Attach the configuration export showing the scan frequency in force.

evidenceHint.en: Dated export or screenshot of the passive discovery tool's configuration showing a scan schedule of weekly or more often, the fields reported per discovered asset, and any configured exclusions

title.en: Export the weekly asset report the passive discovery tool generates

description.en: Take the tool's asset report for each week of the period and keep it as the primary artifact the audit asks for, each carrying its scan date and the assets discovered with the attributes the tool reports. Where a scheduled scan produced no report, leave the gap visible rather than substituting the previous week's — a repeated report is indistinguishable from a working scan until somebody reads the dates, and by then the inventory has been trusted for weeks. Attach the reports for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Weekly passive discovery reports covering the period, each carrying its own scan date and the assets discovered with their reported attributes, with any week that produced no report identified as such

title.en: Update the asset inventory from each passive discovery scan and log the change

description.en: After each weekly scan, reconcile its report into the enterprise asset inventory: add assets the scan discovered that the inventory does not hold, correct attributes that disagree, and log each edit with the scan date it derives from and who made it. The control ties updates to scans, so that link back to a specific scan is the load-bearing field — an update record unable to name the scan behind it cannot evidence that updates follow scans, however diligent the updating was. Attach the inventory change log for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Asset inventory change log for the period with one entry per edit giving the asset, the change made, the person who made it, and the scan date the change derives from

title.en: Compare the latest passive discovery scan against the asset inventory and record what is unreflected

description.en: Put the most recent scan report side by side with the current inventory and record, per discovered asset, whether the scan's finding is reflected: present and matching, present but disagreeing on an attribute, or absent from the inventory entirely. Absent assets are the finding the comparison exists to produce; disagreeing attributes are the quieter one and the one that survives longest. Name an owner and a correction against each non-matching row, and re-check after the correction that the inventory now holds it. Attach the comparison with the scan report it was drawn from.

evidenceHint.en: Comparison of the latest scan report against the asset inventory, one row per discovered asset marked matching, disagreeing or absent, with an owner, a correction and a post-correction re-check against each non-matching row

text.en: Take the most recent scan report and match each discovered asset to the inventory.
Mark each asset present and matching, present but disagreeing, or absent from the inventory.
Record which attribute disagrees for each partially matching asset.
Name an owner and a correction against every non-matching row.
Re-check after correction that the inventory now holds the asset and its attributes.

title.en: Confirm from the passive discovery tool's scan history that each week ran and updated the inventory
