description.en: Being configured and having run are separate claims, and this task tests the second: read the tool's own scan history for the period and build a per-week table giving the date the scan ran, whether a report was produced, and the inventory update entry that followed it. A week with a configured schedule but no scan in the history, or a scan with no resulting update, is the exception — record its reason and what was done to close it. Attach the table with the scan history extract it was built from.

evidenceHint.en: Per-week table for the period showing the scan date taken from the tool's own history, whether a report was produced, the inventory update that followed, and the reason and remedy for any week missing either

controls.title: Email Gateway File Type Filtering
controls.objective: To prevent unnecessary or potentially harmful file types from entering the organization's network through the email gateway, enhancing overall email security.
controls.successCriteria:
The email gateway is configured correctly to filter out unauthorized file types.
The logs demonstrate effective blocking of unauthorized file types and allowance of only approved file types.
The list of approved file types aligns with the file types observed in the gateway logs.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the configuration settings of the email gateway system.
Gather recent logs from the email gateway showing blocked and allowed file types.
Retrieve a list of approved file types permitted through the email gateway.

Analysis:
Assess the email gateway settings to verify the implementation of file type filtering.
Review the logs to confirm the blocking of unauthorized file types and the allowance of approved file types.
Compare the list of approved file types with the email gateway settings to ensure alignment.

Output:
A report detailing the configuration settings of the email gateway.
A log analysis report showing blocked and allowed file types.
A comparison report between approved file types and those observed in the logs.

title.en: Record the file types approved to pass the email gateway, with the reason each is permitted

description.en: This control turns on a list of approved file types, and the later reconciliation has nothing to compare against until that list exists as a stated artifact rather than as whatever the gateway happens to be configured with today. Record each permitted extension and, where the gateway inspects content, the true file type behind it; give the business reason it is needed and the owner who asked for it. Cover archives and container formats explicitly, since permitting a container implicitly permits whatever it carries. Attach the approved file-type list with its issue date and approval.

evidenceHint.en: Dated approved email file-type list giving each permitted type, the business reason for it, the requesting owner and the position taken on archives and container formats

title.en: Configure the email gateway to block file types outside the approved list

description.en: Set the gateway's filtering rules so that the approved list is what passes and everything else is blocked, rather than a block list of known-bad extensions that every new file type defeats by default. Where the product supports it, act on the detected file type rather than the extension alone. Decide and configure what happens to a blocked message — rejected, quarantined, or delivered with the attachment stripped — because the log analysis later reads that outcome and cannot interpret it otherwise. Attach the exported gateway configuration showing the rules in force and the date they were applied.

evidenceHint.en: Exported email gateway configuration showing the file-type filtering rules in force, whether detection is by extension or by content, the disposition applied to a blocked message and the date the rules were applied

title.en: Collect the gateway log of blocked and allowed file types for the period

description.en: Pull the gateway's own record of file-type decisions over the period: each message's file type, the verdict applied, the rule that produced it, the direction and the date. Keep both halves — the blocks evidence the filter working, and the allows are what the reconciliation reads to find a type passing that was never approved. Where the gateway retains logs for less than the review period, record that retention limit as a finding rather than presenting a shorter window as if it were complete. Attach the log extract for the period under test.

evidenceHint.en: Email gateway log extract for the period listing the file types blocked and allowed with the rule applied to each verdict, and a note of any retention limit that shortens the window

title.en: Reconcile the gateway configuration against the approved file-type list

description.en: Read the rules actually in force out of the gateway and set them beside the approved list line by line. Two failures are being looked for: a type the configuration permits that is not on the list, and a type on the list the configuration does not in fact permit — the second is what generates the exception requests that later erode the filter. Record a verdict per line and, for each mismatch, whether the configuration or the list is the thing that is wrong and who will correct it. Attach the comparison.

evidenceHint.en: Line-by-line comparison of the gateway's live filtering rules against the approved file-type list, each mismatch marked as a configuration error or a list error with a named owner

title.en: Review the gateway log for file types delivered that the approved list does not carry

description.en: Take the allowed half of the log extract, reduce it to the distinct file types actually delivered in the period, and check each against the approved list. A type delivered that is not on the list is the finding this control's success criteria turn on: the configuration and the list can agree with each other while a bypass rule, a per-sender exception or an unfiltered inbound path lets something else through entirely. Record how each unapproved delivery occurred and the corrective action taken. Attach the log analysis report.

evidenceHint.en: Log analysis report listing the distinct file types delivered in the period, each marked against the approved list, with the route and the corrective action recorded for every unapproved delivery

text.en: Reduce the allowed log entries to the distinct file types actually delivered.
Mark each delivered type present or absent from the approved file-type list.
For every absent type, trace the rule or path that let the message through.
Record the corrective action taken and the owner accountable for it.

controls.title: Logging Management
controls.objective: To ensure comprehensive logging of activities, exceptions, faults, and relevant events across all systems, and safeguard the integrity and confidentiality of log data.
controls.successCriteria:
All audited systems are logging events as per policy requirements, capturing necessary details.
Log data is securely stored, protected from unauthorized access or manipulation, and retained according to the defined policies.
Regular log reviews are conducted, with anomalies investigated and appropriately actioned.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Retrieve a current list of all logging systems and applications in use (from the IT Asset Inventory).
Obtain recent log files from a sample of critical systems (e.g., servers, network devices, applications).
Gather documentation on log configuration settings and log retention policies.
Collect evidence of log analysis activities, such as reports or summaries of log reviews.

Analysis:
Verify that each system's logs include necessary details such as user IDs, system activities, event times, device identities, network addresses, and protocols.
Assess the configuration settings against the logging policy to ensure compliance with data collection, storage, and protection requirements.
Examine log analysis reports to check for regular review, identification of anomalies, and follow-up actions.
Cross-reference log retention policies with actual log files to confirm adherence to retention schedules.

Output:
A report summarizing the logging configurations and practices of each audited system.
A compliance matrix comparing current practices against policy requirements.
Analysis reports of log reviews, highlighting any discrepancies or concerns.

title.en: Inventory every system, application and device required to log, with its log destination

description.en: The auditor's first request is the current list of logging systems and applications in use, and this inventory is the denominator every later task counts against — the compliance matrix scores each row, and the sampling test draws from it. Build it from the IT Asset Inventory rather than from the log platform's own source list, so a system producing no logs at all appears as a row with an empty destination instead of being invisible. For each row record the system owner, the class of system it is (server, network device, application, security tool), where its logs are written, and whether a copy is held anywhere other than the system that generated them. Attach the dated inventory; a row with a blank destination is a finding to carry forward, not a reason to drop the row.

evidenceHint.en: Dated logging scope inventory drawn from the IT Asset Inventory, one row per system with owner, system class and log destination populated

text.en: Extract the in-scope systems, applications and network devices from the IT Asset Inventory.
Record the owner and the system class on every row so the documented logging requirements can be applied by class.
Record where each system writes its logs and whether a copy is held off the system itself.
Mark the rows whose logs never leave local disk, and the rows producing no logs at all.
Date the inventory and hold it as the population the sampling test and the matrix both run against.

title.en: Record the mandatory log fields and retention period for each class of system

description.en: The documented logging requirements are the yardstick the compliance matrix scores against, so they have to name fields and durations rather than principles. For each system class in the inventory, record in the Logging and Monitoring Policy the events that must be logged — activities, exceptions and faults — and the fields every event must carry: user ID, the activity performed, the date and time of the event, the device identity, the network address and the protocol used. Against each class also record how long its logs are retained and where they are held. Where a class of system cannot emit one of the required fields, record that limitation and the compensating source that supplies it rather than quietly dropping the field from the requirement. Attach the issued policy version showing the mandatory-field table and the retention table.

evidenceHint.en: Issued Logging and Monitoring Policy version containing the mandatory-field table per system class and the retention period recorded against each class

title.en: Restrict and protect access to the log store so log data cannot be read or altered

description.en: Log data is evidence only while it is intact, so the store holding it has to be configured against tampering and against casual reading. Apply and record the access model: who may read logs, who may administer the platform, and that nobody may edit or delete an event before its retention period ends. Turn on whatever the platform offers to make that demonstrable — append-only or immutable storage, separation of the administrator role from the reviewer role, and the platform's own audit trail of who reached the log data. Attach the configuration export or screenshots showing the access lists, the retention setting and the tamper protection actually in force on the store.

evidenceHint.en: Log store configuration export showing the read and administer access lists, the retention setting, and the immutability or tamper-protection control in force

text.en: List the accounts and groups that can read logs and separate them from those that administer the platform.
Remove edit and delete rights over events still inside their retention period.
Enable the platform's own audit trail of who read or exported log data.
Export the resulting access lists and retention setting as the evidence for this task.

title.en: Review the logs on the defined cycle and record every anomaly with the action taken

description.en: On each review cycle the reviewer works through the sources in the inventory, records which were examined and over what period, and writes down each anomaly found — a run of failed authentications, an unexplained privilege change, a gap where a source stopped sending. Every anomaly carries the investigation performed, the conclusion reached, and the action taken or the reason none was needed, so the record shows the review happened rather than merely that it was scheduled. A cycle that found nothing is still written up naming the sources examined, because an empty finding list is evidence only when it is clear the logs were actually read. Attach the log review report for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Log review report for the period naming the sources examined, each anomaly found, its investigation, and the action taken or the reason none was needed

title.en: Test a sample of critical systems' live log output for the required fields and retention

description.en: Pull recent log files straight from a sample of critical systems — servers, network devices and applications — rather than from a dashboard summary, and read individual events to confirm each mandatory field the policy sets is actually populated: user ID, activity, event time, device identity, network address and protocol. In the same pass find the oldest event still retrievable from each sampled source and set it against the retention period the policy sets for that class, which is what shows retention is honoured rather than merely configured. Record per system which fields were present, which were empty, and what retention was observed. Attach the sampled log extracts alongside the results table.

evidenceHint.en: Field and retention test results per sampled system, with the raw log extracts they were read from and the oldest retrievable event date for each source

text.en: Draw the sample so that servers, network devices and applications are each represented.
Pull raw log files from each sampled system rather than a summary or dashboard view.
Read individual events and mark each mandatory field as present or empty.
Find the oldest event still retrievable and compare it with the retention period for that class.
Record the observed result per system and keep the extracts as the evidence behind it.

title.en: Assess every inventoried system's logging configuration against the policy in a compliance matrix

description.en: Take the inventory row by row and read each system's live logging configuration — what it collects, where it sends it, how long it keeps it and who can reach it — then score it against the Logging and Monitoring Policy in one matrix, a row per system and a column per policy requirement. Mark every cell compliant, partially compliant or non-compliant rather than leaving it blank, and give each non-compliant cell a named owner and a remediation date. The summary of this matrix is the report on the logging configuration and practices of each audited system that the control calls for. Attach the matrix together with the configuration outputs it was scored from.

evidenceHint.en: Logging compliance matrix scoring every inventoried system against each policy requirement, with an owner and a remediation date against each non-compliant cell

controls.title: Change Management Oversight
controls.objective: Ensure that all changes to information processing facilities and information systems adhere to the established change management procedures.
controls.successCriteria:
All changes to information processing facilities and information systems are fully documented, authorized, and comply with the established change management procedures.
Operating documentation and ICT continuity plans are updated in accordance with the changes made.
There are no instances of non-compliance or unauthorized changes.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain a comprehensive list of all information processing facilities and information systems.
Collect the complete record of change requests and change records since the last audit.
Acquire detailed documentation of change management procedures, including planning, authorization, testing, and implementation processes.

Analysis:
Verify that each change record includes planning, impact assessment, authorization, testing, and implementation details.
Assess whether changes communicated to relevant parties are in line with the change management procedures.
Examine the documentation for evidence of emergency and contingency planning, including fall-back procedures.
Ensure that operating documentation and ICT continuity plans have been updated as per the changes made.

Output:
A detailed report outlining the compliance of each change record with the change management procedures.
A summary of discrepancies or non-compliance issues, if any.
An updated list of all changes, categorizing them into minor, major, and emergency changes.

title.en: List every information processing facility and information system the change procedure covers

description.en: Compile the population the change procedure applies to: the information processing facilities and the information systems running on them, each with the owner accountable for changes to it and the change route it follows. Draw it from the systems actually in operation rather than from a project list, and mark any system deliberately outside the procedure with the approval that put it there. This list is the denominator the change-record test counts against, so a system missing from it is a system whose changes nobody will ever test. Attach the list with owner and change route populated for every row.

evidenceHint.en: List of information processing facilities and information systems in scope of the change procedure, each with its accountable owner and change route, and an approval recorded against any deliberate exclusion

title.en: Set out planning, impact assessment, authorisation, testing and implementation in the change procedure

description.en: Write the procedure so that a change record can be tested against it: what must be planned before a change is raised, what the impact assessment has to cover, who authorises a change at each category, what testing is required before implementation and what evidence of it is kept, and who must be told a change is happening. Name the authorising roles rather than individuals so the procedure survives a leaver. Every element listed here is one an auditor will look for in a sampled record, so an element the procedure does not require is one no record will carry. Attach the issued procedure.

evidenceHint.en: Issued change management procedure specifying the planning, impact assessment, authorisation, testing, implementation and communication requirements, with the authorising role named for each change category

title.en: Set out the emergency change route and the fall-back procedure for a change that fails

description.en: A change made at three in the morning to restore service still has to be recorded, so the procedure needs an emergency route that says who can authorise a change without the standard approval, what may be done under it, and how the record and the authorisation are completed after the fact. Alongside it, state the fall-back the standard route requires: what a change record must carry to describe how the change is reversed, who decides to invoke that reversal, and how far into the implementation the reversal remains possible. Attach the procedure section covering emergency changes and fall-back.

evidenceHint.en: Procedure section covering the emergency change route — its authoriser, its limits and how the record and authorisation are completed afterwards — and the fall-back detail every standard change record must carry

title.en: Record each change with its impact assessment, authorisation, test result and notification

description.en: Every change to a listed facility or system gets a record carrying the plan, the impact assessment, the authorisation with the authoriser named, the result of the testing performed, the implementation detail and the fall-back that applied. Record the notification actually sent to the affected parties with its date and recipients rather than assuming the ticket sufficed, because the procedure's communication requirement is tested against that evidence and nothing else. Where a change went through the emergency route, complete the record and the authorisation afterwards as the procedure requires and mark it as an emergency change. Attach the change records raised in the period.

evidenceHint.en: Change records for the period, each carrying the plan, impact assessment, named authoriser, test result, implementation detail, fall-back, and the notification sent to affected parties with its date and recipients

text.en: Raise the change record before implementation, carrying the plan and the systems it touches.
Complete the impact assessment, including the effect on dependent systems and on users.
Obtain and record the authorisation from the role the procedure names for that change category.
Record the testing performed and its result, attaching the output rather than summarising it.
Send the notification the procedure requires and record its date and recipients on the change.
Record the implementation detail and the fall-back that would have been used had it failed.

title.en: Update the operating documentation and ICT continuity plan affected by each implemented change

description.en: A change that alters how a system is run or recovered leaves two documents wrong until somebody corrects them. As part of closing each implemented change, revise the operating documentation — runbooks, procedures, configuration references — and the ICT continuity plan entries the change touches, and record the document version issued against the change record. Where a change touches neither, record that determination explicitly, because a blank is indistinguishable from a missed update when the record is read six months later. Attach the revised documents with the change reference they were issued under.

evidenceHint.en: Revised operating documentation and ICT continuity plan versions issued against implemented changes, each carrying its change reference, plus the explicit nil determination recorded for changes that touched neither

title.en: Test every change record since the last audit against the procedure and categorise it

description.en: Take the complete set of change records raised since the last audit and test each against the procedure: whether the planning is present, the impact assessment complete, the authorisation from the right role, the testing evidenced, the implementation recorded and the affected parties told. Categorise each change as minor, major or emergency so the population can be read by risk, and for emergency changes check the record and the authorisation were completed after the fact. Reconcile against the systems list to find changes made to a listed system with no record at all, which is the finding the record set by itself can never show. Attach the compliance report and the categorised change list with owners against each non-compliance.

evidenceHint.en: Change compliance report testing every record since the last audit against each procedure element, the change list categorised minor, major or emergency, and a summary of non-compliances and unrecorded changes with accountable owners

text.en: Pull the complete set of change records raised since the last audit.
Test each record for planning, impact assessment, authorisation, testing and implementation detail.
Categorise each change minor, major or emergency and check each emergency change carries its record and authorisation.
Reconcile the records against system change logs to find changes implemented with no record at all.
List every non-compliance with the record reference, the missing element and an accountable owner.

controls.title: Compliance Review Control
controls.objective: To ensure regular review of compliance with the organization's information security policy, specific policies, rules, and standards.
controls.successCriteria:
All aspects of the information security policy and specific policies are regularly reviewed and complied with.
Effective corrective actions are implemented in response to identified non-compliances.
Continuous improvement in the compliance review process with effective utilization of automatic tools, where applicable.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the latest versions of the organization’s information security policy and topic-specific policies.
Gather records of the previous compliance reviews, including any instances of non-compliance and corrective actions taken.
Collect reports of automatic measurement and reporting tools used for compliance review (if applicable).
Retrieve records of managerial actions taken in response to non-compliance, including corrective action plans and their outcomes.

Analysis:
Review the compliance review records to assess adherence to the information security policy and specific policies.
Examine instances of non-compliance to identify trends or recurring issues.
Evaluate the effectiveness of corrective actions taken in response to previous instances of non-compliance.
Assess the utilization and effectiveness of automatic measurement and reporting tools in the compliance review process.
Analyze managerial reports for thoroughness in addressing non-compliance and the efficacy of corrective actions.

Output:
A summary report detailing the findings of the compliance review.
A list of any current non-compliances and recommendations for corrective actions.
An evaluation report on the effectiveness of previously implemented corrective actions.
Recommendations for improvements in the compliance review process or policy adjustments, if needed.

title.en: Schedule each information security policy for compliance review with a named reviewer

description.en: Compliance review has no scope until the policies subject to it are listed. Take the information security policy and every topic-specific policy in force, and record against each the version in force, the part of the organisation it applies to, the person who will review compliance with it and how often that review happens. A policy in force but absent from this schedule is the one nobody reviews, so build the list from the policies actually issued rather than from the ones the reviewer already looks at. Attach the schedule; it is the population later review records are checked for completeness against.

evidenceHint.en: Compliance review schedule listing the information security policy and every topic-specific policy in force, each with its version, the area it covers, the named reviewer and the review frequency

title.en: Record which policy requirements an automated tool measures and which need a manual check

description.en: Work down the policies in the schedule and split their requirements into two sets: those an automated measurement or reporting tool already evidences — configuration baselines, patch state, access reports — and those only a person can check by reading records or observing practice. Name the tool and the specific report for each automated requirement, and the check and the expected evidence for each manual one. This mapping is what makes the review repeatable and what the control's expectation of automated tools is assessed against; the requirements landing in neither column are the ones nobody is in fact reviewing. Attach the mapping.

evidenceHint.en: Requirement-to-check mapping per policy naming, for each requirement, either the automated tool and report that measures it or the manual check and the evidence it produces, with unmapped requirements flagged

text.en: Break each policy in the schedule into the requirements a reviewer can test.
Mark the requirements an existing automated tool already measures.
Name the tool and the specific report evidencing each automated requirement.
Define the manual check and the evidence expected for every remaining requirement.
Flag requirements with neither an automated nor a manual check as a gap to close.

title.en: Review each policy against its mapped checks and record a result per requirement

description.en: At each scheduled review, work through the policy's requirements using the mapped tool report or manual check and record a compliant or non-compliant result for each, with the evidence relied on and the date it was examined. Record the requirements the reviewer could not test, and why, rather than leaving them unmarked — an unmarked requirement reads as compliant to everyone who sees the record afterwards, which is how a gap survives several cycles. The reviewer named in the schedule owns the record. Attach the completed review record for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Completed compliance review record per policy giving a compliant, non-compliant or not-tested result for every requirement, with the evidence examined and the date it was examined

title.en: Raise a corrective action with an owner and target date for every non-compliance the review recorded

description.en: Every non-compliant result becomes a corrective action carrying the requirement breached, the cause as far as it is understood, the action agreed, the accountable owner and the target date. Route to management the decisions an owner cannot take alone — resourcing, an accepted risk, a policy that no longer matches how the organisation actually works — and record what management decided. Hold the actions in one place across review cycles rather than inside each review document, because the recurrence analysis later needs them as a single set. Attach the corrective action plan with the management response recorded against it.

evidenceHint.en: Corrective action plan carrying, per non-compliance, the requirement breached, the cause, the action agreed, the accountable owner, the target date and the management response

title.en: Retest the policy requirement behind every closed corrective action to confirm the non-compliance has not returned

description.en: Take the corrective actions marked closed since the last cycle and test the requirement again rather than reading the closure note: the closure records that something was done, and this task establishes whether it worked. Record for each the requirement, the action taken, the retest result, and a verdict of effective, ineffective, or effective only while a temporary measure holds. Reopen the ineffective ones against the same owner instead of raising them as fresh findings, so their history stays attached. Attach the retest results.

evidenceHint.en: Retest results for every corrective action closed since the last cycle, giving the requirement, the action taken, the retest outcome and an effective, ineffective or temporary verdict

title.en: Evaluate non-compliances across review cycles for recurring issues and report them to management

description.en: Set this cycle's non-compliances against previous cycles' and identify what keeps returning — the same requirement, the same part of the organisation, or the same cause surfacing under different requirements. A requirement that fails every cycle and is corrected every cycle is evidence of a policy that does not fit the organisation or a control that is not sustainable, and reporting it as a fresh finding each time is how that stays hidden. Put the recurring items to management with a recommendation: change the policy, change the control, or accept the risk. Attach the trend analysis and the report issued.

evidenceHint.en: Trend analysis across review cycles naming each recurring non-compliance, its frequency and its cause, with the recommendation put to management and the decision management took

controls.title: Audit Log Retention Compliance
controls.objective: Ensure that audit logs across all enterprise assets are retained for a minimum of 90 days to comply with regulatory and organizational standards.
controls.successCriteria:
All enterprise assets are configured to retain logs for at least 90 days.
Sampled log entries demonstrate compliance with the 90-day retention period.
Log integrity and confidentiality are adequately maintained.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain an inventory of all enterprise assets (servers, workstations, network devices, applications, etc.).
Collect configuration settings or reports from logging mechanisms (like SIEM systems) to verify log retention settings.
Gather a sample of log entries from various systems to verify the earliest log entry date.

Analysis:
For each asset, verify that log retention settings are configured to retain logs for at least 90 days.
Examine the sample log entries to ensure logs cover the required retention period.
Review system configurations to ensure that log integrity and confidentiality are maintained during the retention period.

Output:
Configuration reports or screenshots showing log retention settings.
Spreadsheet or report detailing log entry dates for each sampled system.
Documentation of log integrity and confidentiality measures.

title.en: Inventory every enterprise asset that generates audit logs

description.en: Build one row per enterprise asset in scope — servers, workstations, network devices and applications — and against each record the logging mechanism it uses, the destination its logs are written to (local disk, syslog collector, SIEM index) and the owner who can produce a configuration export for it. An asset that generates logs nowhere is still a row: the blank destination is the finding. This inventory is the denominator the retention check, the sampling test and the reconciliation all count against, so a class of asset missing here is a class of asset never tested. Attach the inventory carrying the date it was compiled.

evidenceHint.en: Dated inventory of enterprise assets with, per row, the asset type, the logging mechanism, the log destination and the named owner

text.en: Enumerate servers, workstations, network devices and applications from the asset register and the log collector's own source list.
Record for each asset the logging mechanism in use and whether it writes locally, to a collector or to the SIEM.
Name the owner able to produce a configuration export and a log sample for that asset.
Mark assets that generate no audit log at all so the gap is visible rather than absent.

title.en: Set every asset's log retention to at least 90 days and export the setting

description.en: Work down the inventory and, on each asset or on the collector that holds its logs, set the retention period to 90 days or longer, then export the setting as it now reads rather than as it was intended — a screenshot or configuration report per asset or per SIEM index is what the auditor asks for. Where retention is governed centrally, one export covering the indices is enough provided it names the assets it applies to. Where an asset cannot be configured to 90 days, record the maximum it supports and refer the shortfall to that asset's owner with the gap stated in days. Attach the configuration reports together with the list of assets each one covers.

evidenceHint.en: Configuration reports or screenshots showing the retention period configured for each asset or SIEM index, with the assets each report covers

title.en: Document the integrity and confidentiality measures protecting logs in retention

description.en: Separately from the retention setting, record what stops a retained log being read or altered before its 90 days elapse: who holds read access to the store, which accounts can delete or modify entries, whether write-once or immutability is enabled, and how logs are protected in transit from the asset to the collector. Name the measure per log store rather than describing the principle once, because the store with no answer is what this task exists to surface. Attach the documentation of integrity and confidentiality measures with the access list it rests on.

evidenceHint.en: Documentation of log integrity and confidentiality measures per log store, naming access holders, deletion and modification rights, immutability settings and transport protection

title.en: Record the earliest available log entry date for each sampled system

description.en: Draw a sample across the inventory covering every asset class, and on each sampled system query the oldest audit log entry that can still be retrieved. Capture the system, the date of that earliest entry, the number of days it is from today, and a pass or fail against the 90-day floor. Read the age from the log store itself rather than from the retention setting — a system configured for 90 days holding only 14 days of entries because rotation or forwarding is failing is precisely the case a configuration export cannot show. Attach the completed sheet, with a remediation owner named against every fail.

evidenceHint.en: Sampling sheet with one row per sampled system giving the earliest retrievable log entry date, the days of coverage, a pass or fail against 90 days and an owner for each fail

text.en: Draw the sample so every asset class in the inventory is represented at least once.
Query each sampled system's log store for the oldest entry still retrievable.
Record the earliest entry date and compute its age in days from the test date.
Mark pass or fail against the 90-day floor and note the cause where a system fails.
Name a remediation owner and target date against every failing system.

title.en: Reconcile the configured retention against the log coverage actually observed

description.en: Put the configuration exports and the sampling results side by side and report, per asset, whether what is configured and what is held agree. The disagreements are the finding: an asset configured to 90 days holding 14, an asset absent from the collector entirely, an asset whose retention was never set. Give each disagreement a cause and an accountable owner, and carry the unresolved ones into the report's conclusion so the next cycle starts from them. Attach the reconciliation with the configuration exports and the sampling sheet it was derived from.

evidenceHint.en: Reconciliation report listing every inventoried asset with its configured retention, its observed log coverage, an agree or deviate verdict and an owner for each deviation

controls.title: Unauthorized Asset Management
controls.objective: To ensure that all assets on the network are authorized and compliant with company policies. Unauthorized assets should be identified and addressed on a weekly basis.
controls.successCriteria:
All unauthorized assets are accurately identified and reported.
Each unauthorized asset is assessed for risk and appropriate action is taken (e.g., removal from the network, denial of remote access, or quarantine).
Documentation of actions taken for each unauthorized asset is maintained.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain a current inventory list of all network-connected assets.
Run a network scan to identify all connected assets.
Obtain logs of network access and security alerts related to unauthorized assets.

Analysis:
Compare the network scan results with the inventory list to identify unauthorized assets.
Analyze network access logs and security alerts to confirm any unauthorized asset activity.
Determine the status (active/inactive) and risk level of each identified unauthorized asset.

Output:
A report listing all unauthorized assets identified during the scan.
A log analysis report highlighting unauthorized asset activities.
A risk assessment report for each unauthorized asset.

title.en: Mark the authorisation status of every asset on the network-connected inventory

description.en: A scan can only reveal an unauthorised asset if the inventory says what authorised means, so work the current inventory of network-connected assets and give each row an explicit authorised or not-authorised status. Populate the identifying attribute the scan will actually match on — the hardware address in most cases — because a comparison run on names or asset tags reports differences that are only naming differences, and a weekly list of those trains everyone to ignore it. Attach the inventory with a status on every row and the count of rows still unmarked.

evidenceHint.en: Network-connected asset inventory carrying an authorised or not-authorised status on every row, the scan-matching attribute populated, and the count of rows still unmarked

title.en: Set the action each risk level triggers for an unauthorised asset

description.en: Decide in advance what happens to an unauthorised asset at each risk level, so the weekly response is a decision already made rather than one argued afresh each time: which findings lead to removal from the network, which to denial of remote access, and which to quarantine. Write the standard against the risk levels the assessment actually assigns, so every level the weekly pass can produce has a response mapped to it — a level with no mapped action is where the list stops being acted on. Attach the issued response standard.

evidenceHint.en: Issued unauthorised asset response standard mapping every risk level the assessment can assign to removal from the network, denial of remote access or quarantine

title.en: Run the weekly network scan and list the assets the inventory does not authorise

description.en: Scan the network each week for connected assets and set the results against the authorised inventory, matching on the identifying attribute the inventory carries. Produce the report the audit asks for: one row per asset present on the network with no authorised inventory entry, giving its addresses, the segment it was seen on, and the date and time it was observed. Record the scan's own coverage — the ranges actually scanned — beside the results, because an asset sitting on an unscanned range is not an absence of unauthorised assets. Attach the weekly unauthorised asset report.

evidenceHint.en: Weekly unauthorised asset report listing each asset found on the network with no authorised inventory entry, its addresses, segment and observation time, alongside the address ranges the scan actually covered

text.en: Run the scan across the ranges the network is known to use, recording the ranges covered.
Match each discovered asset to the inventory on its hardware address.
List every asset with no authorised inventory entry, with its addresses and segment.
Record the date and time each unauthorised asset was observed on the network.
Report the scan coverage beside the results so unscanned ranges stay visible.

title.en: Confirm each unauthorised asset's activity from the network access logs and security alerts

description.en: For every asset on the week's unauthorised list, pull what the network access logs and security alerts say about it: when it connected, what it reached, how much traffic it carried, and whether an alert had already fired on it. This is what separates a device that appeared briefly from one that has been operating unnoticed for months, and it is the input the risk assessment reads. Where the logs hold nothing at all for an asset, record that as an absence of evidence rather than as inactivity — they are different findings. Attach the log analysis report.

evidenceHint.en: Log analysis report covering each unauthorised asset found, giving its connection times, the systems it reached, any alerts raised on it, and an explicit note where the logs held no record of it at all

title.en: Assess and record the status and risk level of every unauthorised asset found

description.en: Give each unauthorised asset a status — active or inactive on the network — and a risk level reasoned from what the log analysis showed: what the device reached, whether it holds or could reach sensitive information, and whether it is attributable to a known holder. State the reasoning in a line against each asset rather than the level alone, because the level selects the response and an unexplained level is the one that gets argued down when the response is inconvenient. Attach the risk assessment covering every asset on the week's list.

evidenceHint.en: Risk assessment covering every unauthorised asset found, giving its active or inactive status, its assigned risk level and the one-line reasoning that produced that level

title.en: Reconcile every unauthorised asset found against the action recorded to close it

description.en: Put the unauthorised assets identified across the period's weekly passes against the actions actually recorded — removed from the network, remote access denied, or quarantined — with the date each took effect and who performed it. Report the assets still open, how long they have been open, and why. This is what evidences that unauthorised assets are addressed rather than merely listed each week, and the age of the open items is the figure that shows whether the weekly cadence is real or nominal. Attach the reconciliation with the action records behind it.

evidenceHint.en: Reconciliation of every unauthorised asset identified in the period against the action taken, its effective date and the operator who applied it, with the still-open assets listed by age and reason

text.en: Collect the unauthorised assets identified across every weekly pass in the period.
Match each to the action record that closed it and the date the action took effect.
List the assets with no action recorded, and how long each has been open.
Record the reason each open item remains open and who is accountable for closing it.

controls.title: ISMS Review and Monitoring
controls.objective: Validate the effectiveness and updates of the ISMS.
controls.successCriteria: ISMS is regularly reviewed, audited, and updated as necessary.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence: 
Records of internal audits, ISMS reviews, and related findings. 
Changes or updates made to the ISMS documentation. 

Analysis: 
Evaluate the frequency and results of audits and reviews. 

Output: 
Overview of ISMS performance and areas of improvement.

title.en: Log each completed internal audit and ISMS review with the findings it raised

description.en: As each audit or review is held, record the date it took place, the scope actually covered, who conducted it, the participants where it was a review, and every finding raised with its severity and the owner who accepted it. Attach the audit report or the review minutes themselves rather than a summary: the finding text is what later tasks track to closure, and a summary loses the detail that makes a finding actionable.

evidenceHint.en: Internal audit reports and ISMS review minutes for the period, each showing date, scope, participants and the findings raised with severity and owner

text.en: Record the date, scope and conductor of each audit or review held.
Attach the audit report or the management review minutes as issued.
List each finding raised with its severity and the owner accepting it.

title.en: Record every change to the ISMS documentation against the finding that drove it

description.en: Keep a change log for the ISMS document set: per amended document, the version before and after, the date, the person who authorised the change, and the audit finding, review action or external development that prompted it. This is what evidences that the ISMS is updated as necessary rather than merely reviewed — a review cycle that raises findings and changes nothing is the failure mode this record makes visible. Where a finding was closed without any documentation change, record that decision and its rationale against the finding rather than leaving the absence unexplained. Attach the change log covering the period.

evidenceHint.en: ISMS documentation change log for the period showing document, version before and after, date, authoriser and the finding or trigger that drove each change

title.en: Evaluate the frequency and the results of the period's audits and reviews

description.en: Take the dates of the audits and reviews held and calculate, per ISMS area, the interval between each one and the previous cycle covering that area — that interval is what the control means by frequency, and it is the number an assessor recalculates rather than takes on trust. Alongside it, record what each audit or review actually produced: findings raised, findings closed, and areas examined and found sound. Where an ISMS area shows no audit or review in the period at all, record it as uncovered rather than omitting it, because an area nobody looked at reads identically to one with nothing to report. Attach the evaluation with the audit records and review minutes behind it.

evidenceHint.en: Frequency and results evaluation giving, per ISMS area, the dates of the audits and reviews held, the interval between successive cycles, the findings each produced, and the areas with no coverage in the period

text.en: Group the period's audits and reviews by the ISMS area each covered.
Calculate the interval between each cycle and the one before it.
Record the findings each audit or review raised and which were closed.
List every ISMS area with no audit or review during the period.

title.en: Publish an overview of ISMS performance and the improvement areas it identifies

description.en: Draw the period's audit findings, review outcomes and documentation changes into the overview this control outputs: what the ISMS is doing well, where findings cluster, which findings remain open and how old they are, and the improvement areas management is being asked to act on. Name an accountable owner against each improvement area, because an overview whose improvements carry none is a description rather than a monitoring output. Attach the issued overview.

evidenceHint.en: Issued ISMS performance overview covering findings raised and closed, the age of open findings and the improvement areas with an accountable owner named against each

text.en: Summarise the findings raised, closed and still open across the period.
Show the age of each open finding against the date it was raised.
Identify where findings cluster by ISMS area or by common root cause.
Name an accountable owner for each improvement area proposed.

controls.title: Disclosure Record-Keeping and Monitoring
controls.objective: To ensure complete, accurate, and timely records of authorized and unauthorized disclosures of personal information.
controls.successCriteria:
All authorized disclosures are accurately and completely recorded and comply with internal policies.
Records of unauthorized disclosures are complete, timely, and aligned with incident reports.
The organization's record-keeping practices meet data protection regulatory requirements.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the record logs of all disclosures of personal information.
Access incident reports related to unauthorized disclosures or breaches.
Gather policy documents regarding disclosure procedures and incident response.

Analysis:
Cross-check the disclosure logs against internal policies to verify authorized disclosures.
Review incident reports to assess the accuracy and completeness of unauthorized disclosure records.
Compare records with data protection regulations to ensure compliance in record-keeping.

Output:
A comprehensive report on all recorded disclosures of personal information.
Analysis summary of incident reports and response effectiveness.
Compliance assessment with internal and regulatory standards.

title.en: List every route by which personal information is disclosed outside the organisation

description.en: A record of all disclosures is only complete if the ways personal information can leave are known, so start there: regulatory and law-enforcement requests, data subject access responses, disclosures to processors and suppliers, transfers to group companies, customer and partner integrations, marketing lists, and the ad hoc routes — an emailed spreadsheet, a support attachment — that carry personal information out without any system boundary being crossed. For each route record the recipient type, the data categories it carries, the authorising basis the disclosure procedure requires for it, and the log in which a disclosure made by that route is recorded. A route with no log is the gap this task exists to surface. Attach the completed route list.

evidenceHint.en: List of disclosure routes with recipient type, data categories, the authorising basis required and the log that records disclosures made by that route

text.en: Enumerate routes from the processing record, the supplier register and the integration inventory.
Add the ad hoc routes: emailed extracts, support attachments and printed material.
Add the statutory routes: regulator, law enforcement and court-ordered disclosures.
Record the authorising basis the disclosure procedure requires for each route.
Name the log each route writes to, and mark the routes that write to none.

title.en: Set the fields every disclosure record must carry in the disclosure procedure

description.en: Fix in the procedure itself what a disclosure entry must contain to satisfy both the internal policy and the data protection record-keeping obligations the organisation is subject to: the date of the disclosure, the route and the recipient, the data categories and the number of records or individuals involved, the purpose, the lawful basis or authorising instrument, who approved it and when, and how the information was transferred. Add the fields an unauthorised disclosure needs on top of those — the date it occurred, the date it was discovered, and the reference of the incident report raised for it. Legal/DPO confirms the field set against the applicable regulation. Attach the issued procedure version showing the required field set for authorised and unauthorised disclosures alike.

evidenceHint.en: Issued disclosure procedure version setting the required record fields for authorised and unauthorised disclosures, naming the record-keeping requirement each field satisfies

title.en: Record every authorised disclosure of personal information in the disclosure log as it is made

description.en: Whoever makes a disclosure completes the log entry as part of making it, populating the fields the procedure sets and attaching or referencing the authorisation that permitted it — the approval, the contract clause, the data subject's own request or the statutory instrument. A disclosure made under a standing arrangement, such as a recurring supplier feed, is logged once against that arrangement with the period it covers rather than being left out because it is routine. Attach the disclosure log extract for the period with the authorisation reference populated on every entry.

evidenceHint.en: Disclosure log extract for the period with every entry carrying the recipient, data categories, record counts, purpose, authorising basis and approver

title.en: Record every unauthorised disclosure in the log and link it to its incident report

description.en: An unauthorised disclosure is entered in the same log as soon as it is discovered, carrying the incident report reference so the two records can be read together, and it stays open until the incident closes. Record the date the disclosure occurred and the date it was discovered separately — the gap between them is what the timeliness test reads — together with the data categories and the number of individuals affected as known at the time and as revised when the investigation finishes. Where the incident report and the log entry disagree on scope, the entry records the revision rather than being overwritten. Attach the unauthorised disclosure entries for the period with their incident report references.

evidenceHint.en: Unauthorised disclosure entries for the period, each linked to its incident report and showing the occurrence date, the discovery date, the data categories and the individuals affected

title.en: Cross-check the disclosure log against the procedure and report the authorisation exceptions

description.en: Take the period's authorised entries and test each against the disclosure procedure: was the route one the procedure permits, was the authorising basis the one it requires for that route, was the approval given by somebody empowered to give it and given before the disclosure was made, and are the mandatory fields populated. Then work the check in the other direction across a sample of routes — pull the traffic each route actually carried and look for disclosures with no log entry at all, because a log tested only against itself cannot show what is missing from it. Attach the report on recorded disclosures with every exception listed, each carrying an owner and a remediation date.

evidenceHint.en: Report on recorded disclosures testing each entry against the procedure, listing unauthorised, unapproved or incomplete entries and any disclosure found with no log entry, each with an owner

text.en: Test each entry's route and authorising basis against what the procedure requires.
Confirm the approval was recorded before the disclosure was made and by an empowered approver.
Check the mandatory fields are populated on every entry in the period.
Sample the routes and look for disclosures the log never received.
List each exception with a named owner and a date to clear it.

title.en: Reconcile the incident reports against the unauthorised disclosure entries and report the delays and gaps

description.en: Set the period's privacy incident reports beside the unauthorised disclosure entries and match them both ways: an incident involving personal information with no corresponding log entry, and a log entry with no incident report behind it. For each matched pair compare the data categories, the individuals affected and the dates the two records carry, and record every disagreement. Measure the interval between discovery and the entry being recorded so the timeliness of the record-keeping is stated as a number rather than asserted. Attach the analysis summary with the matched-pair working and every unmatched item named.

evidenceHint.en: Reconciliation of incident reports to unauthorised disclosure entries, listing unmatched items both ways, the discovery-to-record interval per case and every disagreement in scope or dates

controls.title: Audit Testing Security Control
controls.objective: To ensure that audit testing of information systems is conducted securely, minimizing the risk to operational integrity and confidentiality.
controls.successCriteria:
All audit tests are conducted within the agreed scope and access limitations.
Devices used for audit purposes meet established security requirements.
Auditor access to systems and data is appropriately monitored and logged.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain a schedule of planned audit tests, including details of the systems and data to be accessed.
Collect written agreements between auditors and management regarding the scope and access level of audit tests.
Get evidence of security measures for devices used in audits (e.g., antivirus status, patch levels).
Acquire copies of logs recording auditor access to systems and data.

Analysis:
Verify that the scope of each audit test matches the agreed terms.
Confirm that auditor access to systems and data is appropriately limited (e.g., read-only access, use of isolated copies of system files).
Check that security requirements for devices used in audits are met.
Review logs to ensure that auditor access is properly monitored and recorded.

Output:
A report detailing the adherence of each audit test to the agreed terms.
Verification documentation for the security status of devices used in audits.
A comprehensive log review report.

title.en: Schedule the planned audit tests with the systems and data each will access

description.en: Before testing begins, produce the schedule naming each planned audit test, the auditor or team performing it, the window it runs in, and precisely which systems and which data it will reach. Derive the systems and data from what the test actually requires rather than from a general grant, because this schedule is the baseline the completed tests are later compared against and an over-broad entry here licenses over-broad access. Attach the schedule as agreed with the auditors, showing a system and data list against every planned test.

evidenceHint.en: Audit test schedule listing each planned test with its auditor, its window, and the systems and data it will access

title.en: Agree the scope and access limitations of each audit test in writing with management

description.en: For every test on the schedule, put in writing what the auditor may do and how far their access extends: read-only rather than change access, work against isolated copies of system files where that is the arrangement, the accounts to be used, and the period the access is open for. The agreement is signed by the auditor and by the manager accountable for the systems in scope before any access is granted, so the terms exist independently of the test that will be measured against them. Attach the signed agreements, one per scheduled test.

evidenceHint.en: Written agreements between the auditors and management, one per test, stating the scope, the access level granted and the period it is open

text.en: State the systems and data in scope for the test, taken from its schedule entry.
Fix the access level: read-only, change access, or work against isolated copies of system files.
Name the accounts the auditor will use and the window in which they are enabled.
Record any system or dataset explicitly excluded from the test.
Have the auditor and the accountable manager sign before any access is granted.

title.en: Record the security state of every device used for audit testing before the test begins

description.en: Each device an auditor connects with — laptop, appliance or virtual machine — is checked before access is enabled and the check is written down: the device identifier, its owner, the antivirus product and whether it is running with current definitions, and the patch level of the operating system and tooling. Where a device does not meet the requirement, record what was done about it — remediated, replaced, or the test deferred — rather than leaving the row open. After the fact this record is the only proof that the device state was known at the time. Attach the device verification records covering the tests carried out in the period.

evidenceHint.en: Device verification record per audit device showing the identifier, owner, antivirus status, patch level and the disposition of any device that failed the check

title.en: Log auditor access to systems and data for the duration of each test

description.en: Enable and retain logging on the accounts and systems named in each agreement so auditor activity is recorded while the test runs: the account used, the system and data reached, the timestamps and the actions performed. Where the auditor works against isolated copies of system files, log access to those copies too, since that is where the data actually was. Confirm at the close of each test that the logs covering its window were captured and stored before the accounts are disabled. Attach the access log extract covering each test carried out in the period.

evidenceHint.en: Auditor access log extract per test showing the account, the system and data reached, the timestamps and the actions performed within the test window

title.en: Compare each completed audit test against the scope and access limitations agreed for it

description.en: For every test that ran in the period, set what the access logs show actually happened against what the signed agreement permitted: systems reached inside or outside scope, the access level exercised against the level granted, work done against isolated copies where that was the agreed arrangement, and activity inside or outside the agreed window. Record a conforming or exception verdict per test and describe each exception in full, naming the manager it was referred to. Attach the adherence report with the agreements and log extracts it was built from.

evidenceHint.en: Adherence report scoring each completed audit test against its written agreement, with every exception described and referred to a named manager

text.en: List the tests that ran in the period and pull the agreement signed for each.
Set the systems and data the logs show were reached against those the agreement named.
Check the access level actually exercised against the level the agreement granted.
Confirm the activity fell inside the agreed window and used the named accounts.
Describe every exception found and name the manager it was referred to.

title.en: Review the auditor access logs for completeness across every test on the schedule

description.en: Monitoring is only as good as its coverage, so examine the logs themselves rather than what they contain: every test on the schedule has an access log covering its full window, the log names the auditor account that was used, and no gap in the record coincides with a period the test was running. Record per test whether the log was complete, partial or absent, and raise a logging change with a named owner wherever a system could not produce a usable record. Attach the log review report.

evidenceHint.en: Log review report recording, per scheduled test, whether auditor access was logged completely, partially or not at all, with a named owner against each logging gap

controls.title: Email Authentication and Verification
controls.objective: Ensure the organization's email system adheres to DMARC, SPF, and DKIM standards to mitigate risks associated with spoofed or modified emails.
controls.successCriteria:
SPF, DKIM, and DMARC configurations are accurately implemented as per organizational standards.
Email traffic log analysis shows a reduction in spoofed or unauthorized email activities.
Email security policies and procedures are consistently followed and documented.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain a current configuration report of the email system.
Gather DNS records showing SPF, DKIM, and DMARC configurations.
Collect recent email traffic logs for analysis.
Retrieve documented email security policies and procedures.

Analysis:
Verify that SPF records are correctly set up in DNS to authenticate outbound emails from the organization's domain.
Ensure DKIM signatures are applied on outbound emails, and the corresponding DKIM DNS records are properly configured.
Check that DMARC policies are defined in DNS and align with organizational security policies, particularly for handling failed email authentications.
Review email traffic logs to identify instances of email spoofing or authentication failures and assess the effectiveness of the DMARC policy.

Output:
Report on SPF, DKIM, and DMARC configuration settings.
Analysis of email traffic logs with identified spoofing or authentication issues.
Compliance assessment report with email security policies and procedures.

title.en: Register every domain and sending service that emits email for the organisation

description.en: SPF, DKIM and DMARC are published per domain, so the configuration cannot be assessed until the domains and the services sending on their behalf are written down. Take the organisation's registered domains — including parked and legacy ones, which are spoofed precisely because nobody sends from them and nobody watches them — and against each list the platforms that send: the mail system itself, marketing tools, ticketing and billing systems, and any application sending transactional mail. Record the owner of each sending service. Attach the list; it is the row set the DNS records and the traffic analysis are both read against.

evidenceHint.en: List of every registered domain, parked and legacy ones included, with the sending services authorised to send from each and the named owner of each service

title.en: Publish an SPF record for each sending domain authorising only its known senders

description.en: For every domain on the list, publish an SPF record naming the sending services identified for it and no others, closed with a policy telling receivers what to do with anything else. Domains that send nothing get a record authorising nothing, which is the whole of the protection available to them. Watch the DNS lookup limit as services are added, because an SPF record that exceeds it fails to evaluate and produces the same practical result as having none at all. Attach the DNS record export showing the published SPF for every domain on the list.

evidenceHint.en: DNS export of the SPF record published for every listed domain, showing the authorised senders and the closing policy, including the authorise-nothing records on non-sending domains

title.en: Enable DKIM signing on outbound mail and publish the matching selector records

description.en: Turn on DKIM signing at each sending service on the list and publish that selector's public key in DNS for the domain it signs for. Confirm on a real message from each service that a signature is present and verifies against the published key, rather than relying on the service's own configuration page — a service configured to sign but sending unsigned is invisible until a receiver reports it. Record the selector, the key length and the rotation position for each service. Attach the DNS export together with the verified message headers.

evidenceHint.en: DKIM selector DNS records per sending service, plus message headers captured from each service showing a signature that validates against the published key

text.en: Enable DKIM signing at each sending service identified for the domain.
Publish the selector's public key in DNS for the domain being signed for.
Send a message through each service and capture the resulting headers.
Confirm the signature verifies against the published key, not merely that it is present.
Record the selector, key length and rotation position for each sending service.

title.en: Publish the DMARC policy and reporting addresses in DNS in line with the email security policy

description.en: Publish a DMARC record on each domain declaring how a receiver should treat a message that fails authentication, and set that treatment to what the documented email security policy requires rather than to whatever is safest to deploy — the gap between those two is the finding a reviewer looks for here. Include the aggregate reporting address so the reports receivers generate arrive somewhere the later review can read them alongside the traffic logs. Record the alignment mode chosen and the reason. Attach the DNS export for every domain on the list.

evidenceHint.en: DMARC DNS record export for every listed domain showing the published policy, the alignment mode and the reporting addresses, set beside the treatment the documented email security policy requires

title.en: Review the DMARC aggregate reports and mail traffic logs for authentication failures

description.en: Each period, read the DMARC aggregate reports and the email traffic logs together and work through what failed authentication: the source that sent it, the domain it sent for, whether it failed SPF, DKIM or alignment, and what the receiver did with it. Separate the two populations that look identical in the data — a legitimate service the organisation forgot to authorise, which is fixed by correcting the records, and a third party spoofing the domain, which is what the policy exists to stop. Record a disposition against each source. Attach the analysis for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Period analysis of DMARC aggregate reports and mail traffic logs listing each failing source, the domain it sent for, the check it failed, the receiver's action, and its disposition as an unauthorised legitimate sender or as spoofing

title.en: Assess the live SPF, DKIM and DMARC configuration against the email security policy

description.en: Query the published records for every domain on the list and set the observed values beside what the documented email security policy and procedures require, producing the compliance assessment this control asks for. Read DNS directly rather than the change ticket that was supposed to have applied it. Give each domain a pass or deviation verdict per mechanism and, for every deviation, the accountable owner and the agreed correction — including domains on the list carrying no record at all, which a configuration report organised by sending service will never surface. Attach the assessment with the raw query output behind it.

evidenceHint.en: Email authentication compliance assessment giving a pass or deviation verdict per domain for SPF, DKIM and DMARC against the documented policy, with the raw DNS query output and an owner named against each deviation

controls.title: Utility Protection and Resilience
controls.objective: To ensure that information processing facilities are adequately protected from disruptions caused by utility failures, including power, telecommunications, and other essential services.
controls.successCriteria:
All utility support equipment is configured, operated, and maintained as per manufacturer specifications.
Regular maintenance and inspection of utility support equipment are conducted and documented.
Effective network segregation is in place for utility support systems.
Emergency response plans are comprehensive, up-to-date, and effective in handling utility disruptions.
Redundant and diverse utility feeds are implemented where necessary for critical utilities.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain a detailed inventory of all utility support equipment (e.g., generators, UPS, HVAC systems) used in the information processing facilities.
Acquire maintenance and inspection records for the utility support equipment.
Gather documentation on the configuration and network segregation of utility support systems.
Collect evidence of the implementation of diverse utility feeds, where applicable.
Obtain emergency response plans, including details of emergency lighting, communication systems, and location of emergency cut-off switches and valves.

Analysis:
Assess the inventory of utility support equipment against manufacturer specifications for proper configuration, operation, and maintenance.
Review the maintenance and inspection records to verify regular and appropriate servicing of the utility support equipment.
Examine the documentation on network segregation to ensure utility equipment is appropriately separated from the information processing network.
Analyze the implementation of diverse utility feeds for redundancy and resilience.
Evaluate the emergency response plans for completeness and effectiveness in handling utility disruptions.

Output:
A report detailing the status of utility support equipment and their compliance with manufacturer specifications.
A compliance checklist against the regular maintenance and inspection of utility support equipment.
A review report on network segregation and security measures for utility support systems.
An evaluation report of emergency response plans and redundancy measures.

title.en: Inventory every generator, UPS, HVAC unit and other utility support equipment

description.en: List each item of utility support equipment serving the information processing facilities — generators, UPS units, HVAC plant, fuel stores, and water and telecommunications terminations — and against each row record the make and model, the facility and room it serves, the manufacturer's specified operating configuration and the servicing interval the manufacturer states. The manufacturer columns are not background: they are the yardstick the maintenance log and the compliance assessment are both read against, so a row with no specification reference cannot be assessed later and is not finished. Attach the dated inventory together with the specification sheets it was populated from.

evidenceHint.en: Dated utility support equipment inventory, one row per item, giving make and model, the facility served, the manufacturer's specified configuration and the stated servicing interval, with the specification sheets attached

text.en: Walk each facility and list every generator, UPS, HVAC unit, fuel store and utility termination serving it.
Record the make, model and serial number of each item, and the room or plant area it occupies.
Record which information processing facility each item supports, so a failure traces to what it takes down.
Cite the manufacturer specification for each item and copy its stated servicing interval into the row.
Date the inventory and hold it as the population the maintenance log and the assessment both run against.

title.en: Document how utility support systems are segregated from the information processing network

description.en: Utility plant carries its own management interfaces — UPS network cards, generator controllers, HVAC building-management systems — and the control asks for these to sit apart from the network carrying information processing. Produce the documentation an auditor asks for: for every managed utility item in the inventory, the VLAN or physical segment it sits on, the addresses it can reach and be reached from, and the firewall or access-list rule that enforces the boundary. Where an item is unmanaged and carries no network interface, record that explicitly so it is not mistaken for an omission. Attach the segregation documentation with the rule extracts backing it.

evidenceHint.en: Network segregation documentation for utility support systems giving segment, addressing and the enforcing firewall or access-list rule per managed item, and an explicit nil against each unmanaged item

title.en: Record the redundant and diverse feed arrangement for each critical utility

description.en: For every utility the facilities depend on — power, telecommunications, water, cooling — record whether a second feed exists, whether it is genuinely diverse (a separate supplier, a separate physical route into the building, a separate substation or exchange) or merely a duplicate of the same path, and which critical facility each feed serves. A single feed is a legitimate answer where the availability requirement does not call for more; what is not legitimate is leaving it unstated. Flag every critical utility on a single or duplicated-path feed and name the owner carrying that risk. Attach the record with the supply contracts or route diagrams that evidence the diversity claimed.

evidenceHint.en: Utility feed record naming, per critical utility, the number of feeds, the supplier and physical route of each, whether the diversity is genuine or duplicated, and the flagged single-feed utilities with a named risk owner

title.en: Set out emergency lighting, communications and cut-off locations in the emergency response plan
