description.en: The emergency response plan has to be usable by somebody standing in a dark plant room, so it must name locations rather than principles: where the emergency lighting covers and how long it runs, which communication system is used when the primary telephony is down and who answers it, and the exact location of every emergency power cut-off switch and water, gas or fuel shut-off valve. Record who is authorised to operate each cut-off and how they are reached out of hours. Walk the locations to confirm the plan matches the building as it stands rather than as it was built. Attach the issued plan with the floor markings or photographs that fix each cut-off location.

evidenceHint.en: Issued emergency response plan showing emergency lighting coverage and rated runtime, the fallback communication system and its responder, and a located list of every emergency cut-off switch and shut-off valve with its authorised operator

text.en: Record the emergency lighting coverage per area and the runtime the units are rated for.
Name the communication system used when primary telephony fails, and who is on the other end of it.
Locate every emergency power cut-off switch and fuel, water or gas shut-off valve, room by room.
Name the person or role authorised to operate each cut-off, and how they are reached out of hours.
Walk the route with the plan in hand and correct any location that has moved since it was written.

title.en: Log each maintenance and inspection visit against the manufacturer's servicing interval

description.en: Every time utility support equipment is serviced, inspected or load-tested, record the item, the date, who performed the work, what was done and what condition was found, and carry forward the date the next visit falls due from the manufacturer's interval held on the inventory. Where a vendor performs the work under contract, file their service report rather than re-keying it, and record separately the in-house checks that leave no vendor paperwork. This log is what evidences that the equipment is maintained rather than merely owned, and a gap longer than the stated interval is visible in it without further analysis. Attach the maintenance and inspection records for the period under test.

evidenceHint.en: Maintenance and inspection records for the period, one entry per visit giving item, date, engineer, work performed, condition found and the next due date derived from the manufacturer's interval

title.en: Assess each item's configuration and operation against its manufacturer specification

description.en: Take the inventory row by row and compare the state the equipment is actually in against the manufacturer's specification held against it — load on a UPS or generator against its rated capacity, fuel and battery reserves against stated runtime, HVAC set points and filter condition against specification, and the servicing record against the stated interval. Read these from the equipment and its records rather than from the plan, since plant that has drifted past its rating is exactly what this task exists to find. Produce the status report with a compliant or non-compliant verdict per item and, against every non-compliance, an accountable owner and the remediation agreed. Attach the report with the readings it was derived from.

evidenceHint.en: Utility equipment status report listing every inventoried item with its observed configuration and load, the manufacturer value compared against, a compliant or non-compliant verdict, and an owner and remediation for each non-compliance

text.en: Read the current load, reserve and set points from each item of utility support equipment.
Compare each reading against the manufacturer's rated value recorded on the inventory.
Check the maintenance log shows a visit inside the stated servicing interval for every item.
Record a compliant or non-compliant verdict per item, with the reading that decided it.
Name an owner and an agreed remediation against every non-compliant item and carry the open ones forward.

controls.title: POI Device Inspection
controls.objective: Ensure Point of Interaction (POI) devices are regularly inspected for tampering or unauthorized substitution to maintain security and integrity.
controls.successCriteria:
All POI devices are accounted for in the inventory and have up-to-date inspection logs.
Inspection logs demonstrate thorough examination for tampering and unauthorized substitution.
No evidence of tampering or unauthorized substitution is found, or if found, appropriate actions are documented and resolved.
Inspection personnel are well-informed about the procedures and consistently adhere to them.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain a comprehensive inventory list of all POI devices from the Asset Management System.
Collect inspection logs and reports documenting periodic inspections of POI device surfaces.
Gather statements or acknowledgments from personnel responsible for conducting the inspections.

Analysis:
Verify each POI device in the inventory has corresponding inspection logs, ensuring regular and timely inspections.
Review inspection logs and reports for any signs of tampering, unauthorized substitution, or attachment of skimming devices.
Assess the awareness and adherence of inspection personnel to the established inspection procedures.
Examine any reported incidents or discrepancies noted during inspections for adequate follow-up and resolution.

Output:
A comprehensive spreadsheet linking each POI device to its latest inspection report.
A summary of findings from the inspection reports, highlighting any irregularities or concerns.
Documentation of follow-up actions taken for any incidents of tampering or unauthorized substitution detected.

title.en: Record every POI device in the asset management system with its location and serial number

description.en: The inspection programme's population is the device inventory, and a device missing from it is never inspected and never missed. Pull the current list from the Asset Management System and reconcile it against what is physically present at each till, counter and unattended terminal, adding anything found on the floor that the system does not hold and retiring anything the system holds that no longer exists. Record the make, model, serial number, site, position and the person responsible for inspecting it. Attach the inventory export carrying the date it was reconciled against the floor.

evidenceHint.en: POI device inventory export from the Asset Management System giving make, model, serial number, site, position and named inspector for every device, dated to the floor reconciliation

title.en: Document what an inspector checks on a POI device and how a suspected tamper is escalated

description.en: The assessment tests whether inspection personnel adhere to an established procedure, so the procedure has to exist and be specific enough to follow standing at the terminal: which surfaces and seals to examine, how to confirm the serial number matches the inventory row for that position, what a skimming overlay or an added cable looks like on the models actually in use, and how often each device is inspected. It must also say what an inspector does on a suspicion: who is called, whether the device is taken out of service, and that it is not disturbed further. Attach the issued procedure.

evidenceHint.en: Issued POI inspection procedure naming the surface, seal and serial checks per device model, the inspection interval, and the escalation route on a suspected tamper

text.en: List the device models in use and the tamper indicators specific to each of them.
Set the checks an inspector makes on surfaces, seals, ports and attached cabling.
Require the serial number to be read from the device and matched to the inventory row for that position.
State the inspection interval and who covers a site when the named inspector is absent.
Set the escalation route and the point at which a suspect device is withdrawn from service.

title.en: Collect a signed acknowledgement of the inspection procedure from every named inspector

description.en: The assessment gathers statements or acknowledgements from the personnel who conduct inspections and asks whether they are aware of the procedure and follow it. Brief each person named against a device in the inventory on the procedure and on the tamper indicators for the models they cover, then have them acknowledge in writing that they have received it and understand the escalation route. Anyone named as an inspector without an acknowledgement is the gap this task exists to surface, so record them as outstanding rather than dropping them from the list. Attach the acknowledgements together with the outstanding list.

evidenceHint.en: Signed acknowledgements of the POI inspection procedure from each named inspector, with the dated briefing record and the list of inspectors still outstanding

title.en: Log each POI device inspection against that device's inventory record

description.en: Every time a device is inspected, write the result against that device's inventory row rather than into a free-standing sheet, so a device that has gone uninspected shows as an empty row instead of an absence nobody counts. Record the date, the inspector, the checks completed, the serial number as read from the device rather than as copied from the record, and the outcome: clear, or a suspicion raised with its reference. Where a device could not be inspected, record why and when it will be. Attach the inspection log for the period.

evidenceHint.en: POI inspection log for the period, one dated entry per device per inspection, giving inspector, checks completed, the serial as read, and a clear or suspicion outcome

title.en: Record the follow-up and resolution of every suspected tamper or substitution raised

description.en: Each suspicion an inspection raises needs its own trail: the device, what was observed, whether the device was withdrawn, who examined it and what was concluded. Close each entry with the resolution and its date, and where the conclusion was that there was no tamper, say what established that. The assessment looks specifically for adequate follow-up on reported incidents and discrepancies, so an entry left at reported with no outcome is itself the finding. Attach the follow-up records for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Follow-up record for each suspected tamper or substitution giving device, observation, action taken, examiner, conclusion and the closure date

title.en: Match every POI device in the inventory to its latest inspection and list the devices missed

description.en: Build the sheet the assessment asks for, one row per device from the inventory carrying the date of its most recent inspection and a reference to that inspection record, and use it to find the devices with no inspection at all and the devices whose last inspection is older than the interval the procedure sets. Report those two lists with the site and the named inspector behind each, because a cluster under one name is a coverage problem rather than a device problem. Attach the reconciliation sheet.

evidenceHint.en: Device-to-inspection reconciliation sheet covering every inventory row, with the never-inspected and overdue lists and the site and inspector behind each entry

controls.title: Records Protection and Management Control
controls.objective: To ensure the authenticity, reliability, integrity, and usability of organizational records throughout their lifecycle, including creation, storage, access, and disposal.
controls.successCriteria:
Records are managed and protected according to the organization’s guidelines.
The retention schedule is strictly followed for all record types.
No unauthorized access or manipulation of records is detected.
Electronic storage systems are adequate to ensure record availability and integrity over time.
Effective management of cryptographic keys and programs for the duration of the records’ retention period.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the organization’s records management guidelines and retention schedule.
Gather a sample of records from various categories (e.g., HR, financial, legal) and their storage media.
Access logs and change management records for these sample records.
Collect details of the systems used for electronic record storage, including any cryptographic keys and programs.

Analysis:
Review the records management guidelines against the provided requirement for comprehensiveness.
Verify that the retention schedule is being followed for the sample records.
Check the access logs for any unauthorized access or manipulation.
Assess the electronic storage systems for adequacy in preserving records’ readability and accessibility over time.
Ensure cryptographic keys and programs for encrypted archives are adequately managed.

Output:
A report on compliance with records management guidelines.
A spreadsheet or document comparing each sampled record against its retention schedule and handling requirements.
An analysis report on the security and adequacy of electronic storage systems.
A review report on the management of cryptographic keys and programs.

title.en: Register every record category with its storage medium and holding system

description.en: Build one row per record category the organisation holds — HR, financial and legal at minimum, plus operational categories — capturing the medium it lives on (paper, file share, SaaS system, offline archive), the system or physical location holding it, and the named contact who can produce a record from that holding when it is sampled. IT Operations supplies the system and location details for electronic holdings. Where a category is held in more than one place, give each holding its own row so nothing is covered only by implication. This register is the population the retention schedule, the sampling test and the retrieval test all run against. Attach the completed register; a category with a blank medium or holding system is not done.

evidenceHint.en: Record-category register export listing, per category and per holding, the storage medium, the holding system or physical location, and the named retrieval contact

title.en: Record the retention period and disposal method for each record category

description.en: Extend the retention schedule so every category in the register carries a retention trigger (creation, contract end, employee exit), the retention period counted from that trigger, and the disposal method appropriate to the medium it is held on (secure deletion, crypto-erase, shredding). Beside each period, cite the source that set it — the named legal or regulatory obligation where one drives it, otherwise the internal decision. Cross-check the schedule against the register and close every gap: a category present in the register but absent from the schedule, or present with a blank period, is the gap this task exists to close. Attach the schedule showing full coverage of the register.

evidenceHint.en: Retention schedule with one row per record category showing trigger, retention period, disposal method and the source that set the period, cross-referenced to the register

title.en: Map each encrypted archive to the key and reader software needed to open it

description.en: For every archive holding records in encrypted or proprietary form, record the key identifier, where the key is escrowed, its named custodian, and the software plus exact version required to decrypt and render the content. Compare each key's rotation or expiry date against the retention end date of the records it protects, and flag any archive whose key or reader program lapses before those records reach the end of their retention period. Legal/DPO supplies the retention end dates. Attach the mapping with the flagged rows and a named remediation owner against each.

evidenceHint.en: Key-and-program mapping for encrypted archives showing key id, escrow location, custodian, reader software version, and key lifetime set against record retention end

text.en: List every archive whose records are stored encrypted or in a proprietary format.
Record the key identifier, escrow location and named custodian for each archive.
Record the decryption and rendering software, with its exact version, for each archive.
Compare key rotation or expiry dates against the retention end date of the records protected.
Flag archives whose key or reader software lapses first and name a remediation owner.

title.en: Test a sample of HR, financial and legal records against the retention schedule

description.en: Draw a sample from the register covering HR, financial and legal categories at minimum, and for each sampled record capture its identifier, category, creation or trigger date, the disposal date its schedule row implies, and its actual state today (live, archived, disposed, overdue). Mark a pass or fail per record. Against every fail — a record held past its disposal date, or destroyed before it — write a remediation owner and target date in the same sheet, so the finding and its disposition travel together. Attach the completed comparison sheet: it evidences that the schedule is followed, not that it exists.

evidenceHint.en: Completed sampling sheet with one row per sampled record showing category, trigger date, scheduled disposal date, actual state, pass or fail outcome and remediation owner for each fail

text.en: Draw the sample so that HR, financial and legal categories are each represented.
Record each sampled record's identifier, category and retention trigger date.
Derive the scheduled disposal date from the retention schedule row for its category.
Compare the record's actual state against that derived date and mark pass or fail.
Write a remediation owner and target date against every record marked fail.

title.en: Test the sampled records' access and change logs for unauthorised access or manipulation

description.en: Pull the access history and change management records covering the sampled records for the period under test, and examine them for reads by accounts outside the category's authorised group, edits or deletions of records already closed, and changes made without a change record. Disposition every hit either as authorised — naming the change record or approval that covers it — or as an exception referred for investigation. IT Operations supplies the log extracts; where a holding system produces no usable log, record that as a finding against that system rather than leaving the row blank. Attach the extract alongside the dispositioned exception list; an empty exception list is evidence only when the extract shows the logs were actually read.

evidenceHint.en: Access and change-log extract for the sampled records plus the exception list showing each hit dispositioned as authorised or referred, and any system that produced no usable log

title.en: Test that the longest-stored record in each electronic storage system still opens and renders

description.en: For every electronic storage system in the register, pull back the record that has been in storage longest and confirm it can still be opened and read: note the retrieval time, the software and version that rendered it, whether content and metadata were intact, and any dependency — a key, a licence, an obsolete format — that made retrieval difficult. Record a result per system and raise a migration or format-conversion item, with a named owner, wherever a record could not be read or rendered incomplete. Attach the test log; it is what evidences that electronic storage remains adequate over time.

evidenceHint.en: Retrieval test log with one row per storage system: record retrieved, retrieval time, rendering software and version, readability outcome and any migration item raised

text.en: Select the longest-stored record available in each electronic storage system.
Retrieve the record and record how long the retrieval took to complete.
Open it and confirm content and metadata render intact, naming the software version used.
Note any key, licence or obsolete format the successful retrieval depended on.
Raise a migration or format-conversion item, with an owner, for each unreadable record.

controls.title: Authority Contact Compliance
controls.objective: Ensure timely and appropriate contact with relevant authorities and adherence to regulatory requirements in the event of information security incidents.
controls.successCriteria:
All necessary contacts with authorities in response to information security incidents are made in accordance with the established policy.
Regular and effective communication with special interest groups is maintained.
The organization demonstrates awareness and understanding of current and upcoming information security regulations as applicable.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain a record of all reported information security incidents from the Incident Management log.
Gather documentation of communications with relevant authorities related to these incidents.
Access the policy document outlining the protocol for contacting authorities in the event of an information security incident.
Collect records of regular updates and communications with special interest groups.

Analysis:
Review each reported incident to determine if it necessitated contact with authorities according to the policy guidelines.
For each incident where contact was required, verify that the relevant authorities were appropriately notified.
Assess the regularity and relevance of communications and consultations with special interest groups, ensuring alignment with current and upcoming regulatory expectations.

Output:
A report listing all reviewed incidents and the corresponding actions taken.
Documentation verifying communications with authorities and special interest groups.
An assessment report on the adherence to the policy for contacting authorities.

title.en: Collect the period's reported incidents from the incident management log

description.en: Take the incident management log for the period and produce the population this control tests against: one row per reported information security incident carrying its reference, the date and time reported, its category and severity, and the systems and data involved. Those are the facts the policy's contact criteria get applied to, so a row without them cannot be assessed at all. Include incidents later closed as false positives, marked as such, so the assessment can show it read the whole log rather than a filtered view of it. Attach the extract with the date it was taken.

evidenceHint.en: Dated extract of the incident management log for the period, one row per reported incident with category, severity and the systems and data involved

title.en: Record which authority each incident type must be reported to, and within what time

description.en: Work from the policy that sets the protocol for contacting authorities and turn it into a table an on-call responder can apply at three in the morning: the trigger that creates the obligation, the authority or regulator it runs to, the named contact route, and the time limit the policy states where it states one. Cover every incident type the policy addresses, because a trigger the table omits is the one that gets missed. Where the policy is silent on a trigger the organisation is plausibly subject to, flag that gap rather than filling it from assumption. Attach the table with the policy clauses each row derives from.

evidenceHint.en: Authority notification table giving trigger, authority, contact route and stated time limit per incident type, cross-referenced to the policy clauses it derives from

text.en: List the notification triggers the policy sets, by incident type.
Name the authority and the contact route each trigger runs to.
Record the time limit the policy states for each notification.
Flag any trigger the organisation is subject to that the policy does not cover.

title.en: Document each authority notification with its date, channel and acknowledgement

description.en: Every time an incident meets a notification trigger, keep the proof that contact was actually made: the submission itself or a copy of its content, the date and time it was sent, the channel used, the authority reference or acknowledgement received back, and any follow-up correspondence. The acknowledgement is the part most often missing and is what distinguishes a notification sent from one received. Where an authority requires a staged report — an initial notification followed by a fuller one — hold both against the same incident reference so the sequence can be read. Attach the notification records for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Authority notification records for the period: submission content, date and time sent, channel, the acknowledgement or reference received back, and any follow-up correspondence, filed against the incident reference

title.en: Log the organisation's participation in special interest groups over the period

description.en: Record each security forum, sector body or specialist group the organisation participates in, and against each one the contacts made during the period: briefings received, advisories acted on, meetings attended and who attended them. Keep the material received rather than just the fact of receipt, because relevance is assessed against content. Where a membership lapsed or a group produced nothing during the period, record that as well — the control tests regularity, and a dormant membership counted as an active one overstates it. Attach the participation log together with the material it references.

evidenceHint.en: Special interest group participation log for the period listing each group, the contacts and advisories received with dates, the attendee, and any membership that lapsed or produced nothing

title.en: Assess each incident against the notification triggers and whether contact was required and made

description.en: Take the incident population row by row and apply the notification table: record whether a trigger was met, which authority it ran to, whether contact was made, and the elapsed time between the incident being reported and the notification being sent, set against the stated limit. Each row carries a verdict — not required, required and made in time, required and made late, or required and not made — and every verdict beyond the first two carries an owner and an agreed remediation. This is the adherence assessment the control outputs, so attach it with the incident and notification references standing behind each row.

evidenceHint.en: Adherence assessment listing every reviewed incident with the trigger applied, the notification decision, elapsed time against the stated limit, a verdict per incident and an owner for each exception

text.en: Apply the notification table to each incident and record the trigger met.
Record whether contact was made and the authority it was made to.
Calculate the elapsed time from report to notification against the limit.
Give each incident a verdict of not required, in time, late or not made.
Name an owner and a remediation for every late or missed notification.

title.en: Review the regulatory changes the group communications surfaced against the organisation's obligations

description.en: Read the advisories, briefings and consultations captured in the participation log for what they say about current and upcoming information security regulation, and record against each one whether it changes an obligation the organisation holds — a new notification trigger, a shortened deadline, a newly competent authority. Every item that does changes the notification table, so carry it there with a named owner rather than leaving it in a reading list. Where the log surfaced nothing relevant across the whole period, say so explicitly: that is a finding about the groups chosen, not a clean result. Attach the review with the source material it cites.

evidenceHint.en: Regulatory horizon review citing each advisory or briefing considered, the obligation it affects, and the change carried into the notification table with a named owner

controls.title: Documented Procedures Compliance
controls.objective: Ensure that all information processing facilities operate in accordance with documented procedures to maintain information security.
controls.successCriteria:
All operational activities conform to the documented operating procedures.
Documented procedures are regularly reviewed, updated, and authorized.
Responses to errors and system failures are in line with the documented procedures.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the current list of documented operating procedures.
Collect evidence of operating procedure implementations, such as system configuration records, backup logs, and error handling reports.
Gather recent updates or changes made to the operating procedures.

Analysis:
For each operational activity, verify that the existing implementation aligns with the documented procedures.
Review the update history of the operating procedures to ensure they are regularly reviewed and authorized.
Examine instances of error handling and system failures to assess if the responses adhered to the documented procedures.

Output:
A comprehensive report comparing the actual operational practices against the documented procedures.
A log of updates and changes to the operating procedures, along with authorization records.
An analysis report of error handling and system failure incidents.

title.en: Inventory the documented operating procedures and the facility each one governs

description.en: Produce the current list of documented operating procedures the control asks for, and against each one record the information processing facility or activity it governs, its issued version and date, the review cycle it states where it states one, and the role authorised to approve it. Build the list from the facilities side as well as the document side: an activity running with no documented procedure is a gap this task exists to expose, and it will never appear if the list is copied out of the document library alone. Flag procedures that state no review cycle rather than assuming one for them. Attach the inventory with the date it was compiled.

evidenceHint.en: Dated inventory of documented operating procedures with the facility or activity each governs, issued version and date, stated review cycle and authorising role, plus the activities found running with no procedure

text.en: List the operating procedures currently issued, with version and date.
Record the facility or operational activity each procedure governs.
Walk the facilities list for activities with no documented procedure.
Record the stated review cycle, or flag the procedure as stating none.
Record the role authorised to approve each procedure as issued.

title.en: Collect the configuration records, backup logs and error reports each procedure produces

description.en: Each documented procedure should leave a trace when it runs — a system configuration record, a backup completion log, an error handling report. For the period under test, gather that output per procedure and hold it against its inventory row, so the comparison later has something to read rather than an assertion to accept. Where a procedure produces no trace at all, record that: an untraceable procedure cannot be evidenced as followed, and that is a finding about the procedure rather than about the period. Attach the collected output indexed by procedure.

evidenceHint.en: Operational output for the period indexed by procedure — system configuration records, backup logs and error handling reports — plus the list of procedures that produced no trace at all

title.en: Record every procedure update with its date, author and authorisation

description.en: Hold a change log covering the operating procedures: which procedure changed, the version before and after, what changed in substance, the date, who made the change and who authorised it. The authorisation is the part the control names explicitly, so a change recorded without one is incomplete rather than merely undocumented. Keep superseded versions accessible, because the practice comparison reads the version that was in force during the period under test rather than the one in force today. Attach the change log with the authorisation records standing behind it.

evidenceHint.en: Operating procedure change log for the period showing procedure, version before and after, the substance of the change, date, author and the authorisation record for each change

title.en: Verify each facility's actual operating practice against its documented procedure

description.en: Take the inventory row by row and establish what the facility actually does — from the configuration records and logs and, where those do not settle it, by watching the activity performed — then set that against the procedure version in force during the period. Record a conformance verdict per procedure, naming the specific step that diverged where one did, and give every divergence an accountable owner and an agreed remediation. Do not resolve a divergence by editing the procedure to match practice as part of this task: which of the two is wrong is a decision to record, not one to assume. Attach the comparison report with the records it was derived from.

evidenceHint.en: Practice-versus-procedure comparison report covering every inventoried procedure, with the diverging step named, a conformance verdict, and an owner and remediation against each divergence

text.en: Read the practice actually followed from the configuration records and logs.
Observe the activity performed where the records do not settle the question.
Set the observed practice against the procedure version in force at the time.
Record a conformance verdict and name the step that diverged, if any.
Assign an owner and an agreed remediation to each divergence found.

title.en: Test each procedure's review and authorisation history against its stated cycle

description.en: For every procedure in the inventory, take the date it was last reviewed and the date it was last authorised from the change log and compare both against the review cycle the procedure states. Record per procedure whether it sits within cycle, is overdue and by how long, or is unassessable because no cycle is stated. Overdue and unassessable are both findings and both need a named owner; the second is the one that quietly persists, because a procedure with no stated cycle can never be late. Attach the test sheet showing the dates and the cycle each was measured against.

evidenceHint.en: Review currency test sheet listing each procedure's last review and authorisation dates against its stated cycle, with an in-cycle, overdue or no-cycle-stated verdict and an owner for each exception

title.en: Assess each error and system failure against the response its procedure prescribes

description.en: Take the errors and system failures recorded during the period and, for each, set the response actually taken against the response the relevant operating procedure prescribes: who was notified, what containment or recovery steps were run and in what order, and whether the escalation the procedure names was used. Record a verdict per incident and, where the response departed from the procedure, whether the departure caused harm and what is being changed as a result. Where a failure was handled with no applicable procedure at all, that gap goes back to the inventory as a missing procedure. Attach the analysis with the error reports it reads.

evidenceHint.en: Error and failure handling analysis covering each incident in the period: the prescribed response, the response actually taken, a verdict, and the procedure gap or change arising from each departure

controls.title: Storage Media Lifecycle Management
controls.objective: Ensure the secure management of storage media throughout its lifecycle, including acquisition, use, transportation, and disposal, in alignment with the organization's classification scheme and handling requirements.
controls.successCriteria:
The policy for storage media management is comprehensive and adhered to.
All storage media acquisitions, disposals, and transportations are documented and authorized.
Usage and removal of storage media are properly logged and aligned with the audit trail requirements.
Cryptographic measures and environmental protections are adequately implemented.
Regular data transfers to new storage media are conducted to prevent data degradation.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the policy document outlining the management of storage media.
Collect records of storage media acquisitions and disposals.
Gather documentation of storage media transportation, including authorization records.
Acquire logs of storage media usage, removals from premises, and disposal procedures.
Retrieve details of cryptographic measures implemented for information protection on storage media.
Obtain evidence of environmental protection measures for storage media.
Collect records of periodic data transfers to new storage media to avoid degradation.

Analysis:
Review the storage media management policy to ensure it covers all lifecycle stages.
Verify that records of acquisitions and disposals align with policy requirements.
Analyze transportation and authorization records for compliance with the policy.
Assess the logs of usage and removals to ensure adherence to audit trail requirements.
Examine the implementation of cryptographic measures on storage media containing sensitive information.
Evaluate the protection measures against environmental threats.
Analyze the periodic data transfer records to ensure mitigation of degradation risks.

Output:
A report detailing compliance of storage media management with the policy.
A spreadsheet summarizing acquisitions, disposals, transportations, and usage of storage media.
Documentation evidencing cryptographic measures and environmental protections.
Audit findings on the periodic data transfer practices for storage media.

title.en: Register every class of storage medium in use with the classification of information it carries

description.en: The policy has to align media handling to the organisation's classification scheme, which needs the two lined up first. List each class of storage medium the organisation holds, including removable drives, backup tapes, optical media, the disks inside equipment awaiting decommission, and against each record the highest classification of information it carries, where it is stored, who has custody, and the lifecycle stage it is in. Attach the register with the date it was compiled.

evidenceHint.en: Storage media register listing each media class with its highest information classification, storage location, named custodian and current lifecycle stage

title.en: Set the acquisition, use, transport and disposal requirements for each media class in the policy

description.en: Write the policy the assessment reads first, and cover every lifecycle stage the objective names rather than disposal alone, which is where these policies usually stop. For each media class in the register state who may acquire it and how the acquisition is recorded, the handling required while it is in use, the authorisation and packaging required before it leaves the premises, and the disposal method with the record made when a medium is destroyed. Say which requirements follow from the classification, so that a change in classification changes handling without a policy rewrite. Attach the issued policy version.

evidenceHint.en: Issued storage media management policy version covering acquisition, use, transport, removal from the premises and disposal requirements for each media class

text.en: State the acquisition route and the record made when a medium enters service.
Set the handling rules in use for each classification the register names.
Set who authorises a medium leaving the premises and what that authorisation records.
Name the disposal method for each media class and the record made when a medium is destroyed.
State the interval at which data is moved to fresh media to avoid degradation.

title.en: Record the encryption and the environmental protection applied to each media class

description.en: Two of the artifacts the assessment collects are the detail of the cryptographic measures protecting information on storage media and the evidence of protection against environmental threats. Against each register row record the encryption in force, naming the algorithm, where the key lives and who holds it, or state explicitly that the class is unencrypted and why that is acceptable at its classification. Then record the conditions the medium is kept in: temperature and humidity control, fire and water protection, and the physical security of the store itself. Attach the schedule with the configuration or facility evidence behind each entry.

evidenceHint.en: Media protection schedule giving, per media class, the encryption applied with its key custody or a stated unencrypted exception, and the environmental controls of its store

title.en: Log every media acquisition, removal from the premises and disposal with its authorisation

description.en: One log covering the whole lifecycle is what makes the audit trail the success criteria call for reconstructable: each entry carries the medium's identifier, the event, whether acquired, issued, taken off the premises, returned or disposed, the date, the person, and the authorisation reference wherever the policy requires one. For a disposal hold the disposal record against the entry; for a removal from the premises hold the authorisation the policy requires. Attach the log for the period together with the authorisations and disposal records it refers to.

evidenceHint.en: Storage media lifecycle log for the period giving medium identifier, event, date, person, authorisation reference, and the disposal or transport record behind each entry

title.en: Move data from ageing media to fresh media on the policy's interval and record each transfer

description.en: Media degrade whether or not anyone reads them, so the transfer has to be scheduled rather than triggered by a failed restore. Work from the register: for each media class carrying data that must outlive the medium, copy it to fresh media at the interval the policy sets, verify the copy is readable rather than only that it was written, and record the source medium, the destination, the date, the verification performed and what happened to the source afterwards. Attach the transfer records for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Data transfer records for the period showing source medium, destination medium, date, the readability verification performed, and the disposal of each superseded medium

title.en: Compare the acquisition, transport and disposal records against the policy's requirements

description.en: Sample the lifecycle log across all three stages and read each sampled entry back against the policy: was the acquisition recorded, did the removal carry the authorisation the policy demands, did the disposal produce the record the policy names, and did the handling match the classification on the register. Produce the compliance report with a pass or fail per sampled entry and, for each fail, the requirement missed and the owner. State the sample size and how it was chosen, because an unstated sample makes the report unrepeatable. Attach the report and the summary spreadsheet behind it.

evidenceHint.en: Storage media compliance report with the sample basis stated, a pass or fail per sampled acquisition, transport and disposal, and the missed requirement and owner behind each fail

controls.title: Data Leakage Prevention
controls.objective: Ensure the implementation and effective functioning of Data Leakage Prevention measures across all systems, networks, and devices that process, store, or transmit sensitive information.
controls.successCriteria:
All systems, networks, and devices identified are confirmed to have effective DLP measures in place.
DLP tools are correctly configured and operational, with no unauthorized disclosures of sensitive information.
Incidents of data leakage, if any, are adequately addressed with appropriate response and remediation actions.
Strict adherence to user access controls and data transfer policies is maintained.
Training and awareness programs are effective in educating employees about data leakage risks and prevention.
Backups of sensitive information are adequately protected with robust encryption and access controls.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain a list of all systems, networks, and devices used for processing, storing, and transmitting sensitive information.
Acquire configuration details and operational logs of Data Leakage Prevention (DLP) tools deployed in the organization.
Collect recent incident reports and logs pertaining to data leakage events, if any.
Retrieve documentation on user access controls related to copying, pasting, and uploading of data to external services.
Gather evidence of training and awareness programs conducted for employees on data leakage prevention.
Obtain backup policies and evidence of encryption and access controls for backed-up data.

Analysis:
Verify that all listed systems, networks, and devices are equipped with appropriate DLP measures.
Analyze DLP tool configuration and operational logs to ensure sensitive data is being correctly identified, monitored, and protected against unauthorized disclosure.
Review incident reports and logs for any data leakage events and assess the response and remediation actions taken.
Examine user access controls to ensure compliance with policies on data transfer restrictions.
Evaluate the effectiveness of training and awareness programs in imparting knowledge on data leakage risks and prevention.
Assess the adequacy of encryption and access controls applied to backed-up data, ensuring sensitive information is adequately protected.

Output:
A comprehensive report detailing the DLP measures in place for each system, network, and device.
Analysis report of DLP tool effectiveness and incident handling.
Assessment report on user access controls and compliance with data transfer restrictions.
Training and awareness program effectiveness report.
Backup policy compliance report, with a focus on encryption and access control measures.

title.en: Inventory the systems, networks and devices that process, store or transmit sensitive information

description.en: Build the population this control acts on: one row per system, network path or device class holding or carrying sensitive information, giving the sensitive data categories it handles, whether it processes, stores or transmits them, the accountable owner, and the data leakage prevention measure covering it today. Work outward from where sensitive information is created rather than from where the DLP agent is already deployed, so a system holding sensitive data with no measure appears as a gap instead of staying invisible. Attach the inventory with the coverage column populated on every row, including the rows whose coverage is none.

evidenceHint.en: Inventory of systems, networks and devices handling sensitive information, showing the data categories, whether it is processed, stored or transmitted, the owner and the DLP measure covering each row

text.en: List the systems and repositories where sensitive information is created or stored.
Add the network paths and external services over which sensitive information is transmitted.
Add the end-user devices and removable media that hold or carry it.
Record the sensitive data categories each row handles and its accountable owner.
Mark the DLP measure covering each row, writing none where there is no coverage.

title.en: Configure the data leakage prevention tooling against the sensitive data categories on the inventory

description.en: Set the DLP tooling so every sensitive data category the inventory names is identified by a rule or classifier, and record for each monitored channel — email, web upload, cloud storage, removable media, clipboard, print — whether the rule alerts or blocks and which users it applies to. This is where the restrictions on copying, pasting and uploading data to external services actually take effect, so the exported configuration doubles as the documentation of those user access controls. Export the configuration rather than describing it, and list every inventory row the tooling cannot cover together with the compensating measure applied instead. Attach the configuration export and the uncovered-rows list.

evidenceHint.en: DLP configuration export showing the rule or classifier per sensitive data category and, per channel, whether it alerts or blocks and who it applies to, plus the list of inventory rows it cannot cover

title.en: Record the encryption and access controls protecting backups of sensitive information

description.en: For every backup set holding sensitive information, write down the encryption applied to it at rest and in transit, the accounts able to restore from it, and how that restore access is authorised and reviewed. Read the values from the backup system's own settings rather than from what the backup policy promises, and where the two disagree the discrepancy is the finding this task produces. Where a backup set is held by a third party, record where it is held and how the encryption and access controls applied there were evidenced. Attach the record with the backup configuration extracts behind it.

evidenceHint.en: Record of the backup sets holding sensitive information with the encryption applied, the accounts able to restore, the authorisation route, and the configuration extracts they were read from

title.en: Log every data leakage alert and record the incident each genuine event produced

description.en: Keep the DLP tooling's operational log for the period and, for each alert that turns out to be a genuine leakage or attempted leakage, open an incident record carrying what left or nearly left, the channel it used, the person or system involved, the response taken and the remediation completed. Alerts dispositioned as false positives are recorded as such with the reason, so the log shows the alerts were read rather than accumulated. Where the period produced no leakage event, the log extract is still the evidence — a nil return with no extract behind it proves nothing. Attach the log extract with the incident records it produced.

evidenceHint.en: DLP operational log extract for the period plus an incident record per leakage event giving the channel, the data involved, the response taken and the remediation completed

title.en: Train staff on data leakage risks and record who completed it

description.en: Run the awareness activity that tells staff which information is sensitive, which transfer channels are restricted, and what to do when the tooling blocks them, and keep the record of it: the material used and its date, the audience it was aimed at, who completed it, and the result of whatever comprehension check the programme includes. Cover the roles the inventory shows actually handle sensitive information, since that is the population this control is about; HR holds the completion data. Attach the training material with the completion record for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Data leakage awareness training material with its date, and the completion record for the period showing the audience covered and any comprehension result

title.en: Assess the effectiveness of the DLP tooling and the handling of the period's incidents

description.en: Set the inventory against the deployed configuration to find rows carrying sensitive information with no effective measure, then take a sample of the period's alerts and incidents and test how each was handled: was it triaged, was the disposition recorded, was the remediation completed and by whom. Report both together with a pass or exception verdict per finding, and give every exception a named owner and a date to clear it. Attach the assessment with the coverage gaps and the sampled alerts it was built from.

evidenceHint.en: DLP effectiveness assessment listing the inventory rows without effective coverage and the sampled alerts with how each was handled, every exception carrying an owner and a clearance date

text.en: Set every inventory row against the deployed configuration and list those with no effective measure.
Sample the period's alerts across each monitored channel, including those closed as false positives.
Check each sampled alert was triaged and its disposition recorded as the procedure requires.
Confirm the remediation recorded against each genuine incident was actually completed.
Assign an owner and a clearance date to every coverage gap and handling exception.

controls.title: Centralized AAA Management
controls.objective: Ensure that network Authentication, Authorization, and Auditing (AAA) processes are centralized and consistently applied across all systems and platforms.
controls.successCriteria:
All accounts and their roles are consistent with the Access Matrix.
All change requests have been executed following the established procedures and authorization protocols.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the Access Matrix listing all systems with focus on those requiring AAA.
Capture screenshots or reports showing the current state of AAA settings on a sample of these systems.
Gather a list of recent access management change requests.

Analysis:
For each system in the Access Matrix, verify that AAA configurations match the prescribed standards and policies.
For each account shown in the screenshots/reports, ensure it aligns with what the Access Matrix authorizes.
Review all change requests to confirm they adhere to established processes for modifying access rights and AAA configurations.

Output:
A collection of screenshots or system reports.
A spreadsheet or report verifying each account against the Access Matrix.
A report detailing the review of change requests, highlighting any discrepancies or process deviations.

title.en: Record in the Access Matrix every system and the AAA service it authenticates against

description.en: Work down the system list and, against each entry, record where authentication happens (the central identity service, or a local account store), where authorisation roles are defined, and where its audit records land. Systems still holding local accounts or their own role tables are the exceptions this task exists to name — record each with the reason it is not yet centralised and a named owner, rather than omitting it. The completed matrix is the population every later verification samples from, so a system missing here is a system nothing checks.

evidenceHint.en: Access Matrix export with an authentication source, authorisation source and audit-log destination against every listed system, and each decentralised system flagged with a reason and owner

text.en: List every system in scope, including those reached only over the network by administrators.
Record whether each authenticates against the central identity service or a local account store.
Record where each system's authorisation roles are defined and where its audit records are sent.
Flag every system not yet centralised with the reason and a named owner.

title.en: Set the required AAA configuration for each class of system in the matrix

description.en: Write down what correct looks like before anything is sampled against it: the authentication source and protocol each class of system must use, the role-to-entitlement mapping the central service is expected to deliver, and the destination and retention of the audit stream. Without this the later verification degrades into an opinion about screenshots. Cover every class the matrix contains, including the systems flagged as not yet centralised, so that a deviation reads as a deviation rather than as a gap in the standard.

evidenceHint.en: Issued AAA configuration standard giving, per system class, the authentication source and protocol, the authorisation role mapping, and the audit-log destination and retention

title.en: Capture the live AAA settings and account listing from a sample of matrix systems

description.en: For each system in the cycle's sample, take the configuration report or screenshot showing the authentication source in force, the roles defined and the accounts holding them — read from the system itself rather than from its build documentation, since documentation that agrees with the standard while the system does not is exactly the failure this evidence exists to catch. Label every capture with the date and the operator so the verification knows what point in time it is reading. Attach the collected screenshots and system reports for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Dated screenshots or system reports per sampled system showing its authentication source, defined roles and current accounts, each labelled with capture date and operator

title.en: Verify every account and role in the captures against the Access Matrix

description.en: Put one row per captured account beside what the matrix authorises and mark it matched, unauthorised, or authorised but absent. An account present on the system and missing from the matrix is a finding; a matrix entitlement with no live account is a stale authorisation and is worth closing too. Against every mismatch record the accountable owner and the corrective action agreed — removal, a matrix correction, or a documented exception. Attach the verification spreadsheet covering the full sample rather than the exceptions alone.

evidenceHint.en: Verification spreadsheet with one row per captured account showing its matrix entitlement, a matched or mismatched verdict, and for each mismatch the accountable owner and corrective action

text.en: Load the captured account and role listings alongside the Access Matrix entries.
Mark each captured account matched, unauthorised, or authorised but not present.
Check each sampled system's AAA configuration against the standard's values for its class.
Record an accountable owner and a corrective action against every mismatch found.

title.en: Check each access management change request against the authorisation procedure

description.en: Take the change requests raised in the period and read each for what the procedure requires: a named requester, the entitlement granted or removed, the authorisation the procedure calls for, and a record that the change was executed as approved. Compare the executed state against the request, so that a change approved for one entitlement and executed as another is caught rather than passed on the strength of its paperwork. List deviations with the request identifier and the step that was skipped. Attach the review with a compliant or deviation verdict per request.

evidenceHint.en: Change request review listing every access management request in the period with its recorded authorisation, the entitlement approved against the entitlement executed, and a compliant or deviation verdict naming the step skipped

controls.title: Secure SAD Deletion
controls.objective: To ensure that all Sensitive Authentication Data (SAD) is not retained post-authorization and is rendered unrecoverable immediately after the authorization process is complete.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Retrieve the list of all systems handling SAD.
Obtain system configurations and logs showing SAD handling and deletion processes.
Acquire documented procedures related to SAD deletion and data retention.

Analysis:
Review system configurations and logs to verify that SAD is not stored post-authorization.
Examine documented procedures to ensure they align with the policy of not retaining SAD after authorization.
Analyze data deletion methods to confirm they render SAD unrecoverable immediately after authorization.

Output:
Report detailing system configurations and logs.
Compliance checklist comparing documented procedures against actual practices.
Analysis report of data deletion methods and their effectiveness.

title.en: List every system handling sensitive authentication data and the elements each one touches

description.en: Build the population the whole control runs against: each system that captures, transmits, processes or could hold sensitive authentication data, and against each the specific elements involved — full magnetic stripe or chip track data, the card verification code, and the PIN or PIN block. Record for each element whether the system captures it, passes it on, or has any route by which it could persist, and name the owner who can produce configuration and log extracts from that system. A system that handles none of it is recorded with an explicit nil rather than omitted, so the list can be shown to be complete rather than merely short. Attach the dated list with the authorisation path it was derived from.

evidenceHint.en: Dated list of systems handling sensitive authentication data naming, per system, the elements involved and whether each is captured, transmitted or capable of being stored, with the system owner named

text.en: Walk the authorisation path end to end and list every system the data passes through.
Record which sensitive authentication elements each system touches, element by element.
Note any store, log, queue or file through which a system could retain an element.
Name the owner who can produce configuration and log extracts from each system.

title.en: Write the deletion procedure naming the method and the moment of deletion for each system

description.en: The control tests documented procedures against actual practice, so the procedure has to be specific enough to be falsified by that test. For every system on the list, state which sensitive authentication element it holds, the method that removes it, and the exact point in the authorisation flow at which that method runs, read against the control's requirement that the data is rendered unrecoverable once authorisation completes. Where a system does not remove it at that point, state the interval the data survives and record it as an exception, rather than writing the delay into the procedure as though it were the standard. Name the person accountable for each system's step. Attach the issued procedure with a completed row for every system on the list.

evidenceHint.en: Issued sensitive authentication data deletion procedure with one row per system giving the element held, the deletion method, the point in the flow at which it runs and the accountable owner

title.en: Record the configuration in each system that removes the data once authorisation completes

description.en: Document the settings that make the procedure real: the retention or purge setting on each store, the log level and any field masking or suppression rule that keeps the data out of application and web server logs, the lifetime applied to temporary files and caches, and the setting on any queue or buffer the data passes through. Take every value from the running system rather than from a build template, and record the date each was read, because a configuration record carrying no date cannot evidence a period. Where a system offers no setting and relies on code to delete, cite the module that performs the deletion instead of leaving the row blank. Attach the configuration extracts per system.

evidenceHint.en: Dated configuration extracts per system showing the purge or retention setting, the log masking rule and the temporary-file lifetime that remove sensitive authentication data after authorisation

title.en: Search each system's stores and logs for sensitive authentication data retained after authorisation

description.en: Over the period under test, search every store, log file, temporary directory and export named on the system list for values matching track data, card verification codes and PIN blocks. Record per system what was searched, the patterns used, the volume examined and the hits found, and state a nil result explicitly rather than by omitting the line. Preserve each hit's location and record identifier before anything is removed, because the location is what identifies which deletion step failed and removing the data first destroys that. Attach the search output for every system on the list, including the ones that returned nothing.

evidenceHint.en: Search output per system covering stores, logs, temporary files and exports for the period, naming the patterns used, the volume examined and every hit with its location, with nil results stated explicitly

title.en: Test that each deletion method leaves the data unrecoverable and record what recovery was attempted

description.en: The control asks whether the deletion methods render the data unrecoverable, which is a stronger claim than the data no longer being visible through the application. For each distinct method in the procedure, delete a seeded test record and then attempt recovery by the routes available to somebody with access to the underlying system: reading the raw store, undelete or file-carving tools against the medium, and the backup or replica copies of the same data. Record per method how recovery was attempted, with what tools, and whether anything came back. A method that leaves recoverable data is reported against the method rather than the system, because it will fail everywhere that method is used. Attach the test record.

evidenceHint.en: Deletion method test record naming, per method, the recovery routes and tools attempted and whether any sensitive authentication data was recovered, with the systems each method covers

text.en: List the distinct deletion methods the procedure uses rather than testing system by system.
Delete a seeded test record with each method under the conditions the procedure states.
Attempt recovery from the raw store, from the medium, and from backup or replica copies.
Record the tools and routes attempted alongside whether any data came back.
Report a recoverable result against the method so every system using it is covered.

title.en: Score the documented procedure against observed practice in a compliance checklist

description.en: Take the procedure clause by clause and record, against each, what was actually observed in the configuration record, the search output and the deletion tests, then mark pass or fail. Two failure shapes matter separately and the checklist distinguishes them: practice that falls short of the procedure, and a procedure clause that no longer describes how the system works, which is corrected in the procedure rather than in the system. Every fail carries the evidence line that produced it, a named owner and a date to clear it, so the checklist can be re-read next period against the same clauses. Attach the completed checklist as the control's compliance record for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Compliance checklist with one row per procedure clause giving the observed practice, a pass or fail verdict, the evidence line it rests on, and an owner and date against every fail

controls.title: Vulnerability Management Control
controls.objective: To ensure that all technical vulnerabilities within the organization's information systems are identified, evaluated, and appropriately mitigated.
controls.successCriteria:
All information systems are regularly scanned for vulnerabilities, and identified vulnerabilities are promptly addressed.
Updates and patches are effectively applied to mitigate identified vulnerabilities.
Third-party libraries and source codes are regularly reviewed and updated to ensure they do not introduce vulnerabilities into the system.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain an inventory of all information systems including details like software vendor, software name, version numbers, and current deployment state.
Gather recent reports from vulnerability scanning tools.
Collect records of recent penetration tests or vulnerability assessments.
Retrieve documentation of recent software updates or patches applied.
Acquire a list of all third-party libraries and source codes used, along with their vulnerability tracking records.

Analysis:
Cross-reference the system inventory with vulnerability scan reports to verify coverage and identify any unaddressed vulnerabilities.
Review the penetration test or vulnerability assessment reports to assess the effectiveness of the current vulnerability management processes.
For each applied software update or patch, verify that it addresses relevant vulnerabilities and check for successful implementation.
Examine the use of third-party libraries and source codes, ensuring they are up to date and free from known vulnerabilities.

Output:
A comprehensive spreadsheet or report detailing the findings from the vulnerability scans and assessments.
Documentation verifying the successful application of updates and patches.
A report on the status of third-party libraries and source codes, highlighting any potential vulnerabilities.

title.en: Inventory the information systems with their software vendor, name, version and deployment state

description.en: Produce the technical inventory this control is measured against: one row per system or software installation carrying the vendor, the product name, the version actually running and its deployment state — production, staging, decommissioned or awaiting replacement. Read the versions from the systems themselves or from the management tooling rather than from a procurement record, because a stale version number is what makes a clean scan report meaningless. This inventory is the denominator the scan-coverage reconciliation counts against. Attach the dated inventory export.

evidenceHint.en: Dated information systems inventory export listing the software vendor, name, running version and deployment state for every row

title.en: Catalogue the third-party libraries and source components in use with their vulnerability tracking status

description.en: Compile the list of third-party libraries, packages and externally sourced code the applications depend on, giving for each the version in use, the application depending on it, the source its vulnerability information is tracked from, and the vulnerabilities currently open against that version. Generate it from the build's own dependency manifests rather than from memory, so transitive dependencies are included, and mark the components no longer maintained upstream so replacement can be planned before a vulnerability forces it. Attach the list with the date it was generated and the applications it covers.

evidenceHint.en: Third-party library and source component list giving, per component, the version in use, the dependent application, the tracking source and the vulnerabilities open against that version

text.en: Generate the dependency list from each application's build manifests, including transitive dependencies.
Record the version in use and the application that depends on each component.
Name the source each component's vulnerability information is tracked from.
List the vulnerabilities currently open against each version in use.
Mark the components no longer maintained upstream so replacement can be planned.

title.en: Scan the inventoried systems for vulnerabilities and retain each run's report

description.en: Run the vulnerability scans across the systems on the inventory and keep every run's report with its date, the scope actually scanned, the tool and signature version used, and the findings ranked by severity. Record the systems that were in scope but returned no result — unreachable, credentialed scan failed, agent not reporting — because in a summary those are indistinguishable from systems that scanned clean, and that ambiguity is what this column removes. Attach the scan reports for the period together with the scope statement each was run under.

evidenceHint.en: Vulnerability scan reports for the period giving, per run, the date, the scope scanned, the tool and signature version, the ranked findings, and the in-scope systems that returned no result

title.en: Record every patch and software update applied, with the vulnerability it closes and the check that it took effect

description.en: For each update or patch applied in the period, write down the system it went to, the version before and after, the vulnerability or advisory it addresses, the date and who applied it, and the verification that the change is actually in place — a rescan, a version query, or the deployment tooling's own confirmation. An update recorded as applied but never verified is the failure this task exists to catch, so the verification column is not optional and a blank in it is an open item. Attach the patch record for the period with the verification output behind it.

evidenceHint.en: Patch and update record for the period showing the system, the before and after version, the vulnerability addressed, the date and operator, and the verification that the change is in place

title.en: Reconcile the systems inventory against the scan reports and the findings still open

description.en: Take the inventory row by row and confirm each row appears in a scan run in the period; then take each open finding and confirm it carries an owner and a remediation date. The output is the findings report the control calls for, carrying two lists — inventoried systems that no scan covered, and vulnerabilities identified but not yet addressed — with the accountable owner beside each. Systems missing from the scans are reported as unknown rather than as clean, because that is the distinction a summary count destroys. Attach the report with the inventory and scan extracts it was derived from.

evidenceHint.en: Reconciliation report listing the inventoried systems no scan covered and the vulnerabilities still unaddressed, each with an accountable owner and a remediation date

text.en: Match every inventory row against the scans run in the period and list the rows with no coverage.
Collect the open findings from each scan report and de-duplicate them by system and vulnerability.
Set each open finding against the patch record to see whether it has already been closed.
Name an accountable owner and a remediation date against every finding still open.
Report the uncovered systems as unknown, separately from the systems that scanned clean.

title.en: Review the latest penetration test findings against the vulnerability management process

description.en: Read the most recent penetration test or vulnerability assessment report and ask what each finding says about the process rather than only about the system: was it something the scans should have detected and did not, was it a known finding that remediation had not yet reached, or was it genuinely new. Record the answer per finding, then turn the pattern into the process changes it implies — scan scope, credentialed access, remediation timescales — each with a named owner. Attach the assessment report alongside the analysis of what it revealed about the process.

evidenceHint.en: Penetration test or vulnerability assessment report with the per-finding analysis against the scanning and remediation process, and the process changes it produced with their owners

controls.title: Equipment Maintenance Compliance
controls.objective: To ensure all organizational equipment is maintained according to specified guidelines, preserving the availability, integrity, and confidentiality of information.
controls.successCriteria:
All equipment is maintained as per supplier recommendations and organizational guidelines.
Maintenance is carried out exclusively by authorized personnel, with all activities properly recorded.
Effective security measures are in place for off-premises maintenance, including confidentiality agreements.
Compliance with all maintenance requirements imposed by insurance is achieved.
Equipment inspection post-maintenance confirms no tampering and proper functionality.
Secure disposal or re-use of equipment is conducted as per organizational standards.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain a comprehensive list of all equipment under the organization’s maintenance program.
Collect maintenance records, including service schedules, repair logs, and authorization documents for maintenance personnel.
Acquire documentation of any equipment taken off-premises for maintenance, along with associated security measures.
Gather records of maintenance-related compliance with insurance requirements.
Obtain inspection reports of equipment post-maintenance to verify no tampering and proper functionality.
Secure disposal or re-use records for equipment marked for disposal.

Analysis:
Cross-check each piece of equipment against maintenance schedules and records to ensure compliance with supplier recommendations.
Verify that only authorized personnel have conducted maintenance and that all activities are properly documented.
Review security measures and confidentiality agreements related to off-premises maintenance.
Confirm adherence to insurance-mandated maintenance requirements.
Analyze post-maintenance inspection reports to ensure equipment integrity and functionality.
Examine disposal or re-use records for compliance with secure disposal measures.

Output:
A comprehensive spreadsheet or report detailing the maintenance status of each piece of equipment.
Documentation verifying the authorization and qualifications of maintenance personnel.
A report on the security measures for off-premises maintenance.
Compliance reports with insurance-imposed maintenance requirements.
Inspection reports for post-maintenance equipment checks.
Records of secure disposal or re-use of equipment.

title.en: Register every item in the maintenance programme with its service interval and insurance conditions

description.en: The auditor's first request is the comprehensive list of equipment under the maintenance programme, and this register is the denominator every later task counts against. Give each item a row carrying its type, location, owner, the maintenance interval its supplier recommends, the date it was last serviced and the date it is next due. Add a column for any maintenance condition an insurance policy imposes on that item — a required inspection frequency, an approved-servicer restriction — and read those conditions off the policy documents rather than from memory, because an item failing an insurance condition is uninsured rather than merely overdue. Facilities supplies the details for premises equipment. Attach the register with no blank interval or next-due date.

evidenceHint.en: Equipment maintenance register listing every item with its owner, location, supplier-recommended service interval, last-serviced date, next-due date and any insurance-imposed maintenance condition

text.en: Enumerate every item under the maintenance programme from the asset inventory and the service contracts in force.
Record the supplier-recommended service interval for each item from its manual or support contract.
Read each insurance policy for maintenance conditions and attach them to the items they bind.
Record the last-serviced date and derive the next-due date for every row in the register.
Date the register and hold it as the baseline the maintenance log is reconciled against.

title.en: Record which personnel and firms are authorised to maintain each class of equipment
