description.en: Maintenance carried out by somebody unauthorised is the failure this control exists to prevent, so produce the authorisation documentation an auditor asks for: a list naming each internal engineer and each external servicing firm, the equipment classes each may work on, the qualification or contract that authorises them, and the expiry date of that authorisation where it has one. An entry whose authorisation has lapsed is listed as lapsed rather than deleted, because the maintenance log is read against this list for the whole period. Attach the list with the certificates or contract references behind it.

evidenceHint.en: Authorised maintainer list giving each internal engineer and external firm, the equipment classes they may service, the qualification or contract authorising them and its expiry date

title.en: Set the security terms for equipment sent off the premises for maintenance

description.en: Equipment leaving the site carries its information with it, so record before the next despatch what has to happen: what protective measure applies to the information the item holds before it is released, who authorises the release, how the item is tracked while it is away, and the confidentiality obligation the receiving firm accepts. Hold a signed confidentiality agreement for every firm that receives equipment off-premises — Procurement obtains it as part of the servicing contract, and a firm without one cannot receive equipment until it is signed. Attach the off-premises procedure together with the signed agreements, one per receiving firm named on the authorised maintainer list, and the list of firms holding none.

evidenceHint.en: Off-premises maintenance procedure plus a signed confidentiality agreement for each external firm that receives equipment, with the list of firms holding none

title.en: Log every maintenance visit with the item, the engineer and the work performed

description.en: Each time an item is serviced or repaired, write a record carrying the equipment identifier, the date, the engineer or firm who performed the work, the authorisation they hold on the maintainer list, a description of what was done and whether any part or storage medium was replaced or removed. Where the item went off the premises, cross-reference the release authorisation and the return date. Where a supplier issues its own service report, file that rather than re-keying it, and record separately the work done in-house that generates no supplier paperwork. This log is what shows the programme is being run rather than merely scheduled. Attach the maintenance and repair log for the period under test.

evidenceHint.en: Maintenance and repair log for the period showing per event the equipment identifier, date, engineer or firm, their authorisation, the work performed and any part or medium removed

title.en: Inspect each item returned from maintenance for tampering and correct function

description.en: Before an item goes back into service after maintenance, check it and record the result: that the enclosure, seals and cabling show no sign of interference, that no unexpected hardware has been added, that the storage media present are the ones that left, and that the item operates correctly against the function it performs. Where a device holds information, read the software state as part of the same tamper check — an account added or a setting altered by the servicer is interference as much as a broken seal is. Record a pass or a finding per item, and record the disposition of every item carrying a finding rather than returning it to service unremarked. Attach the post-maintenance inspection reports for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Post-maintenance inspection reports, one per returned item, recording the physical tamper check, the software-state check, the functional check and a pass or finding

text.en: Check enclosure, seals and cabling for signs of interference before powering the item on.
Confirm the storage media present are the ones recorded as leaving with the item.
Test the item against the function it performs and record the observed outcome.
Check the item for accounts or settings the servicer left changed on it.
Record the disposition of every item whose inspection raised a finding.

title.en: Cross-check each item's completed maintenance against its interval and insurance conditions

description.en: Work down the register row by row and compare the maintenance actually recorded in the log against the supplier-recommended interval and the insurance condition that item carries, producing the maintenance status report the control calls for. Mark each item compliant, overdue, or serviced by an unauthorised party, and treat the third as a finding in its own right rather than folding it into overdue — they have different consequences. For every overdue item give the days overdue, the accountable owner and the date it is booked in where it has been; for every insurance breach, name the maintenance condition the policy imposed and the service that missed it. Attach the report with the register and log extracts it was built from.

evidenceHint.en: Maintenance status report covering every registered item with its due date, last service, a compliant, overdue or unauthorised-servicer verdict, and an owner plus booked date for each exception

controls.title: Active Network Asset Discovery
controls.objective: Ensure all assets connected to the enterprise's network are identified and catalogued daily.
controls.successCriteria:
The Active Discovery Tool identifies all known assets and potential rogue devices daily.
The tool's operation aligns with the configured schedule without any missed executions.
Discrepancies between the tool’s findings and the asset inventory are investigated and resolved.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the daily reports generated by the Active Discovery Tool.
Gather network configuration and topology documentation.
Retrieve logs from the Active Discovery Tool for audit period.

Analysis:
Verify the completeness and accuracy of the Active Discovery Tool's daily reports against network configuration and topology documentation.
Assess the Active Discovery Tool's logs to ensure it operated as scheduled daily.
Cross-check identified assets with the enterprise's asset inventory to identify any unregistered or rogue devices.

Output:
Daily Active Discovery Tool reports.
Comparison spreadsheet matching discovered assets against the official asset inventory.
Log analysis report confirming the tool's operational frequency and accuracy.

title.en: Record every network segment the discovery tool must scan, from the topology documentation

description.en: Derive the scan scope from the network configuration and topology documentation rather than from the tool's existing configuration — the segment nobody scans is the one the tool's own settings will never reveal. Record each subnet or VLAN, the site it serves, and whether it is in scope for active discovery, with a written reason against any exclusion such as an operational technology segment or a third-party managed range. This list is what each daily report's completeness is judged against. Attach the scope list cross-referenced to the topology documentation it was built from.

evidenceHint.en: Scan scope list of every subnet and VLAN with its site, an in-scope or excluded status and a written reason per exclusion, cross-referenced to the network topology documentation

title.en: Configure the discovery tool to run daily across every in-scope segment

description.en: Set the schedule and target ranges so each in-scope subnet is covered every day, and configure the tool to emit a report per run and to log run start, completion and failure. Retain that run log across the audit period, because it is what tells a missing report from a missed run. Attach the schedule and target-range configuration beside the scope list so the two can be read against each other and any uncovered segment shows up as a difference.

evidenceHint.en: Discovery tool schedule and target-range configuration showing daily coverage of every in-scope segment, together with the run-log destination and its retention across the audit period

title.en: File the daily discovery report for every day of the period

description.en: Keep the report the tool produces each day, carrying the run date, the ranges scanned and the assets found, and retain the full set for the audit period rather than the most recent few — the population is what shows the tool ran daily, and a report set with holes is itself the finding. Where a run failed or covered only part of the scope, keep the partial output and note why instead of replacing it with a rerun that hides the gap. Attach the daily reports for the period under test.

evidenceHint.en: The full set of daily Active Discovery Tool reports for the period, one per day, each showing run date, ranges scanned and assets discovered, with partial runs retained and annotated

title.en: Match each day's discovered assets against the asset inventory and investigate the unmatched

description.en: Reconcile every discovered address or hostname to a record in the asset inventory. Devices with no inventory record are the potential rogue devices this control exists to surface: capture the address, the MAC or hostname, the segment and the time first seen, and name who is investigating. Inventory records that no scan has seen across the period are the other half of the discrepancy and belong in the same sheet. Attach the comparison showing each unmatched device and how it was resolved — registered, removed from the network, or still open.

evidenceHint.en: Comparison spreadsheet matching discovered assets to asset inventory records, listing every unmatched device with segment, first-seen time, named investigator and resolution

text.en: Load the day's discovery report alongside the current asset inventory export.
Match every discovered address or hostname to an asset inventory record.
List unmatched devices with their segment, MAC or hostname and the time first seen.
List inventory records that no scan observed at any point in the period.
Name an investigator per unmatched device and record whether it was registered or removed.

title.en: Account for every day in the period with no completed discovery run

description.en: Read the tool's own logs across the audit period and count completed runs against the days in scope, then explain each shortfall — an outage, a credential or licence expiry, a scope change, or a scan that started and never finished. A day accounted for is not the same as a day scanned, so record which segments went unobserved on each missed day, which is what lets the resulting asset gap be sized rather than merely noted. Attach the log analysis stating runs expected, runs completed and a cause per missed day.

evidenceHint.en: Log analysis report for the period giving runs expected against runs completed, and the cause plus the unscanned segments for every missed or partial day

controls.title: Web Filtering Compliance
controls.objective: Ensure that access to external websites is effectively managed to minimize exposure to malicious content and adherence to organizational web filtering policies.
controls.successCriteria:
Web filtering tools are configured in compliance with the organizational policy.
No unauthorized access to blocked websites or categories is detected.
All personnel have received and completed training on web filtering and secure use of online resources.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the configuration settings of web filtering tools used on all organizational devices (laptops and mobile phones).
Gather a list of blocked websites and categories as per the web filtering policy.
Collect records of user access logs to external websites.
Acquire training attendance records and materials related to web filtering and secure online resource usage.

Analysis:
Review the configuration settings of web filtering tools to ensure they align with the defined policy (e.g., blocking malicious websites, restricting access to certain categories).
Cross-reference the list of blocked websites and categories with those accessed in user logs to identify any policy violations or lapses in filtering.
Analyze training records to confirm all personnel have received appropriate training on web filtering and secure online resource usage.

Output:
A report detailing the configuration settings of web filtering tools.
A spreadsheet comparing blocked websites/categories with user access logs.
A summary of training records and materials related to web filtering and online resource usage.

title.en: List every laptop and mobile device in scope and the filtering tool that enforces on it

description.en: Web filtering only works on devices it actually reaches, so build the coverage list first: one row per organisational laptop and mobile phone, giving the user, the operating system, the filtering tool or profile that enforces on it and the date that tool last saw the device report in. A device present in the asset inventory but absent from every filtering console is the gap this task exists to surface — record it as uncovered with an owner rather than omitting it. This list is the denominator the configuration reconciliation and the access-log comparison both run against. Attach the coverage list with the uncovered devices identified.

evidenceHint.en: Device coverage list naming every organisational laptop and mobile device, its user, the enforcing filtering tool or profile and its last check-in, with uncovered devices flagged and owned

title.en: Record the site categories and named sites the web filtering policy blocks

description.en: Produce the blocklist an auditor asks for as its own artifact: every category the policy denies, every specifically named site denied outside a category, and against each entry the reason the policy gives for the denial — malicious content is the one the objective names. Where the policy denies a category to most users but permits it to a named group, record both, because access the blocklist does not describe reads as a filtering lapse when the logs are compared against it. This list is the standard the tools' live configuration is compared against, so it has to name categories and sites rather than describe intent. Attach the issued blocklist with the date it was issued.

evidenceHint.en: Issued web filtering blocklist giving each blocked category and named site with the policy reason, and any category the policy permits to a named group of users

title.en: Compare external-site access logs against the blocklist and disposition every hit

description.en: Pull the user access logs to external websites for the period and test them against the blocklist: every request to a blocked category or named site that was allowed through is a hit, and each hit is dispositioned as access the blocklist records that group as permitted, as a filtering lapse where the tool should have blocked it and did not, or as a policy violation referred onward. Keep the last two apart, because a lapse is fixed in the tool and a violation is handled with the user. Where a device on the coverage list produced no log at all for the period, record that as its own finding rather than reading the absence as clean. Attach the comparison spreadsheet with the dispositions.

evidenceHint.en: Access-log comparison spreadsheet for the period listing each request to a blocked category or site with its device, user and disposition as permitted access, filtering lapse or policy violation, plus the devices producing no log

text.en: Extract external-site access logs for the period from every filtering tool on the coverage list.
Match each logged request against the blocked categories and named sites in the blocklist.
Disposition each hit as permitted access, a filtering lapse or a policy violation.
Raise a configuration fix for each lapse and refer each violation to the accountable manager.
Record any device on the coverage list that produced no log for the period as a finding.

title.en: Deliver the web filtering and secure online resource training and record attendance

description.en: Run the training session covering what the filtering blocks and why, how to request an exception, and how to use online resources safely, then record attendance against the staff roster rather than against the attendee list — the artifact that matters is the list of people who have not completed it. Keep the materials used, dated to the session, since the auditor asks for the materials as well as the records. Where a new joiner has arrived since the last session, show either their completion or their scheduled date. Attach the attendance record, the roster reconciliation naming everyone outstanding, and the materials delivered.

evidenceHint.en: Training attendance record reconciled against the staff roster, naming everyone outstanding with a scheduled date, together with the dated training materials delivered

title.en: Reconcile each filtering tool's live configuration against the issued blocklist

description.en: Export the configuration actually in force from every filtering tool on the coverage list and read it against the issued blocklist entry by entry — a tool whose documentation matches the policy while its running configuration does not is exactly the failure this task catches. Produce the configuration report the control calls for, recording per tool which blocked categories and named sites are enforced, which are absent, and which rules exist in the tool but appear nowhere in the blocklist. Carry in the devices the coverage list marked uncovered, because a correct configuration that reaches no device blocks nothing. Attach the report with the raw configuration exports behind it.

evidenceHint.en: Web filtering configuration report per tool listing enforced, missing and undeclared rules against the issued blocklist, the raw configuration exports behind it, and the devices covered by no tool

controls.title: Intellectual Property Rights Compliance
controls.objective: To ensure that the organization's procedures and practices effectively protect its intellectual property rights and comply with relevant laws and internal policies.
controls.successCriteria:
All intellectual property assets are properly documented, licensed, and used in compliance with relevant laws and internal policies.
There are no instances of unauthorized use, duplication, or transfer of intellectual property assets.
Staff are adequately trained and contractually bound to uphold intellectual property rights.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain a list of all digital and physical assets that are considered intellectual property (e.g., software, documents, media files).
Gather copies of all software licenses, ownership proofs (like patents, copyrights, trademarks registrations), and user agreements.
Collect recent audit logs and reports related to intellectual property assets.

Analysis:
Verify each asset against the intellectual property register to confirm proper documentation and licensing.
Cross-check the software licenses and user agreements to ensure they are up-to-date and in compliance with the terms.
Review audit logs for unauthorized access, duplication, or transfer of intellectual property assets.
Assess staff training records and contracts for inclusion of intellectual property rights awareness and obligations.

Output:
A verified spreadsheet of all intellectual property assets with corresponding licenses and ownership proofs.
A report on the compliance status of each asset with regards to intellectual property laws and policies.
A summary of staff training and contractual commitments concerning intellectual property rights.

title.en: Inventory every digital and physical asset the organisation holds as intellectual property

description.en: Build the intellectual property register: one row per asset — software the organisation wrote or licenses, documents, designs, media files, databases, and any physical embodiment — carrying what the asset is, where it is held, the business owner, and whether the organisation owns it or holds it under licence from someone else. That ownership column is what routes each row to the proof it needs in the next task, so a blank there stalls the register. Include assets held on third-party platforms and in team-controlled repositories, because those are the rows an inventory drawn from the asset management system alone will miss. Attach the register with the date it was compiled.

evidenceHint.en: Dated intellectual property register listing each digital and physical asset with its location, business owner and an owned-or-licensed value populated for every row

text.en: List the software, documents, designs, media and databases held.
Record where each asset is held and who owns it in the business.
Mark each row as owned by the organisation or held under licence.
Add assets held on third-party platforms and in team repositories.
Record the physical embodiments of intellectual property held on site.

title.en: Record the licence or ownership proof held for each asset in the register

description.en: Against every register row, attach the document that establishes the organisation's position: the software licence and its entitlement count for assets held under licence, and the patent, copyright registration, trademark certificate, assignment or contributor agreement for assets the organisation owns. Record the term or expiry where the document carries one and the number of seats or installations the licence permits, since those are the values the compliance check reads. A row whose proof cannot be produced is recorded as unevidenced rather than as compliant — that list is the first output of this task. Attach the completed register with the proofs indexed against it.

evidenceHint.en: Intellectual property register with the licence, patent, registration or assignment attached per asset, showing term or expiry and permitted seats, plus the list of rows carrying no proof

title.en: Review the audit logs for unauthorised use, duplication or transfer of intellectual property

description.en: For the period, pull the access, copy and transfer logs covering the systems the register says hold intellectual property, and read them for the three events the control names: use by accounts outside the authorised group, duplication to unmanaged locations, and transfer outside the organisation. Disposition every hit either as authorised — naming the approval, project or contract that covers it — or as an exception referred for investigation. Where a holding system produces no usable log, record that as a finding against the system rather than leaving its rows unexamined. Attach the log extract with the dispositioned exception list; an empty exception list evidences nothing unless the extract shows the logs were actually read.

evidenceHint.en: Access, copy and transfer log extract for the systems holding intellectual property, each hit dispositioned as authorised or referred, and every system that produced no usable log named

title.en: Record each staff member's intellectual property training and contractual acknowledgement

description.en: Produce the staff summary the control outputs: per individual, the intellectual property awareness training completed and when, and the signed contract or agreement clause binding them to the organisation's intellectual property obligations. Cover everyone the organisation's intellectual property obligations bind, and where an agreement extends them to contractors handling registered assets, cover those individuals on the same basis. Rows missing either the training or the signed clause are what this task hands to remediation. Attach the summary with the training completion records and contract clause references behind it.

evidenceHint.en: Staff summary listing per individual the intellectual property training completed with date and the signed contractual clause reference, with the gaps named

title.en: Verify each asset's licence and user agreement against its terms and report the compliance status

description.en: Go through the register asset by asset and check three things against the proof attached to it: that the licence or registration is still in term, that actual usage sits inside what it permits — seat counts, installation counts, permitted purposes and territories — and that the user agreement in force matches the version held on file. Record a compliant, breached or unevidenced verdict per asset, naming the specific term breached where there is one, and give every non-compliant row an owner and a remediation. This is the per-asset compliance report the control outputs. Attach it with the usage figures it was checked against.

evidenceHint.en: Per-asset compliance report giving a compliant, breached or unevidenced verdict with the term breached, the usage figures checked against it, and an owner and remediation for each exception

text.en: Check each licence and registration is still within its stated term.
Compare actual seat, installation or usage counts with what is permitted.
Confirm the user agreement in force matches the version held on file.
Record a compliant, breached or unevidenced verdict for each asset.
Name an owner and a remediation against every non-compliant row.

controls.title: Network Security Compliance
controls.objective: Ensure the security of information in networks and protect connected services from unauthorized access.
controls.successCriteria:
Network diagrams and configuration files are current and accurately reflect the network setup.
Network security procedures and controls are effectively implemented and align with organizational policies.
Network security monitoring indicates no unauthorized access and proper handling of security incidents.
Controls for virtualized networks are robust and comply with security standards.
All change requests and executed changes are in accordance with the organization’s change management procedures.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain an updated list of network devices, including routers, switches, and firewalls.
Collect recent network diagrams and configuration files for all network devices.
Gather documentation of network security procedures and controls, including segregation of duties between network and ICT system operations.
Retrieve logs and records of network security monitoring, including logs from firewalls, intrusion detection systems, and access control lists.
Acquire details of implemented controls for virtualized networks, such as SDN and SD-WAN configurations.
Get a record of all change requests related to network security since the last audit.

Analysis:
Review network diagrams and configuration files to confirm they match actual network device settings and are up-to-date.
Evaluate the adequacy of network security procedures and controls, focusing on segregation of duties, authentication mechanisms, and network device hardening.
Analyze network security monitoring logs to identify any anomalies or unauthorized access attempts.
Assess the effectiveness of controls in place for virtualized networks, ensuring logical separation and security measures align with policy.
Compare change requests against executed changes in network configurations to verify adherence to change management procedures.

Output:
Compiled network diagrams and configuration files.
Report on the review of network security procedures and controls.
Analysis of network security monitoring logs.
Evaluation report of virtualized network controls.
Spreadsheet or report correlating change requests with executed changes.

title.en: Inventory the routers, switches and firewalls making up the network

description.en: List every network device in service — routers, switches, firewalls, and their virtual equivalents where the network is software-defined — with its role, its physical or logical location, its management address, its firmware version and the owner accountable for it. Build it from the devices actually reachable on the management network rather than from the asset register, so a device that somebody installed and nobody recorded appears as a row. This list is the population the diagrams, the configuration capture and the change correlation all run against. Attach the dated device list.

evidenceHint.en: Dated network device list covering routers, switches and firewalls with each device's role, location, management address, firmware version and accountable owner

title.en: Update the network diagrams and capture the running configuration of every device on the list

description.en: Redraw the network diagrams so they show the segments, trust boundaries and connections as they exist now, and take a configuration backup from each device on the list on the same date so the two can be read against each other. Where the diagram and the running configuration disagree — a segment that no longer exists, a link the diagram does not show — correct the diagram and record what was found, because that discrepancy list is as much the evidence this task produces as the diagram is. Attach the dated diagrams with the configuration set they were reconciled against.

evidenceHint.en: Dated network diagrams with the matching per-device configuration capture, and the list of discrepancies found between them with how each was resolved

text.en: Take a configuration backup from every device on the list in a single dated run.
Redraw the diagrams to show the current segments, trust boundaries and inter-site links.
Read each device's running configuration against the segment the diagram places it in.
Correct the diagram wherever it disagrees with the configuration and record what differed.
Date the diagram set and store it beside the configuration capture it was reconciled against.

title.en: Document the network security procedures, including the split of duties between network and system operations

description.en: Issue the procedures governing how the network is operated and secured: who may change network configuration and who may change the ICT systems attached to it, and why those are different people; how administrators authenticate to network devices; and the hardening baseline each device class is built to. State the segregation explicitly rather than leaving it implicit in job titles, because that separation is exactly what the review will look for and cannot infer. Attach the issued procedure version together with the hardening baseline it references.

evidenceHint.en: Issued network security procedure covering the segregation of network and ICT system operations duties, administrator authentication, and the device hardening baseline

title.en: Record the controls keeping virtualised networks logically separated

description.en: Where the network is virtualised — software-defined networking, SD-WAN overlays, virtual switching, cloud virtual networks — record what enforces the logical separation between tenants, environments or trust zones: the segmentation constructs in use, the policy governing traffic between them, and the administrative boundary controlling who can change them. Export the configuration that implements it rather than describing the intent, and name any pair of environments the configuration does not in fact keep apart. Attach the record with the SDN or SD-WAN configuration extracts behind it.

evidenceHint.en: Record of the virtualised network controls with the SDN or SD-WAN configuration extracts showing the segmentation constructs, the inter-zone traffic policy and the administrative boundary

title.en: Triage the network security monitoring alerts and record the disposition of each

description.en: Each period, work through what the firewall, intrusion detection and access-control-list logs raised and record a disposition against every alert examined: expected traffic, a misconfiguration to correct, or suspected unauthorised access referred as an incident. Keep the log extract the triage was done from alongside the dispositions, so that a quiet period is evidenced by logs that were read rather than by an absence of reports. Attach the extract and the disposition list for the period, with the incidents referred from it.

evidenceHint.en: Firewall, intrusion-detection and access-control-list extract for the period with a disposition recorded against every alert triaged, and the incidents referred from it

title.en: Correlate every network change request against the configuration change actually executed

description.en: Take the network change requests raised since the last audit and set them against the changes the device configurations actually show, using the dated configuration captures as the comparison. Produce the correlation sheet with three outcomes per row: requested and executed as approved, requested but never executed, and executed with no request behind it. The third is the finding this task exists to surface — record the device, the change, when it appeared and who made it, and refer it under the change management procedure. Attach the correlation sheet with the change records and configuration differences it was built from.

evidenceHint.en: Correlation sheet setting each network change request against the executed configuration change, flagging requests never executed and changes made with no request, with the configuration differences behind them

text.en: List the network change requests raised since the last audit with their approval state.
Compare the dated configuration captures to find the changes actually made in the same period.
Match each executed change to the request that approved it.
Flag the requests that were approved but never executed.
Record device, change, date and author for every change with no request, and refer it.

controls.title: Function Segregation and Security Control
controls.objective: Ensure that primary functions with different security levels on the same system component are either isolated from each other, or all functions are secured to the level required by the function with the highest security need. This control aims to prevent primary functions with lower security needs from affecting the security of functions with higher security needs.
controls.successCriteria:
All system components with multiple primary functions are either effectively isolated, or their security measures comply with the highest security level required.
Documentation and configuration analysis confirm that lower security functions do not compromise the security of higher security functions.
Any discrepancies or non-compliances are identified and documented for further action.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain a list of all system components hosting multiple primary functions.
Collect configuration details of these system components, including security settings and access controls.
Gather documentation or logs that demonstrate the isolation or security measures implemented for these functions.

Analysis:
Review the list of system components to identify those with multiple primary functions.
For each system component, analyze the configuration details to verify that either isolation is in place, or security settings meet the requirements of the highest security function.
Examine the documentation or logs to validate that the implemented measures effectively segregate or secure the functions as per the criteria.

Output:
A detailed report of system components with multiple primary functions and their respective security configurations.
An analysis report verifying the adequacy of segregation or security measures.
Compliance or discrepancy notes for each system component reviewed.

title.en: Identify every system component that hosts more than one primary function

description.en: Work through the asset inventory and pull out the components — servers, appliances, virtual hosts, container platforms — that carry more than one primary function, and give each one a row naming every primary function it hosts and the owner of each. A component whose second function is only implied belongs on the list as much as one where the co-tenancy was designed: a database sharing a host with a web front end, a management agent that also terminates remote access. This list is the population every later task works from, so a component missing here is a component nobody analyses. Attach the list carrying the date it was compiled.

evidenceHint.en: List of system components hosting multiple primary functions, one row per component naming each function it hosts and the function owner, carrying the date compiled

text.en: Filter the asset inventory to components serving more than one named business or technical function.
Add hosts where a management, backup or monitoring function runs alongside the primary workload.
Name every primary function per component and the owner accountable for it.
Date the list and hold it as the population the configuration review runs against.

title.en: Rate the security level of each primary function and record the governing level per component

description.en: For every function on the list, record the security level it requires — the sensitivity of the data it handles and the exposure it carries — and then record, per component, the highest of those levels. That highest level is the yardstick the component's configuration is judged against later, so it is settled once here rather than re-argued during the review. Where two functions on one component sit at different levels, note the difference explicitly: that pairing is exactly what the control exists to catch. Attach the rated list showing every function and the governing level derived from it.

evidenceHint.en: Rated function list giving each primary function's required security level and, per component, the highest level that governs it

title.en: Record the isolation or the uplift chosen for each multi-function component

description.en: Each component has to end at one of two positions: its functions are isolated from each other, or every function on it is secured to the governing level recorded earlier. Write down which position applies and what implements it — the virtualisation or container boundary, the network or process separation, the access controls that keep the lower-security function away from the higher — naming the specific setting or rule rather than the intent. Where neither position holds today, record the gap with a named owner and the remediation agreed for it, rather than a description of the plan. Attach the decision record covering every component on the list.

evidenceHint.en: Decision record naming, per multi-function component, whether isolation or uplift to the governing level applies and the specific setting, boundary or access control implementing it

text.en: Choose isolation or uplift for each component and record which position applies.
Name the mechanism enforcing it — hypervisor, container, network or process boundary.
Record the access controls preventing the lower-security function reaching the higher one.
Where neither position holds, record the gap with a named owner and the remediation agreed.

title.en: Capture the security configuration and isolation evidence for each multi-function component

description.en: Export, per component, the configuration details an auditor asks for — security settings, access controls, and the log or documentation showing the isolation actually operating — and hold them together as one evidence set for the period. Take the export from the running system rather than from a build document, and record the date and the command or console it came from so the set can be reproduced. A component whose isolation leaves no machine trace needs a written statement of how it was observed and by whom, in place of the export. Attach the evidence set.

evidenceHint.en: Per-component configuration export covering security settings and access controls, plus the isolation logs or documentation, each labelled with its capture date and source

title.en: Verify each component's configuration against the security level of its highest function

description.en: Read the captured configuration for every component against the governing security level recorded for it and write a verdict per component: adequate segregation, adequate uplift, or a discrepancy. Where a discrepancy is found, say which lower-security function is able to affect the higher one and through what — that sentence is what makes the finding fixable, and its absence is why such findings recur. Carry every discrepancy out with an accountable owner and an agreed remediation. Attach the analysis report with the compliance or discrepancy note for each component reviewed.

evidenceHint.en: Analysis report with one compliance or discrepancy note per multi-function component, naming for each discrepancy the exposed function, the route to it and the remediation owner

controls.title: Internal Control Deficiency Assessment and Communication
controls.objective: To ensure timely evaluation and communication of internal control deficiencies to the responsible parties, including senior management and the board of directors, and to monitor the effectiveness of corrective actions.
controls.successCriteria:
All identified internal control deficiencies are assessed and reported accurately.
Communications regarding deficiencies are timely and directed to the appropriate parties.
Corrective actions are effectively implemented and monitored, with progress aligning with the organization's internal control standards.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain reports or records of the latest evaluations of internal control efficiencies.
Gather communications related to identified deficiencies, directed towards responsible parties, senior management, and the board of directors.
Collect documentation on corrective action plans and progress updates.

Analysis:
Review evaluation reports to confirm if internal control deficiencies were identified and assessed appropriately.
Examine communication records to verify that deficiencies were communicated in a timely manner to the correct parties.
Assess corrective action plans and progress reports to ensure deficiencies are being addressed effectively and within a reasonable timeframe.

Output:
Compiled list of identified internal control deficiencies.
Record of communications regarding deficiencies.
Summary report on the status of corrective actions.

title.en: Register every internal control deficiency identified in the period with its assessed severity

description.en: Draw the deficiencies from the internal control evaluations that identified them and give each one a row carrying the reference, the control it affects, the date identified, the source that identified it, a description of the deficiency, and the severity assessed for it. Record the basis on which severity was assessed rather than the label alone, because severity is what decides who has to be told and how quickly. This register is the compiled deficiency list the control outputs and the population every later task runs against. Attach it with the evaluation reports the rows were drawn from.

evidenceHint.en: Dated internal control deficiency register with the affected control, date identified, identifying source, description, assessed severity and the basis for that severity, referenced to the evaluation reports behind it

text.en: Gather the internal control evaluations covering the period under test.
Raise a register row for each deficiency those sources identified.
Record the control affected and the date the deficiency was identified.
Assess a severity and record the basis on which it was assessed.
Reference each row back to the evaluation report it came from.

title.en: Record the reporting route and timing each deficiency severity requires

description.en: Set out which parties a deficiency must be reported to at each severity — the control owner, responsible line management, senior management, and the board of directors — and the time within which each must be told, which is where the organisation states what it means by timely at that severity. The control's whole timeliness and appropriateness test is read against this, so a severity band with no stated recipient or no stated time cannot be tested and is a gap to close here rather than at review. Attach the routing table with the authority behind each threshold.

evidenceHint.en: Deficiency reporting routing table giving, per severity band, the parties to be informed up to senior management and the board and the time limit for each, with the authority it derives from

title.en: Log each deficiency communication with its recipient, date and content

description.en: Every time a deficiency is reported onward, keep the record: which deficiency, who it went to by name and role, the date and channel, and what was actually said — the report, paper or minute itself rather than a note that a conversation happened. Board and senior management communications are usually minuted, so cite the meeting and agenda item; communications to control owners usually are not, and this is where they get captured. Where a deficiency was reported more than once as it escalated, hold each communication separately with its own date so the escalation path can be read. Attach the communication records for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Deficiency communication records for the period showing the deficiency reference, named recipient and role, date, channel and the report or minute item that carried it

title.en: Record the corrective action plan and progress updates for each open deficiency

description.en: Against every deficiency in the register that is not already closed, hold a corrective action plan naming what will be done, the owner accountable for doing it, the target completion date, and the evidence that will show it is complete. Update each plan on the cycle the organisation runs, recording the date of the update, the progress made, and any revised target date with the reason it moved — a target that has slipped three times with no recorded reason is exactly the signal this record exists to make visible. Attach the plans with their dated progress updates for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Corrective action plans for every open deficiency naming owner, target date and the completion evidence expected, plus dated progress updates and the reason recorded against each revised target

title.en: Test each deficiency's communication date and recipient against the route its severity requires

description.en: Take the register and the communication log together and, per deficiency, record the date it was identified, the date each required party was told, the elapsed time between them, and whether the parties told match the routing table for its severity. Mark each row on time and complete, late, or not communicated, and record for every exception the reason and the owner who will close it. Read the deficiencies whose severity required senior management or board notification first: those are where the control's objective bites and where an omission matters most. Attach the timeliness test with the register and communication references behind each row.

evidenceHint.en: Communication timeliness test listing per deficiency the identification date, the date each required party was told, elapsed time against the required limit, and a verdict with an owner for each exception

text.en: Set each deficiency's identification date beside its communication dates.
Check the parties told against the routing table for that severity.
Calculate elapsed time and compare it with the limit the route sets.
Mark each row on time and complete, late, or not communicated.
Record the reason and a named owner for every exception marked.

title.en: Assess corrective action progress against plan and report the deficiencies still open

description.en: For every corrective action, compare where it actually stands against its plan and target date, and check the completed ones against the evidence the plan said would show completion — an action closed without that evidence is reported as unevidenced rather than as done. Produce the status summary the control outputs: actions completed, actions in progress and within target, actions overdue with their age, and the deficiencies that remain open with the risk they leave standing. Escalate the overdue set through the routing table rather than only listing it here. Attach the summary with the completion evidence it relies on.

evidenceHint.en: Corrective action status summary showing completed actions with their completion evidence, actions in progress against target, overdue actions with their age, and the deficiencies still open

controls.title: Malware Protection Compliance
controls.objective: To ensure that malware protection measures are effectively implemented and maintained across all IT systems and devices.
controls.successCriteria:
All IT systems and devices have malware protection measures installed, correctly configured, and regularly updated.
Malware scans are conducted as per the prescribed frequency and scope, with appropriate actions taken on any detections.
All users have received and understood malware protection training.
Any instances of disabled malware protection measures are fully compliant with the organizational policy, including proper authorization and justification.
Procedures for obtaining files and software from external sources are robust and effectively mitigate risks of malware introduction.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain a list of all IT systems and devices, categorized by type (e.g., endpoint devices, servers, network devices).
Gather current configurations and settings of malware detection and prevention tools across these systems and devices.
Collect recent reports of malware scans and their results.
Acquire records of user awareness training sessions and materials related to malware protection.
Retrieve documentation on procedures for disabling malware protection measures and their justifications, if any.

Analysis:
For each system and device, verify if malware protection tools are installed, correctly configured, and updated regularly.
Compare malware scan reports with the expected frequency and scope of scanning as per the policy.
Review user training records to ensure all users have undergone appropriate malware awareness training.
Analyze the documentation of disabled malware protection measures to confirm they comply with policy requirements, including the authorization and justification process.
Examine the procedures for obtaining files and software from external networks or media to ensure protective measures against malware are in place.

Output:
A detailed report listing the malware protection status of each system and device.
A summary of findings from the review of malware scan reports.
A compliance report on user awareness training related to malware protection.
An assessment report on the authorization and justification of disabled malware protection measures.
An evaluation report on the procedures for external file and software acquisition and their compliance with malware protection standards.

title.en: Inventory every system and device with the malware protection installed on it

description.en: Build the population the whole control is measured over: one row per endpoint, server and network device, categorised by type, giving the malware detection or prevention tool installed, its version, and the date its detection definitions last updated. A device with no tool is the most important row in the inventory — record it as none rather than leaving the cell empty, and give it an owner. Where a platform cannot run the standard tool, say what compensating measure applies instead. Build the inventory from the management consoles and the asset register together rather than from either alone, since a console only knows the agents that report in. Attach the dated inventory.

evidenceHint.en: Dated inventory of every IT system and device by type, giving the malware protection tool and version installed, the definition date, and an explicit none plus an owner where no tool is present

text.en: List endpoints, servers and network devices from the asset register, categorised by device type.
Read each malware tool's management console for the agents that are actually reporting in.
Record the tool, version and definition date against every device, or none where absent.
Name an owner for each device carrying no protection and any compensating measure in place.
Date the inventory and hold it as the population the later tasks are counted against.

title.en: Set the scan frequency, scope and definition-update interval for each device type

description.en: Write the standard the scan reports will be read against, in values rather than principles: for each device type in the inventory, the scan frequency, what a scan covers, the maximum age permitted for detection definitions, and the action required when something is found — quarantine, removal, escalation. Cover in the same standard how files and software brought in from external networks or removable media are handled before use, because that is where malware enters an otherwise well-scanned estate. State where a device type is exempt from a requirement and why, since an unstated exemption reads as a failure every cycle. Attach the issued standard with a complete row for every device type the inventory contains.

evidenceHint.en: Issued malware protection standard with a row per device type giving scan frequency, scan scope, maximum definition age and action on detection, plus the handling required for files and software from external networks or removable media

title.en: Record every instance of disabled malware protection with its justification and approver

description.en: Malware protection is sometimes turned off legitimately, and the register of those instances is what separates an authorised exception from an unnoticed gap. Each time protection is disabled or a scanning exclusion added, write a row carrying the device, exactly what was disabled, the technical justification, the person who approved it, the date it was disabled and, where protection has since been restored, the date of that restoration. Work the open rows each period so an exception nobody has revisited is visible as still open. An exclusion found with no approver behind it is recorded as unauthorised — that flag list is the finding this register produces. Attach the register for the period with the authorisation records behind it.

evidenceHint.en: Disabled-protection and exclusion register for the period showing per entry the device, what was disabled, the justification, the approver, the date it was disabled and the restoration date where protection has been restored, with unauthorised entries flagged

title.en: Record each malware scan run and the disposition of every detection

description.en: For the period under test, keep the scan reports showing which devices were scanned, when, and against what scope, together with what happened to each detection — quarantined, removed, restored, or escalated as an incident. Export these from the management console rather than summarising them by hand, and cover separately any device whose scans run outside that console. A device present in the inventory that appears in no scan report for the period is reported as unscanned rather than omitted, because an absent row is otherwise indistinguishable from a clean one. Attach the scan reports for the period with the detection dispositions.

evidenceHint.en: Malware scan reports for the period giving per device the scan date and scope, plus the disposition of every detection, and the list of inventoried devices appearing in no report

title.en: Deliver malware awareness training and record completion against the user roster

description.en: Run the user awareness training covering how malware arrives, what the standard requires of users handling files from external networks and removable media, and how to report a suspected infection. Record completion against the full user roster so the artifact names the people outstanding rather than only the people who attended, and keep the materials used, dated, because the auditor asks for materials as well as records. Where a user cannot complete the session within the period, record their scheduled date against their name. Attach the completion record reconciled to the roster together with the training materials.

evidenceHint.en: Malware awareness training completion record reconciled against the full user roster, naming everyone outstanding with a scheduled date, plus the dated training materials delivered

title.en: Test each inventoried device's tool status, definition currency and last scan date

description.en: Take the inventory row by row and read from the device or its management console what is true today — whether the tool is installed and running, how old its definitions are, and when it last completed a scan of the required scope — then score each row against the standard's values for that device type. Produce the malware protection status report the control calls for, carrying a pass or a named failure mode per device: no tool, tool present but stopped, definitions beyond the maximum age, or no scan within the required frequency. Give each failure an owner and a remediation date. Attach the report with the console output it was derived from.

evidenceHint.en: Malware protection status report covering every inventoried device with its observed tool state, definition age and last scan date, a pass or named failure mode against the standard, and an owner plus remediation date per failure

text.en: Read the running state of the malware protection tool on every device in the inventory.
Record the age of each device's detection definitions on the day of the test.
Record the date each device last completed a scan of the required scope.
Score every row against the standard's values for that device type.
Assign an owner and a remediation date to each device that failed.

controls.title: Information Security Training Compliance
controls.objective: To ensure all personnel receive appropriate information security training and are aware of information security policies relevant to their job function.
controls.successCriteria:
All personnel have completed the required information security training.
Training materials adequately cover the organization's information security policy, specific policies, and procedures.
Post-training assessments indicate effective knowledge transfer and understanding of information security responsibilities.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the training records database, including records for new hires and existing staff.
Collect documentation of the information security awareness, education, and training program, including materials used (e.g., presentations, e-learning modules).
Gather results of assessments or quizzes conducted after training sessions.

Analysis:
Review the training records to verify that all personnel have completed the required information security training.
Analyze training materials to ensure they cover key topics: organization's information security policy, topic-specific policies, and relevant procedures.
Assess the effectiveness of training by analyzing the results of post-training assessments or quizzes.

Output:
A report detailing the completion status of training for all personnel.
A review summary of the training materials for completeness and relevance.
An analysis report of post-training assessment results.

title.en: List the personnel owed security training and what each job function is required to take

description.en: The completion figure this control reports is a fraction, and this task builds its denominator. Take the current personnel record — employees, contractors and anyone else holding access — and record against each person their job function and the training that function requires, because the control asks for training appropriate to the job rather than one course for everybody. Flag new hires with their start date, since the records for new hires are checked separately from those for existing staff. Where a job function has no training assigned to it, record that as a gap for Management to resolve rather than defaulting those people to the general course and reporting them complete. Attach the population list with the date it was extracted.

evidenceHint.en: Dated personnel training population list naming, per person, their job function, the training that function requires, and whether they are a new hire with their start date

title.en: Map each module of the training material to the policy or procedure it teaches

description.en: The material is tested for coverage of the organisation's information security policy, the topic-specific policies and the relevant procedures — a check that cannot be made by reading a slide deck end to end. Produce the coverage map instead: one row per policy or procedure in scope, the module and the screen or slide that teaches it, and the version of the material the mapping was made against. Rows left with no module against them are the material's gaps and are the output this task exists to produce, so carry them into a change request against the material rather than reporting the map as complete. Attach the map naming the material version it describes.

evidenceHint.en: Coverage map linking every information security policy and procedure in scope to the training module and screen that teaches it, naming the material version and listing the policies no module covers

text.en: List the information security policy, the topic-specific policies and the procedures in scope.
Walk the training material and record which module and screen addresses each of them.
Record the material version the mapping was made against so it can be re-checked later.
Raise a change request against the material for every policy with no module behind it.

title.en: Build the post-training assessment so every question traces to a module of the material

description.en: Completion says a person sat the course; the assessment is what evidences that the knowledge transferred. Build the question set so each question is traceable to a module of the material and, through the coverage map, to the policy it teaches — that traceability is what later allows a low score to be read as a training gap rather than as a hard question. Record on the published set the score that is treated as demonstrating understanding, so that results are comparable across the whole population and between periods rather than read impressionistically. Attach the published question set with the per-question mapping and that score recorded on it.

evidenceHint.en: Published post-training assessment question set with each question mapped to the training module it tests, carrying the score treated as demonstrating understanding

title.en: Record each person's training completion and assessment score in the training records

description.en: As each person completes the training, write to the training records database the version of the course they took, the completion date, the assessment score and the pass or fail outcome. New hires are recorded against their start date so that the interval between joining and completing is visible in the record rather than reconstructed afterwards. Where somebody takes the assessment more than once, keep every attempt rather than only the passing one, because the retake pattern is part of what the effectiveness analysis reads. Attach the training records export covering the period, covering every person on the population list including those with no completion recorded against them.

evidenceHint.en: Training records export for the period showing, per person, the course version, completion date, assessment score, the outcome against the recorded score and every attempt sat

title.en: Report training completion for every person against the training their function requires

description.en: Join the training records to the population list and produce the completion report the control calls for: who has completed the training their job function requires, who has not, and how long each outstanding person has been outstanding. Report new hires separately from existing staff, because the two failures have different causes — an onboarding step that never fired, against a refresh that was not taken — and are fixed in different places. State the completion figure as a fraction of the population list rather than of the people who started the course, since a report drawn only from the training system counts nobody it never enrolled. Attach the completion report with the outstanding list named person by person.

evidenceHint.en: Completion report reconciling the training records against the personnel population list, split by new hire and existing staff, naming every person whose required training is outstanding

text.en: Join the training records to the population list on the person, not on the email address alone.
Mark each person complete or outstanding against the training their function requires.
Split the outstanding list into new hires and existing staff and report the two separately.
State the completion figure as a fraction of the population list, not of those enrolled.

title.en: Analyse the assessment scores question by question to find the topics not landing

description.en: Take the assessment results for the period and calculate the pass rate per question rather than per person: a question the population reliably fails names a topic the material teaches badly, and that is the finding the control's effectiveness analysis exists to produce. Read each weak question back through its module mapping to the policy it teaches, and raise a change against that module with a named owner. Report the overall pass rate, the spread of scores and the weakest questions together, so that effectiveness is stated as a measurement rather than an opinion about whether the training seemed useful. Attach the analysis with the raw result set it was computed from.

evidenceHint.en: Assessment analysis report giving the pass rate per question, the overall pass rate and the spread of scores, and a change raised with an owner against every module whose questions the population fails

controls.title: Segregation of Duties Compliance
controls.objective: To ensure that duties and responsibilities within the organization are appropriately segregated to prevent conflicts of interest and to maintain the integrity of operations.
controls.successCriteria:
All accounts and their roles must comply with the segregation of duties as outlined in the Access Control Matrix.
All change requests must follow the established process and have proper authorization and justification, ensuring no conflicts of interest or policy breaches.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the Access Control Matrix to identify roles and access rights for systems related to critical functions such as finance, HR, IT, and operations.
Gather screenshots or system reports showing current account roles and access levels for these systems.
Collect a log of change requests for access rights and roles since the last audit, including approvals and justifications.

Analysis:
For each account in the critical systems, verify against the Access Control Matrix to ensure that the roles and access rights are authorized and do not present conflicts of interest.
Review each change request log to confirm that they adhere to the segregation of duties policy, including appropriate approvals and justification for changes.

Output:
Compiled screenshots or system reports of current account roles and access levels.
A spreadsheet or report verifying each account against the Access Control Matrix.
A detailed analysis report of change requests, highlighting compliance or deviations from the policy.

title.en: List the finance, HR, IT and operations systems and the roles each defines in the Access Control Matrix

description.en: Name the systems supporting critical functions and, for each, the roles it defines and the transactions or rights each role carries — a role name with no statement of what it can do cannot be tested for a conflict. Include the administrative roles in every system, since those are the ones that most often silently confer both halves of a conflicting pair. Where a critical-function system is missing from the matrix entirely, add it rather than testing around it. Attach the matrix extract covering every critical-function system with its roles and their rights.

evidenceHint.en: Access Control Matrix extract listing each finance, HR, IT and operations system, the roles it defines and the transactions or rights each role carries

title.en: Record the role combinations that must never be held by one account

description.en: Turn the segregation principle into a testable list: the pairs of roles or rights that create a conflict of interest when one account holds both — raising and approving a payment, changing an application and releasing it to production, creating a user and granting that user rights, adjusting payroll and approving it. State the systems each pair spans, because a conflict split across two applications is the kind a per-system access review never sees. Where a pair is not currently separated, keep it on the list as an unresolved conflict with a named accountable owner rather than dropping it, so it is counted as a deviation instead of being quietly retired.

evidenceHint.en: Conflict list naming every incompatible role or rights pair, the systems each pair spans, and a named accountable owner against any pair not currently separated

text.en: Work through each critical function and identify its initiate, approve and record steps.
Write each incompatible pair with the roles and systems carrying the two halves.
Include cross-system pairs where the two halves sit in different applications.
Name an accountable owner for every pair the organisation has not yet separated.

title.en: Export the current account roles and access levels from each critical-function system

description.en: Take the account and role listing from every system named in the matrix extract, read from the system itself and labelled with the export date and the operator who took it. Include service and disabled accounts rather than filtering to human users: a service account holding both halves of a conflicting pair is still a conflict, and a disabled account holding them becomes one the moment somebody re-enables it. Attach the compiled exports and screenshots for the period as the input the conflict test runs against.

evidenceHint.en: Dated account and role exports or screenshots from each critical-function system, covering human, service and disabled accounts, each labelled with export date and operator

title.en: Test each account against the conflict list for an incompatible role combination

description.en: Combine the exports into one account-to-role view spanning all critical systems, then evaluate every account against the conflict list, including the pairs whose halves sit in different applications. Mark each account clear or conflicted and, against each conflict, record the two rights held, the accountable manager and the remediation agreed. Attach the verification spreadsheet covering every account exported, not the conflicted ones alone.

evidenceHint.en: Verification spreadsheet with one row per account across all critical systems, a clear or conflicted verdict, and for each conflict the two rights held, the accountable manager and the remediation agreed

text.en: Combine the per-system exports into one account-to-role view across all critical systems.
Evaluate every account against each pair on the conflict list, cross-system pairs included.
Record the two conflicting rights and the accountable manager for each conflicted account.
Record the remediation agreed against each conflicted account and who owns it.

title.en: Check each access change request for approval and a recorded justification

description.en: Take the change requests raised since the last audit and read each for an approver independent of the requester, a written justification, and evidence that the entitlement was tested against the conflict list before it was applied. Requests that granted a right creating a conflict matter most here: list them with the request identifier, the conflict created and whether that right is still held today. Attach the analysis with a compliant or deviation verdict per request and the deviations carried into its conclusion.

evidenceHint.en: Change request analysis listing each request with its approver, justification and conflict check, a compliant or deviation verdict, and any request that created a conflict still held today

controls.title: Objective Clarity and Risk Assessment Control
controls.objective: To ensure that the entity's objectives are specified with clarity, enabling the identification and assessment of risks relating to these objectives.
controls.successCriteria:
The entity's objectives are clearly documented and reflect management's decisions and industry considerations.
Objectives are in compliance with applicable accounting standards, laws, and regulations.
There is a clear basis for resource allocation in relation to the objectives.
Risk tolerances are adequately documented and aligned with the objectives.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain and review the documented objectives for operations, external financial and non-financial reporting, internal reporting, and compliance.
Acquire evidence of management's decisions on structure, industry considerations, and performance goals.
Collect documentation on tolerances for risk, applicable accounting standards, and relevant laws and regulations.
Gather records of resource allocation based on operations objectives.

Analysis:
Evaluate if the documented objectives reflect management's choices and industry considerations.
Assess whether the objectives consider acceptable levels of risk variation and if they are in compliance with accounting standards and laws.
Analyze the alignment of the objectives with the entity's actual activities and transactions.
Review the basis for resource allocation in relation to the objectives.

Output:
A report detailing the assessment of the alignment and clarity of objectives.
A compliance matrix comparing objectives with applicable standards, laws, and regulations.
Documentation of risk tolerances in relation to each set of objectives.

title.en: Document the entity's objectives for operations, external reporting, internal reporting and compliance

description.en: The first request an assessor makes is the documented objectives across every category, and an objective that lives only in a strategy deck is not documented. Produce one register with a row per objective carrying the category it belongs to — operations, external financial reporting, external non-financial reporting, internal reporting, or compliance — the management owner, and the performance goal it is measured by. A category left empty is a finding in its own right: an entity with no documented internal reporting objective cannot show that risks to internal reporting were ever assessed. Attach the register with the date it was compiled.

evidenceHint.en: Objectives register with a row per objective giving category, management owner and performance goal, covering operations, external financial and non-financial reporting, internal reporting and compliance

text.en: Collect the stated objectives from strategy, budget and board papers into one place.
Assign each objective to exactly one of the five categories the control names.
Record the management owner and the performance goal each objective is measured by.
Record where each objective is documented today, naming the document and its date.
Flag any category holding no objective and refer it back to management to state one.

title.en: Record the management decision and industry consideration behind each objective

description.en: An objective the entity cannot explain is an objective it cannot defend. Against every row in the register capture what management actually decided — the structure chosen, the performance goal set, the trade-off accepted — and the industry consideration that shaped it, citing the dated record in which management took the decision rather than reconstructing the reasoning afterwards. Where an objective has since changed, keep the prior statement and the date it was superseded, so the register shows movement rather than only the current position. Attach the annotated register with the dated decision records it cites.

evidenceHint.en: Objectives register annotated with the management decision and industry consideration behind each objective, each citing the dated record in which management took it

title.en: Define the tolerance for acceptable variation in performance against each objective

description.en: For every objective in the register set the range of performance the entity is prepared to accept before the variation becomes a risk that has to be acted on, expressed as a value or a band rather than as a sentiment. State who set it, when, and what happens when performance falls outside it, including who is told. An objective with no tolerance cannot generate a risk, so a blank here quietly removes that objective from the risk assessment altogether; treat blanks as the outstanding work of this task, not as an acceptable state. Attach the tolerance documentation set against each objective in the register.

evidenceHint.en: Risk tolerance documentation giving, per objective, the acceptable variation band, who set it and when, and the escalation triggered when performance falls outside the band

title.en: Build the matrix mapping each objective to the accounting standards, laws and regulations it must satisfy

description.en: Take the objectives register and, row by row, name the external requirements the objective is bound by — the applicable accounting standards for the reporting objectives, and the laws and regulations for the compliance and operations ones — together with the internal owner who confirms each is met. Legal/DPO supplies the legal and regulatory citations and Finance the accounting standards; the matrix is where those answers are recorded against a specific objective rather than kept as a general list nobody has mapped. Where an objective is subject to no external requirement, record that explicitly, so the empty cell reads as a checked answer rather than as unfinished work. Attach the completed matrix with the citations it carries.

evidenceHint.en: Compliance matrix with a row per objective naming the applicable accounting standards, laws and regulations, the owner confirming each, and an explicit nil entry where none apply

text.en: Ask Legal/DPO for the laws and regulations that bind each objective by category.
Ask Finance for the accounting standards that apply to each reporting objective.
Record each citation against the specific objective it binds, not against the category.
Name the internal owner who confirms compliance with each cited requirement.
Record an explicit nil where an objective is subject to no external requirement.

title.en: Record the resources allocated against each operations objective
