description.en: Each time resources are committed — budget, headcount, capital — record which operations objective the commitment serves and the basis on which the amount was set, so the allocation record can be read against the objectives register rather than only against the ledger. Two patterns are worth surfacing as they arise: a commitment that serves no objective in the register, which suggests an objective the entity is pursuing but has not written down, and an objective that received nothing, which suggests an objective in name only. Attach the allocation records for the period showing the objective each allocation was made against.

evidenceHint.en: Resource allocation records for the period showing, per allocation, the operations objective it serves and the basis on which the amount was set, with objectives that received no allocation listed

title.en: Assess whether the documented objectives match the entity's actual activities and transactions

description.en: Sample the entity's actual activity for the period — significant transactions, projects underway, and where the workforce's time was spent — and test each against the objectives register: does the register hold an objective this activity serves, and does every objective in the register show activity behind it. Record a verdict per objective and per sampled activity, and write the two failure shapes up separately, because activity serving no objective and an objective with no activity call for opposite corrections. Note also any objective stated so loosely that no activity could be shown to breach it, since that is precisely the clarity failure this control exists to catch. Attach the assessment report with the sample it was drawn from.

evidenceHint.en: Objective alignment assessment report giving a verdict per objective and per sampled activity, separating objectives with no supporting activity from activity serving no documented objective, and naming objectives too loosely stated to test

text.en: Draw a sample of significant transactions, live projects and workforce time for the period.
Match each sampled activity to an objective in the register, or record that none fits.
Check every objective in the register for activity that demonstrably serves it.
Write the unmatched activities and the unsupported objectives up as separate lists.
Name any objective stated too loosely for an activity to be tested against it.

controls.title: Configuration Management Compliance
controls.objective: To ensure that the configurations of hardware, software, services, and networks adhere to the established security standards and templates.
controls.successCriteria:
All hardware, software, services, and network configurations align with the established standard templates.
All configuration changes are properly documented, approved, and comply with the change management process.
The standard configuration templates are up-to-date and effectively address current security requirements and technological changes.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the list of all hardware, software, services, and network assets currently in use.
Gather the most recent versions of the standard configuration templates.
Collect records of configuration changes made since the last audit, including change requests and their implementation details.

Analysis:
For each asset, compare its current configuration with the standard configuration template to identify deviations.
Review the configuration change records to verify that each change:
Was properly documented.
Followed the established process for change management.
Had the necessary approvals.
Assess the templates against new threats, vulnerabilities, and updates in technology to ensure they remain current and comprehensive.

Output:
A report detailing the comparison between each asset's configuration and the standard templates.
A spreadsheet or similar document listing each configuration change, its compliance with the standard process, and approval status.
An evaluation report on the currentness and comprehensiveness of the standard configuration templates.

title.en: List every hardware, software, service and network asset with the template that governs it

description.en: Build the register the comparison runs against: one row per hardware item, software product, service and network device in use, with the standard configuration template that applies to it and the owner who operates it. An asset with no template named is the finding to resolve first — it cannot be compared against anything, and it is where configuration drift goes unnoticed for longest. Draw the population from what is actually in use rather than from the procurement record. Attach the register with the template reference populated for every row, or the row explicitly marked as needing one.

evidenceHint.en: Asset register listing every hardware, software, service and network asset in use with its owner and the standard configuration template that governs it, and every untemplated asset marked as such

title.en: Issue a standard configuration template for each asset class in the register

description.en: For every class of asset the register names, write the template that defines its secure baseline in checkable terms — the settings, their required values, the services and accounts permitted, and the logging expected — so a configuration can be compared against it mechanically rather than by judgement. Version each template and record what changed between versions, because the comparison report has to state which version an asset was measured against and a verdict against an unnamed version cannot be re-checked. Attach the current template set with its version history.

evidenceHint.en: Current versions of the standard configuration templates, one per asset class, each stating settings with their required values and carrying a version identifier and change history

title.en: Compare each asset's running configuration against its template and record the deviations

description.en: Read the configuration each asset is actually running — from the asset itself or the tool holding its state, not from its documentation — and compare it setting by setting against the template version that governs it. Record one row per asset with the template version compared against, each deviation found with the observed value beside the required value, and whether the deviation is an accepted exception carrying an approval or unapproved drift. An asset that could not be read is recorded as not assessed with the reason, rather than passing by absence. Attach the comparison report with the raw configuration output behind it.

evidenceHint.en: Configuration comparison report giving, per asset, the template version compared against, each deviation with its observed and required values, its approved or unapproved status, and any asset recorded as not assessed with the reason

text.en: Collect the running configuration from each asset, or from the tool that holds its state.
Compare each setting against the required value in the template version governing that asset.
Record every deviation with the observed value set beside the required value.
Mark each deviation approved, citing the exception, or unapproved and therefore drift.
Record any asset that could not be read as not assessed, with the reason it could not be read.

title.en: Test the configuration changes since the last audit for documentation and approval

description.en: Take every configuration change made since the last audit and check three things against each: that it was documented at the time rather than reconstructed afterwards, that it followed the change management process rather than being applied directly to the asset, and that it carried the approval the process requires with the approver named. Record the result per change with the change reference, the asset affected, its process compliance and its approval status. Cross-check against the comparison report, since an unapproved deviation with no change record behind it is a change made outside the process entirely. Attach the sheet.

evidenceHint.en: Configuration change sheet listing every change since the last audit with the asset affected, whether it followed the change process, its approval status and approver, and the unapproved deviations carrying no change record at all

title.en: Reassess each configuration template against current threats, vulnerabilities and technology

description.en: Templates written once decay: the platform gains settings the template never mentions, a published vulnerability makes a permitted setting unsafe, and updated hardening guidance moves a required value. Review each template against the vulnerabilities and advisories published since it was last issued and against the current version of the platform it governs, and record per template whether it remains adequate, what specifically has changed, and the amendment required. Where a template is amended, note that the next comparison will report new deviations across the estate, so the remediation effort is carried in the report rather than arriving as a surprise. Attach the evaluation.

evidenceHint.en: Template evaluation report covering every standard configuration template with its last-issued date, the threats, vulnerabilities and platform changes reviewed against it, an adequate or amend verdict, and the amendment raised

controls.title: Physical Security Monitoring Control
controls.objective: Ensure continuous monitoring of physical premises to detect and prevent unauthorized access or suspicious behavior using surveillance systems and alarms.
controls.successCriteria:
Complete coverage of critical areas by surveillance systems and alarms.
No evidence of unauthorized access or suspicious behavior in the review period.
Compliance with relevant standards for system testing and maintenance.
Full adherence to local laws and regulations regarding surveillance and data protection.
All physical access to sensitive areas accounted for and authorized.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the list of installed surveillance systems (CCTV, motion detectors, contact detectors, sound sensors) and their locations within the organization’s premises.
Secure access logs from surveillance systems, including video footage, alarm activation records, and system integrity checks.
Collect records of periodic testing and maintenance of surveillance systems and alarms.
Obtain physical access logs to sensitive areas (e.g., server rooms, data centers).
Gather documentation on compliance with local laws and regulations related to surveillance and data protection.

Analysis:
Review surveillance system and alarm locations against the organization's physical security layout to ensure coverage of all critical areas, including external doors and accessible windows.
Analyze access logs and video footage for any signs of unauthorized access or suspicious activities.
Verify the regularity and thoroughness of system testing and maintenance against organizational standards.
Cross-reference physical access logs to sensitive areas with authorized personnel lists to identify any unauthorized access.
Assess compliance with local laws and regulations concerning surveillance, data protection, and retention periods.

Output:
A report detailing the surveillance system and alarm coverage.
Summary of findings from the analysis of access logs and video footage.
Compliance report with local laws and regulations.
Records of system testing and maintenance.
Physical access log audit results.

title.en: Record every surveillance device and alarm installed with its position on the site layout

description.en: The coverage assessment reads the device list against the physical security layout, so both have to exist and refer to the same places. List every CCTV camera, motion detector, contact detector and sound sensor installed, and against each record its position on the site plan, the area it covers or the opening it protects, whether it records or only alerts, and where its output goes. A device that is fitted but connected to nothing is recorded as such, because that is exactly the failure this list exists to expose. Attach the device list keyed to the site layout drawing.

evidenceHint.en: Surveillance and alarm device list keyed to the site layout giving device type, position, the area or opening covered, whether it records or only alerts, and the destination of its output

title.en: Record the lawful basis, viewing authorisation and footage retention for each surveillance system

description.en: Surveillance is regulated where it is installed, and the assessment asks for documentation of compliance with local law and data protection, retention periods included. For each system record the lawful basis relied on, the retention period actually configured for footage and alarm records, who may view footage and on what request, and the jurisdiction whose rules apply where sites span more than one. Where the configured retention differs from the documented one, the configured value is the fact: record it and raise the difference. Legal/DPO owns the basis and Facilities owns the configuration. Attach the compliance record with the retention settings exported from each system.

evidenceHint.en: Surveillance compliance record per system: lawful basis, the footage retention exported from the system itself, viewing authorisation and the applicable jurisdiction

title.en: Review the period's alarm activations and footage and record each unauthorised or suspicious event

description.en: Work through the alarm activation records for the period and the footage covering them, plus the footage for any out-of-hours access, and record what each one actually was: a legitimate entry, a fault, a test, or a genuine unauthorised access or suspicious behaviour. Each entry carries the date and time, the device, the area, the person where identified and the disposition, and anything escalated carries its incident reference. A nil return is recorded as the systems examined and the dates covered, so that finding no events is distinguishable from nobody looking. Attach the findings summary with the activation records it was built from.

evidenceHint.en: Findings summary for the period listing every alarm activation and reviewed footage event with device, area, disposition and incident reference, plus the activation records examined

title.en: Log each test and maintenance visit for every surveillance system and alarm

description.en: The assessment verifies the regularity and thoroughness of testing and maintenance against the organisation's standards, which needs a record naming what was tested rather than only that a visit happened. For each system log the date, who attended, what was tested, image quality and coverage for a camera, activation and signalling for a detector, integrity of the recording chain for the platform, the result, and any fault raised with the date it was fixed. Include the system integrity checks the recording platform performs on itself. Attach the testing and maintenance records for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Testing and maintenance records for the period, per system: date, attendee, the checks performed, the result, and each fault raised with its closure date

title.en: Compare device coverage against the site layout and list every uncovered critical area

description.en: Take the site layout, mark what each listed device actually covers, and then find what is left: external doors, accessible windows, service entrances, loading bays and the approaches to server rooms and data centres. Report every critical area with no coverage, every area covered only by a device that alerts and does not record, and every camera whose field of view has been obstructed or moved since it was commissioned. Each gap carries an owner and a decision to fit, relocate, or formally accept with the reason. Attach the coverage report marked up on the layout.

evidenceHint.en: Surveillance coverage report marked on the site layout listing each critical area, its covering device or none, and an owner and decision against every uncovered area

text.en: Mark each device's actual field of view or protected opening on the current site layout.
List the external doors and accessible windows with no device covering them.
Flag the areas covered only by a device that alerts but does not record.
Assign each gap an owner and a fit, relocate or formally accept decision.

title.en: Cross-check the physical access logs for sensitive areas against the authorised personnel list

description.en: Pull the access logs for the server rooms, data centres and any other area listed as sensitive, and read every entry against the people authorised for that area on the date of the entry rather than against today's list, which quietly absolves anyone whose access has been removed since. Record each entry with no matching authorisation, each authorisation still held by someone who has left or changed role, and each area whose log could not be produced at all. Attach the access log audit results naming the version of the authorisation list used.

evidenceHint.en: Access log audit results per sensitive area: unmatched entries, authorisations held by leavers or role-changers, areas with no retrievable log, and the authorisation list version used

controls.title: Test Information Security Management
controls.objective: Ensure that test information within development and testing environments is selected, protected, and managed effectively to maintain the confidentiality and integrity of operational information and prevent unauthorized access or use.
controls.successCriteria:
All test environments exhibit robust access control procedures equivalent to those in operational environments.
Each instance of operational information being copied to a test environment is duly authorized and documented.
Comprehensive and accurate logs are maintained for the copying, usage, and deletion of operational information in test environments.
Effective data protection measures (removal or masking) are implemented when sensitive information is used for testing.
Test information is securely stored and strictly used for testing purposes, with no evidence of tampering or unauthorized use.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Retrieve a list of all environments where test information is used, including development and testing setups.
Collect documentation or records of authorization for operational information copied to test environments.
Obtain logs detailing the copying, use, and deletion of operational information in test environments.
Gather evidence of data protection measures, such as data masking or removal in test environments.
Secure storage proofs for test information, ensuring it is used solely for testing purposes.

Analysis:
Review the list of environments to verify the application of appropriate access controls, mirroring those in operational environments.
Assess authorization records to confirm that each instance of copying operational information to test environments was properly authorized.
Analyze logs to ensure comprehensive tracking of operational information usage and its subsequent deletion after testing.
Evaluate data protection measures to confirm the safeguarding of sensitive information used in testing.
Inspect storage security measures and usage limitations of test information to validate its protection against tampering and unauthorized use.

Output:
A report summarizing the access control measures in test environments.
A spreadsheet or document listing all authorizations for copying operational information.
A detailed log review report.
An assessment report of data protection measures.
A security analysis report of the storage and usage of test information.

title.en: Inventory every environment where test information is used and the operational data each holds

description.en: List the development, testing and any other non-production environment where test information is used, and against each record whether it holds data copied from an operational system, which system that was, and who owns the environment. An environment whose data provenance is unknown goes on the list marked unknown — that row is a finding and the starting point for the authorisation review, not a reason to omit it. Attach the inventory as the population the access control, masking and log tasks all run against.

evidenceHint.en: Inventory of environments using test information, giving for each the operational source system its data came from, the environment owner, and an explicit unknown where provenance cannot be established

title.en: Apply access controls to each test environment equivalent to those on the operational system its data came from

description.en: For every environment holding data copied from an operational system, compare its access control against the source system's and close the difference: the same restriction on who may read the data, the same authentication requirement, the same privilege boundaries. Where equivalence cannot be reached, record the residual difference and the compensating control rather than declaring the environment compliant. Attach the access control comparison per environment together with the access lists it was drawn from.

evidenceHint.en: Access control comparison per test environment setting its controls against the source operational system's, with the residual difference and compensating control recorded wherever equivalence was not reached

title.en: Record the masking or removal applied to each sensitive field before it enters a test environment

description.en: For every operational dataset used for testing, record field by field what happens to the sensitive elements — removed, masked, or carried through unchanged — and the method used. A field carried through unchanged is not automatically a failure, but it must appear on the list with its reason, because a specification listing only the masked fields cannot be checked for completeness. Attach the specification with a sample of the transformed output showing the rules took effect.

evidenceHint.en: Field-level masking specification per dataset stating removed, masked or unchanged for every sensitive field, the method used, and a sample of transformed output showing the rules applied

text.en: List the operational datasets used for testing and the sensitive fields in each.
Decide and record removal, masking or unchanged for every sensitive field.
Name the masking method applied so the result can be reproduced and checked.
Record the reason a field is carried through unchanged and the exposure it leaves.
Take a sample of the transformed output and hold it as proof the rules ran.

title.en: Authorise and record every copy of operational information into a test environment

description.en: Each copy of operational information into a test environment is authorised before it happens and recorded afterwards: what was copied, from which system, into which environment, who requested it, who authorised it and the date. This control is tested on each instance being duly authorised and documented, so a standing blanket approval covering all future copies does not satisfy it. Attach the authorisation register for the period alongside the requests it records.

evidenceHint.en: Authorisation register for the period with one row per copy of operational information into a test environment, naming the data, source system, destination environment, requester, authoriser and date

title.en: Log the copying, use and deletion of operational information in each test environment

description.en: Maintain a log covering the whole life of test information in the environment — when it arrived, who accessed it while it was there, and when it was deleted once testing finished. The deletion entry is the one most often missing and the one this control names explicitly, so a dataset still resident after its testing purpose ended is recorded as an open item with an owner. Export the environment's own audit trail where it produces one rather than re-keying it by hand. Attach the log for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Test information log or environment audit export for the period covering arrival, access and deletion of each operational dataset, with open items named for datasets still resident after testing ended

title.en: Test the stored test information for use outside testing and for unauthorised change

description.en: Sample the test information holdings in the inventory and examine the storage and access evidence for the two things this control names: use for a purpose other than testing, and modification or tampering by an account with no reason to touch it. Check also that the storage protection matches what the dataset's sensitivity requires. Disposition each hit as authorised, naming what covers it, or as an exception referred for investigation. Attach the analysis with the storage and access evidence it was read from.

evidenceHint.en: Security analysis of test information storage and usage naming each sampled holding, its storage protection, and every instance of non-testing use or unauthorised change dispositioned as authorised or referred

controls.title: Input Validation and Recording
controls.objective: Ensure the completeness and accuracy of system inputs to meet product, service, and reporting requirements.
controls.successCriteria:
All system inputs meet defined requirements for completeness and accuracy.
Validation processes are executed effectively and accurately.
System input activities are recorded completely and accurately in a timely manner.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Retrieve lists of system inputs for critical services and products.
Obtain records of input validation processes and results.
Collect logs of system input activities and change requests.

Analysis:
Assess each system input against predefined requirements to confirm compliance.
Review validation process records to ensure thorough and accurate execution.
Analyze logs to verify the completeness and accuracy of recorded system input activities.

Output:
Detailed report evaluating the compliance of system inputs with set requirements.
Analysis documentation of validation process effectiveness.
Compiled log assessments ensuring accurate and complete record-keeping.

title.en: List the system inputs feeding each critical service and product

description.en: Start from the products and services the organisation is accountable for and work back to what feeds them: interface and file feeds from other systems, supplier and partner data, user-entered records, batch loads, and the manual adjustments applied at period end. For each input record its source, the system and process that receives it, the frequency and expected volume, and the product, service or report that depends on it — an input with no named consumer is either dead or undocumented, and both are findings. Engineering lead owns the list; IT Operations supplies the interface detail. Attach the input list with a named consumer and a named owner on every row.

evidenceHint.en: List of system inputs per critical service and product, giving the source, receiving system, frequency, expected volume, dependent output and named owner

text.en: Take each critical service and product and trace back the data it depends on.
Record interface feeds, file loads, supplier data, user entry and period-end adjustments alike.
Capture the source, receiving system, frequency and expected volume for each input.
Name the product, service or report each input feeds, and flag inputs with no consumer.
Name the owner accountable for each input's completeness and accuracy.

title.en: Record the completeness and accuracy requirement for every input on the list

description.en: For each input, write down what correct looks like in terms a check can be built against: the mandatory fields, the permitted formats and value ranges, the referential rules linking the input to reference data, and the control total or record count that proves nothing was lost in transit. State the requirement the dependent product, service or report imposes rather than the one the source happens to meet — the requirement belongs to the consumer, and writing down what the source already does guarantees the later test passes. Attach the requirements definition with an entry for every input on the list.

evidenceHint.en: Input requirements definition giving the mandatory fields, formats, ranges, referential rules and control totals for every input on the list

title.en: Configure the validation check enforcing each requirement and record where it runs

description.en: Build or identify the check that enforces every requirement, and record for each one where it runs — at the interface, inside the receiving application, or in a downstream reconciliation — and what happens when it fails: reject the item, quarantine it for review, or accept it with a warning. Record who is notified on a failure and where failed items wait, because a quarantine nobody watches is the same as no check at all. Requirements with no check behind them are what this task produces as a gap, each with an owner and a date. Attach the validation mapping showing the requirement, the check, its location, its failure behaviour and its notification route.

evidenceHint.en: Validation mapping from each input requirement to the check that enforces it, its location, failure behaviour and notification route, with an owner for every requirement carrying no check

text.en: Match every requirement to the check that enforces it, or record that none exists.
Record where each check runs: interface, receiving application or downstream reconciliation.
State the failure behaviour for each check: reject, quarantine or accept with a warning.
Name who is notified on failure and where quarantined items wait for disposition.
Give every requirement with no check an owner and a date to close it.

title.en: Record the result of every validation run, including the disposition of rejected items

description.en: Each validation run writes a record carrying the input, the run date, the records offered, accepted, rejected and quarantined, the control total comparison where one applies, and the reason attached to each rejection. Rejected and quarantined items are then dispositioned — corrected and resubmitted, accepted under an approval, or discarded — with the disposition and the person who made it recorded against the item, because an unresolved rejection is missing data in the dependent product whether or not the check fired. Attach the validation run records for the period with the rejection dispositions completed.

evidenceHint.en: Validation run records for the period showing offered, accepted, rejected and quarantined counts, control total comparisons, rejection reasons and the disposition of every rejected item

title.en: Log every system input activity and change request against the input it affects

description.en: Record the activity on each input as it happens: the run or receipt, who or what initiated it, when it happened and when the record of it was made, the volume received, and any manual adjustment made to the data after it landed, naming the person who made it and why. Where an input, its interface, its mapping or its validation rules change, raise a change request stating which inputs and which dependent products it affects, and file it against those inputs so the log explains a step change in volume or rejection rate rather than leaving it unexplained. Attach the input activity log and the change requests raised in the period.

evidenceHint.en: Input activity log for the period showing each run, when it happened and when it was recorded, volumes and manual adjustments, together with the change requests raised against those inputs

title.en: Test a sample of inputs against their defined requirements and report the exceptions

description.en: Draw a sample covering every critical service and product, and test the input records it selects against the requirements definition rather than against the validation checks — a check that was never configured passes everything, so testing the check would confirm the wrong thing. For each sampled input compare the received data against its mandatory fields, formats, ranges and control totals, and confirm the activity log holds a run for it: a period with a dependent report produced and no logged input is an exception in its own right. Score pass or fail per input with the failed requirement named, and give each failure an owner and a remediation date. Attach the compliance report with the sampling working behind it.

evidenceHint.en: Input compliance report scoring each sampled input against its defined requirements, naming the failed requirement, listing missing log entries and giving an owner for every exception

controls.title: Breach Notification Compliance
controls.objective: Ensure timely and appropriate notification of breaches and incidents to affected data subjects, regulators, and other relevant parties.
controls.successCriteria:
All breach notifications comply with the established procedures.
Notifications are timely, complete, and accurately reflect the nature and extent of the breach.
Compliance with legal and regulatory requirements in breach notification.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Collect all records of data breaches and incidents reported in the review period.
Obtain copies of breach notifications issued to affected parties.
Review policy documents outlining the breach notification process.

Analysis:
Verify each incident against the breach notification policy to ensure compliance with notification procedures.
Assess the timeliness and adequacy of notifications sent to affected data subjects and regulators.
Check for completeness and accuracy in the content of the notifications.

Output:
A report summarizing adherence to breach notification procedures.
Analysis of the timeliness and adequacy of breach notifications.
Documentation highlighting any discrepancies or non-compliance in breach notification.

title.en: Record every notifiable party and the notification window its governing requirement sets

description.en: Build the notification obligations register covering the parties this control names as owed a notice — affected data subjects, regulators, and other relevant parties such as a controller or contractual counterparty. One row per party, carrying the legal, regulatory or contractual requirement that creates the duty, the notification window that requirement itself sets, and the delivery channel plus current contact address. Take no window from custom or memory: cite the source that sets it. Legal/DPO establishes the windows; Security engineering confirms which systems and data categories fall in scope. Attach the completed register, dated and version-marked.

evidenceHint.en: Breach notification obligations register listing, per row, the notifiable party, the requirement creating the duty, its notification window and the contact route

text.en: List the jurisdictions and data categories the Privacy Policy commits the organisation to cover.
Name each party owed a notice — data subject, regulator, counterparty — and the requirement creating that duty.
Quote the notification window from the cited requirement, never from practice or memory.
Record the delivery channel and current contact address for each regulator and counterparty listed.
Date and version-mark the register, then circulate it to whoever assesses reported incidents.

title.en: Publish a notification template per audience carrying every required content field

description.en: Produce one template for each audience in the obligations register — data subject, regulator, counterparty — and populate its field list from the requirements that register cites rather than from a generic sample. Every template must carry the fields that let a notice state the nature and extent of the breach, which is what this control tests notifications for. Pair the templates with a pre-dispatch completeness checklist naming each field, so an incomplete notice cannot be sent unnoticed. Legal/DPO owns the wording; Security engineering supplies the technical description blocks. Attach the template pack and the checklist.

evidenceHint.en: Breach notification template pack, one per audience, with the pre-dispatch content completeness checklist naming each required field

title.en: Log the awareness time and the notifiability decision for every reported breach

description.en: For each incident entered in the breach and incident records, record the timestamp at which the organisation became aware, the notifiability determination against each triggered row of the obligations register, who made that determination, and when. Where the decision is not to notify, record the reason in the same row — a blank is indistinguishable from an unmade decision. Legal/DPO makes the call; this task is the durable record of it and the clock start that the timeliness test reads.

evidenceHint.en: Breach and incident register extract for the period showing, per incident, the awareness timestamp, notifiability decision, decision-maker and rationale

title.en: File the as-sent copy and dispatch timestamp of every notification issued

description.en: For each notification actually sent, store the as-sent copy — data subject notice, regulator submission, counterparty letter — with its dispatch timestamp and whatever receipt the channel returns, including the regulator's submission or case reference where one is issued. File it against the incident id so a reviewer can move from register row to issued notice without asking anyone. Later corrections or follow-up submissions are filed as further copies, never as edits to the original.

evidenceHint.en: Per-incident notification file: as-sent copies of each notice, dispatch timestamps, and regulator submission or case references

title.en: Test the period's incidents against the notification procedure and report every discrepancy

description.en: Take every incident recorded in the review period and test each one: whether a notification was required, whether it was issued, the elapsed time from awareness to dispatch measured against the window in the obligations register, and whether the notice content carried each field on the completeness checklist. Produce the adherence report naming each discrepancy by incident id and the specific requirement missed. Legal/DPO supplies the issued notices, Security engineering the awareness timestamps.

evidenceHint.en: Breach notification adherence report for the period, with per-incident timeliness and content findings and a discrepancy list keyed by incident id

text.en: Pull every incident logged in the review period from the breach and incident records.
Match each incident to the obligations register rows that it triggers.
Compare each awareness-to-dispatch elapsed time against the recorded window.
Check each issued notice against the template completeness checklist.
List every discrepancy with its incident id and the requirement that was missed.

controls.title: URL Request Audit Logging
controls.objective: Ensure the collection and storage of URL request audit logs on all enterprise assets where appropriate and supported, to monitor and analyze web traffic for security and operational efficiency.
controls.successCriteria:
All enterprise assets that support URL request logging have it enabled and properly configured.
URL request audit logs are regularly reviewed and stored in accordance with organizational policies and standards.
Any irregularities or security concerns identified in the URL request logs are addressed and documented.
Including existing criteria, such as all accounts and their roles being as per the Access Matrix, and change requests following the procedure.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Retrieve a list of all enterprise assets capable of URL request logging.
Obtain URL request audit logs from a representative sample of these assets.
Acquire documentation on the configuration settings for URL request logging on these assets.
In addition to the existing evidence gathering steps, like getting the list of systems from the Access Matrix, etc.

Analysis:
Verify that all listed enterprise assets have URL request logging enabled and are appropriately configured.
Examine the URL request audit logs for signs of irregular activity or patterns that might indicate security concerns.
Cross-reference the URL request logs with other network activity logs for comprehensive analysis.
Plus the existing analysis steps, such as comparing accounts against the Access Matrix, reviewing change requests, etc.

Output:
A comprehensive list of enterprise assets with their URL request logging status.
Copies of URL request audit logs.
A report detailing the analysis of the URL request logs and any findings or recommendations.
Along with the existing outputs, like screenshots, spreadsheets checking each account, etc.

title.en: List every enterprise asset capable of URL request logging with its current status

description.en: Enumerate the assets that can record URL requests — web proxies, secure web gateways, next-generation firewalls, endpoint agents and any cloud web-filtering service — and give each a row carrying whether URL request logging is currently enabled, disabled or unsupported on that platform. An asset that cannot log URL requests belongs in the list marked unsupported rather than being left out, because 'where appropriate and supported' is a judgement somebody has to be able to see was made. Attach the list; it is the population every later task in this control samples from.

evidenceHint.en: List of enterprise assets capable of URL request logging, each row giving the platform, the enabled, disabled or unsupported status and the owner

title.en: Record the URL request logging configuration in force on each capable asset

description.en: For every asset the list marks capable, capture the configuration as it actually reads: which fields are recorded (requesting client, full URL or hostname only, timestamp, action taken), where the records are sent, and how long they are held there. Export the settings rather than transcribing them, and note explicitly where a platform records only the hostname, since that is what limits the analysis a later task can perform. Attach the configuration documentation for each asset against the list row it belongs to.

evidenceHint.en: Configuration exports or documented settings per capable asset showing the URL request fields recorded, the log destination and the retention applied

title.en: Review the sampled URL request logs for irregular activity and record each finding

description.en: Pull URL request logs from a representative sample of the capable assets for the period under test and work through them for the patterns that indicate a security concern: requests to newly registered or known-bad domains, repeated requests on a machine-like interval, large uploads to consumer file-sharing services, and traffic from a client that has no business reaching the destination. Every hit gets a row naming the client, the destination, the time and the disposition — benign and why, or referred for investigation. An empty findings list is evidence only when the extract shows the logs were actually read. Attach the log extract with the dispositioned findings list.

evidenceHint.en: URL request log extracts for the sampled assets plus a findings list giving client, destination, time and a benign or referred disposition per hit

text.en: Select the sample so each capable platform contributes at least one asset.
Pull the URL request logs covering the whole period under test for those assets.
Search for requests to newly registered, uncategorised or known-bad destinations.
Look for beaconing intervals and upload volumes inconsistent with the client's role.
Disposition every hit as benign with a reason or refer it for investigation.

title.en: Cross-reference the sampled URL request logs against other network activity logs

description.en: Take each finding and the busiest clients in the sample and look for the same client and time window in the other network records — DNS query logs, firewall session logs and endpoint telemetry — recording whether the URL request is corroborated, contradicted, or has no counterpart at all. A missing counterpart is itself reportable: it usually means one of the two log sources is not receiving from that asset. Attach the cross-reference working paper showing, per checked event, the sources consulted and the outcome.

evidenceHint.en: Cross-reference working paper listing each checked event, the other network log sources consulted and whether the activity was corroborated, contradicted or absent

title.en: Check the accounts on the URL logging systems against the Access Matrix

description.en: Take the systems the Access Matrix names for this control and list every account that currently holds access to them together with the role it holds, then compare each account and role against what the Matrix says it should be. Record one row per account with a matches or exception verdict; the exceptions are accounts absent from the Matrix, accounts holding a wider role than it grants, and accounts belonging to leavers. Each exception carries the action taken and who took it. Attach the account comparison spreadsheet with the system access exports it was built from.

evidenceHint.en: Account comparison spreadsheet, one row per account per system, giving the role held, the role the Access Matrix grants, a matches or exception verdict and the action taken on each exception

title.en: Test that changes to URL logging configuration followed the change procedure

description.en: Take the configuration changes made to URL request logging during the period — from each platform's own change history where it keeps one — and find the change request behind each. Record per change the date it was made, the change request reference behind it and the date that request was raised, then read the pair against what the change procedure actually requires. Changes with no request behind them at all are the finding this task produces, and each gets an owner and a retrospective disposition. Attach the change sample with the request records it was matched against.

evidenceHint.en: Change sample listing each URL logging configuration change with the date it was made, its change request reference, the date that request was raised and the disposition of any change made without one

controls.title: Privileged Access Rights Management
controls.objective: Ensure that the allocation, use, and management of privileged access rights are restricted and controlled in accordance with the organization's access control policy and industry best practices.
controls.successCriteria:
All privileged accounts and their roles are in accordance with the Access Control Matrix.
All change requests for privileged access have followed the established procedure and policy.
The authorization process for privileged access rights is robust and compliant with organizational standards.
Effective measures are in place for the awareness, management, and expiry of privileged access rights.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the list of systems with privileged access rights (from Access Control Matrix).
Capture screenshots of privileged accounts on each system.
Retrieve the list of privileged access change requests and approvals since the last audit.
Gather documentation on the authorization process for privileged access rights.

Analysis:
For each privileged account on the system, verify if it aligns with the Access Control Matrix.
Review privileged access change requests to ensure they have followed the organization's access control policy.
Assess the authorization process and records for granting and revoking privileged access rights.
Examine the management and expiry procedures for privileged access rights.
Evaluate the measures taken to make users aware of their privileged access rights and mode.
Analyze the re-authentication or authentication step-up processes implemented for privileged access rights.

Output:
Screenshots documenting the privileged accounts on each system.
A spreadsheet cross-referencing each privileged account with the Access Control Matrix.
A spreadsheet detailing and verifying each privileged access change request and its compliance with the policy.
A report on the assessment of the authorization process and management of privileged access rights.

title.en: Record every system carrying privileged access rights and the privileged roles it defines

description.en: From the Access Control Matrix, list the systems holding privileged rights and, per system, the roles that confer them and what each of those roles can do — domain and local administration, database owner, hypervisor and console access, cloud tenancy owner, security tool administration. Break-glass and emergency accounts belong on this list too: they carry the highest rights and are the least likely to appear in a routine role export. This list is the population every later task counts against. Attach it with the privileged roles and their rights recorded against every system.

evidenceHint.en: List of systems carrying privileged access rights, the privileged roles each defines and what those roles can do, break-glass and emergency accounts included

title.en: Document the route for granting, revoking and expiring a privileged access right

description.en: Write the procedure a requester, an approver and an operator all follow: who may request a privileged right, who authorises it, what evidence of need is required, how the grant is recorded so it can be found at review time, how long it lasts before it expires, and the route by which it is withdrawn once it is no longer needed. State the default lifetime explicitly — a right with no stated expiry is the one that outlives the reason it was granted for. Attach the issued procedure covering grant, revocation and expiry end to end.

evidenceHint.en: Issued privileged access procedure covering request and evidence of need, the authoriser, how grants are recorded, the default expiry period and the revocation route

text.en: Name who may request a privileged right and what evidence of need must accompany it.
Name the authoriser for each privileged role and the approval record they leave behind.
State how each grant is recorded so it can be found again at review time.
State the default lifetime after which a privileged right expires unless it is renewed.
State how a right is withdrawn once it is no longer needed, and who triggers the withdrawal.

title.en: Configure step-up authentication for entry into each privileged role

description.en: Apply re-authentication or an authentication step-up at the point a privileged right is used rather than only at session start, so that a session opened with ordinary credentials cannot silently exercise administrative rights. Cover each privileged role on the list. Where a system cannot enforce a step-up, record it as an exception with the compensating control that stands in its place — access only from a managed jump host, for instance — and a named owner, rather than leaving it configured as it was. Attach the per-system configuration and the exception list.

evidenceHint.en: Per-system configuration evidence showing re-authentication or step-up required before privileged role use, plus the list of systems unable to enforce it with their compensating control and owner

title.en: Issue each holder a statement of the privileged rights they hold and when those rights expire

description.en: Send every privileged-right holder a statement naming the rights they hold, the systems those rights apply to, the mode of use expected — that the right is exercised from a managed host and under a separate account, for example — and the expiry date. Keep the acknowledgement each holder returns: that record is what evidences the awareness measure, rather than a claim that people were told. Non-responders and holders who reply that a right is no longer needed both generate follow-up, the first a chase and the second a revocation. Attach the statements and the acknowledgement record.

evidenceHint.en: Issued privileged-rights statements with the acknowledgement record per holder, and the follow-up list of non-responders and of rights the holder declared no longer needed

title.en: Cross-reference every privileged account on each system against the Access Control Matrix

description.en: Capture the privileged account listing from each system on the list and set it beside what the matrix authorises. Mark each account authorised, unauthorised or expired, and treat an account whose grant has passed its expiry date exactly as an unauthorised one — that is what makes the expiry rule real rather than decorative. Against each exception record the accountable owner and whether the right was removed or the matrix corrected. Attach the cross-reference spreadsheet together with the per-system screenshots it was built from.

evidenceHint.en: Cross-reference spreadsheet of every privileged account against its Access Control Matrix entitlement with authorised, unauthorised or expired verdicts, plus the per-system privileged account screenshots

text.en: Capture the privileged account listing from every system on the privileged-systems list.
Match each account to a matrix entitlement and to the grant record behind it.
Mark accounts whose grant has passed its expiry date as exceptions alongside unauthorised ones.
Record the owner and the outcome — right removed or matrix corrected — for each exception.

title.en: Verify each privileged access change request followed the documented authorisation route

description.en: Read every privileged access request and approval raised since the last audit against the procedure: requester, evidence of need, the authoriser the procedure names, the grant record, and an expiry actually set. Confirm the right provisioned matches the right approved — a request approved for read access and provisioned as an owner role is precisely the deviation the paperwork alone will not show. Record a compliant or deviation verdict per request, naming the step skipped. Attach the verification covering the whole period.

evidenceHint.en: Privileged access change request verification listing each request with its authoriser, the right approved against the right provisioned, the expiry set, and a compliant or deviation verdict naming the step skipped

controls.title: Warning and Communication Procedures
controls.objective: Ensure effective communication and coordination with internal and external stakeholders during a disruption to minimize impact and facilitate a structured response.
controls.successCriteria:
Communication procedures are comprehensive, detailing all required aspects (what, when, with whom, how).
Emergency contact information is up-to-date and readily available.
All communications during disruptions are logged and documented.
The media response plan is clear and has been followed during incidents.
Structured communication with emergency responders is evidenced.
Records of disruptions show detailed documentation of actions and decisions.
Exercises of communication procedures are conducted regularly, with reports indicating successful outcomes.
Interested parties are appropriately alerted during disruptions.
Coordination between responding organizations is evidenced and effective.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:

Obtain the documented communication procedures outlining the communication process with internal and external interested parties.
Get the list of emergency contact information for employees and key stakeholders.
Acquire records of communications sent and received during the last disruption.
Retrieve the details of the organization’s media response plan.
Collect records of communications with emergency responders.
Gather evidence of periodic exercises of the communication procedures, including after-action reports.

Analysis:

Verify that the communication procedures include details on what, when, with whom, and how to communicate during a disruption.
Ensure that the procedures cover how to receive, document, and respond to communications from interested parties, including national or regional risk advisory systems.
Check for evidence that means of communication were available and used during a disruption.
Review records to confirm that structured communication was facilitated with emergency responders.
Validate that a media response plan exists and was followed, including a communication strategy.
Examine logs of disruptions to confirm that details, actions taken, and decisions made were documented.
Ensure procedures include alerting interested parties potentially impacted by a disruption.
Confirm that coordination and communication with multiple responding organizations were appropriately managed.
Review the exercise programme to verify that the warning and communication procedures are tested regularly.

Output:

Screenshots of documented communication procedures.
List of emergency contact information.
Records and screenshots of communication logs during disruptions.
Copy of the media response plan.
Records of communications with emergency responders.
After-action reports from exercise programmes.

title.en: Register the emergency contact details for employees and key stakeholders

description.en: Build the contact list the response teams will actually reach for: the employees, the key stakeholders the communication procedure names, and the emergency responders who have to be contacted during a disruption. Record for each entry who verified it and when, so the list can be shown to be up to date rather than merely to exist, and record where the list is held so it is readily available at the point it is needed. A wrong number is discovered at the worst possible moment, which is why the verification date is a column and not a footnote. Attach the list with the verification date populated for every entry.

evidenceHint.en: Emergency contact list covering employees, key stakeholders and emergency responders, each entry carrying its contact route and the date it was last verified and by whom, with where the list is held

text.en: List the employees, key stakeholders and responders that must be reachable.
Record the contact route held for each entry on the list.
Record who verified each entry and the date the verification was made.
Record where the list is held so responders can reach it when it is needed.

title.en: Document what is communicated during a disruption, when, with whom and how

description.en: Write the communication procedure so it answers all four for each audience: what is said, at what point in the disruption, to whom, and through which channel. Include how communications arriving from interested parties and from national or regional risk advisory systems are received, documented and answered, and the point at which parties potentially impacted by a disruption are alerted rather than told afterwards. Attach the documented procedure showing the four elements populated for every audience it names.

evidenceHint.en: Documented warning and communication procedure stating, per audience, what is communicated, when, with whom and how, together with the route for receiving, documenting and answering inbound communications

text.en: List the internal and external audiences that must be communicated with.
State for each audience what is communicated and at which point of the disruption.
Name the channel used to reach each audience during a disruption.
Describe how inbound messages and risk advisories are received, documented and answered.
State when parties potentially impacted by a disruption are alerted.

title.en: Document the media response plan and the communication strategy it follows

description.en: Produce the media response plan the organisation will actually work to when a disruption draws attention: the communication strategy behind it, the audiences it addresses and the route by which a media approach reaches the plan rather than being answered ad hoc. Keep it short enough to be followed under pressure — this control asks that the plan be clear and that it was followed during incidents, and a plan nobody can act from fails on both counts. Attach the media response plan as issued, and note against it the incidents in the period in which it was followed.

evidenceHint.en: Copy of the media response plan carrying its communication strategy and the route a media approach follows, with a note of the incidents in the period in which it was followed

title.en: Log every communication sent and received during a disruption with the decisions taken

description.en: While the disruption runs, keep a single log carrying each communication in time order: the time, the party, whether it was sent or received, the channel, the content, and the action or decision it produced. Record the decisions in the same log rather than a separate one, because the value of the record afterwards is the sequence — what was known, when, and what was decided on the strength of it. Note where a listed channel failed and which fallback was used instead. Attach the disruption log for the period under test.

evidenceHint.en: Disruption communication log in time order giving time, party, direction, channel, content and the action or decision taken, including any channel failure and the fallback used

title.en: Record each contact with emergency responders and other responding organisations

description.en: Where emergency responders or other responding organisations are involved, record each contact separately from the general log: who was contacted or made contact, the time, what was requested or provided, and how the response was coordinated where more than one organisation was involved. This separate record is what evidences structured communication with responders and genuine coordination rather than parallel independent responses. Where no responder was involved in the period, record the nil return instead. Attach the responder contact record for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Record of communications with emergency responders and other responding organisations giving each contact, its time, what was requested or provided and how the response was coordinated, or a nil return

title.en: Exercise the warning and communication procedures and record the after-action findings

description.en: Exercise the communication procedure on its own terms rather than relying on it being touched incidentally during a wider continuity test: attempt contact through the channels the procedure lists, record which audiences were reached and which were not, check whether the contact entries were correct, and confirm the media response plan's route was followed. Write the after-action report naming what failed, the contact entries corrected as a result and the procedure changes raised, each with an owner. Attach the after-action report with the contact list corrections it produced.

evidenceHint.en: After-action report from the communication procedure exercise showing which audiences were reached, the contact entries found wrong and corrected, and the procedure changes raised with owners

controls.title: Legal Compliance Verification
controls.objective: To ensure continuous alignment with legal, statutory, regulatory, and contractual requirements relevant to information security.
controls.successCriteria:
All legal, statutory, regulatory, and contractual requirements are identified, documented, and regularly updated.
Compliance actions, policies, and training are effectively aligned with these requirements.
Any specific legal advice or consultations are adequately addressing the relevant legal complexities.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the most recent documentation of legal, statutory, regulatory, and contractual obligations.
Gather records of compliance efforts, including policy updates, training logs, and compliance reports.
Retrieve documentation of any legal advice or consultations sought, particularly regarding cryptography and cross-border data transfers.

Analysis:
Review the documentation of legal, statutory, regulatory, and contractual obligations to ensure it is current and comprehensive.
Examine compliance efforts to verify they are in line with these obligations, focusing on policy implementation, employee training, and reporting mechanisms.
Assess the adequacy of legal consultations, especially in areas with specific legal requirements like cryptography.

Output:
A report detailing the status of compliance with each legal, statutory, regulatory, and contractual requirement.
A compliance matrix aligning obligations with specific actions and policies.
A summary of legal consultations and advice, highlighting any areas of concern.

title.en: Register every legal, statutory, regulatory and contractual requirement bearing on information security

description.en: Build the register this control is measured against: one row per obligation naming its source instrument, the jurisdiction or counterparty it comes from, what it actually requires of the organisation in operational terms, the internal owner accountable for it, and the date the row was last confirmed against that source. Include the contractual obligations carried in customer and supplier agreements alongside the statutory and regulatory ones, since those are the obligations most often held only in the contract file and invisible to a compliance review. Attach the register with an owner and a confirmation date on every row.

evidenceHint.en: Obligations register listing each legal, statutory, regulatory and contractual requirement with its source, its jurisdiction or counterparty, the internal owner and the date last confirmed

text.en: Collect the statutory and regulatory instruments applying in each jurisdiction of operation.
Extract the information security obligations from the customer and supplier contracts in force.
Write what each obligation requires in operational terms rather than as a citation.
Name the internal owner accountable for each obligation and confirm it with that person.
Date every row against the version of the source it was read from.

title.en: Map each registered obligation to the policy, control or action that satisfies it

description.en: Work down the register and, against every obligation, name what actually meets it: the policy clause, the implemented control, the term passed down to a supplier, or the recurring activity that discharges it. That mapping is the compliance matrix the control calls for. Where nothing meets an obligation, record the gap explicitly with an owner and the date it is to be closed by — a blank cell and a declared gap are not the same thing, and only one of them can be worked. Attach the matrix showing every register row either addressed or flagged.

evidenceHint.en: Compliance matrix aligning every registered obligation with the policy, control or action satisfying it, and an owner plus a target date against each declared gap

title.en: Record the policy updates, training and compliance reports produced against each obligation

description.en: Keep the evidence that the matrix is being lived rather than filed: the policy versions issued or updated in the period and the obligation that drove each change, the training delivered with who completed it, and the compliance reports produced or submitted with their dates and recipients. HR holds the training completion data and Legal/DPO the reporting record. Tie each item back to the obligation it serves, so the activity record can be read directly against the matrix instead of being taken on trust. Attach the period's policy version history, training log and compliance reports.

evidenceHint.en: Compliance activity record for the period — policy versions issued, training delivered with completions, and compliance reports produced — each tied to the obligation it serves

title.en: File the legal advice obtained on cryptography and cross-border data transfers

description.en: Where specialist legal advice is sought — the control names cryptography and cross-border data transfers as the areas that attract it — file the consultation with the question that was put, the adviser who answered, the date, the advice given, and what the organisation did in consequence. That last element is the one usually missing and the one that shows the advice was acted on rather than merely collected. Where a known area of legal complexity has had no advice sought, record that too, so the file shows the shape of what is and is not covered. Attach the consultation file for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Legal consultation file for the period giving, per consultation, the question asked, the adviser, the date, the advice given and the action taken in consequence

title.en: Report the compliance status of every requirement on the obligations register

description.en: Check every register row against the instrument or contract as it stands now — amended legislation, new regulatory guidance, contracts signed or renegotiated since the last review — and update or add the rows that have moved. Then report a status against each requirement: met, partially met with the shortfall described, or not met with the owner and the date it will be. Where the legal position is unsettled or the advice inconclusive, call it out as an area of concern rather than scoring it, since a confident verdict there would be the misleading answer. Attach the status report with the updated register.

evidenceHint.en: Compliance status report giving a met, partially met or not met verdict per registered requirement, with the updated register and the areas of concern called out separately

text.en: Check each register row against the current version of the instrument or contract behind it.
Add the obligations arising from legislation, guidance or contracts entered since the last review.
Record a met, partially met or not met verdict against every requirement.
Describe the shortfall and name an owner for each requirement not fully met.
Call out the unsettled legal positions as areas of concern rather than scoring them.

controls.title: Business Continuity Strategy Review
controls.objective: Ensure the effectiveness and adequacy of business continuity strategies and solutions based on the outputs from business impact analysis (BIA) and risk assessment.
controls.successCriteria:
All identified strategies meet the BIA and Risk Assessment requirements.
Strategies demonstrate a comprehensive approach to managing disruptions before, during, and after events.
Adequate resources are allocated and available for implementing the strategies.
Past disruptions are effectively mitigated, and recovery objectives are met within the required timeframes.
The organization demonstrates continuous improvement in its business continuity planning.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:

Obtain the latest Business Impact Analysis (BIA) report.
Obtain the latest Risk Assessment report.
Collect the documented business continuity strategies and solutions.
Gather records of disruptions and the implemented continuity strategies from the past year.

Analysis:

Strategy Review:
Compare the identified strategies in the documentation with the requirements stated in the BIA and Risk Assessment.
Verify that the strategies meet the requirements for continuing and recovering prioritized activities within identified timeframes and agreed capacity.
Ensure the strategies consider options for before, during, and after disruptions.
Confirm that the strategies include measures to reduce the likelihood of disruptions, shorten the period of disruption, and limit the impact on the organization's products and services.
Check that the strategies account for the availability of adequate resources (people, data, infrastructure, ICT, etc.).

Implementation Review:
Validate that the selected strategies align with the organization's risk appetite and consider associated costs and benefits.
Verify that resources required for implementing the strategies are adequately determined and available.
Review records of disruptions to assess whether the implemented strategies effectively mitigated the impact and met recovery objectives.

Output:

Documentation comparing strategies with BIA and Risk Assessment requirements.
List of identified gaps and recommendations for improvement.
Report on the adequacy of resources allocated for the strategies.
Record of analysis of past disruptions and effectiveness of the implemented strategies.
Spreadsheet summarizing the findings and compliance status of each strategy.

title.en: Record the recovery timeframe and agreed capacity of every prioritised activity

description.en: Take the latest business impact analysis and the latest risk assessment and pull out the requirement every strategy will be judged against: the prioritised activities, the timeframe within which each must be resumed, the capacity agreed for that resumption, and the disruption risks the risk assessment identifies. Cite the version and date of both source reports, because a strategy assessed against a superseded impact analysis passes against the wrong requirement and nothing downstream can detect it. Attach the requirement baseline carrying those citations.

evidenceHint.en: Requirement baseline listing every prioritised activity with its recovery timeframe and agreed capacity, plus the disruption risks identified, citing the BIA and risk assessment versions used

title.en: Map each continuity strategy to the prioritised activities it covers

description.en: Set the documented continuity strategies against the requirement baseline row by row, recording which activity each strategy continues or recovers and the measures it provides before, during and after a disruption — reducing the likelihood of disruption, shortening its duration, and limiting the impact on products and services. Prioritised activities that no strategy covers, and strategies that serve no prioritised activity, are both outputs of this mapping and both have to appear in it. Attach the comparison document showing the mapping and the two gap lists it produces.

evidenceHint.en: Strategy-to-activity comparison document giving the before, during and after measures per strategy, the prioritised activities with no strategy, and the strategies serving no prioritised activity

text.en: List the documented continuity strategies and the solutions implementing them.
Link each strategy to the prioritised activities in the requirement baseline.
Record the measures each strategy provides before, during and after a disruption.
List the prioritised activities that no documented strategy covers.
List the strategies that serve no prioritised activity in the baseline.

title.en: Record the people, data, infrastructure and ICT each strategy needs and its availability

description.en: For every strategy in the mapping, determine the resources its execution depends on — the people and their skills, the data, the premises and equipment, the ICT services and the third parties — and record for each whether it is available today, available on invocation under a standing arrangement, or not currently secured. The lines marked not secured are the substance of the resource adequacy report this control asks for, so each one carries the strategy it blocks and a named owner. Attach the resource register with an availability position on every line.

evidenceHint.en: Resource register per strategy covering people, data, infrastructure, ICT and third parties, with an availability position on each line and an owner against every resource not secured

title.en: Record the cost, benefit and risk-appetite basis for each selected strategy

description.en: For each strategy that was selected, write down what it costs to hold ready, the benefit it delivers against the requirement baseline, and how it was judged to sit inside the organisation's stated risk appetite. Where an option was considered and rejected on cost or benefit, record it beside the selected one, because the rejected alternative is what shows the choice was made deliberately rather than by default. Attach the selection record covering every strategy in the mapping.

evidenceHint.en: Strategy selection record giving the cost to hold ready, the benefit against the requirement baseline, the alternatives rejected on cost or benefit, and the risk-appetite basis for each selected strategy

title.en: Log each disruption with the strategy invoked and the recovery time achieved

description.en: For every disruption in the period, record what happened, which prioritised activities were affected, which continuity strategy was invoked, the time the activity was actually resumed and the capacity it resumed at. Set both against the timeframe and capacity in the requirement baseline and record whether the objective was met. Note anything that had to be improvised because the strategy did not fit the event — that is the input the review needs most, and it never appears in the strategy document itself. Attach the disruption record for the period, or the nil return where there was none.

evidenceHint.en: Disruption record for the period giving the activities affected, the strategy invoked, the actual recovery time and capacity against the objective, and any improvisation required, or a nil return

title.en: Assess each strategy against its requirement and record the gaps and recommendations

description.en: Give every strategy a compliance status against the requirement baseline: does it deliver resumption within the required timeframe at the agreed capacity, are the resources it depends on available, and did it meet the recovery objective on the occasions it was actually invoked. Where a strategy has never been invoked, mark it untested rather than passing it on paper. Each gap carries a recommendation, an owner and a target date, and the unresolved ones are carried into the conclusion. Attach the findings summary with the disruption analysis behind it.

evidenceHint.en: Strategy findings summary giving a compliance status per strategy against timeframe, capacity, resource availability and invocation outcome, with a recommendation, owner and target date per gap

text.en: Set each strategy against the recovery timeframe and capacity it must deliver.
Check the resource register for anything the strategy needs and does not have.
Read the disruption record for occasions the strategy was actually invoked.
Mark strategies never invoked as untested rather than giving them a pass.
Write a recommendation, owner and target date against every gap recorded.

controls.title: Sector-Specific Risk Tolerance Analysis
controls.objective: To ensure that the organization's determination of risk tolerance is informed and aligned with its role in critical infrastructure and influenced by sector-specific risk analysis.
controls.successCriteria:
The Risk Management Policy and Risk Register accurately reflect the organization's risk tolerance as influenced by its role in critical infrastructure and sector-specific risk analysis.
Evidence shows that sector-specific risk analyses are actively used to inform and update the organization's risk tolerance levels.
Decision-making processes regarding risk tolerance are documented and demonstrate consideration of sector-specific risks and critical infrastructure role.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
