Collect the organization's Risk Management Policy and Risk Register.
Gather documentation on sector-specific risk analyses and reports.
Obtain records of decision-making processes regarding risk tolerance levels.

Analysis:
Review the Risk Management Policy and Risk Register to identify how risk tolerance levels are defined and updated.
Examine sector-specific risk analyses to determine how they inform the organization's risk tolerance.
Analyze decision-making records to confirm that sector-specific information and critical infrastructure considerations are incorporated into risk tolerance determinations.

Output:
A report summarizing findings from the Risk Management Policy and Risk Register review.
Compilation of sector-specific risk analyses and how they align with the organization's risk tolerance.
Analysis of decision-making records regarding risk tolerance.

title.en: Register the sector-specific risk analyses that inform the organisation's risk tolerance

description.en: Collect the sector-specific risk analyses and reports the tolerance is meant to draw on and record each in a register carrying its publisher, publication date, the version held, and why it applies to this organisation — the sector it covers, or the part of the organisation's critical-infrastructure role it speaks to. An analysis nobody can produce on request cannot be shown to have informed anything, so hold the document itself alongside the register row rather than a reference to where it was read. Attach the register with the source documents it points to.

evidenceHint.en: Register of sector-specific risk analyses and reports giving publisher, publication date, version held and why each applies to this organisation, with the source documents attached

text.en: Collect the sector risk analyses and reports the organisation actually receives.
Record publisher, publication date and version held for each analysis collected.
Record why each applies here — the sector it covers or the role it speaks to.
Store the source document itself alongside its register row, not merely a reference.

title.en: Define each risk tolerance level in the Risk Management Policy against the sector analysis that informs it

description.en: State the tolerance levels in the policy as thresholds a risk owner can apply — the assessed level at which a risk must be treated, and the level above which it cannot be accepted — and cite against each the sector analysis or critical-infrastructure obligation that set it there rather than at a neighbouring value. Where the organisation's critical-infrastructure role makes a threshold stricter than a purely commercial reading would give, say so in the policy text, because that sentence is what an assessor is looking for when testing whether the role influenced the tolerance at all. Attach the issued policy version showing the thresholds and their cited sources.

evidenceHint.en: Issued Risk Management Policy version carrying the tolerance thresholds and the sector analysis or critical-infrastructure consideration cited against each

title.en: Apply the policy's tolerance thresholds to every entry in the Risk Register

description.en: Work through the Risk Register and set, on each entry, the tolerance threshold that applies to it under the policy and whether the entry's current assessed level sits inside or outside that threshold. Entries outside tolerance carry a named owner and a treatment decision on the entry itself; entries to which no threshold applies are the gap this task surfaces and are referred back to the policy rather than left blank. Mark where the applicable threshold is the stricter critical-infrastructure one, so the register shows which risks are governed by the sector obligation and which by the general policy — without that marking the register cannot evidence the influence the control is about. Attach the register export showing the threshold and the inside-or-outside verdict on every entry.

evidenceHint.en: Risk Register export showing, per entry, the applicable tolerance threshold, whether the assessed level sits inside or outside it, which entries are governed by the stricter critical-infrastructure threshold, and the owner and treatment on every entry outside tolerance

title.en: Record every decision that sets or revises a risk tolerance level

description.en: Each time a tolerance level is agreed or changed, write the decision down with the date, who took it, the sector analysis or critical-infrastructure consideration weighed, the value before and after, and the reasoning — including the cases where sector input was considered and deliberately not followed, which is a legitimate outcome but an indefensible silence. Where the decision was taken in a committee the minute is the record; where it was taken outside one, produce the equivalent note rather than letting the changed value in the policy speak for itself. Attach the decision records covering the period.

evidenceHint.en: Risk tolerance decision records for the period, each giving the date, the decision-taker, the sector analysis or critical-infrastructure consideration weighed, the value before and after, and the reasoning

title.en: Map each sector analysis to the tolerance decision that weighed it

description.en: Take the source register row by row and follow each analysis forward: which tolerance level did it cause to be reviewed, which decision record shows it being weighed, and what changed — or, where nothing changed, what reasoning was recorded for leaving the level where it was. An analysis that appears in the register but in no decision record is the finding this task exists to produce, because it shows a source held but not used, and that is exactly the difference between a tolerance informed by sector risk and one merely accompanied by it. Attach the trace with the unused sources listed and a named owner against each.

evidenceHint.en: Trace linking every registered sector analysis to the tolerance decision that weighed it and the resulting change or recorded no-change, with the analyses that reached no decision listed separately and owned

text.en: Take each analysis in the source register in turn, oldest first.
Find the tolerance decision record in which that analysis was weighed.
Record what the tolerance level was before and after, or the reasoning for no change.
List the analyses that appear in no decision record as the trace's exception list.
Name an owner and a date against each analysis on that exception list.

controls.title: Capacity Management Oversight
controls.objective: To ensure effective monitoring and adjustment of resource usage in line with current and projected capacity requirements for information processing facilities, human resources, and other critical systems.
controls.successCriteria:
The Capacity Management Plan accurately reflects current and projected business needs and IT infrastructure.
System utilization is optimized and aligned with the organization’s capacity requirements.
Historical trends and future projections of resource usage are realistic and actively managed.
Stress-tests confirm system readiness for peak demands.
Management demonstrates proactive engagement and decision-making in capacity management matters.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the latest Capacity Management Plan and related documents.
Gather system utilization reports for key information processing facilities, including cloud services if applicable.
Collect historical data on resource usage trends and future projections.
Retrieve records of recent stress-tests conducted on systems and services.
Acquire minutes of meetings where capacity management issues and decisions were discussed.

Analysis:
Review the Capacity Management Plan for completeness and alignment with current business needs and IT infrastructure.
Analyze system utilization reports to verify that system tuning and monitoring are being effectively applied.
Compare historical and projected resource usage trends to assess the accuracy of future capacity projections.
Evaluate the outcomes of stress-tests to confirm system readiness for peak performance requirements.
Scrutinize meeting minutes to ensure ongoing managerial engagement and proactive decision-making regarding capacity management.

Output:
A compiled report detailing findings from the Capacity Management Plan and utilization reports.
A comparative analysis of historical vs. projected resource usage.
Summary of stress-test results and their implications.
Overview of management discussions and decisions on capacity management.

title.en: Inventory the processing facilities, services and roles whose capacity is managed

description.en: Capacity management has no denominator until the resources under it are written down, and this control reaches past servers — the objective names information processing facilities, human resources and other critical systems. Build one row per resource carrying what it is, its owner, the capacity measure that actually matters for it (CPU, storage, throughput, licence seats, trained staff available) and the source that measure is read from. Include cloud services, whose capacity is elastic but neither unlimited nor free and whose limits are contractual as well as technical. Attach the register; it is what the Capacity Management Plan and every utilisation report are read against.

evidenceHint.en: Capacity scope register listing each processing facility, service and staffed role under capacity management with its owner, its capacity measure and the source that measure is read from

title.en: Record current and projected capacity requirements per resource in the Capacity Management Plan

description.en: Extend the Capacity Management Plan so every resource in the register carries the capacity available today, the capacity consumed today, the requirement projected forward and the business change that drives that projection — a headcount plan, a customer commitment, a seasonal peak. A projection with no stated driver cannot be assessed for realism, which is precisely what this control asks a reviewer to do. Name the utilisation threshold at which action is taken for each resource, the action itself and its owner. Attach the issued version of the plan showing full coverage of the register.

evidenceHint.en: Issued Capacity Management Plan covering every register row with capacity available and consumed, the forward projection, the business driver behind it, and the action threshold with the owner who acts on it

text.en: Record the capacity available and the capacity consumed today for each register row.
State the forward requirement and name the business change that drives it.
Set the utilisation threshold at which action becomes necessary for each resource.
Name the action taken at that threshold and the owner who takes it.
Check the plan against the register for completeness and close any resource it omits.

title.en: Record period utilisation for each processing facility and cloud service against the plan's thresholds

description.en: Collect the utilisation figures for every resource in the register over the period and report them against the thresholds the plan sets, including cloud services where consumption is metered and billed rather than provisioned. Show the tuning and monitoring actually applied during the period — capacity added, workloads moved, limits raised, alerts that fired — so the report evidences that utilisation is managed rather than merely measured. Attach the utilisation report set with every threshold breach called out and the response to it recorded.

evidenceHint.en: Utilisation reports for the period covering each register row, showing observed usage against the plan's thresholds, every breach and the tuning or monitoring action taken in response

title.en: Test each system carrying a stated peak demand at that peak and record the headroom left

description.en: For every resource whose plan entry names a peak — a seasonal load, a launch, a month-end run — test it at that level and record what happened: the load applied, the point at which response times or error rates degraded, the headroom left against the stated requirement, and whether the system met it. A test recorded as passed with no margin captured tells a reviewer nothing about readiness for the next peak, which is what this control is assessing. Raise a capacity item with a named owner for every system that failed or passed with no headroom. Attach the stress-test records.

evidenceHint.en: Stress-test records per system showing the load applied, the degradation point, the headroom left against the stated peak requirement and any capacity item raised with its owner

title.en: Record the capacity decisions taken at the management meeting and the actions agreed

description.en: Put the period's utilisation reporting, forward projections and stress-test outcomes in front of management, and minute what was decided: capacity to procure, work to defer, thresholds to change, risk accepted. Record the decision, its owner and its date against each item, because this control tests managerial engagement through the minutes and a minute recording that capacity was discussed evidences attendance rather than decision-making. Attach the minutes covering the period under test.

evidenceHint.en: Minutes of the management meetings at which capacity was considered, recording each decision taken, the owner assigned to it and the date

title.en: Evaluate the plan's projections against the utilisation actually observed and revise the plan

description.en: Set the utilisation actually observed over the period beside what the plan projected for it, resource by resource, and record the variance. Where a projection was wrong, say why — an unstated driver, a change in the business, a measure read from the wrong source — and correct the plan itself rather than only the number, since an uncorrected cause reproduces the same error next cycle. Carry any resource trending toward its threshold ahead of schedule into the next management capacity discussion. Attach the comparison together with the plan revisions it produced.

evidenceHint.en: Historical-versus-projected utilisation comparison per resource with the variance explained and the resulting Capacity Management Plan revisions attached

text.en: Set the observed utilisation for the period beside the plan's projection for each resource.
Record the variance and, where it is material, why the projection was wrong.
Correct the plan entry, its stated driver or its data source, not only the figure.
Flag resources trending toward their threshold earlier than projected.
Carry the flagged resources into the next management capacity discussion.

controls.title: Equipment Security and Protection
controls.objective: Ensure secure siting and protection of equipment to minimize risks from physical and environmental threats, unauthorized access, and information leakage.
controls.successCriteria:
All equipment is sited securely and in compliance with organizational guidelines for minimizing physical and environmental risks.
Effective controls are in place and functioning as intended to protect against physical and environmental threats.
Only authorized personnel have access to sensitive equipment areas.
Environmental conditions are consistently monitored and maintained within safe parameters for equipment operation.
Compliance with policies and procedures for handling sensitive data and protecting equipment from information leakage and other risks.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Compile a comprehensive inventory of all information processing equipment.
Obtain floor plans showing the current siting of all equipment.
Collect policies and procedures related to equipment protection, including guidelines for environmental conditions, physical security measures, and handling of sensitive data.
Gather records of environmental monitoring (temperature, humidity, etc.) for areas with critical equipment.
Acquire documentation on physical and environmental protection measures implemented (e.g., lightning protection, vibration control, electromagnetic shielding).
Retrieve logs or records of access to areas with sensitive equipment.

Analysis:
Cross-reference equipment inventory with floor plans to verify secure and appropriate siting.
Evaluate existing protection measures against best practices for physical and environmental security.
Review environmental monitoring records to identify any conditions potentially harmful to equipment operation.
Assess access logs to ensure only authorized personnel have access to sensitive equipment areas.
Examine compliance with established guidelines for handling sensitive data and equipment, including checking against risks like water damage, fire, theft, and electromagnetic interference.

Output:
A report detailing the findings from the cross-referencing of equipment siting.
An assessment report on the adequacy of physical and environmental protection measures.
A summary of environmental condition monitoring results and any identified risks.
An analysis of access control effectiveness.
Compliance report regarding data handling and equipment protection guidelines.

title.en: Map every item of information processing equipment to its position on the site floor plan

description.en: The siting assessment cross-references the equipment inventory against the floor plans, and it can only be done once both name the same rooms. Take the inventory of information processing equipment, servers, network devices, storage, printers and the workstations that handle sensitive information, and record for each the room it stands in, its position within that room, and whether that room is access controlled. Anything found on the floor and absent from the inventory goes in, and anything in the inventory with no findable location is listed as unlocated. Attach the inventory keyed to the floor plan.

evidenceHint.en: Equipment inventory keyed to the floor plan giving asset, room, position within the room, whether the room is access controlled, and the list of unlocated assets

title.en: Record the physical and environmental protection fitted at each equipment location

description.en: Against each location in the inventory record what is actually installed to protect it: fire detection and suppression, water detection and any pipework running overhead, lightning and surge protection, vibration isolation, electromagnetic shielding where it applies, and the restraint or enclosure that protects against theft. Where a protection the organisation's guidelines call for is not fitted, record it as absent with the reason rather than omitting the row, because the absences are what the adequacy assessment reads. Attach the protection schedule with the commissioning or inspection evidence behind each entry.

evidenceHint.en: Protection schedule per equipment location naming the fire, water, lightning, vibration, shielding and anti-theft measures as fitted or absent, with commissioning or inspection evidence

title.en: Log the temperature and humidity readings for every area holding critical equipment

description.en: Record the readings the monitoring in each critical area produces, on the interval the guidelines set, alongside the safe range for the equipment in that area. What matters is the excursions: every reading outside the range is recorded with its duration, its cause, what was done about it, and whether any equipment was affected. An area with no monitoring fitted is recorded as unmonitored on the same sheet, since an empty column and a stable environment otherwise look identical. Attach the environmental monitoring records for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Environmental monitoring records for the period per critical area, stating the safe range, each excursion with its duration, cause and remedy, and the areas that are unmonitored

title.en: Log every entry to the rooms the inventory marks as holding sensitive equipment

description.en: Keep the access record for every area the inventory marks as holding sensitive equipment: badge reads where a system produces them, and the written access record where no badge system covers the door. Each period read the entries against the people authorised for that area and mark each as authorised or unmatched, then send every unmatched entry to a named owner for explanation and record the explanation given. Attach the access log extract for the period with the exception list and its dispositions.

evidenceHint.en: Access log extract for the period per sensitive equipment area, each entry marked authorised or unmatched, with a recorded disposition against every unmatched entry

title.en: Compare each item's actual siting against the floor plan and the organisation's siting guidelines

description.en: Walk the floor plan against reality and produce the siting report the control calls for: equipment standing where the plan does not show it, equipment in an uncontrolled room the guidelines require to be controlled, screens or printer output visible from a window or a public area, and equipment sited under pipework, beside external doors or in circulation space. Each finding carries the asset, the guideline it breaches, the risk it creates and the owner who will move or shield it. Attach the report with the annotated floor plan.

evidenceHint.en: Equipment siting report with an annotated floor plan, each mis-sited item, the guideline it breaches, the resulting risk and the accountable owner

title.en: Assess the protection at each location against the threats its equipment faces and record the gaps

description.en: Read the protection schedule and the period's environmental and access records together, location by location, and judge whether what is fitted actually covers the threats the guidelines identify: water, fire, theft, electromagnetic interference and unauthorised access. A protection that exists but failed its test, or an area whose readings sat outside range for a week, is a gap regardless of what the schedule claims it has. Produce the adequacy assessment with a verdict per location, the gaps, and an owner and remediation against each. Attach the assessment.

evidenceHint.en: Protection adequacy assessment with a verdict per equipment location, the gaps found against water, fire, theft, interference and access, and an owner and remediation per gap

text.en: List the threats the guidelines identify for each equipment location.
Set the fitted protection from the schedule against each threat for that location.
Mark a protection that failed a test, or an excursion left unresolved, as a gap.
Record an owner and an agreed remediation against every gap raised.

controls.title: Confidentiality Agreement Compliance
controls.objective: Ensure that all employees, contractors, and third parties have signed confidentiality agreements that are compliant with the organization's requirements for the protection of information.
controls.successCriteria:
Every individual on the list has a signed agreement that is current and compliant with the organization's standards.
All agreements reflect the latest template in terms of clauses and legal enforceability.
Evidence of regular review and updating of the confidentiality agreement template.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain a complete list of current employees, contractors, and third parties engaged with the organization.
Collect copies of signed confidentiality or non-disclosure agreements for each individual on the list.
Gather records of the most recent review and update of the confidentiality agreement templates.

Analysis:
Verify that each individual on the employee, contractor, and third-party list has a corresponding signed confidentiality agreement.
Compare the terms of each signed agreement against the current template to ensure they include all necessary clauses and meet the organization's current standards.
Assess the dates of agreement signings and template reviews to ensure periodic review and updating are being followed.

Output:
A spreadsheet listing all individuals with a column indicating whether they have a corresponding signed agreement.
A report summarizing any discrepancies between individual agreements and the current template.
Documentation of the last review and update of the confidentiality agreement template.

title.en: List every current employee, contractor and third party who must hold a confidentiality agreement

description.en: Draw the population from the HR system, the contractor register and the supplier records so all three engagement types are represented, one row per person or party, carrying the engagement type, the start date, the business area they work with, and who holds their signed agreement. A third party engaged under a corporate agreement is listed as the party with the named individuals it covers, so the later matching has something to match against. Attach the list with the date it was drawn — it is the denominator the coverage spreadsheet counts against.

evidenceHint.en: Dated list of current employees, contractors and third parties, each with engagement type, start date and the party holding their signed confidentiality agreement

title.en: Record the review and reissue of the confidentiality agreement template

description.en: Review the confidentiality agreement template against the entity's current information protection requirements and its legal enforceability, and record the review as an event: the date, the reviewer, the clauses added, changed or removed, and the version number issued. Legal/DPO owns the wording. Where the review concludes no change is needed, record that conclusion with the same date and reviewer, because what the control asks to see is that a review happened, not only that a change was made. Attach the issued template version together with the review record.

evidenceHint.en: Current confidentiality agreement template with its version number, plus the review record giving the date, the reviewer, the clauses changed, and the decision recorded where no change was made

title.en: File the signed confidentiality agreement and template version for every new engagement

description.en: As each employee, contractor or third party is engaged, file their signed agreement against their row with the signature date and the template version they signed, before they are given access to the information the agreement covers. Where a third party signs a corporate agreement, file it once and record the individuals it covers. Attach the repository export for the period showing each signature, its date and the template version signed, since the version is what the later comparison works from.

evidenceHint.en: Signed agreement repository export for the period listing each signatory, the signature date and the template version signed

title.en: Match every person on the list to a signed agreement and record the gaps

description.en: Take the population list and mark, person by person, whether a signed agreement exists, giving each row a yes or a no. A no is any row where the agreement cannot be produced, is unsigned by either party, or is held only by a supplier who has not provided a copy. Against every no, name the owner responsible for obtaining it and the date it is to be in place. Attach the completed spreadsheet; it is the artifact that shows coverage, and its whole value is in the rows marked no.

evidenceHint.en: Coverage spreadsheet listing every person and party with a signed-agreement yes or no column, and an owner plus target date against every no

title.en: Compare each signed agreement against the current template and report the discrepancies

description.en: For every agreement on file, read the version signed against the current template and record which required clauses it omits or expresses in superseded terms, alongside the signature date so agreements predating the last template review are visible as a group rather than one at a time. Report per signatory the template version held, the clauses missing, and whether the gap is material enough to require re-signature; Legal/DPO decides materiality. Attach the discrepancy report with the re-papering list it produces.

evidenceHint.en: Discrepancy report naming, per signatory, the template version held, the signature date, the clauses missing or superseded, and whether re-signature is required

text.en: Record the template version each signed agreement on file was drawn from.
Read each agreement's clauses against the clause list in the current template.
Note every clause that is absent or worded to a superseded standard.
Have Legal/DPO decide, gap by gap, whether the agreement must be re-signed.

controls.title: Information Deletion Verification
controls.objective: Ensure the secure and compliant deletion of sensitive information from systems, devices, and storage media when no longer required.
controls.successCriteria:
All sensitive information is deleted in accordance with the organization's data retention policy and relevant laws.
Proper documentation and evidence of deletion are maintained for all deletion activities.
Third-party service providers (if used) comply with the organization's requirements for secure information deletion.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain a list of systems, devices, and storage media where sensitive information is stored (referencing the Data Retention and Deletion Policy).
Gather documentation or logs of deletion activities, including methods used (e.g., electronic overwriting, cryptographic erasure).
Collect evidence of deletion verification from third-party service providers, if applicable.

Analysis:
Verify that the deletion methods used align with the organization's data retention policy and relevant laws and regulations.
Confirm that each deletion activity is properly documented and that evidence of deletion is recorded.
For third-party service providers, ensure that the evidence of deletion provided by them is valid and complies with the organization's requirements.

Output:
A report detailing the deletion methods used and their compliance with policies and regulations.
A log or spreadsheet verifying each deletion activity and its adherence to the policy.
A summary of third-party compliance with the information deletion requirement.

title.en: Inventory the systems, devices and storage media holding sensitive information

description.en: The Data Retention and Deletion Policy names the information that must eventually be deleted; this task names where it actually sits. Produce one row per holding — production systems and datastores, backup sets and archives, endpoint devices, removable media, and third-party services processing the data on the organisation's behalf. Record the information type held, its custodian, and whether the holding is under the organisation's control or a provider's, because that last column decides which of the later tasks applies to the row. Backups and archives are the holdings most often missed, and they are where a deletion that succeeded in production is silently undone. Attach the register.

evidenceHint.en: Register of every system, device, storage medium and third-party service holding sensitive information, with the information type, the custodian and an in-house or provider custody value on every row

text.en: List production systems and datastores holding information covered by the retention policy.
Add the backup sets, archives and offline media carrying copies of that same information.
Add endpoint devices and removable media where sensitive information is permitted.
Add third-party services that store or process the information on the organisation's behalf.
Record the custodian and the in-house or provider custody value for every row.

title.en: Record the approved deletion method for each holding and the rule that requires it

description.en: For every row in the register, state the deletion method that applies to it — electronic overwriting, cryptographic erasure, physical destruction, provider-executed deletion — and cite what requires it: the clause of the data retention policy, or the law or regulation driving it where one does. A method chosen without a cited source cannot be assessed for compliance with policy and law, which is the analysis this control asks for. Where a holding cannot technically support the method its data class calls for, record that as a gap with a named owner rather than silently substituting a weaker method. Legal/DPO confirms the legal citations. Attach the method table.

evidenceHint.en: Deletion method table mapping each holding to its approved deletion method and citing the retention policy clause or legal requirement behind it, with unsupported holdings flagged and owned

title.en: Log every deletion with its method, scope and the person who performed it

description.en: Each time sensitive information is deleted, record what was deleted, from which holding, the method used, who requested it, who performed it and the date. Where a retention job deletes automatically, export the job's own record rather than re-keying it, and log separately the manual deletions and media destructions that leave no machine trace — those are exactly the events an export will not contain. Where destruction produces a certificate, file it with the log entry. This record set is what evidences that deletion happens, as distinct from being scheduled. Attach the deletion log for the period under test.

evidenceHint.en: Deletion log or retention-job export for the period showing the information deleted, the holding, the method used, the requester, the operator and the date, with destruction certificates filed alongside

title.en: Collect deletion evidence from every third-party provider holding sensitive information

description.en: For each provider-custody row in the register, request and file the provider's evidence that the information was deleted when required — a certificate of deletion, a signed confirmation, or a system-generated report naming the data and the date. Check that what arrives actually names the data in question and a date, because a general assurance that the provider deletes data on termination evidences a policy rather than an act. Where a provider will not produce evidence, record the refusal against the row as the finding and name the owner who will pursue it with that provider. Attach the evidence received together with the list of providers that produced none.

evidenceHint.en: Third-party deletion certificates or confirmations naming the data deleted and the date it was deleted, plus the list of providers that produced no evidence and the owner named to pursue each

title.en: Test a sample of logged deletions against the approved method and the retention policy

description.en: Draw a sample of deletions from the log covering every deletion method in use, and check three things for each: that the method recorded is the method approved for that holding, that the deletion happened within the period the retention policy requires, and that the information is in fact gone — verified by attempting retrieval wherever the holding permits it, including from backups. Mark a pass or fail per sampled deletion and record a remediation owner against every fail. Attach the verification sheet; it is what turns a deletion log into evidence of compliant deletion.

evidenceHint.en: Deletion verification sheet with one row per sampled deletion showing the method used against the method approved, the timing against the retention policy, the retrieval check performed, a pass or fail outcome and a remediation owner for each fail

text.en: Draw the sample so that every deletion method in use is represented in it.
Compare the method recorded against the method approved for that holding.
Check the deletion date against the retention period the policy sets.
Attempt retrieval, including from backups, wherever the holding allows it.
Mark pass or fail and name a remediation owner against every fail.

controls.title: Inquiry and Complaints Resolution
controls.objective: To ensure effective receipt, addressing, and resolution of inquiries, complaints, and disputes from data subjects and others.
controls.successCriteria:
All inquiries, complaints, and disputes are handled in a timely, effective, and compliant manner as per established procedures.
Adequate documentation and communication are maintained for each case.
Continuous monitoring and improvement are evident in handling inquiries and complaints.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Collect records of all inquiries, complaints, and disputes received since the last audit.
Obtain documentation of the responses and resolutions provided.
Review policy documents and procedures related to the management of inquiries, complaints, and disputes.

Analysis:
Assess each case to verify adherence to the established resolution process.
Evaluate the timeliness and effectiveness of responses and resolutions.
Check for completeness and appropriateness of communication with the individuals who raised the inquiries or complaints.

Output:
A comprehensive report detailing the handling of inquiries, complaints, and disputes.
Analysis summary of resolution effectiveness and timeliness.
Documentation of any gaps or non-compliance in the resolution process.

title.en: List every channel on which an inquiry, complaint or dispute can reach the organisation

description.en: Receipt is the first thing this control asks for, and a case that never reaches the register can be neither handled nor counted. List the channels: the privacy mailbox, the website form, the support desk, the phone line, postal mail, correspondence forwarded by a regulator, and the account managers and staff who are approached in person. For each channel record who monitors it, how often, and the exact route by which something arriving there becomes a case in the register — the manual step where somebody must decide to log it is where cases are lost, so record that step explicitly. Attach the channel list with a named monitor and a route to the register on every row.

evidenceHint.en: List of inquiry, complaint and dispute channels with the named monitor, the monitoring frequency and the route by which a case arriving there reaches the register

text.en: Enumerate the channels including the mailbox, web form, support desk, phone line and post.
Add the indirect routes: regulator correspondence, account managers and staff approached in person.
Name who monitors each channel and how often they do so.
Record the step at which something on that channel becomes a register entry.
Mark any channel with no route into the register as a gap with a named owner.

title.en: Record the resolution steps and response commitment for each case type in the procedure

description.en: Set out, per case type — a data subject request, a privacy complaint, a service or billing dispute, a third-party inquiry — the steps between receipt and closure: who acknowledges it and what the acknowledgement says, who investigates, who is empowered to decide the outcome, when escalation is required and to whom, and what closing the case requires. Against each type state the response and resolution commitment the organisation is held to, citing the regulation or contract that sets it where one does and stating it as an internal commitment where none does, so that the timeliness test later has a stated number to measure against rather than an opinion. Attach the issued procedure version carrying the steps and the commitment for every case type.

evidenceHint.en: Issued inquiry, complaint and dispute procedure giving the resolution steps, decision and escalation points and the stated response commitment for each case type, with the source of each commitment

title.en: Set the case record fields every inquiry, complaint and dispute must carry

description.en: Publish the case record template and fix the fields that make a case auditable after everyone involved has forgotten it: the date and channel of receipt, the identity of the person raising it and how they may be contacted, the case type, what was actually asked or alleged in their own words, the handler, each action taken with its date, every communication sent to them with its date and its content or attachment, the outcome and the reason for it, the closure date, and any referral to a regulator. Communication is scored on this record in the review, so a case closed without its outbound messages recorded is scored as uncommunicated. Attach the published template with the procedure clause that makes its completion a condition of closing a case.

evidenceHint.en: Published case record template and the procedure clause requiring every field to be complete before a case can be closed

text.en: List the receipt fields: date, channel, the identity of the person and their contact route.
List the substance fields: case type and what was asked or alleged in their own words.
List the handling fields: handler, each action with its date, and any escalation made.
List the communication fields: every message sent, its date and its content or attachment.
List the closure fields: outcome, the reason for it, closure date and any regulator referral.

title.en: Log every inquiry, complaint and dispute in the case register from receipt to closure

description.en: Every case is entered in the register on the day it is received, whichever channel it arrived on, and its entry is completed as it is handled so the register can be read at any moment to say what is open, with whom, and for how long. Cases resolved at first contact are logged too — leaving them out is what makes complaint volumes look flat while the channels get busier. Where the person who raised it never replies to a request for information, record that and its date rather than closing the case silently. Attach the case register covering every case received since the last audit, showing open and closed cases alike.

evidenceHint.en: Case register covering every inquiry, complaint and dispute received since the last audit, showing the channel, receipt and closure dates, handler, current status and outcome

title.en: Test a sample of closed cases against the procedure and its response commitment

description.en: Draw a sample spanning case types and channels, and test each closed case against the procedure: were the required steps performed and in order, was the decision taken by the person empowered to take it, was escalation applied where the procedure required it, and does the record hold the communications that were supposed to be sent. Measure the elapsed time from receipt to acknowledgement and from receipt to closure against that case type's stated commitment, and record it as a number per case. Score pass or fail with the breached step or the missed commitment named, and give every failure an owner. Attach the completed testing sheet.

evidenceHint.en: Case testing sheet scoring each sampled case against the procedure steps and its response commitment, with the elapsed times, the breached step named and an owner for every failure

text.en: Draw the sample so every case type and every channel is represented.
Check each procedure step was performed, in order, and by an empowered decision maker.
Confirm the record holds the communications the procedure requires to be sent.
Record the elapsed time to acknowledgement and to closure against the stated commitment.
Name the breached step or missed commitment on every failure and assign an owner.

title.en: Group the period's cases by cause and record the improvements raised from them

description.en: Read the register for the period as a whole rather than case by case: group the cases by the cause behind them and by the channel they arrived on, count each group, and set this period's counts against the last so a rising cause becomes visible. For every group large enough or serious enough to act on, record the improvement raised — a process change, a system change, a wording change or a retraining — with an owner and a due date. Then take the improvements raised at the last review and record whether they were implemented and whether their cause recurred afterwards, since an improvement that did not stop the cause is the finding this task is for. Attach the analysis with the new actions and the status of the previous period's actions.

evidenceHint.en: Case trend analysis grouping the period's cases by cause and channel, with each improvement raised carrying an owner and due date and the status of the previous period's actions

controls.title: Threat Identification and Documentation
controls.objective: To ensure that all internal and external threats are identified, documented, and maintained in the Risk Register in accordance with organizational cybersecurity policies.
controls.successCriteria:
The Risk Register accurately reflects all identified internal and external threats.
The process for identifying and documenting threats is consistently followed and documented.
Risk assessment activities align with the entries in the Risk Register, ensuring thoroughness and accuracy.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the most recent version of the Risk Register.
Collect documentation of the process for identifying and documenting threats (e.g., meeting minutes, emails, reports).
Retrieve the records of the latest risk assessment activities.

Analysis:
Review the Risk Register to ensure it includes both internal and external threats, clearly identifying each threat's nature, source, and potential impact.
Verify that the process for identifying and documenting threats is followed as per the organization’s policy, including the assessment of new threats and updates to existing threats.
Compare the Risk Register entries with the records of risk assessment activities to confirm consistency and completeness.

Output:
Annotated Risk Register highlighting reviewed entries.
Report summarizing compliance with the threat identification and documentation process.
Comparative analysis of Risk Register and risk assessment records.

title.en: Catalogue the internal and external threat sources the Risk Register draws on

description.en: Every register entry has to name the source that raised it, so start by writing down where the organisation looks. List the external sources — sector and national advisories, vendor and vulnerability feeds, peer incident reporting, penetration test and assessment output — and the internal ones — incident records, change and architecture reviews, audit findings, staff reporting — and record against each the named owner who reviews it for new threats. A source with no owner will deliver nothing to the register, and its presence in a policy is what disguises that. Attach the catalogue; it is the population both the identification procedure and the completeness review run against.

evidenceHint.en: Threat source catalogue listing each internal and external source with the named owner who reviews it for new threats

text.en: List the external advisories, feeds and assessment outputs the organisation subscribes to.
List the internal sources: incidents, change reviews, audit findings and staff reports.
Name the reviewing owner for each source and confirm they accept it.
Record what each owner does with a source when it raises something new.
Mark sources with no named owner as the outstanding work of this catalogue.

title.en: Document the procedure for raising a new threat and updating an existing register entry

description.en: Write the operating procedure an analyst follows at the keyboard: which trigger starts an assessment, who may raise a threat, what has to be recorded before it is accepted onto the register, and how an existing entry is revised when its source, likelihood or impact changes. Cover the update path explicitly and not only the creation path — a register that only ever grows is the common failure here, and it shows up later as entries that no longer match the assessment records. Name the cybersecurity policy clause the procedure implements so the two documents can be read against each other. Attach the issued procedure.

evidenceHint.en: Issued threat identification and documentation procedure covering the triggers, who may raise a threat, the record required before an entry is accepted, and the path for updating an existing entry

text.en: Name the triggers that start a threat identification activity, including scheduled source review.
State who may raise a threat and what they must record before it is accepted.
Write the update path for revising an existing entry when its assessment changes.
Cite the cybersecurity policy clause the procedure implements.

title.en: Record the nature, source and potential impact of every threat on the register

description.en: Work through the Risk Register and complete three fields on every threat entry: what the threat actually is, stated in terms of an actor or an event rather than a category; whether it is internal or external, with the source that raised it; and the impact it would have if realised, expressed against the assets or services affected. Entries carrying only a title are the work this task exists to finish, and an entry whose internal-or-external marking is blank cannot be counted in the completeness review at all. Attach the register export showing all three fields populated on every threat entry.

evidenceHint.en: Risk Register export showing, for every threat entry, its stated nature, its internal or external classification with the source that raised it, and its potential impact on named assets or services

title.en: Log each threat identification activity and the register entries it produced

description.en: Every time the organisation looks for threats — a scheduled review of a source in the catalogue, a risk workshop, an assessment following an incident or a change — record it: the date, who took part, the sources considered, the threats raised, and for each threat the register entry it created or the existing entry it updated. Where an activity raised nothing, record that too, because it is the only evidence that the source was reviewed at all rather than skipped. These records are the minutes, emails and reports an auditor asks for, and they are what shows the documented procedure was operated rather than merely written. Attach them for the period under test.

evidenceHint.en: Threat identification activity records for the period — minutes, reports or notes — each naming the date, participants, sources considered, threats raised, and the register entry created or updated for each, including activities that raised nothing

title.en: Test that the documented threat identification procedure was followed for the period

description.en: Take the source catalogue and the activity records together and check the procedure ran as written: was every source in the catalogue reviewed by the owner it names, did every threat raised reach the register carrying the record the procedure requires, and were existing entries revised when their assessment changed. Report a verdict per procedure step with the exceptions named beneath it rather than an overall opinion — the corrective action for a source nobody reviewed is nothing like the one for an entry nobody updated. Attach the compliance report with the sample of activities and entries it was built from.

evidenceHint.en: Threat identification process compliance report giving a verdict per procedure step, the exceptions named under each step, and the sample of activity records and register entries tested

title.en: Verify that every threat in the latest risk assessment records reached the Risk Register

description.en: Set the most recent risk assessment records beside the register and run the comparison in both directions: every threat the assessment identified should appear as a register entry with a matching nature, source and impact, and every register entry should trace back to an assessment or activity record that raised it. Mark each entry reviewed on the register itself, so the annotated export shows what was covered and what was not. Keep the two mismatch types on separate lists — an assessed threat that never reached the register is a documentation failure, while a register entry no assessment supports is usually a stale entry that should have been updated or closed. Attach the annotated register alongside the comparative analysis.

evidenceHint.en: Annotated Risk Register marking each entry reviewed, plus the comparative analysis listing separately the assessed threats absent from the register and the register entries no assessment record supports

text.en: Take the latest risk assessment records and list every threat they identified.
Find the matching register entry for each and compare nature, source and impact.
Trace every register entry back to the assessment or activity record that raised it.
Annotate the register to mark which entries this review actually covered.
Write the unregistered threats and the unsupported entries up as two separate lists.

controls.title: Dormant Account Management
controls.objective: Ensure all dormant accounts are identified and either disabled or deleted after 45 days of inactivity.
controls.successCriteria:
All user accounts are active or have been disabled/deleted as per the 45-day inactivity policy.
Documentation and system logs corroborate the actions taken on dormant accounts.
No accounts remain active beyond 45 days of inactivity without appropriate justification or exception.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain a list of all user accounts from the system's user management database.
Retrieve system logs or reports showing the last login date for each account.
Access records of disabled or deleted accounts for the period since the last audit.

Analysis:
For each account, calculate the duration of inactivity since the last login date.
Cross-reference with records of disabled or deleted accounts to verify compliance.
Identify any accounts that have been inactive for over 45 days and have not been disabled or deleted.

Output:
A report listing all user accounts with the date of last activity.
A compliance report identifying any accounts that have been inactive for over 45 days and their current status (active, disabled, or deleted).
Documentation of any actions taken (such as disabling or deleting accounts) since the last audit.

title.en: List every account store the inactivity rule applies to and the field that carries last activity

description.en: Name each directory, application and cloud tenancy holding user accounts and record, per store, the attribute or report giving an account's last successful sign-in and how far back that source retains it. A store whose last-login history is retained for less than the inactivity window cannot evidence compliance at all, and finding those is the point of this task — record each with an owner and the change needed. State how service and shared accounts are treated, since an inactivity rule written for people will otherwise sweep them up. Attach the store list with a last-activity source against every entry.

evidenceHint.en: Account-store list naming each directory or application in scope, its last-activity attribute or report, that source's retention window, and the stated treatment of service and shared accounts

title.en: Record the exception route that allows an account to stay enabled past the inactivity threshold

description.en: Some accounts sit idle legitimately — break-glass credentials, seasonal staff, accounts tied to an annual process. Write down who may authorise such an exception, the justification it must carry, and where the approved register is held so the compliance review can read it. Without this the review cannot tell a justified dormant account from a missed one and every one of them reads as a deviation. Attach the exception procedure together with the current register of approved exceptions.

evidenceHint.en: Exception procedure naming the authoriser and the justification an exception must carry, plus the current register of approved dormant-account exceptions

title.en: Produce the account inactivity report showing last activity and days idle for every account

description.en: Pull every account from the stores on the list and compute days since last successful sign-in, carrying the account identifier, its store, its owner and its current state — enabled, disabled or deleted. Accounts that have never signed in need an explicit value rather than a blank, since an account created two months ago and never used is exactly the case the rule is aimed at. Attach the report for the period; it is the denominator the disable action and the compliance review both work from.

evidenceHint.en: Account inactivity report listing every account with its store, owner, last activity date, days idle and current enabled, disabled or deleted state, never-used accounts included explicitly

title.en: Disable or delete each account past forty-five days idle and record the action taken

description.en: Work the report's over-threshold rows, setting aside only those carrying an approved exception, and disable or delete each account according to the treatment its account type calls for. For each, record the account, the store, the days idle at the time, the action taken, who took it and when — that record is what corroborates the action afterwards, and an account found disabled with no record is indistinguishable from one disabled for an unrelated reason. Attach the action record for the period, including the accounts left enabled and the exception each relied on.

evidenceHint.en: Record of accounts disabled or deleted in the period with store, days idle, action, actor and date, plus the accounts left enabled and the approved exception each cites

text.en: Filter the inactivity report to accounts past forty-five days since last activity.
Set aside the accounts covered by an entry in the approved exception register.
Disable or delete each remaining account according to its account type's treatment.
Record the account, days idle, action taken, actor and date for every account touched.

title.en: Reconcile the over-threshold accounts against the disable and delete records

description.en: Take every account the inactivity report shows past forty-five days and account for each one: disabled or deleted with a matching action record, or still enabled under an approved exception carrying its recorded justification. Anything else — an account still enabled with neither an action record nor an approved exception — is the deviation this control exists to catch, and each is listed with its owner and the date it was raised. Attach the compliance report showing every over-threshold account and its disposition.

evidenceHint.en: Compliance report listing every account over forty-five days idle with its current status, the matching disable or delete record or approved exception, and an owner against each unresolved account

controls.title: Data Masking Compliance
controls.objective: Ensure that sensitive data, such as PII, is adequately protected through data masking, pseudonymization, or anonymization techniques in compliance with the organization’s policies and applicable legislation.
controls.successCriteria:
All systems and databases containing sensitive data employ adequate data masking, pseudonymization, or anonymization techniques as per policy requirements.
Recent changes or updates to data protection techniques are in compliance with organizational policies and do not compromise the integrity of data protection.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain a list of systems and databases where sensitive data (e.g., PII) is stored or processed.
Gather configuration settings or implementation details demonstrating data masking, pseudonymization, or anonymization techniques used.
Collect recent change logs or system updates related to data masking configurations.

Analysis:
Review the list of systems and databases to identify those containing sensitive data.
Analyze configuration settings or implementation details to verify that data masking, pseudonymization, or anonymization techniques are properly implemented.
Examine change logs or system updates to ensure that any modifications to data masking techniques align with policy requirements and do not compromise data protection.

Output:
A report detailing the systems and databases containing sensitive data and their respective data protection techniques.
A compliance assessment report evaluating the implementation of data masking, pseudonymization, or anonymization techniques.
A change log analysis report highlighting any recent modifications and their compliance status.

title.en: Register every system and database that stores or processes sensitive personal data

description.en: Build one row per system or database holding sensitive data, naming the data categories it carries, the environment it runs in, and the owner who can produce a sample of its stored values on request. Include the non-production copies: a masked production database and an unmasked copy of it in test are the same data with different protection, and only the register makes that visible. This register is the population the technique mapping and the compliance assessment both run against, so a system missing from it is a system never assessed. Attach the register with the date it was compiled.

evidenceHint.en: Register of systems and databases holding sensitive data, one row per system giving the data categories, environment and owner, carrying the date compiled

text.en: Query the data inventory and schema catalogue for stores holding personal identifiers.
Add processing systems that handle sensitive data without storing it long term.
List the non-production, analytics and backup copies of every production store found.
Record the data categories, the environment and a named owner against each row.

title.en: Set the required protection technique for each sensitive data category

description.en: For every data category the register names, record which technique the policy requires — masking, pseudonymisation or anonymisation — the form it has to take (which characters survive a mask, whether a pseudonym is reversible and who holds the mapping), and the legislative basis where the requirement comes from law rather than internal choice. Anonymisation and pseudonymisation carry different consequences in data protection law, so the two are named separately rather than collapsed into one option. Legal/DPO owns the legislative column; Engineering lead confirms each form is implementable. Attach the issued requirement table.

evidenceHint.en: Issued requirement table giving, per sensitive data category, the required technique, the form it must take and the policy or legislative basis behind it

title.en: Record the masking configuration in force for each registered system

description.en: Against every row of the register, capture how the protection is actually implemented — the masking rule, view, policy object or transformation job, named precisely enough that somebody else could find it — and which fields it covers. Attach the configuration settings themselves rather than a summary of them: the auditor's request is for the configuration, and a table saying masking is enabled evidences nothing. Any registered system with no technique in force is recorded as such, with an owner, rather than left blank, because a blank reads as unchecked. Attach the mapping with the configuration extracts behind it.

evidenceHint.en: Technique mapping per registered system naming the masking, pseudonymisation or anonymisation implementation and the fields it covers, with the configuration extracts behind it

title.en: Log every change made to a data-masking configuration

description.en: Each time a masking, pseudonymisation or anonymisation configuration is altered — a rule changed, a field added to or dropped from scope, a transformation job disabled — record the system, the field affected, what changed, who made the change and the date. Export the log from the system that holds it where one exists, and record separately the changes applied by hand that leave no machine trace. This log is what lets the review judge whether recent updates kept protection intact rather than quietly narrowing it. Attach the change log for the period under test.

evidenceHint.en: Data-masking configuration change log for the period showing system, field, change made, who made it and the date for each entry

title.en: Sample stored values from each registered system and confirm they are protected

description.en: For every system on the register, pull a sample of the values a user or an administrator would actually see and read them against the requirement table: a field required to be masked that returns clear text is a fail regardless of what the configuration claims. Cover the non-production copies in the same pass, since that is where protection is most often absent altogether. Record a pass or fail per system with the sampled output behind it, and a remediation owner and date against every fail. Attach the compliance assessment report.

evidenceHint.en: Compliance assessment report with a pass or fail per registered system, the sampled output supporting each verdict and a remediation owner for every fail

text.en: Pull a sample of stored or displayed values for each protected field per system.
Read each sample against the technique the requirement table demands for that category.
Repeat the sampling against the non-production and analytics copies of the same data.
Record a pass or fail per system and attach the sampled output as its evidence.
Name a remediation owner and date for every field returning unprotected values.

title.en: Assess each masking configuration change in the period against the requirement table

description.en: Take the change log and judge every entry on one question: did the change leave the field's protection at or above what the requirement table demands? Changes that narrowed coverage — a field removed from a rule, a transformation relaxed to serve a reporting need — are the ones to write up in full, with the reason recorded at the time and whether the protection that remains still meets the table. Attach the change-log analysis naming each change, its compliance status, and every change carried forward as a finding.

evidenceHint.en: Change-log analysis listing each masking configuration change in the period with its compliance status against the requirement table and the findings carried forward

controls.title: BCMS Effectiveness and Maintenance
controls.objective: Ensure the continuous effectiveness and maintenance of the Business Continuity Management System (BCMS), excluding Business Impact Analysis (BIA), Awareness, Documentation, and overall Operation parts.
controls.successCriteria:
All BCMS policies and procedures are current, comprehensive, and relevant.
Regular tests and drills are conducted, and outcomes are documented and acted upon.
BCMS review meetings are held regularly, with documented minutes showing active participation and continuous improvement efforts.
The BCMS is updated regularly to reflect changes in the organization or external environment.
Corrective and preventive actions are effectively addressing identified issues and improving the BCMS.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:

Obtain the list of BCMS policies and procedures.
Acquire records of BCMS tests and drills conducted in the last year.
Gather minutes from BCMS review meetings.
Collect BCMS maintenance records, including updates to the system.
Obtain the list of corrective and preventive actions taken.

Analysis:

Review the BCMS policies and procedures for completeness and relevance.
Verify that tests and drills are conducted regularly and document their outcomes.
Analyze minutes from BCMS review meetings to ensure continuous improvement and management involvement.
Check maintenance records to confirm that the BCMS is updated periodically.
Evaluate the effectiveness of corrective and preventive actions taken to address issues identified in the BCMS.

Output:

A report summarizing the review of BCMS policies and procedures.
Documentation of tests and drills outcomes.
Minutes from review meetings.
Records of BCMS updates.
A summary of corrective and preventive actions taken, along with their effectiveness.

title.en: Register every BCMS policy and procedure with its owner, version and last review date

description.en: Produce the single list of the documents that make up the business continuity management system — policies, procedures, plans and standing instructions — each with its owner, its current version, the date it was last reviewed and, where one is set, the interval at which review falls due. Documents held outside the document management system still count, and they are the ones most likely to be stale, so record where each one is held. This register is the population the currency review reads row by row. Attach the register; a row with no last-review date is not done.

evidenceHint.en: BCMS document register listing every policy, procedure and plan with its owner, current version, last review date, the review interval where one is set, and where the document is held

title.en: Record the outcome of each BCMS test and drill and the actions it raised

description.en: For every test and drill run in the year, keep a record carrying the date, the scope exercised, who took part, what was observed, whether it met its objective, and the actions raised with their owners. Hold the records in date sequence so the gap between drills is readable, because this control asks whether tests and drills are conducted regularly and a folder of individually successful records cannot answer that question. Attach the test and drill records for the last year together with the actions they produced.

evidenceHint.en: Test and drill records for the last year in date sequence, giving date, scope, participants, the observed outcome against the objective and the actions raised with owners

title.en: Record the attendees, decisions and improvement actions of each BCMS review meeting

description.en: Minute every BCMS review meeting so the record shows who attended, what was put in front of them, what was decided and which improvement actions were raised with owners and dates. Record which of the attendees were management, because management involvement is one of the things this control looks for and it is visible only on the attendance line. Minutes recording items as noted, with no decision attached, evidence a meeting rather than a review. Attach the minutes for every meeting held in the period.

evidenceHint.en: Minutes of every BCMS review meeting in the period showing who attended and in what capacity, the material reviewed, the decisions taken and the improvement actions raised with owners and dates

title.en: Log every update made to the BCMS and the change that prompted it

description.en: Keep a maintenance log with one row per change to the management system: what was changed, the version before and after, the date, who made it, and the organisational or external change that prompted it — a reorganisation, a new site, a new supplier, a regulatory change, an exercise finding. A change with no recorded prompt cannot be told apart from an edit, and this control is asking for evidence that the system tracks its environment rather than merely being tidied. Attach the maintenance log for the period.

evidenceHint.en: BCMS maintenance log with one row per update giving the document changed, the versions before and after, the date, the author and the organisational or external change that prompted it

title.en: Review each BCMS policy and procedure for currency, completeness and relevance

description.en: Work down the document register and give each document a verdict on three counts: is it inside its review interval, does it still describe how the organisation actually operates, and does it cover the scope it claims. Read it alongside the maintenance log so a document that went unchanged through a year of organisational change is flagged rather than passed for looking tidy. Every document failing on any of the three gets an owner and a target revision date. Attach the review report covering every row of the register.

evidenceHint.en: BCMS document review report giving a currency, completeness and relevance verdict for every register row, with an owner and target revision date against each document that failed

text.en: Check each document against its review interval and its last review date.
Confirm the document still describes how the organisation operates today.
Confirm the document covers the whole scope that it claims to cover.
Read the maintenance log for documents unchanged through material change.
Name an owner and a target revision date for every document that failed.

title.en: Assess whether each corrective and preventive action closed the issue that raised it

description.en: Take the list of corrective and preventive actions and, for each, identify the issue it was raised against, what was actually done, and the evidence that the issue has not recurred since — a drill that exercised the fixed area, a log that no longer shows the fault, a document now carrying the change. Mark each action effective, ineffective or too early to tell, and re-open the ineffective ones with a new owner rather than leaving them recorded as closed. Attach the summary of actions with their effectiveness verdicts and the evidence behind each.

evidenceHint.en: Summary of corrective and preventive actions giving the issue behind each, the action taken, the evidence of non-recurrence and an effective, ineffective or too-early verdict

controls.title: Use of Personal Information Control
controls.objective: To ensure personal information is used strictly for the purposes identified and consented to by the data subjects, in alignment with the entity’s privacy objectives.
controls.successCriteria:
All uses of personal information are in accordance with the purposes for which consent was given by data subjects.
No deviations from consented purposes without obtaining appropriate additional consent.
Complete alignment of personal information usage with the entity’s privacy objectives and data subject consent.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Acquire a list of systems and processes where personal information is used.
Obtain documentation of the intended purposes for which personal information is used in each system.
Gather records of consent forms or agreements indicating the purposes for which data subjects have consented to the use of their information.

Analysis:
Review the documentation to verify that the use of personal information aligns with the purposes consented to by the data subjects.
Cross-check the purposes stated in the consent forms with the actual usage in each system or process.
Assess whether any use of personal information deviates from the intended purposes and if so, whether proper consent was obtained for such use.

Output:
A comprehensive report detailing the analysis of how personal information is used in relation to data subject consent.
A compliance matrix comparing the stated purposes in consent forms against actual usage in systems and processes.
Documentation of any deviations from consented purposes and subsequent actions taken.

title.en: List every system and process that uses personal information and the purpose each use serves

description.en: Build the population the compliance matrix will be scored against: one row per system or process that uses personal information, naming the data categories it uses, what it does with them, and the purpose that use serves stated specifically enough to be compared with a consent form — 'service delivery' cannot be compared with anything, 'sending appointment reminders by SMS' can. Include the uses that are not obvious from a system inventory: analytics over production data, model training, testing with copied live data, and personal information passed to a supplier for that supplier's own purposes. Attach the list with a specific purpose stated on every row and a named owner for each use.

evidenceHint.en: List of systems and processes using personal information, each with the data categories used, the specific purpose the use serves and a named owner

text.en: Enumerate uses from the processing record, the application inventory and the integration list.
Add the non-obvious uses: analytics, model training and testing with copied live data.
Add personal information passed to a supplier for that supplier's own purposes.
State each purpose specifically enough that it can be matched to a consent form.
Name the owner accountable for each use on the list.

title.en: Cite the consent form or agreement wording that authorises each use on the list

description.en: Against every row record which consent form, agreement or notice authorises that use, the version in force when the data was collected, and the exact wording that covers the purpose — a reference to a document is not enough, because the question the review answers is whether the words themselves cover the use. Where a use rests on a basis other than consent, record that basis rather than leaving the cell blank, so the rows genuinely relying on consent are the ones this control tracks. A row with neither a wording nor an alternative basis is already a deviation and goes to the deviation log rather than waiting for the matrix. Attach the mapping with the cited wording and version against each row.

evidenceHint.en: Mapping from each use to the consent form or agreement version and the exact wording that authorises it, or to the alternative basis where consent is not relied on

title.en: Set the approval gate a new or changed use of personal information must pass

description.en: Write into the procedure the step that stops a use running ahead of the consent covering it: who must be told when a new purpose is proposed or an existing one broadened, what they are given in order to decide (the data categories, the purpose, the individuals affected and the consent wording currently in force), who decides whether existing consent covers it, and what must happen when it does not — obtain additional consent, re-scope the use, or refuse it. Name where the gate sits in the change and product processes so it is reached rather than remembered. Attach the issued procedure version showing the gate, the decision maker and the outcomes it can produce.

evidenceHint.en: Issued procedure version defining the approval gate for new or changed uses of personal information, the decision maker and the required outcome when existing consent does not cover the use

title.en: Record each new or changed use of personal information and the consent obtained for it

description.en: Every proposal reaching the gate is recorded whatever its outcome: the use proposed, the data categories and individuals it affects, the decision on whether existing consent covers it and who took that decision, and where it did not, the additional consent obtained — the wording used, when it was sought, how many individuals gave it and how many did not — or the decision to re-scope or refuse. Uses that proceeded without passing the gate are recorded here too, taken from the change records, because they are the population the deviation log is built from. Attach the register of new and changed uses for the period with the consent evidence attached to each entry.
