evidenceHint.en: Register of new and changed uses for the period, each showing the gate decision and either the additional consent obtained with its wording and response counts or the decision to re-scope or refuse

title.en: Build the compliance matrix comparing each system's actual use against its consented purpose

description.en: Take the list row by row and establish what each system actually does with the personal information rather than what it was documented to do — read the queries, jobs, integrations, exports and audience definitions that touch the data — then set that observed use against the consent wording cited for it. Score each row as within the consented purpose, outside it, or unclear, and state on every row both the observed use and the wording it was compared with, so the score can be checked by somebody else. Attach the compliance matrix together with the configuration and query output the observed use was read from.

evidenceHint.en: Compliance matrix scoring each use as within, outside or unclear against its consented purpose, showing the observed use and the consent wording it was compared with

text.en: Read each system's actual use from its queries, jobs, integrations and exports.
Set the observed use beside the consent wording cited for that row.
Score the row as within, outside or unclear against the consented purpose.
Record the evidence behind the observation so the score can be re-checked later.
Carry every row scored outside or unclear into the deviation log.

title.en: Record each deviation from a consented purpose with the action taken to resolve it

description.en: For every row the matrix scored outside its consented purpose or unclear, open an entry stating the use, the systems and data categories involved, the individuals affected and how the deviation arose. Record the action taken and its date: the use stopped, additional consent obtained from the affected individuals, the data deleted, or the purpose re-scoped and the wording updated — and where the resolution is still open, the owner and the date it is due. An entry closed by deciding the use was acceptable after all carries the reasoning and the name of whoever accepted it, because that is the decision an auditor will want to read. Attach the deviation log with the evidence of each action taken.

evidenceHint.en: Deviation log listing every use scored outside or unclear against its consented purpose, with the action taken and its evidence, or the owner and due date where the resolution is still open

controls.title: Effective Data Discovery Compliance
controls.objective: To ensure that data discovery methods are effective in discovering cleartext PAN across all system components and file formats and that their effectiveness is confirmed at least once every 12 months.
controls.successCriteria:
Data discovery methods are capable of identifying cleartext PAN in all reviewed system components and file formats.
The effectiveness of data discovery methods is tested and confirmed at least once every 12 months.
The annual review process for the effectiveness of data discovery methods is well-documented and adheres to the 12-month cycle.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain a list of all system components and file formats used within the organization.
Acquire the latest data discovery test results, including the methods used and their effectiveness in identifying cleartext PAN.
Gather documentation of the annual review process for the effectiveness of data discovery methods.

Analysis:
For each system component and file format, assess whether the data discovery methods used can effectively identify cleartext PAN.
Review the annual test results to verify the effectiveness of data discovery methods.
Evaluate the annual review process documentation to ensure compliance with the 12-month review cycle.

Output:
A report detailing the capability of data discovery methods for each system component and file format.
A summary of the effectiveness of data discovery methods based on the latest test results.
A compliance report on the annual review process for data discovery methods.

title.en: List the system components and file formats data discovery must cover

description.en: Build the coverage list in two parts: every system component that could hold cardholder data — databases, file shares, mail stores, application servers, backups, log stores and endpoints — and every file format those components hold, including compressed archives, spreadsheets, PDFs, images and proprietary exports. Each row names the component or format and the owner who can grant the discovery tool access to it. This list is the denominator the capability verdict is reported against, so a format nobody thought of is a format the annual confirmation will never test. Attach the list carrying the date it was compiled.

evidenceHint.en: Dated list of system components and file formats in scope for data discovery, each row naming the owner who can grant the discovery tool access

title.en: Record which discovery method covers each system component and file format

description.en: Against every row of the coverage list, name the discovery method applied to it — the tool, the scan profile and the pattern set used to recognise a PAN — and where one tool covers several rows say so explicitly rather than by implication. Rows with no method against them are the gap this task exists to surface, and each carries an owner and a decision: bring it into the scope of an existing tool, acquire a method for it, or record why the component cannot hold cleartext PAN. Attach the mapping with the unaddressed rows listed separately.

evidenceHint.en: Mapping of discovery tool, scan profile and pattern set to each system component and file format, with the rows carrying no method listed separately and an owner against each

title.en: Document the annual effectiveness review, its inputs and its 12-month cycle

description.en: Write down how the effectiveness of the discovery methods is confirmed: who runs the confirmation, what triggers it, which inputs it consumes, how the result is recorded, and the requirement that no more than 12 months separates one confirmation from the next. Name where the confirmation record is filed, because the interval check a later task performs is only possible if successive records are findable. Attach the issued procedure showing the 12-month cycle stated as a requirement rather than as an intention.

evidenceHint.en: Issued annual effectiveness review procedure naming the owner, trigger, inputs, the 12-month interval requirement and where each confirmation record is filed

title.en: Seed PAN-format test values in every component and file format and record what discovery finds

description.en: Run the confirmation by placing test values in recognisable PAN format into each system component and each file format on the coverage list, then run the discovery method mapped to that row and record whether the value was found. Capture per row the method used, the scan date, found or not found, and where not found whether the method failed to reach the location or reached it and did not recognise the value — those are different defects with different fixes. Remove the test data when the run completes and record its removal. Attach the test results covering every row of the coverage list.

evidenceHint.en: Data discovery test results with one row per system component and file format giving the method used, the scan date, a found or not-found outcome and the failure mode where not found

text.en: Generate test values in PAN format and record where each one is placed.
Cover every system component and every file format the coverage list names.
Run the mapped discovery method against each seeded location and capture its output.
Record found or not found per row, separating no access from no recognition.
Remove the seeded test values and record the date each one was removed.

title.en: Report a detection verdict for every system component and file format

description.en: Turn the test results into the capability report the control calls for: one line per component and per format stating whether the discovery methods in use can effectively identify cleartext PAN there. Rows that failed carry the reason from the test, a remediation owner and a target date; rows never tested because no method covers them are reported as untested rather than as passing, which is the distinction that makes this report worth reading. Attach the report with the test results it was derived from.

evidenceHint.en: Capability report giving a can-detect, cannot-detect or untested verdict per system component and file format, with reason, owner and target date on every non-passing row

title.en: Check the interval between successive effectiveness confirmations against 12 months

description.en: Retrieve the dated record of this confirmation and of the one before it, put the two dates side by side and record the elapsed months. Where the gap exceeds 12 months, or where no prior record can be found, state that plainly with the reason and the date the cycle is being reset from. Attach the compliance report on the annual review process with both dated confirmation records behind it.

evidenceHint.en: Annual review compliance report giving the dates of this and the previous effectiveness confirmation, and the elapsed interval against the 12-month requirement

controls.title: Secure Coding Compliance
controls.objective: To ensure that secure coding practices are consistently applied in all software development activities.
controls.successCriteria:
All reviewed projects demonstrate adherence to the organization's secure coding standards.
Developers involved in software development are adequately trained in secure coding practices.
Third-party and open-source components are used and managed in compliance with the organization's policies.
No critical vulnerabilities are found during the security testing of the software.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Retrieve the list of all ongoing and recently completed software development projects.
Collect documentation related to secure coding standards and practices used in these projects.
Obtain reports from static and dynamic security testing, code reviews, and penetration tests.
Gather training records for developers on secure coding practices.
Request details of third-party and open-source software components used in the projects.

Analysis:
Review the documentation to confirm the application of secure coding practices as per the organization's guidelines.
Examine static and dynamic testing reports, code review findings, and penetration test results for evidence of adherence to secure coding standards.
Verify that all developers involved in the projects have received adequate training in secure coding practices.
Assess the usage and management of third-party and open-source components for compliance with secure coding and sourcing policies.

Output:
A report detailing the adherence to secure coding practices in each project.
A compliance matrix comparing actual practices against the organization's secure coding standards.
A summary of training completion for developers.
An assessment report on third-party and open-source software component usage.

title.en: Inventory the development projects in scope with their code repositories and the languages each uses

description.en: List every software development project running or recently closed with the repositories it owns, the languages and frameworks written in them and the team writing the code. The repository and language columns are what make the list usable: the secure coding standard is tested against code, so a project named without its repository cannot be sampled, and a language the standard does not cover cannot be scored against it. Attach the inventory dated at compilation as the population the testing, component and training tasks all draw on.

evidenceHint.en: Dated inventory of ongoing and recently completed development projects giving, per project, the code repositories it owns, the languages and frameworks in use and the delivery team

title.en: Record the secure coding standard's rules and the projects and languages each rule binds

description.en: Take the secure coding standard and express it as rules that can be checked against code, each one saying which languages, frameworks or project types it applies to. A rule that applies to everything in principle and to nothing in practice is why adherence reviews return an opinion instead of a result. Where a project uses a language the standard does not cover, record that gap here rather than scoring the project against rules that do not fit it. Attach the issued standard with the applicability mapping.

evidenceHint.en: Issued secure coding standard with an applicability mapping stating, per rule, the languages, frameworks or project types it binds, plus the languages in use that the standard does not yet cover

title.en: Register each project's security-testing findings with their severity and closure status

description.en: Collect the static analysis, dynamic analysis, code review and penetration test reports held for each inventoried project and register what they found: the finding, the code or component it sits in, its severity, and whether it is closed or still open. Record the closure of every critical finding explicitly — this control is tested on no critical vulnerabilities being found during security testing, which cannot be shown from a register that lists findings and stops. Where a project has no report at all, register it as untested rather than leaving it to read as clean. Attach the findings register with the reports it was built from.

evidenceHint.en: Security-testing findings register per project, with the static and dynamic analysis output, code review records and penetration test reports behind it, giving each finding's severity and closure status

text.en: Collect the static and dynamic analysis output held for each inventoried project.
Add the code review records, naming the reviewer and the scope each covered.
Add the penetration test report and the project version it examined.
Register each finding with its severity and the code or component it sits in.
Record whether each finding is closed, and close every critical one.
Register a project holding no test report at all as untested, not as clean.

title.en: Record the third-party and open-source components each project uses with their approval and version status

description.en: Keep a register of the third-party and open-source components the inventoried projects pull in, carrying the component, the version in use, whether its use was approved under the organisation's policy and when it was last updated. Build it from the projects' dependency manifests rather than from developer recollection, because the transitive dependencies are exactly what recollection omits. Attach the register with the manifests it was derived from.

evidenceHint.en: Third-party and open-source component register per project, derived from the dependency manifests, giving component, version in use, approval status under the organisation's policy and the date it was last updated

title.en: Record secure coding training completion for every developer on the inventoried projects

description.en: Keep the completion record for the developers writing code on the projects in the inventory: who has completed the secure coding training, when, and which course it covered. Record non-completions by name against their project rather than reporting a completion percentage — this control is tested on the developers involved in the projects being adequately trained, and an aggregate figure cannot answer that for a specific project. HR supplies the completion data. Attach the training summary for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Secure coding training summary listing every developer on the inventoried projects with their completion date and the course completed, and the non-completions named against the project each works on

title.en: Map each project's observed coding practice against the secure coding standard and report the deviations

description.en: Build the compliance matrix this control's output calls for: one row per project and rule, showing whether the practice observed in the testing reports, code reviews and component register meets the rule that binds it. Draw the verdict from the evidence gathered rather than from the project's own assertion, and against each deviation record its severity, the owner and the remediation agreed. Attach the matrix and the adherence report summarising the position across the projects reviewed.

evidenceHint.en: Secure coding compliance matrix scoring each project against every applicable rule, with the evidence reference behind each verdict and the severity, owner and remediation recorded against each deviation

text.en: List each project beside the secure coding rules the mapping says bind it.
Read the testing reports and code reviews for evidence against each rule.
Record a met or deviation verdict with the evidence reference behind it.
Set each deviation's severity and agree a remediation owner and date.
Summarise the deviations recurring across projects in the adherence report.

controls.title: Clock Synchronization Control
controls.objective: Ensure all information processing systems within the organization are synchronized to an approved, reliable time source for accurate time-stamping and consistency across systems.
controls.successCriteria:
All systems are synchronized to the approved standard reference time.
Time synchronization configurations comply with organizational policies and best practices.
Discrepancies in time settings, especially in cloud and hybrid environments, are identified and addressed.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain a list of all information processing systems from the IT inventory.
Capture screenshots or system reports showing the current time settings and synchronization source for each system.
Collect documentation of the organization's defined standard reference time and approved external time sources.
Gather configuration details of NTP or PTP protocols implemented across the network.

Analysis:
Verify that each system's clock is synchronized to the approved standard reference time.
Check that the time synchronization settings (e.g., NTP, PTP configurations) are consistent with organizational policies and best practices.
For systems utilizing cloud services, assess the synchronization mechanism and note any discrepancies.
Evaluate the use of multiple external time sources for reliability and manage any variance observed.

Output:
A comprehensive report detailing the time settings and synchronization status of each system.
An analysis document comparing actual settings against policy requirements and best practices.
A summary of discrepancies or issues found during the audit.

title.en: List every information processing system with the time source it synchronises to

description.en: Start from the IT inventory and give each information processing system a row: its identifier, its owner, whether it runs on the premises, in a cloud service or in a hybrid arrangement, and the time source it currently points at as read from the system itself rather than from the build standard. A system whose synchronisation source cannot be read — an appliance exposing no setting, a managed service that does not disclose one — is recorded as undetermined with an owner, because that is a finding rather than an omission. This list is the population the settings capture and the discrepancy analysis both run against. Attach the dated list.

evidenceHint.en: Dated list of every information processing system with its owner, hosting model and the time source it currently synchronises to, with undetermined sources flagged and owned

title.en: Record the standard reference time and the approved external time sources

description.en: Document the reference the whole estate is measured against: the standard reference time the organisation uses, the external time sources approved to supply it, how many are used so a single source drifting does not carry the estate with it undetected, and the maximum offset a system may show before it is treated as out of synchronisation. Name the sources specifically rather than describing a class of them. Without a stated tolerance the later comparison has nothing to fail against, so the tolerance is the part of this task that matters most. Attach the issued time standard, dated.

evidenceHint.en: Issued time standard naming the standard reference time, each approved external time source, the number of sources in use, and the maximum permitted offset before a system is out of synchronisation

title.en: Record the NTP or PTP configuration required for each class of system

description.en: Turn the standard into the configuration detail an operator applies and an auditor reads: for each class of system on the list — server, workstation, network device, virtual machine, cloud-hosted service — the protocol used, the time servers configured, the polling interval, and where the class sits in the local synchronisation hierarchy. Cover the cloud and hybrid classes explicitly and say what the provider supplies against what the organisation configures, because that boundary is where synchronisation is most often assumed rather than set. Attach the configuration standard with a complete entry for every class the system list contains.

evidenceHint.en: Time synchronisation configuration standard giving, per system class, the NTP or PTP protocol, the configured time servers, the polling interval and the hierarchy position, including the cloud and hybrid classes

title.en: Capture each system's current time setting and its offset from the reference

description.en: Work down the system list and record, from the system itself, the time it is showing, the source it is synchronised to, whether synchronisation is reported as healthy, and the offset from the reference time at the moment of capture. Take the system report or screenshot the auditor asks for as the evidence behind each reading rather than transcribing values into a spreadsheet alone. Where a system reports no synchronisation at all, capture that state explicitly — an unsynchronised clock that happens to read correctly today is the one that drifts silently. Attach the time settings report with the captured system output behind it.

evidenceHint.en: Time settings report covering every listed system with its observed time, synchronisation source, synchronisation health and offset from the reference, backed by the captured system reports or screenshots

title.en: Compare the captured offsets and sources against the standard and record each discrepancy

description.en: Read the captured settings against the time standard and the configuration standard, and produce the discrepancy summary the control calls for: systems synchronised to a source that is not approved, systems whose offset exceeds the stated tolerance, systems not synchronising at all, and systems whose protocol or configured servers differ from their class's required entry. Group the cloud and hybrid systems into their own section, since their discrepancies are resolved with the provider rather than locally. Give each discrepancy an owner and an agreed correction, and carry the unresolved ones into the conclusion. Attach the analysis with those corrections named.

evidenceHint.en: Time synchronisation analysis listing every system whose source, offset or protocol configuration deviates from the standard, with a separate cloud and hybrid section, and an owner plus agreed correction per discrepancy

text.en: Compare each system's synchronisation source against the approved external sources.
Compare each captured offset against the maximum permitted by the time standard.
Compare each system's protocol and configured servers against its class's required entry.
Group the cloud and hybrid discrepancies separately for resolution with the provider.
Assign an owner and an agreed correction to every discrepancy recorded.

controls.title: Risk Management Process Verification
controls.objective: Ensure that risk management processes are established, effectively managed, and acknowledged by all organizational stakeholders.
controls.successCriteria:
The Risk Management Policy is complete, up-to-date, and aligns with organizational objectives.
All key stakeholders have been appropriately informed about the Risk Management Process.
Evidence of understanding and agreement from all stakeholders is documented and verified.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the Risk Management Policy documentation.
Collect records of communication or training sessions related to the Risk Management Process.
Gather acknowledgements or sign-offs from stakeholders indicating their understanding and agreement with the Risk Management Process.

Analysis:
Review the Risk Management Policy to verify its comprehensiveness and alignment with organizational objectives.
Examine records of communication or training sessions to ensure they cover all aspects of the Risk Management Process.
Cross-check stakeholder acknowledgements against a list of key stakeholders to confirm everyone's understanding and agreement.

Output:
A copy of the reviewed Risk Management Policy.
A compilation of records from communication or training sessions.
A spreadsheet or report confirming stakeholder acknowledgements and agreements.

title.en: Register every key stakeholder in the risk management process with the role each holds

description.en: The acknowledgement check is a cross-reference against a list of key stakeholders, and without that list it degenerates into counting whichever sign-offs happened to arrive. Name each stakeholder — risk owners, the executive accountable for risk, the department heads who assess risks, and the control and assurance functions — with their role in the process and what each is being asked to acknowledge, which is not the same for a risk owner as for a department head. Record who compiled the list and when, since a list assembled after the acknowledgements were collected proves nothing about coverage. Attach the stakeholder list.

evidenceHint.en: Key stakeholder list naming each stakeholder, the role they hold in the risk management process and what they are required to acknowledge, with the date it was compiled and by whom

text.en: Name the executive accountable for risk and every risk owner under them.
Add the department heads who assess risks and the control and assurance functions.
State the role each stakeholder holds in the process, not just their job title.
State what each is being asked to acknowledge, by role rather than uniformly.
Record who compiled the list and when, before any sign-off is collected.

title.en: Issue the Risk Management Policy covering each stage of the process and the objectives it supports

description.en: Publish the policy so it carries the whole process — how risks are identified, assessed, treated, accepted, escalated and reviewed — with the accountable role named at each stage, and map each stage to the organisational objective it protects so the alignment claim can be tested rather than asserted. Record the version and the date it was issued on the document itself. Where a stage of the process is performed in practice but written down nowhere, that is the gap this task closes: the comprehensiveness review reads the document, not the practice, and will report the stage as absent. Attach the issued policy version.

evidenceHint.en: Issued Risk Management Policy version covering identification, assessment, treatment, acceptance, escalation and review with the accountable role at each stage, mapped to the organisational objectives, carrying its version and issue date

title.en: Train the listed stakeholders on the risk management process and record each session

description.en: Run the session for the stakeholders on the list and record it as evidence: the date, the material presented, who attended, and which stages of the process were covered, so the record can be tested against the policy for completeness rather than only for attendance. Where a stakeholder group needs a different depth — risk owners operating the process against department heads accepting its output — run and record their session separately rather than folding everyone into one register. Follow up absentees with a dated catch-up and record that too. Attach the session material with the attendance records.

evidenceHint.en: Communication or training session records for the period: the material presented, the dated attendance record, the process stages each session covered, and the catch-up record for everyone absent

text.en: Set the session content against the policy so every process stage is covered.
Run separate sessions where stakeholder groups need different depth.
Record the date, the material presented and the stages covered for each session.
Take an attendance record naming each stakeholder present.
Arrange a dated catch-up for every absentee and record it alongside the session.

title.en: Collect a dated acknowledgement from each stakeholder on the list

description.en: Ask each named stakeholder to confirm, in a form carrying their identity and the date, that they have read the Risk Management Policy, understand the process and agree to the role it gives them. The acknowledgement has to name the policy version, otherwise a later revision leaves a file of sign-offs attesting to a document nobody now holds. Record refusals and qualified agreements as given rather than chasing them into a yes — a stakeholder who disputes the role assigned to them is information the process needs, and burying it removes the only signal that the allocation is wrong. Attach the acknowledgements collected against the current policy version.

evidenceHint.en: Stakeholder acknowledgements for the current policy version, each carrying the stakeholder's identity, the version acknowledged and the date, with refusals and qualified responses recorded as given

title.en: Verify the acknowledgements against the stakeholder list and chase the gaps

description.en: Cross-check every name on the stakeholder list against the acknowledgements collected and produce the confirmation sheet: a row per stakeholder showing whether an acknowledgement exists, which policy version it names, and its date. Everyone without one gets a named chase and a target date in the same sheet, and anyone who acknowledged a superseded version counts as outstanding rather than complete — that distinction is the entire value of recording the version. Report coverage as a fraction of the list rather than as a count of sign-offs received, since the two only agree when coverage is total. Attach the completed sheet.

evidenceHint.en: Acknowledgement confirmation sheet with a row per listed stakeholder showing acknowledgement present or absent, the policy version named, the date, and a chase owner and target date against every gap

text.en: Take the stakeholder list as the denominator, not the sign-offs received.
Record against each name whether an acknowledgement exists and which version it names.
Mark anyone who acknowledged a superseded policy version as outstanding.
Name a chase owner and a target date against every outstanding stakeholder.
Report coverage as a fraction of the stakeholder list.

controls.title: Secure System Engineering Compliance
controls.objective: Ensure that all information system development activities adhere to established secure system engineering principles.
controls.successCriteria:
All reviewed projects demonstrate adherence to established secure system engineering principles.
Security principles are consistently applied across all layers of system architecture.
Documentation reflects ongoing updates and reviews of security engineering principles, aligning with current security challenges and technologies.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain a list of recent information system development projects.
Collect design documentation for each project, emphasizing security engineering principles.
Retrieve records of security reviews, threat modeling outputs, and security testing results.
Gather documentation on any use of third-party components and their security assessments.
Acquire evidence of regular updates to security engineering principles and their application in projects.

Analysis:
For each project, verify that security engineering principles (such as “security by design”, “defense in depth”, and “zero trust”) were applied during the design phase.
Review security testing and threat modeling documentation to ensure comprehensive identification and mitigation of vulnerabilities.
Assess the integration of secure coding standards and the application of principles like “least privilege” in each project.
Examine the use of third-party components to ensure compliance with security assessment and update requirements.
Evaluate the currency and relevance of security engineering principles against the latest security threats and technological advances.

Output:
A report detailing the application of secure system engineering principles in each reviewed project.
A comparison matrix correlating project documentation with established security engineering guidelines.
Summaries of any discrepancies or areas of non-compliance.

title.en: Compile the register of information system development projects delivered in the period

description.en: The auditor's first request is a list of recent development projects, and this register is the population every later task in this control counts against. Build it from delivery records - release notes, change tickets, project approvals - rather than from a portfolio slide, so that a project delivered outside the formal pipeline still appears. For each project record the delivering team, the systems or components it changed, the date it went live, and where its design documentation is held, because the review task retrieves that documentation row by row. Mark whether the build used third-party components, since that column produces the population for the component assessment task. Attach the dated register with no blank documentation location.

evidenceHint.en: Dated register of information system development projects for the period, each row naming the delivering team, the systems changed, the go-live date and where the design documentation is held

text.en: Build the project list from release records and change tickets rather than the portfolio view.
Record the delivering team and the systems or components each project changed.
Record where the design documentation for each project is held and who can produce it.
Mark each project's use of third-party components so the component task inherits the population.
Date the register and hold it as the population the design review and matrix are run against.

title.en: Write the secure engineering principles into a standard naming the architecture layer each applies to

description.en: Success here is the principles being applied consistently across every layer of the architecture, which a list of slogans cannot deliver. Issue a standard that names each principle the organisation engineers to - security by design, defence in depth, zero trust, least privilege - and, against each, the architecture layers it governs and what applying it looks like at that layer, so a designer can tell whether their design complies. Fold in the secure coding standards developers are expected to follow and the requirements that apply when a third-party component is introduced. State the issue date and version, because a later task tests whether the standard is still current. Attach the issued standard showing the principle-by-layer table filled in.

evidenceHint.en: Issued secure system engineering standard carrying a completed principle-by-layer table, the secure coding standards and the third-party component requirements, with its version and issue date

title.en: Record the design security review, threat model and security test results for each project

description.en: For every project on the register, hold together the three records an auditor asks for: the design security review that shows the principles were applied at the design phase rather than retrofitted, the threat model with the threats it identified, and the security test results with the mitigation each finding received. Where a project has none of these, record an absent-record entry against its row rather than skipping it - the empty rows are the finding this task produces. The mitigation column matters as much as the finding: a threat model that identifies risks and stops there does not evidence the principle it was written for. Attach the reviews, threat models and test records for the period, filed by project.

evidenceHint.en: Design security review record, threat model output and security test result per project, with the mitigation recorded against every identified threat and finding

text.en: Retrieve the design security review for each project and note who performed it and when.
Attach the threat model output and list the threats it identified for that project.
Attach the security test results and record the mitigation applied to each finding.
Record an absent-record entry for any project row missing one of the three artifacts.
File the set by project so the comparison matrix can be built row by row.

title.en: Record the security assessment and update status of every third-party component the projects use

description.en: Work down the projects the register marks as using third-party components and list the components themselves - library, service or platform - with the version in use, the security assessment carried out before adoption, who carried it out, and whether the version now running is the one that assessment covered. A component whose assessed version has since been superseded, or which was adopted with no assessment at all, is flagged with the project that introduced it and an owner to clear it. Engineering lead supplies the dependency lists; Security engineering owns the assessment verdicts. Attach the component list with an assessment and an update position against every row.

evidenceHint.en: Third-party component list per project showing the version in use, the security assessment and its author, the version that assessment covered, and a flag with owner wherever it is absent or out of date

title.en: Score each project's design documentation against the principles standard in a comparison matrix

description.en: Take the register row by row, read the project's design documentation against the standard, and record for each principle whether the documentation shows it applied, applied in part, or absent - that matrix is the artifact the control's output calls for. Judge the design documentation itself rather than the team's account of it, and write the discrepancies up separately as a summary naming the project, the principle it missed and the accountable owner. A project scored non-compliant carries a remediation and a date into the summary; one scored compliant cites the section of its documentation that evidences it. Attach the matrix and the discrepancy summary together.

evidenceHint.en: Comparison matrix correlating each project's design documentation with the secure engineering principles, plus the discrepancy summary carrying an owner and remediation per non-compliance

text.en: Read each project's design documentation against every principle in the standard.
Score each principle applied, partly applied or absent, citing the documentation section.
List each discrepancy with the project, the principle missed and the accountable owner.
Agree a remediation and a date for every discrepancy and carry them into the summary.

title.en: Reassess the principles standard against current threats and technologies and re-issue it

description.en: The standard has to stay in step with the threats and technologies the organisation actually faces, so at each review read it against the threat models produced in the period, the findings the security tests raised, and the platforms and architectures the projects have adopted since it was last issued. Record for each principle whether it still holds, needs restating, or should be joined by a new one - a platform or architecture adopted since the last issue with nothing in the standard covering it is exactly the gap this task exists to find. Where the standard changes, publish the new version with its date and the reason for each change; where it does not, record that it was read and found current. Attach the review record and the re-issued or reconfirmed standard.

evidenceHint.en: Review record showing the standard read against the period's threat models, test findings and newly adopted technologies, with the re-issued or reconfirmed standard version and its date

controls.title: Secure Asset and Software Management
controls.objective: Ensure secure management and control of enterprise assets and software, including the enforcement of secure network protocols and infrastructure-as-code practices.
controls.successCriteria:
All enterprise assets and software configurations are managed through version-controlled infrastructure-as-code.
Secure network protocols (SSH and HTTPS) are exclusively used for accessing administrative interfaces.
No evidence of insecure protocols (Telnet and HTTP) usage unless justified as operationally essential.
Complete alignment of asset and software management practices with documented standards and policies.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the Inventory of Assets document, including network diagrams and configuration files of devices.
Retrieve version control logs for infrastructure-as-code implementations.
Gather network traffic logs to verify the usage of network protocols (SSH, HTTPS, Telnet, HTTP).

Analysis:
Review the Inventory of Assets and version control logs to ensure that all asset configurations are managed through infrastructure-as-code and are under version control.
Analyze network traffic logs to identify the use of secure network protocols (SSH and HTTPS) and flag any usage of insecure protocols (Telnet and HTTP).
Compare current network and device configurations against documented standards to verify compliance.

Output:
Compiled inventory and version control logs.
Network traffic log analysis report.
Compliance report comparing current configurations with standards.

title.en: Record the infrastructure-as-code repository and path holding each asset's configuration

description.en: Extend the Inventory of Assets with a column naming, per asset, the repository and file path its configuration is defined in, so the inventory itself shows what is managed as code and what is not. Assets configured by hand get an explicit not-managed-as-code value with a named owner, rather than a blank that reads as unchecked. Cover network devices and appliances as well as servers: they are the ones most often configured at the console and reconciled never. Attach the extended inventory together with the derived list of assets outside infrastructure-as-code.

evidenceHint.en: Inventory of Assets extract giving the infrastructure-as-code repository and path per asset, plus the derived list of assets not managed as code with a named owner for each

title.en: Record the administrative interface and permitted protocol for every asset

description.en: For each asset, name the interfaces used to administer it — console, web UI, remote shell, device management port — and the protocol each is reached over, with SSH and HTTPS as the permitted pair. Where Telnet or plain HTTP remains in use, record the operational reason it is essential, the asset owner it sits with, and where that justification is written down; an interface with no recorded reason is a finding, not an exception. Attach the interface and protocol table with the justification register beside it.

evidenceHint.en: Administrative interface and protocol table per asset, with a justification register for every retained Telnet or HTTP interface naming the operational reason it is essential and the asset owner it sits with

title.en: Export the version control history for every configuration change in the period

description.en: Pull the commit history for the infrastructure-as-code repositories covering the period under test, showing per change what was altered, who authored it, and when it was applied to the estate. Where a configuration was changed directly on an asset and reconciled into code afterwards, mark that entry: the gap between the two timestamps is what shows whether the code is leading reality or trailing it. Attach the exported history covering every repository the inventory points at.

evidenceHint.en: Version control log export for the period, one entry per configuration change with its author, the date it was applied and the assets affected

title.en: Flag every Telnet or HTTP session to an administrative interface in the network traffic logs

description.en: Read the network traffic logs for the period for administrative access, separate the sessions by protocol, and list every Telnet or plain HTTP session that reached an administrative interface with its source, destination asset and timestamp. Check each one against the justification register: a flagged session on an asset with no accepted justification is the finding this task produces, and a justified one still shows whether the compensating restriction held. Attach the traffic log analysis with the flagged session list.

evidenceHint.en: Network traffic log analysis for the period listing administrative sessions by protocol and, for each Telnet or HTTP session, the source, destination asset, timestamp and whether a justification exists

title.en: Compare each asset's running configuration against the documented standard

description.en: Take the configuration actually running on each asset — read from the device or its live state, not from the repository — and compare it against the documented standard for that asset class and against the code that is supposed to define it. Three outcomes get recorded per asset: it matches, it has drifted from the code, or the standard itself is silent on the setting in question. Every deviation carries the setting, the observed and expected values, an owner and an agreed remediation. Attach the compliance report with the configuration output it was derived from.

evidenceHint.en: Compliance report per asset comparing running configuration against the documented standard and the infrastructure-as-code definition, with observed and expected values for each deviation and a named remediation owner

text.en: Read the running configuration from each asset rather than from its build document.
Compare it against the documented standard for that asset class.
Compare it against the infrastructure-as-code definition the inventory points to.
Record matches, drift from the code, and settings the standard does not cover.
Assign an owner and an agreed remediation to every deviation recorded.

controls.title: Explicit Consent for Sensitive Data
controls.objective: To ensure explicit consent is obtained and documented for the collection of sensitive personal information, in line with the entity's privacy objectives.
controls.successCriteria:
All sensitive personal information is collected with documented explicit consent from data subjects.
Consent procedures are clear, specific to sensitive data, and in line with privacy policies and regulations.
Data subjects are adequately informed about the necessity of consent and consequences of non-consent for sensitive data collection.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Gather a list of systems and processes where sensitive personal information is collected.
Obtain examples of consent forms or mechanisms used for collecting sensitive data.
Review any recent changes to consent procedures or policies.

Analysis:
Evaluate the consent forms/mechanisms to ensure they are explicit, clear, and specific to the collection of sensitive data.
Check that the processes for obtaining consent align with the updated privacy policies and regulatory requirements.
Verify that data subjects are informed of the consequences of not providing consent.

Output:
A comprehensive report on the evaluation of explicit consent procedures for sensitive data.
A compliance checklist for each system and process, assessing the adequacy of consent mechanisms.
Documentation of the review of policy changes and their implementation in consent processes.

title.en: List every collection point at which sensitive personal information is captured

description.en: Build the population the compliance checklist is scored against, one row per collection point rather than per system, because a single system may capture sensitive data on a web form, a phone script and a paper form with different wording on each. For each row record the sensitive categories captured, taking the definition of sensitive personal information from the Privacy Policy rather than assuming one, together with the system the data lands in, who collects it, and the consent mechanism used there today. Include collection points a supplier operates on the organisation's behalf. Attach the list with the sensitive categories and the current consent mechanism named on every row.

evidenceHint.en: List of collection points capturing sensitive personal information, each with the sensitive categories captured, the receiving system, the collector and the consent mechanism in use today

text.en: Enumerate collection points per channel: web forms, portals, phone scripts, paper forms and in-person capture.
Add the collection points a supplier operates on the organisation's behalf.
Record which sensitive categories each point captures, category by category.
Name the system the data lands in and the person or team that collects it.
Record the consent mechanism in use at that point today, or record that there is none.

title.en: Set the consent wording at each collection point to name the sensitive categories and the effect of refusal

description.en: Rewrite the consent text used at every collection point so it does the three things this control requires: it names the specific sensitive categories being collected rather than referring to personal data in general, it states the purpose in terms the individual can act on, and it says plainly what happens if consent is refused — which service becomes unavailable, which step cannot proceed. Make the consent action explicit and separate: a choice that must be actively given rather than assumed, and not bundled with acceptance of terms. Legal/DPO confirms each wording against the Privacy Policy and the applicable regulation. Attach the approved wording per collection point with its version and the date it goes live.

evidenceHint.en: Approved consent wording per collection point, each version naming the sensitive categories, the purpose and the consequence of refusing consent, with its go-live date

title.en: Record where each consent is stored and how it can be produced for a named individual

description.en: Explicit consent is only documented if it can be retrieved for a specific person on request, so record for every collection point where the consent record is written, what it captures — the individual's identity, the timestamp, the form or script version they were shown, the categories consented to and the consent action itself — and the exact steps by which somebody produces it for a named individual. Then run that retrieval once against a real record and note how long it took and what came back. A collection point that cannot produce a per-individual record is the finding here, and it carries an owner and a date. Attach the mapping together with the retrieval test result.

evidenceHint.en: Consent record mapping per collection point giving the storage location, captured fields and retrieval route, with the result of a retrieval test run for a named individual

text.en: Record where the consent record is written for each collection point.
List the fields it captures, including the form or script version shown to the individual.
Write down the steps by which somebody produces that record for a named individual.
Run the retrieval once against a real record and note the time taken and what came back.

title.en: Record the explicit consent captured at each collection of sensitive personal information

description.en: Every collection of sensitive personal information writes its consent record at the moment of collection, carrying the individual, the date and time, the wording version shown, the sensitive categories consented to and the consent action taken. Where consent is refused, record that too together with the effect applied — the collection not made, the step not taken — because a refusal with no recorded effect is indistinguishable from an ignored refusal. Collection points a supplier operates supply their consent records for the same period rather than holding them. Attach the consent records for the period alongside the collection volumes they should account for.

evidenceHint.en: Consent records for the period showing the individual, date and time, wording version and categories consented to, with refusals and the effect applied, set against collection volumes

title.en: Record every change to a consent procedure, form or policy with the review that approved it

description.en: When consent wording, a collection mechanism, a sensitive category or the Privacy Policy text behind them changes, raise a change record stating what changed, which collection points it affects, why the new version still satisfies the policy and the applicable regulation, and whether consents already collected remain valid under it or must be obtained again. The record carries the reviewer, the decision and the date, and is filed against the wording version it produced, so any consent record can be read back to the text actually shown at the time. Attach the change records raised since the last review with the wording versions they produced.

evidenceHint.en: Change records for consent procedure, form and policy changes since the last review, each showing the affected collection points, the reviewer and decision, the resulting wording version and the treatment of existing consents

title.en: Score each collection point's consent mechanism on the compliance checklist

description.en: Work down the list and test each collection point against the criteria this control sets: the consent is explicit and separately given, the sensitive categories are named, the purpose is specific, the consequence of refusal is stated, the mechanism matches the Privacy Policy version in force, and a consent record exists and can be produced. Test the live collection point as an individual meets it — the deployed form, the script actually read — rather than the approved wording, since the gap between the two is exactly what this checklist exists to find. Score pass or fail per criterion with the observed wording quoted on any failure, and assign each gap an owner and a date. Attach the completed checklist with the evaluation report drawn from it.

evidenceHint.en: Completed compliance checklist scoring each collection point against every consent criterion, quoting the observed wording on failures, with an owner and a date for each gap

text.en: Test the live form or script as an individual meets it, not the approved document.
Check the consent is explicit, separately given and not bundled with other terms.
Check the sensitive categories and the purpose are both named specifically.
Check the consequence of refusing consent is stated plainly and specifically.
Confirm a consent record exists for that point and can be produced on request.

controls.title: Secure Equipment Disposal and Reuse Control
controls.objective: Ensure all equipment containing storage media is properly sanitized of sensitive data and licensed software before disposal or reuse.
controls.successCriteria:
All equipment slated for disposal or reuse has undergone appropriate data sanitization.
Physical destruction of storage media is conducted where necessary, with adequate documentation.
All organizational labels and markings are removed from the equipment.
Compliance with secure disposal and reuse policy is fully documented and verifiable.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain a list of all equipment scheduled for disposal or reuse.
Secure documented evidence of data sanitization processes (e.g., certificates of data destruction, software sanitization logs).
Gather records of physical destruction of storage media, if applicable.
Collect documentation detailing the removal of labels and markings identifying the organization.

Analysis:
Verify each equipment against the disposal/reuse list to ensure no item is overlooked.
Examine data sanitization records to confirm that all sensitive data and licensed software have been securely overwritten or destroyed.
Review physical destruction records for storage media containing confidential or copyrighted information.
Ensure all labels and markings have been removed from the equipment as per policy.

Output:
A comprehensive report detailing each equipment's sanitization and label removal process.
A checklist verifying the completion of data destruction or overwriting for each item.
Photographic evidence or certificates of destruction, if applicable.

title.en: Register every item scheduled for disposal or reuse with the media and data it holds

description.en: Nothing can be shown to have been sanitised unless it was first known to be in scope, so open a row the moment an item is scheduled: the asset identifier, whether it is going to disposal or to reuse, the storage media it contains including secondary and embedded media, whether it holds confidential information, and whether it carries licensed or copyrighted software. Include items already pulled from service and waiting for collection, because equipment sitting in a holding area is the population most often overlooked. The reconciliation counts against this register, so an item absent from it cannot be evidenced as sanitised at all. Attach the register.

evidenceHint.en: Disposal and reuse register listing each item with its asset identifier, destination, the storage media it contains, whether it holds confidential information, and whether licensed or copyrighted software is present

title.en: Set the sanitisation method required for each media type and the content it holds

description.en: Record which treatment applies to what, so an operator is not deciding it at the bench: for each combination of media type and content the register records, the required method — secure overwriting to a stated standard, or physical destruction — and the point at which destruction is required rather than optional, which for media holding confidential or copyrighted content is what the control turns on. Cover the removal or de-registration of licensed software separately, naming what has to be reclaimed before an item leaves. State what record each method must produce, because that is what makes the later reconciliation possible at all. Attach the issued method matrix.

evidenceHint.en: Sanitisation method matrix giving the required treatment per media type and the content it holds, the point at which physical destruction is required, the licensed-software reclaim step, and the record each method must produce

title.en: Sanitise each item and file the sanitisation log against its register row

description.en: For every item whose method matrix entry is secure overwriting, carry out the sanitisation and record it: the asset identifier, the media serial, the method and tool used with its version, the operator, the date, and the tool's completion or verification result. File the log against the register row so the two read together, and record in the same entry the licensed software reclaimed or de-registered from the item. An item whose tool reported an incomplete pass is not sanitised — record it as such against its register row and leave that row open rather than closing it. Attach the sanitisation logs for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Software sanitisation logs for the period, one per item, giving the asset and media identifiers, the method and tool version, the operator, the date, the verification result and the licensed software reclaimed

title.en: Destroy the media holding confidential or copyrighted content and file the destruction certificate

description.en: Where the method matrix requires physical destruction, destroy the media and keep the record an auditor asks for: the asset and media serial numbers, the destruction method, the date, the operator or the contracted destruction firm, and the certificate of destruction that firm issues. Photograph the destroyed media wherever the certificate does not itself identify the serials, because a certificate naming a quantity rather than a serial cannot be tied back to a register row. Reconcile the serials on the certificate against the serials that left the building on the same collection, and treat any difference as a finding. Attach the certificates with the photographic evidence.

evidenceHint.en: Certificates of destruction and photographic evidence for the period, identifying each destroyed medium by serial, with the destruction method, date and the operator or contracted firm that performed it

title.en: Remove the organisational labels and markings before each item leaves the premises

description.en: Asset tags, inventory labels, service stickers, hostname and network markings and any branding identify the organisation and what the equipment was used for long after the data has gone. Before an item is released for disposal or reuse, strip them and record it: the asset identifier, the labels removed, the person who checked, the date, and a photograph of the item after removal where the record does not otherwise show it. Cover the markings inside the chassis and on the power supply as well as the ones on the outside. An item released with a label still attached is recorded as an exception with the reason rather than quietly corrected. Attach the label removal record.

evidenceHint.en: Label and marking removal record, one row per released item, naming the labels removed, the checker and the date, with a post-removal photograph where one is taken and any exception recorded against the item

title.en: Reconcile the register against the sanitisation, destruction and label removal records

description.en: Take the disposal and reuse register row by row and confirm each item holds the records its method matrix entry requires — a sanitisation log, a destruction certificate, a label removal record — then produce the item-level report the control calls for. The output is a checklist carrying, per item, what was required, what was found, and a complete or incomplete verdict; every incomplete row names the missing record, the accountable owner and the date the item was released. An item released without its record is the finding this task exists to produce, so it is reported rather than closed quietly. Attach the reconciliation with the register and record extracts behind it.

evidenceHint.en: Disposal reconciliation checklist covering every registered item with the records required, the records found, a complete or incomplete verdict, and the owner plus release date for each incomplete item

text.en: Read each register row's method matrix entry to determine which records it requires.
Search the sanitisation logs, destruction certificates and label records for that asset identifier.
Mark the row complete or incomplete and name the specific record that is missing.
Record the release date and the accountable owner for every incomplete row.
Carry the incomplete rows into the report's conclusion as findings rather than closing them.

controls.title: Network Segregation Compliance
controls.objective: Ensure that network domains within the organization are segregated based on trust levels, sensitivity, and criticality, with controlled inter-domain communication.
controls.successCriteria:
Network domains are segregated as per the organizational standards of trust, sensitivity, and criticality.
Gateways are correctly configured to control access between network domains.
Wireless networks for guests are segregated from internal networks with appropriate security measures.
All inter-domain communications comply with the established access control policies and procedures.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the network architecture diagrams detailing the segregation of network domains.
Acquire configuration details of gateways (e.g., firewalls, routers) used for controlling access between domains.
Gather wireless network settings, focusing on segregation measures for guest and internal networks.
Collect logs or records of access control changes and inter-domain communications for a specified period.

Analysis:
Review the network architecture diagrams to verify the segregation of network domains aligns with the organizational standards for trust, sensitivity, and criticality.
Analyze the configuration of gateways to ensure they are set up correctly to control access between network domains as per the policy.
Examine wireless network settings to confirm the effective segregation of guest and internal networks, especially in terms of security restrictions.
Evaluate the logs or records to check compliance with access control policies and procedures, especially for inter-domain communications.

Output:
Network architecture diagrams with annotations on domain segregations.
Configurations report of gateways showing access control settings.
Analysis report of wireless network settings, focusing on segregation and security measures.
Compliance report detailing the review of access control logs and communication records.

title.en: Register each network domain with its trust level, sensitivity and criticality rating

description.en: List the network domains in use — production, corporate, management, guest wireless, third-party, laboratory — and rate each on the three dimensions the standard uses: the trust placed in the devices it holds, the sensitivity of the data it carries and the criticality of the services running on it. Name the owner of each domain and the address ranges it occupies, so that a gateway rule can later be tied back to a domain rather than to an address nobody recognises. Attach the domain register with its ratings complete; a domain with a blank rating cannot be reviewed.

evidenceHint.en: Network domain register giving, per domain, its address ranges, owner and its trust, sensitivity and criticality ratings

title.en: Annotate the network architecture diagrams with each domain boundary and the gateway enforcing it

description.en: Update the architecture diagrams so every domain from the register appears as a bounded region, with the firewall, router or other gateway that controls entry to it named on the boundary itself. A diagram showing connectivity but not where the control sits cannot be read against the segregation standard, which is the whole purpose it serves here. Mark any connection that crosses a boundary without passing a named gateway — those are the ones the review asks about first. Attach the annotated diagrams carrying their revision date.

evidenceHint.en: Annotated network architecture diagrams showing each registered domain as a bounded region with the gateway controlling it named on the boundary, dated at the revision

title.en: Record the permitted traffic between each pair of domains and the rule that enforces it

description.en: For every domain pair allowed to communicate, write down what may pass — source, destination, service and direction — the business reason for it, and the identifier of the gateway rule implementing it, so a rule on a firewall traces to a recorded flow and a recorded flow traces to a live rule. Domain pairs with no permitted communication are recorded explicitly as denied; the deny is as much a decision as the allow, and an unrecorded pair is the one nobody notices opening. Attach the permitted-flow list with the gateway configuration report showing the corresponding access control settings.

evidenceHint.en: Permitted inter-domain flow list keyed to the gateway rule identifier implementing each flow, with the gateway configuration report showing those access control settings

text.en: List every domain pair from the register and mark it permitted or denied.
For each permitted pair record the source, destination, service and direction.
Record the business reason each permitted flow exists and the service it supports.
Name the gateway rule identifier that implements each permitted flow.
Export the gateway configurations showing the rules the list points at.

title.en: Record the guest wireless segregation settings and the restrictions applied to guest traffic

description.en: Capture, for each guest wireless network, the SSID, the VLAN or tunnel it lands in, the authentication it requires, whether client-to-client traffic is blocked, and precisely what a guest device is permitted to reach — which should include no internal domain from the register. Take the settings from the controller configuration rather than the design document, and note any guest network sharing infrastructure with an internal one together with what keeps the two apart. Attach the wireless settings report covering every guest SSID in service.

evidenceHint.en: Guest wireless settings report per SSID giving the VLAN or tunnel, authentication method, client isolation setting and permitted egress, exported from the controller configuration

title.en: Log every access control change made on a domain gateway

description.en: Each time a rule on a gateway between domains is added, changed or removed, record the gateway, the rule, what changed, who requested it, who applied it and the date, exporting the record from the change management or gateway management system rather than reconstructing it afterwards. A rule added for a limited purpose and never removed is the failure this log exists to expose, so an entry says plainly when the rule was meant to be temporary. Attach the gateway access control change record for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Gateway access control change record for the period showing gateway, rule, change made, requester, who applied it, the date and whether the rule was recorded as temporary

title.en: Test the inter-domain communication records against the permitted-flow list

description.en: Take the logged communications crossing domain boundaries for the period and match each observed flow to an entry in the permitted-flow list. Flows with no matching entry and permitted entries with no observed traffic are both reported: the first is traffic nobody recorded, the second is a rule that can probably be retired. Read the gateway change record in the same pass so every live rule traces back to a recorded change, and name the rules that do not. Attach the compliance report naming each unmatched flow, the domains it crossed and the remediation agreed with the domain owner.

evidenceHint.en: Inter-domain communication compliance report matching observed flows to permitted entries, listing every unmatched flow with the domains it crossed, the unused permitted entries and a remediation owner per finding

controls.title: Risk Mitigation Control Activities
controls.objective: To ensure that control activities effectively mitigate risks to the achievement of organizational objectives at acceptable levels.
controls.successCriteria:
Control activities are appropriately designed and implemented to mitigate identified risks.
There is a balanced mix of manual and automated, preventive and detective controls.
Control activities are effectively integrated with risk assessments.
Compliance with segregation of duties or effective implementation of alternative controls where segregation is not feasible.
Control activities are appropriately applied at various levels within the entity.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain a comprehensive list of current control activities implemented across various departments.
Collect documentation or records of risk assessments linked with these control activities.
Acquire reports or logs that demonstrate the functioning of these control activities (e.g., logs of preventive controls, incident response reports for detective controls).

Analysis:
Review the list of control activities to ensure they align with identified risks and are appropriate for the entity's specific factors (environment, complexity, nature, and scope of operations).
Assess the balance and mix of control activity types (manual/automated, preventive/detective) to evaluate their effectiveness in mitigating risks.
Examine evidence of control activities at various levels within the entity to check for thorough implementation and effectiveness.
Verify compliance with segregation of duties or effectiveness of alternative controls where segregation is not practical.

Output:
A comprehensive report detailing the assessment of each control activity.
A matrix or spreadsheet correlating risk assessments with control activities.
Documentation of any gaps or deficiencies in the control activities.

title.en: Inventory every control activity in force across the entity's departments

description.en: Build one row per control activity actually operating, gathered from each department rather than from a central register that may only describe intent: what the activity is, the department and the level within the entity it operates at, whether it is manual or automated, whether it is preventive or detective, how often it runs, and who performs it. Activities that exist in a procedure document but that nobody performs are recorded as such rather than omitted — a control described but not run is the finding, and dropping it from the inventory is what hides it. Attach the inventory with the date compiled; it is the population that the risk matrix, the operating evidence and the design assessment are all run against.

evidenceHint.en: Dated control activity inventory with one row per activity giving department, entity level, manual or automated, preventive or detective, frequency and named performer, including activities documented but not performed

text.en: Ask each department for the control activities its people actually perform.
Record the level within the entity that each activity operates at.
Mark each activity manual or automated, and preventive or detective.
Record how often each runs and who performs it by name or role.
Include documented but unperformed activities, marked as such rather than dropped.

title.en: Map each identified risk to the control activities that mitigate it

description.en: Take the risk assessment records and the control inventory and build the correlation matrix: each identified risk against the control activities that address it, and in each cell what the control does about that risk — prevents it, detects it, or reduces its impact. Two cells matter more than all the others: a risk with no control against it, and a control mapped to no risk. List both explicitly beneath the matrix rather than leaving a reader to infer them from an empty row, because those two lists are what somebody acts on. Record the risk assessment version the mapping was built from so the matrix can be refreshed when the assessment moves. Attach the matrix with both exception lists.

evidenceHint.en: Risk-to-control matrix built from a named risk assessment version, showing what each control does about each risk, with the uncovered risks and the controls mapped to no risk listed explicitly

text.en: Take the identified risks from the current risk assessment as the matrix rows.
Take the control activity inventory as the matrix columns.
Record in each cell whether the control prevents, detects or reduces that risk.
List every risk with no control against it beneath the matrix.
List every control activity mapped to no risk in the assessment.

title.en: Record where segregation of duties applies and the alternative control used where it is not practicable

description.en: For each process in the inventory that carries a segregation requirement — initiation against approval, custody against recording, development against deployment — record who performs each part and whether the separation actually holds under the current assignment rather than under the org chart. Where headcount or structure makes separation impracticable, name the alternative control put in place instead (independent review, transaction reporting to a second person, system-enforced limits), who performs it, and why it is considered to give equivalent assurance. A process that fails separation and names no alternative is an exception with an owner and a date, not a blank row. Attach the segregation analysis.

evidenceHint.en: Segregation of duties analysis per process showing who performs each separated part, whether separation holds under current assignments, and where it does not, the named alternative control, its performer and the equivalence rationale

title.en: Collect the operating logs and incident reports that show each control activity ran

description.en: For the period under test, gather the output each control activity produces — system logs and approval records for the preventive ones, exception reports, alerts and incident response records for the detective ones — and file each against the inventory row it evidences. A control activity whose row has no attached output for the period is reported as unevidenced rather than as failed: the two need different responses, since the first may be a recording gap and the second is a control that did not operate. IT Operations supplies the system-generated logs; the departments supply the manual records. Attach the collected evidence indexed against the inventory.

evidenceHint.en: Operating evidence for the period indexed against the control inventory — preventive control logs and approval records, detective control exception reports and incident responses — with the unevidenced inventory rows listed

title.en: Assess each control activity's design against the risk it mitigates and the entity's operating context

description.en: Work down the inventory and judge, for each activity, whether it would actually mitigate the risk the matrix assigns it given the entity's environment, complexity, and the nature and scope of its operations — a monthly reconciliation is a different proposition in a business processing ten transactions a day than in one processing ten thousand. Record a design verdict per activity with the reasoning, and against every deficiency name the owner and the correction agreed. Keep design failures separate from the operating failures the evidence collection found, because a well-designed control that did not run and a control that ran exactly as designed but could never have worked call for opposite fixes. Attach the assessment report with its deficiency list.

evidenceHint.en: Control activity assessment report giving a design verdict and its reasoning per activity, with design deficiencies listed separately from operating failures and an owner and agreed correction against each

text.en: Read each activity against the risk the matrix assigns it and judge whether it could work.
