Weigh the entity's transaction volume, complexity and operating scope in that judgement.
Record a design verdict and the reasoning behind it for every activity.
Keep design deficiencies apart from controls that simply did not operate.
Name an owner and an agreed correction against every deficiency recorded.

title.en: Evaluate the mix of manual, automated, preventive and detective controls across the entity's levels

description.en: Summarise the inventory by its four attributes and read the result against the risks each group covers: which risks are addressed only by detective controls and so only after the event, which depend on a single manual activity performed by one person, and which levels of the entity carry no control activity at all. The point is not a target ratio, which the control does not specify, but the concentrations the summary exposes. Record each concentration with the risks it leaves exposed and the action agreed. Attach the analysis with the underlying summary it was drawn from.

evidenceHint.en: Control mix analysis summarising the inventory by manual or automated, preventive or detective and entity level, naming the risks covered only by detective or single-person manual controls, the levels carrying no control, and the action agreed for each

controls.title: Secure Disposal of Personal Information
controls.objective: To ensure the entity securely disposes of personal information in a manner that aligns with its privacy objectives and complies with applicable regulations.
controls.successCriteria:
All personal information disposal activities are conducted securely and in compliance with documented policies and procedures.
Disposal practices align with the entity’s privacy objectives and applicable regulatory requirements.
Changes in disposal practices have been properly documented and comply with established privacy objectives.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Compile a list of systems and processes used for the disposal of personal information.
Obtain documentation of the data disposal policies and procedures.
Gather records of data disposal activities and any related change requests since the last audit.

Analysis:
Review disposal policies and procedures to verify compliance with privacy objectives and regulatory requirements.
Examine records of disposal activities to ensure adherence to documented policies and procedures.
Assess change requests related to data disposal for compliance with established processes and privacy objectives.

Output:
A detailed report on the entity’s practices for the secure disposal of personal information.
A compliance spreadsheet assessing the adherence of disposal activities to policies and procedures.
Documentation of review and approval of change requests related to data disposal.

title.en: Compile the list of systems and processes used to dispose of personal information

description.en: List every place personal information ends its life: application and database deletion routines, backup and archive expiry, removable media, end-user devices, paper files, and disposals a supplier or processor performs on the entity's behalf. Work from the systems that hold personal information rather than from the disposal tools already in use, so a system with data and no disposal route shows up as a gap instead of an absence. For each row capture the trigger that starts the disposal (retention rule, deletion request, asset decommissioning) and the named owner. Legal/DPO owns the list; IT Operations supplies the system and asset detail. Attach the completed list with an owner named on every row — it is the population every later task in this control is measured against.

evidenceHint.en: List of systems, media and processes used to dispose of personal information, each with its disposal trigger and named owner

text.en: Include live databases, backups, archives and any replica or reporting copy.
Add the paper, removable-media and end-user-device routes, not only applications and databases.
Add disposals carried out by suppliers or processors on the entity's behalf.
Record the trigger that starts each disposal: retention rule, deletion request or decommissioning.
Name the accountable owner on every row and confirm it with that person.

title.en: Record the approved destruction method and standard for each medium on the list

description.en: For every row of the disposal list, write into the disposal procedure the method that renders the personal information unrecoverable and the standard or setting that method must meet — cross-cut shredding for paper, cryptographic erase or degauss for magnetic media, overwrite or physical destruction for solid-state media, hard delete plus backup-copy expiry for database records. Where a supplier performs the destruction, name the supplier and the agreement under which they do it. Security engineering sets the technical settings; Legal/DPO confirms each method satisfies the Privacy Policy and the regulatory obligations for that data category. Attach the updated procedure showing a method and standard against every row, with none left blank.

evidenceHint.en: Disposal procedure section mapping an approved destruction method and standard to every medium on the list

title.en: Define the disposal record that must be completed at the moment of destruction

description.en: Destruction leaves nothing behind to inspect, so the record made while it happens is the only evidence that survives it. Publish the disposal record template and fix the fields every entry must carry: date and time; the requester and the owner who authorised it; the data categories with record counts or asset identifiers (serial number, asset tag, tape label, table name and row count); the method used, taken from the approved list; the operator who performed it; the witness where the procedure requires one; and the supplier certificate reference where a third party destroyed it. IT Operations and the disposal owners are the people who will complete it. Attach the published template together with the procedure text that makes a completed record a precondition of releasing the medium or running the deletion.

evidenceHint.en: Published disposal record template and the procedure clause requiring it to be completed before destruction

text.en: List the identifiers that outlive each medium: serial number, asset tag, tape label, table and row count.
Add the authorisation fields: requester, approving owner, and the retention rule or request that triggered it.
Add the execution fields: method used, operator, witness, date and time, supplier certificate reference.
Amend the procedure so the record must be complete before the medium is released or the deletion runs.
Circulate the template to every disposal owner on the list and record their acknowledgement.

title.en: Log every disposal of personal information in the disposal register as it is carried out

description.en: Each time personal information is destroyed under this procedure, the operator completes the disposal record and files it in the register as part of closing the disposal, attaching the supplier's certificate of destruction where a third party carried it out. IT Operations reconciles the register against the decommissioning and deletion tickets raised in the same period, so that nothing is destroyed without a surviving record, and chases any ticket closed with no matching entry. Attach the register extract for the period showing every disposal with its identifiers, method, operator and authorisation populated.

evidenceHint.en: Disposal register extract for the period, with completed disposal records and any supplier certificates of destruction attached

title.en: Record the review and approval of every change to disposal practices

description.en: When a disposal method, tool, supplier or retention trigger changes, raise it as a change request stating what is changing, which rows of the disposal list and which data categories it affects, and why the new practice still meets the Privacy Policy and the regulatory obligations for that data. The request carries the reviewer's decision and the date it was taken, and the approved request is filed with the disposal procedure version it produced. Legal/DPO is accountable for the decision; Security engineering and IT Operations describe the technical change. Attach the change requests raised since the last audit, each showing its reviewer, decision date and resulting procedure version.

evidenceHint.en: Change requests for disposal practice changes raised since the last audit, each showing the reviewer, the decision and the procedure version it produced

title.en: Score a sample of disposal records against the documented procedure in a compliance spreadsheet

description.en: Draw a sample from the disposal register covering every medium on the disposal list and test each record against the procedure: the method used was the approved one for that medium, the identifiers are specific enough to say which assets or records were destroyed, the authorisation predates the destruction, and any supplier certificate matches the batch identifiers it claims to cover. Score pass or fail per record in the compliance spreadsheet with the exception described in full, and give every failure a named owner and a date to clear it. Attach the completed spreadsheet with the exceptions and their owners.

evidenceHint.en: Compliance spreadsheet scoring each sampled disposal record against the procedure, with every exception described and assigned

text.en: Draw the sample so that every medium on the disposal list is covered at least once.
Check the method recorded against the approved method and standard for that medium.
Confirm the authorisation was recorded before the destruction date and time.
Match each supplier certificate to the batch identifiers it claims to cover.
Name the procedure clause breached beside every record scored as a fail.

controls.title: Cybersecurity Risk Assessment Implementation
controls.objective: To ensure that cybersecurity risk assessments are conducted effectively and in alignment with organizational policies during critical phases of technology projects and services.
controls.successCriteria:
Cybersecurity risk assessments are conducted in accordance with the specified stages and scenarios.
The cybersecurity risk management methodology and procedures are reviewed and updated at planned intervals or upon changes in relevant laws and regulations.
All changes and reviews are approved and properly documented.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the Risk Assessment documentation for recent technology projects, infrastructure changes, third-party service planning, and new technology service/product launches.
Gather records of the Risk Management Committee's meeting minutes and decisions.
Retrieve documented approvals for changes and reviews of the cybersecurity risk management methodology and procedures.

Analysis:
Review the Risk Assessment documentation to verify that assessments were conducted during the early stages of technology projects, before major changes to technology infrastructure, during third-party service planning, and before launching new technology services/products.
Examine the Risk Management Committee's meeting minutes to ensure that risk management procedures are reviewed periodically and align with changes in laws and regulations.
Confirm that all changes and reviews of the risk management methodology and procedures are properly approved and documented.

Output:
A report detailing the findings of the Risk Assessment documentation review.
A summary of compliance with periodic review requirements based on Risk Management Committee records.
An audit trail of approvals and documentation for changes and reviews.

title.en: Define the trigger points at which a cybersecurity risk assessment must be performed

description.en: Write into the cybersecurity risk management methodology the four points this control requires an assessment at — the early stage of a technology project, before a major change to technology infrastructure, during the planning of a third-party service, and before a new technology service or product is launched — and for each, what counts as reaching that point, who is obliged to raise the assessment, and the point by which it has to be complete. The threshold matters more than the list: 'a major change to infrastructure' has to be defined in terms somebody can apply to a specific change request, or the trigger is missed exactly where it matters most. Attach the issued methodology showing the four trigger definitions.

evidenceHint.en: Issued cybersecurity risk management methodology carrying the four assessment trigger points, the threshold that defines each, who is obliged to raise the assessment, and the point by which it has to be complete

text.en: Define what counts as the early stage of a technology project for this organisation.
Define the threshold that makes an infrastructure change major enough to trigger one.
Define the point in third-party service planning at which the assessment is due.
Define how far before a technology service or product launch the assessment must complete.
Name who raises the assessment at each trigger and by when it must be complete.

title.en: Schedule the periodic review of the risk management methodology and its legal change trigger

description.en: Set the planned interval at which the cybersecurity risk management methodology and its procedures are reviewed, name the body that performs the review — the Risk Management Committee, where that is who holds it — and record the off-cycle trigger separately: a change in the laws or regulations the methodology answers to forces a review regardless of when the last one fell. Name who watches for those changes and how they raise one, because an interval nobody owns and a trigger nobody monitors both fail silently and look identical from outside. Attach the approved review schedule with the next review date recorded on it.

evidenceHint.en: Approved review schedule for the cybersecurity risk management methodology giving the planned interval, the reviewing body, the next review date, the legal and regulatory change trigger, and the person who monitors for such changes

title.en: Document the cybersecurity risk assessment run at each trigger point reached

description.en: When a technology project starts, an infrastructure change is proposed, a third-party service is planned or a new technology service or product approaches launch, run the assessment before the point of no return and file the documentation: what was assessed, the scenarios considered, and the risks identified with their treatment. File each assessment against the project, change, engagement or launch it belongs to, so the completeness test can match them later without reconstructing which was which. Attach the assessment documentation produced during the period.

evidenceHint.en: Cybersecurity risk assessment documentation for the period, one per triggering project, infrastructure change, third-party engagement or product launch, each filed against the item it assessed and naming what was assessed, the scenarios considered and the risks identified

title.en: Record the Risk Management Committee's methodology decisions and the approvals behind them

description.en: Minute each occasion the committee reviews the methodology or approves a change to it: the date, who attended, what was reviewed, the change agreed, the legal or regulatory driver where one applied, and the approval itself with the approver named. Keep the approval as its own record rather than relying on the minute to imply it — the audit trail this control asks for is the approvals, and a minute recording a discussion without an approval leaves the change unauthorised on paper however settled it felt in the room. Attach the minutes and the matching approval records for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Risk Management Committee minutes and the matching approval records for the period, each naming the review or change made, its driver, the named approver and the date

title.en: Test that every qualifying project, change, engagement and launch carried an assessment before it proceeded

description.en: Build the period's population from outside the assessment file — the record of projects started, infrastructure changes made, third-party engagements planned and products launched in the period — then read each item against the trigger definitions and look for its assessment. Record per item whether an assessment exists and, where it does, whether its date falls before the point the trigger required, because a late assessment and a missing one are different failures with different corrections. Engineering lead supplies the project and change populations and Procurement the third-party engagements. Attach the review report with the population it was drawn from and the exceptions named.

evidenceHint.en: Risk assessment documentation review report listing every qualifying project, infrastructure change, third-party engagement and launch in the period, whether an assessment exists, whether it predates the trigger point, and the exceptions named

text.en: List the projects, changes, third-party engagements and launches of the period.
Read each item against the trigger definitions to decide whether it qualified.
Look for the filed assessment belonging to each qualifying item.
Compare the assessment date against the point the trigger required it by.
List missing assessments and late assessments as separate exception classes.

title.en: Confirm the methodology was reviewed at the planned interval and after each relevant legal change

description.en: Read the committee records for the period against the review schedule: did each planned review happen and happen on time, and did every change in the applicable laws and regulations produce an off-cycle review within the time the schedule allows. Record a compliance position per obligation citing the minute or approval that evidences it, and where a review was missed, note how long the methodology ran unreviewed and what changed in that window — that duration is the exposure, and it disappears if the finding is recorded only as a missed date. Attach the compliance summary with its citations to the committee records.

evidenceHint.en: Periodic review compliance summary citing, per planned review and per legal or regulatory change trigger, the committee minute or approval that evidences it, with any missed review and the period the methodology ran unreviewed

controls.title: Off-Premises Asset Security Control
controls.objective: To ensure that all devices used outside the organization’s premises, including BYOD, are protected against unauthorized access, misuse, and environmental hazards, and that their usage is authorized and monitored.
controls.successCriteria:
All off-premises devices are authorized and accounted for in the IT Asset Management System.
Complete and accurate chain of custody records for all off-premises devices.
All devices have functional location tracking and remote wipe capabilities.
Full adherence to physical and environmental protection guidelines.
Accurate and comprehensive logs of all equipment and media taken off-premises.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain a list of all devices authorized for off-premises use (from the IT Asset Management System).
Gather device usage logs and chain of custody records for these devices.
Collect evidence of remote wipe capability and location tracking for each device.
Obtain documentation of physical and environmental protection measures followed (manufacturer’s guidelines, security measures in public places, etc.).
Access records of equipment and media removed from the organization’s premises.

Analysis:
Verify each device against the IT Asset Management System for authorization.
For each device, ensure the chain of custody is properly documented and matches the log.
Check that location tracking and remote wipe capabilities are functional and up to date.
Review adherence to physical and environmental protection guidelines for each device.
Cross-verify removal records to ensure all equipment taken off-premises is authorized and logged.

Output:
A report detailing the authorization status of each off-premises device.
Documentation verifying the chain of custody for each device.
Evidence of functional location tracking and remote wipe capabilities.
Compliance report for physical and environmental protection measures.
An audit trail of all equipment and media removed from premises.

title.en: Record every device authorised for off-premises use, including BYOD, in the asset system

description.en: The whole control counts against a list of devices authorised to leave, so it has to be one list and it has to include the personally owned devices, which is where these registers usually stop short. For each device record the asset tag or identifier, whether it is corporate or BYOD, the person it is issued to, the authorisation that permitted off-premises use and who granted it. A device in use off the premises with no authorisation on file is the finding: record it as unauthorised rather than back-filling one. Attach the export from the IT Asset Management System.

evidenceHint.en: IT Asset Management System export of devices authorised for off-premises use giving identifier, corporate or BYOD ownership, holder and the authorising approver

title.en: Enrol each off-premises device in location tracking and remote wipe and record its enrolment state

description.en: Against every device on the authorised list record whether location tracking and remote wipe are enrolled, the management platform holding the enrolment, the date the device last checked in, because an unenrolled or long-silent device is one that cannot be wiped on the day it is lost. For a BYOD device record whether the wipe reaches the whole device or only the corporate container, since that difference decides what actually happens on the day. Devices that cannot be enrolled are listed with the reason and the compensating control accepted. Attach the enrolment report from the management platform.

evidenceHint.en: Management platform enrolment report per authorised device showing location tracking and remote wipe state, last check-in date, the BYOD wipe scope, and the non-enrollable list with reasons

title.en: Set out the physical and environmental handling rules for a device off the premises

description.en: Write the rules a holder is expected to follow away from the office and can be held to: not leaving a device unattended in a public place or visible in a vehicle, screen privacy in transit, the manufacturer's guidance on temperature, moisture and power that applies to the hardware issued, storage while travelling, and the route by which a loss is reported, so that the remote wipe and location tracking can actually be used. Issue it to every holder on the authorised list and record who received it and when. Attach the issued guidance with the distribution record.

evidenceHint.en: Issued off-premises handling guidance covering public-place and in-transit security, the manufacturer's environmental limits and the loss reporting route, with the per-holder distribution record

title.en: Log every item of equipment and media taken off the premises with its holder and return date

description.en: Each removal of equipment or media from the premises is written to one log at the time it happens: what left, who took it, who authorised it, the date out, the expected return and the actual return. That log is the chain of custody the assessment reconciles, and its usefulness depends on the return column being closed rather than left open, so chase the returns and record them. Items on long-term issue are recorded once with the issue date and reviewed rather than logged daily. Attach the removal log for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Off-premises removal log for the period giving item, holder, authoriser, date out, expected return and actual return, plus the list of items still out beyond their expected return

title.en: Test location tracking and remote wipe on a sample of devices and record the result

description.en: An enrolment record says a capability is configured, not that it works, and the assessment asks whether both are functional and up to date. Take a sample across device types and both ownership models, request a location from each, and on a device that can be safely reset execute a wipe and confirm from the platform that it completed. Record the device, the test performed, the response time and the outcome, and raise a fault against every device that did not respond. Attach the test record with the platform output for each test.

evidenceHint.en: Location tracking and remote wipe test record stating the sample basis, and per device the test performed, the platform response and the outcome, with a fault raised for each non-responding device

title.en: Match the removal log against the authorised device list and report each unauthorised removal

description.en: Read the period's removal log row by row against the authorised device list and produce the authorisation status report the control asks for: items taken off the premises that are not on the list, devices on the list with no authorisation record behind them, items whose recorded holder no longer matches the chain of custody, and items still out past their expected return. Each exception carries an owner and the recovery or authorisation action agreed. Attach the report with the audit trail of removals it was built from.

evidenceHint.en: Off-premises authorisation status report giving each device its authorisation state and custody position, with the unauthorised removals, the unreturned items and the custody mismatches listed and owned

controls.title: Threat Intelligence Management
controls.objective: To ensure comprehensive collection, analysis, and utilization of threat intelligence across strategic, tactical, and operational layers, making it relevant, insightful, contextual, and actionable for the organization.
controls.successCriteria:
Threat intelligence sources and methods comprehensively cover strategic, tactical, and operational aspects.
Threat intelligence reports are relevant, insightful, contextual, and actionable.
Effective integration of threat intelligence into the organization's risk management and security processes.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Collect documentation on the threat intelligence sources and methods used (internal and external).
Obtain records of threat intelligence reports and analyses conducted over a specified period.
Gather documentation on how threat intelligence is integrated into the organization's risk management and security processes.

Analysis:
Review the threat intelligence sources and methods for coverage of strategic, tactical, and operational intelligence.
Evaluate the threat intelligence reports for relevance, insightfulness, contextuality, and actionability.
Assess how threat intelligence is incorporated into risk management processes, security testing procedures, and the response to identified threats.

Output:
A report summarizing the evaluation of threat intelligence sources and methods.
A spreadsheet or document assessing the quality of threat intelligence reports.
An assessment report on the integration of threat intelligence into risk management and security processes.

title.en: Register every internal and external threat intelligence source with the layer it feeds

description.en: List the sources intelligence actually arrives from — vendor feeds, sector or government sharing groups, open sources, and the internal ones such as incident records, log analysis and vulnerability findings — marking each strategic, tactical or operational, with the owner who receives it and how often it arrives. Sources that are subscribed but unread are recorded as such: the register is meant to show what informs decisions, not what has been paid for. Attach the source register with every row's layer and owner populated.

evidenceHint.en: Threat intelligence source register naming each internal and external source, whether it is strategic, tactical or operational, its owner and its collection frequency

text.en: List the external feeds, sharing groups and open sources currently subscribed.
Add internal sources such as incident records, log analysis and vulnerability findings.
Mark each source strategic, tactical or operational by what it informs.
Record the owner who receives each source and how often it arrives.
Flag sources that arrive but are read by nobody, rather than omitting them.

title.en: Map where threat intelligence enters risk management, security testing and threat response

description.en: For each of the three processes the control names, record the point at which intelligence enters it, who carries it there, and the record that shows it happened — a risk register entry citing a threat, a test scope updated from a reported technique, an action raised against a specific advisory. Where a process has no entry point today, record that rather than describing an intention; an unconnected feed is the finding this task exists to surface. Attach the integration map covering all three processes.

evidenceHint.en: Integration map naming, for risk management, security testing and threat response, the entry point for intelligence, the owner who carries it there and the record it produces

title.en: Issue threat intelligence reports naming the affected assets and the recommended action

description.en: Produce the reports covering the period under test and make each entry usable: the threat, the source it came from, which of the organisation's systems or data it bears on, why it matters here rather than generally, and the action recommended together with the owner it goes to. A report that surveys the threat landscape without reaching the organisation's own assets is the shape the quality review marks down for context and actionability, so the affected-asset column is not optional. Attach the reports issued during the period under test.

evidenceHint.en: Threat intelligence reports issued in the period, each entry naming the threat, its source, the affected assets or data, the reason it is relevant here and the recommended action with an owner

title.en: Record the action taken on each recommendation in a threat intelligence report

description.en: Every recommendation issued gets a disposition written against it: accepted and actioned, with what was done and when; accepted and scheduled, with the owner and date; or declined, with the reason. Link each disposition to the record it created in the process it fed — the risk register entry, the change, the test, the detection rule — so the integration map is evidenced by outcomes rather than asserted by diagram. Attach the action log for the period, including the recommendations still open.

evidenceHint.en: Threat intelligence action log for the period with one entry per recommendation giving its disposition, owner, date and the risk, change, test or detection record it produced

title.en: Score each report issued in the period for relevance, insight, context and actionability

description.en: Assess the reports one by one against the four qualities the control names, and for each score record the passage in the report that justifies it — a score with no citation is an opinion the next reviewer cannot check or repeat. Note in particular the reports whose recommendations went nowhere in the action log, since that is the strongest available signal that the intelligence was not actionable as written. Attach the assessment sheet with the scores, their citations and the improvements agreed with the report author.

evidenceHint.en: Report quality assessment sheet with one row per report scored on relevance, insight, context and actionability, each score citing the passage supporting it

title.en: Check the source register covers the strategic, tactical and operational layers

description.en: Group the register by layer and judge the coverage of each: which decisions that layer is meant to inform, whether any source actually feeds them, and what is missing — a tactical feed on adversary techniques with no strategic source on sector-level shifts is a gap worth naming. Where a layer rests on a single source, say so, because concentration and absence fail in the same way when the source lapses. Attach the evaluation report with the gaps found and the sourcing action proposed against each.

evidenceHint.en: Source and method evaluation report giving coverage per intelligence layer, the gaps and single-source dependencies found, and the sourcing action proposed for each

controls.title: ICT Continuity Readiness Control
controls.objective: To ensure that the ICT services are planned, implemented, maintained, and tested in alignment with business continuity objectives and ICT continuity requirements.
controls.successCriteria:
The BIA accurately reflects the impact and requirements of ICT services in business continuity.
ICT continuity plans are comprehensive, up-to-date, and in alignment with the BIA outcomes.
Regular testing or drills of the ICT continuity plans demonstrate their effectiveness and readiness.
The organizational structure adequately supports and is competent in managing ICT service disruptions in line with the business continuity objectives.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the Business Impact Analysis (BIA) report that outlines ICT services impact and requirements.
Gather the latest ICT continuity plans, including details on RTOs, RPOs, and strategies for handling disruptions.
Collect records of recent tests or drills conducted to validate the ICT continuity plans.
Acquire documentation of the organizational structure responsible for ICT continuity, including roles and responsibilities.

Analysis:
Review the BIA report to ensure that it accurately identifies and assesses the impacts on ICT services.
Analyze the ICT continuity plans to confirm that they align with the BIA outcomes and include specific RTOs and RPOs for prioritized ICT services.
Examine the test or drill records to verify the effectiveness of the ICT continuity plans and their alignment with business continuity objectives.
Assess the organizational structure documents to ensure there are clear responsibilities and competencies for managing ICT service disruptions.

Output:
A detailed analysis report of the BIA and its alignment with ICT continuity planning.
A compliance report on the ICT continuity plans, including assessments of RTOs, RPOs, and strategies.
Test and drill evaluation report demonstrating the effectiveness of the ICT continuity plans.
An organizational structure review report focusing on ICT continuity management roles and responsibilities.

title.en: Record each ICT service's disruption impact and continuity requirement in the BIA

description.en: Work through the ICT services the business depends on and, for each, record in the business impact analysis what is lost when it is unavailable — the business processes that stop, how the impact grows over time, the point at which it becomes material, and the maximum outage and data loss the business can absorb. Derive the priority order from that impact rather than from who owns the service, because the priority order is what the recovery objectives in the next task are set from. Management supplies the business impact judgement and IT Operations the service dependencies. Attach the BIA report showing every ICT service assessed, with none left unrated.

evidenceHint.en: Business impact analysis report covering every ICT service, giving the business processes affected, the impact over time, the maximum tolerable outage and data loss, and the resulting recovery priority

text.en: List the ICT services the business processes depend on, including those delivered by third parties.
For each service, name the business processes that stop when it becomes unavailable.
Record how the impact grows over time and the point at which it becomes material to the business.
Record the maximum outage the business can absorb and the data loss it can tolerate.
Rank the services into a recovery priority order derived from those impacts, and have it agreed.

title.en: Set an RTO and RPO for every prioritised ICT service, with the strategy that meets it

description.en: For each ICT service the BIA prioritised, write into the ICT continuity plan a recovery time objective and a recovery point objective, and beside them the strategy that actually delivers them — the standby capacity, the backup and restore route, the alternate supplier or the manual workaround. An objective with no strategy behind it is a target rather than a plan, and it is the shape a drill will expose. Check every objective back against the maximum tolerable outage the BIA recorded, and where the strategy cannot meet it, record the shortfall and its owner rather than restating the target. Attach the issued plan with the objective and strategy table complete.

evidenceHint.en: Issued ICT continuity plan containing an RTO, an RPO and the delivering recovery strategy for every prioritised ICT service, with any shortfall against the BIA's tolerable outage recorded and owned

title.en: Name the roles, responsibilities and competencies for managing an ICT service disruption

description.en: Document the structure that runs a disruption: who declares one, who leads the recovery of each prioritised service, who authorises a failover or the invocation of the recovery strategy the plan names for that service, who communicates to the business, and the deputy for each of those when the primary is unavailable. Against each role record the competency it requires and the named individuals who currently hold it, so a gap shows as a gap rather than as an unfilled box. Reach out of hours matters as much as the name, so record how each holder is contacted. Attach the issued structure document with current names against every role.

evidenceHint.en: ICT continuity organisational structure document giving each role, its responsibility during a disruption, the competency required, the named holder with out-of-hours contact, and the named deputy

title.en: Run a drill of the ICT continuity plan and record recovery achieved against the stated objectives

description.en: Exercise the plan against a scenario drawn from the highest-priority services rather than one chosen for being easy, and record what actually happened: the time the disruption was declared, the time each service was restored, the data loss incurred, which plan steps were followed and which were found wrong or missing. Compare the achieved recovery time and recovery point against the RTO and RPO the plan states, and where the drill missed them, raise a plan or capacity item with a named owner. Record an aborted exercise as aborted with its reason rather than omitting it. Attach the drill record with its timings and observations.

evidenceHint.en: Drill or test record giving the scenario, participants, declaration and restoration timestamps per service, achieved recovery time and data loss against the stated RTO and RPO, and the items raised with owners

text.en: Choose a disruption scenario that exercises one of the highest-priority ICT services.
Run the recovery from the plan as written, without correcting it mid-exercise.
Timestamp the declaration and the restoration of each service in scope of the scenario.
Record the data loss incurred and compare achieved timings against the plan's RTO and RPO.
Log every plan step found wrong, missing or unusable, and raise it with a named owner.

title.en: Reconcile the ICT continuity plans against the current BIA outcomes

description.en: Read the plan and the BIA side by side and produce the compliance report: every service the BIA prioritised should appear in the plan with an objective no weaker than the tolerable outage the BIA recorded, and no service should carry an objective the BIA does not justify. Pick up the services added or retired since the BIA was written — a service in the plan that no longer exists, and a new service in neither document, are the two failures this reconciliation exists for. Record a verdict per service with the discrepancy and the owner who will close it. Attach the reconciliation.

evidenceHint.en: Reconciliation of the ICT continuity plan against the BIA, one row per service showing the BIA tolerable outage, the plan's RTO and RPO, an aligned or discrepant verdict, and an owner for each discrepancy

controls.title: Cabling Security Control
controls.objective: To ensure the security of cables carrying power, data, or supporting information services, protecting them from interception, interference, or damage.
controls.successCriteria:
All cables carrying power, data, or supporting information services are properly protected.
Underground routing or adequate protection is in place for vulnerable cables.
Power and communication cables are effectively segregated.
Additional security measures for sensitive systems are implemented as required.
Periodical inspections and sweeps are documented and effective.
Controlled access is maintained for patch panels and cable rooms.
Fiber-optic cables are used where necessary.
Cables are labeled for easy identification.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain a list of all cables carrying power, data, or supporting information services within the organization.
Review documentation on the locations and routes of these cables.
Inspect records of cable installation, including specifications and methods used.

Analysis:
Verify that cables are routed underground where possible or adequately protected if above ground.
Ensure that power cables are segregated from communication cables to prevent interference.
Check if sensitive or critical systems have additional security measures in place, such as armored conduit, locked rooms or boxes, alarms at inspection and termination points, and electromagnetic shielding.
Review records of periodical technical sweeps and physical inspections to detect unauthorized devices attached to the cables.
Validate that controlled access measures are implemented for patch panels and cable rooms.
Confirm the use of fiber-optic cables where necessary.
Ensure that cables are labeled at each end with source and destination details for physical identification and inspection.

Output:
Documentation detailing the status of each cable and its security measures.
Records of inspections and sweeps.
Confirmation of cable labeling and segregation.

title.en: Record every power, data and service cable run with its route and termination points

description.en: Everything this control asks to be verified is verified run by run, so the register is the first artifact: each run identified, what it carries, whether power, data, or a supporting service such as telephony or fire alarm signalling, its route from end to end, both termination points, and the system or area it serves. Record where a run passes through public or shared space, and record the runs whose route nobody can document, because an unknown route cannot be assessed and is a finding in its own right. Attach the cable register with the route documentation and installation records it was compiled from.

evidenceHint.en: Cable register listing every power, data and service run with what it carries, its route, both termination points, the system served, and the runs whose route is not documented

title.en: Label each cable at both ends with its source and destination

description.en: Physical identification is what makes an inspection possible at all: an unlabelled run cannot be traced, so it cannot be swept for an attached device and cannot be checked against the register. Work through the register and fit a durable label at each end of every run carrying the run identifier, the source and the destination, and correct the register wherever the physical trace disagrees with what it says. Record the runs that could not be labelled and why. Attach the labelling record showing every register row as labelled or outstanding.

evidenceHint.en: Cable labelling record covering every register row, giving the label fitted at each end and the list of runs left unlabelled with their reasons

title.en: Record the additional protection applied to runs serving sensitive or critical systems

description.en: Identify from the register which runs serve sensitive or critical systems, then record what protects each of them beyond the standard installation: armoured conduit, a locked room or lockable box at inspection and termination points, alarms on those points, electromagnetic shielding, and fibre-optic cable where the interception risk calls for it. Where one of these is required for a run and is not fitted, record it as absent with an accountable owner rather than leaving the cell blank. Attach the schedule with the installation specifications behind it.

evidenceHint.en: Schedule of sensitive and critical cable runs showing armoured conduit, locked enclosure, alarmed inspection points, shielding and fibre as fitted or absent, with an owner against each absence

title.en: Restrict access to every patch panel and cable room and record who holds that access

description.en: Fit and record the controlled access this control requires at each patch panel, riser and cable room: the lock or badge reader in place, and the people who can open it. Reconcile the holder list against current employment and role and remove anyone who no longer needs it. Where a patch panel sits in open or shared space and cannot be enclosed, record that with the compensating measure accepted and by whom. Attach the access list per location with the date it was reconciled.

evidenceHint.en: Access control record per patch panel, riser and cable room: the control fitted, the current holder list with its reconciliation date, and any uncontrolled location with its compensating measure

title.en: Log each technical sweep and physical inspection of the cable runs and anything found attached

description.en: Carry out the periodical physical inspections and technical sweeps at the interval the organisation sets, and record each one: the date, who performed it, the runs and termination points examined, the method used, and what was found, whether an unlabelled or unexpected cable, a device attached at a patch panel, a disturbed seal, or nothing at all. A sweep that finds nothing is recorded with its scope so that a clean result is distinguishable from a sweep not done. Anything found is recorded with what was done about it, by whom and when. Attach the inspection and sweep records for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Inspection and sweep records for the period giving date, performer, the runs and termination points covered, the method, the findings or an explicit nil, and the action taken on anything found

title.en: Check every run's routing and power-to-data segregation against the protection its use requires

description.en: Take the register run by run and record the state this control asks about: whether the run is underground or otherwise adequately protected where it is exposed, whether power and communication cabling are segregated along the route and at the panels, and whether the protection fitted matches the sensitivity of the system it serves. Produce the status document with a verdict per run and, for every run failing on routing, segregation or protection, the exposure it creates and the owner who will remedy it. Attach the status document with the inspection evidence supporting each verdict.

evidenceHint.en: Cable status document with a verdict per run on routing protection, power-to-data segregation and sensitivity-appropriate protection, and the exposure and owner recorded against each failing run

text.en: Record for each run whether it is underground, in conduit, or exposed along its route.
Check power and communication cabling are separated along the route and at the panels.
Compare the protection fitted against the sensitivity of the system the run serves.
Record the exposure and the accountable owner for every run that fails a check.

controls.title: System Processing Compliance
controls.objective: Ensure system processing aligns with defined specifications to achieve product and service objectives.
controls.successCriteria:
Processing activities conform to the defined specifications.
Efficient and effective detection and correction of processing or production activity errors.
Accurate and complete documentation of all processing activities and changes.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain processing specifications documents for key services and products.
Collect logs and records of processing activities, including error detection and correction.
Gather change requests and their resolution documentation since the last audit.

Analysis:
Review processing specifications against actual processing activities to confirm adherence.
Analyze error logs to evaluate the efficiency and effectiveness of error detection and correction processes.
Examine change requests to validate adherence to processing specifications and correction procedures.

Output:
Comparison report between processing specifications and actual activities.
Analysis of error handling efficiency and effectiveness.
Review summary of change requests and resolutions.

title.en: Catalogue the services and products in scope with the specification document that governs each

description.en: The auditor's first request is the processing specifications for key services and products, and this catalogue is what makes that request answerable: one row per service or product, the specification document and version that defines how its processing must behave, the owner of that specification, and the system that actually performs the processing. Build it from the services in production rather than from the documentation shelf, so a service processing live data with no specification appears as a blank cell instead of not appearing at all. That blank is the finding this task produces, not a reason to leave the row out. Attach the catalogue with every row carrying a specification reference or an explicit 'none exists' marker naming the owner who will write one.

evidenceHint.en: Catalogue of in-scope services and products, one row per service, giving the governing processing specification and version, the specification owner, the processing system, and an explicit marker where no specification exists

text.en: List the key services and products in production whose processing is in scope.
Name the specification document and version that governs each one's processing.
Record the system or job that actually performs the processing for that service.
Mark every service that has no specification and name the owner who will write it.
Date the catalogue and hold it as the population the comparison test runs against.

title.en: Record the accepted inputs, processing rules and expected outputs in each specification

description.en: A specification that describes intent cannot be compared against activity, so make each one say what a conforming run looks like in values: the inputs it accepts, the rules applied to them, the outputs those rules should produce, and the checks that establish a run conformed. Work down the catalogue so every service in scope is covered, and where a rule exists only in code, write it into the specification and cite the module it was read from. Where the business cannot state what a conforming result is for part of the processing, record that as undefined rather than inventing one — the comparison test reports those rows as untestable rather than passing them. Attach the issued specification versions.

evidenceHint.en: Issued processing specification per in-scope service, stating the accepted inputs, the processing rules applied, the outputs a conforming run produces and the checks that establish conformance

title.en: Log every processing error with its detection time, correction and re-run outcome

description.en: Each processing or production error gets a record carrying the service it occurred in, when the run happened, when the error was detected, how it was detected (automated check, downstream complaint, manual review), the correction applied, who applied it, and whether the corrected run completed. Include errors caught automatically and silently reprocessed — those are exactly the ones an aggregate success rate hides, and they are what the effectiveness measure later reads. IT Operations supplies the platform-level extracts; the service owner adds the errors detected outside tooling. Attach the error log covering the period under test; a log with corrections but no detection timestamps cannot support the measurement task and is not done.

evidenceHint.en: Processing error log for the period, one row per error, giving service, run date, detection time and method, correction applied, operator and re-run outcome

title.en: Record each change request to processing with its resolution and the specification version it lands in

description.en: For every change request raised against a processing activity since the last audit, record what was requested, who raised it, how it was resolved, and the specification version that now carries the change. A change delivered into production while the specification still describes the previous behaviour is the drift this control exists to catch, so the specification-version column is the load-bearing one and a blank there is a finding rather than an omission. Where a change was made to correct a processing error, cite the error-log entry it answers so the two records can be read together. Attach the change register with its supporting resolution documentation.

evidenceHint.en: Change register for the period listing each processing change request with its requester, its resolution, the specification version carrying it, and any error-log entry it answers

title.en: Compare the period's processing activity against each service's specification

description.en: Take the catalogue row by row and compare what the service actually produced over the period against what its specification says it should produce — record counts against the expected population, output values against the stated rules, and the results of the checks the specification says establish conformance. Read the result from the processing records themselves rather than from a monitoring dashboard's summary, since a dashboard reports the checks somebody configured and this test is looking for the ones nobody did. Produce the comparison report with a conforms or deviates verdict per service, and against every deviation the accountable owner and the agreed correction. Attach the report together with the extracts the verdicts were derived from.

evidenceHint.en: Comparison report covering every catalogued service, giving the observed processing against the specification's rules, a conforms or deviates verdict, and an owner plus correction for each deviation

text.en: Pull the period's processing records for each service in the catalogue.
Compare observed record counts and output values against the specification's rules.
Apply the conformance checks each specification states and record their results.
Mark each service conforms or deviates and note the evidence behind the verdict.
Name an owner and an agreed correction against every deviation recorded.

title.en: Measure detection and correction time for the period's processing errors

description.en: Read the error log and produce the effectiveness analysis the control's output calls for: how long each error took to detect and how long from detection to correction, split by how it was found, so the share detected by the service's own checks is visible next to the share found by somebody downstream. The second number is the one that says whether detection is working. Call out separately any error corrected without a change record and any that recurred after correction, since a repeat is evidence the correction addressed the symptom. Attach the analysis with the error-log extract behind it and a named owner for every improvement it recommends.

evidenceHint.en: Error-handling analysis for the period giving detection and correction times per error, the split between automated and downstream detection, and the list of recurring or unrecorded corrections

controls.title: Automated Software Inventory Management
controls.objective: Ensure comprehensive and automated documentation of all installed software across the enterprise.
controls.successCriteria:
The automated software inventory tool is active and functional on all systems.
All installed software is accurately documented and reflected in the inventory reports.
Regular updates and changes in software installations are consistently tracked and reflected in the inventory tool's logs or histories.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Retrieve reports from the automated software inventory tool detailing installed software across the enterprise.
Obtain system configuration details to verify the presence of the inventory tool on all systems.
Gather change logs or update histories from the inventory tool since the last audit.

Analysis:
Analyze the software inventory reports to confirm that all installed software is accurately documented and updated.
Compare system configurations with inventory reports to ensure the inventory tool covers all systems.
Review change logs or update histories to validate that the software inventory is regularly updated and reflects any changes in installed software.

Output:
Comprehensive report of all installed software.
Verification report confirming the presence and functioning of the inventory tool on all systems.
Analysis document detailing the review of change logs or update histories.

title.en: Compile the list of systems the software inventory tool is required to cover

description.en: The audit compares system configurations against the inventory reports to establish that the tool reaches every system, and that comparison is only as good as the list it counts against — so build the population from sources the inventory tool does not own: the asset register, the directory, the hypervisor and cloud consoles, and the network's own view of what is connected. Record against each entry the system name, its owner and whether it is a server, workstation, virtual machine or cloud instance, so a later gap can be chased to a person rather than to a hostname. Attach the dated population list naming the sources it was built from; it is the denominator every coverage figure in this control is a fraction of.

evidenceHint.en: Dated list of in-scope systems compiled from sources independent of the inventory tool, each with its owner and system type

text.en: Pull system records from the asset register, the directory and the cloud and hypervisor consoles.
Reconcile the sources against each other and resolve entries that appear in one but not another.
Record the owner and the system type against every entry so a later gap has an addressee.
Name the sources used and the compilation date on the list itself before it is filed.

title.en: Enable the inventory tool on every system on the list and record the configuration that proves it

description.en: The control is satisfied only where the tool is active and functional on all systems, which is a claim about configuration rather than about intent. Install or enable the tool's collector on every entry of the population list — an agent where the tool uses one, a credentialed scan where it does not — and then capture, per system, the configuration detail that demonstrates it: the collector version, its running state, the collection schedule and the time it last reported successfully. Where a system cannot take the collector — an appliance, an unmanaged device, a platform the tool does not support — record the reason and the alternative source its software list will come from, because an untracked exception is indistinguishable from a failed deployment. Attach the configuration export covering the whole list.

evidenceHint.en: System configuration export showing the inventory tool's collector version, running state and last successful collection time for every system on the population list, with a reason and alternative source recorded for each exception

title.en: Generate the enterprise software inventory report for the period

description.en: Run the tool's full export across the estate and file it as the period's record: every system it reached, the software installed on each and the version of each package. Record the generation date and the number of systems the report actually covers, because a report that silently omits the systems that failed to report reads identically to one in which every system was clean. Where the tool cannot enumerate a class of software — a portable executable run without installation, or software inside a container image — state that limit on the report rather than leaving the omission to be discovered at the next audit. Attach the report as generated, without hand-editing the rows.

evidenceHint.en: Enterprise software inventory report for the period listing installed software and version per system, carrying the generation date, the count of systems covered and any stated enumeration limit

title.en: Export the tool's software installation and removal history for the period

description.en: The inventory report is a snapshot; the change history is what shows the inventory is maintained rather than compiled once. Export the tool's log of installations, upgrades and removals since the previous export, with the system, the package, the change type and the date on every entry, and record the total number of changes the period contains. Where the tool's history is truncated by its own retention setting, record that retention window on the export, so the period the evidence can actually speak to is stated rather than assumed. File the history alongside the inventory report for the same period so the two are read together.

evidenceHint.en: Software change history export covering the period, one entry per installation, upgrade or removal with system, package, change type and date, and the tool's history retention window recorded

title.en: Reconcile the systems reporting into the tool against the population list

description.en: Set the population list and the inventory report side by side and produce the verification report: which systems reported, which are silent — the tool is installed but has not reported — and which are absent from the tool entirely. Silent and absent are different failures with different fixes, so record which one applies to each system rather than reporting a single coverage percentage. Give every system in either state a named owner and a date by which it will report, and check that each recorded deployment exception is still legitimate rather than a stale carry-over. Attach the verification report; a coverage figure with no exception list behind it is not evidence that the tool covers the estate.

evidenceHint.en: Coverage verification report classifying every system on the population list as reporting, silent or absent, with an owner and target date against each exception

text.en: Match every population-list entry to the inventory report by machine name and network address.
Classify each unmatched system as silent, where the tool is installed but has not reported, or absent.
Investigate a sample of absent systems to establish whether deployment failed or was never attempted.
Re-check each recorded deployment exception to confirm the reason for it still holds.
Name an owner and a target date against every silent or absent system before closing the report.

title.en: Spot-check installed software on a sample of systems against what the report records

description.en: Coverage says the tool sees a system; it does not say the tool sees everything on it. Take a sample spanning the system types on the population list and enumerate the installed software locally on each — from the package manager or the operating system's own installed-programs view — then compare that enumeration against the row the inventory report holds for the same system. Record missing packages, packages the report still shows that are no longer present, and version mismatches. Give every discrepancy a cause where one can be established: a scan the agent could not complete, a software type the tool does not detect, or a system that has not checked in since the change was made. Attach the comparison together with the local enumerations it was built from.

evidenceHint.en: Accuracy check comparing a locally enumerated software list against the inventory report row for each sampled system, with every missing package, stale entry and version mismatch and its cause

controls.title: Recovery Process Documentation
controls.objective: Ensure documented processes are in place to restore and return business activities to normal after a disruption.
controls.successCriteria:
All disruptions have corresponding recovery documentation.
Temporary measures adopted during disruptions align with documented recovery processes.
Post-disruption reviews are comprehensive and include effectiveness assessments.
Restoration timelines meet or exceed documented expectations.
Any deviations are explained and justified in the analysis report.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:

Obtain the documented recovery processes.
Gather records of all disruptions that occurred in the last year.
Collect reports on the temporary measures adopted during each disruption.
Retrieve post-disruption review meeting minutes and reports.

Analysis:

Verify that documented recovery processes exist and are up to date.
Cross-check each disruption record with the documented recovery process to ensure it was followed.
Review reports on temporary measures to ensure they align with documented processes.
Evaluate post-disruption reviews to confirm they include assessments of the effectiveness of the recovery processes.
Compare the actual restoration timelines with the documented expected timelines to identify any deviations and reasons.

Output:

Copies of documented recovery processes.
A list of disruptions with corresponding recovery documentation.
Analysis report detailing adherence to recovery processes for each disruption.
Spreadsheet tracking restoration timelines against expected timelines.
Summary of post-disruption review findings.

title.en: Register every disruption in the period under review with the activities it affected

description.en: Compile the disruption record set the rest of this control is tested against: one row per disruption in the period under review carrying the date and time it began, the business activities and locations affected, the date and time normal operation resumed, and the recovery documentation that applies to it. Draw the population from incident tickets, service outage records and the management minutes that reported them rather than from recollection, so a disruption handled informally still appears. Where a disruption has no corresponding recovery documentation, leave the reference blank and flag the row — that flag list is the first finding this control produces. Attach the register with the source records it was built from.

evidenceHint.en: Disruption register for the last twelve months, each row giving the start and restoration times, the activities affected, and the recovery documentation reference or a flag where none exists

text.en: Draw the population from incident tickets, outage records and management minutes, not from recollection.
Record the start time, the activities affected and the time normal operation resumed for each.
Reference the recovery process document that applies to each disruption on the register.
Flag every disruption for which no recovery documentation exists and carry those flags forward.

title.en: Document the process for returning each disrupted activity to normal, with its expected restoration timeline

description.en: For each business activity that can be disrupted, write the process that takes it from the temporary or degraded state back to normal running: the steps in order, who performs each one, the dependencies that must be back first, and the point at which the activity is declared restored. Against each process record the expected restoration timeline, because that figure is what the timeline comparison later measures actual performance against — a process carrying no expectation cannot be found to have deviated from one. State which temporary measures are pre-approved for use while the activity is degraded, so the measures actually adopted can be checked for alignment rather than judged after the event. Attach the issued recovery process documents with their version and issue date visible.

evidenceHint.en: Issued recovery process documents, each naming the ordered restoration steps, the person accountable for each, the pre-approved temporary measures and the expected restoration timeline

text.en: Write the ordered steps that return the activity from degraded running back to normal.
Name the person accountable for each step and the dependencies that must be restored first.
State the condition under which the activity is declared fully restored.
Record the expected restoration timeline that actual recovery will later be measured against.
List the temporary measures pre-approved for use while the activity remains degraded.

title.en: Record the temporary measures adopted during each disruption as they are put in place

description.en: While a disruption is running, the person leading the response records each temporary measure adopted — the workaround, the manual process, the alternative site or supplier — with the time it was put in place, who authorised it, and the recovery process step it stands in for. Note explicitly where a measure was adopted that the recovery process does not pre-approve, because that is the divergence the later analysis has to explain rather than discover. Record the time each temporary measure was withdrawn as normal operation resumed, so a workaround left permanently in place is visible. Attach the temporary measures report for the disruption.

evidenceHint.en: Temporary measures report per disruption listing each measure adopted, who authorised it, the recovery process step it substituted for, and when it was withdrawn

title.en: Review each disruption after it closes and minute the recovery process's effectiveness

description.en: After every disruption on the register, convene the people who ran the response and minute the review: what the disruption was, what the recovery process said, what was actually done, and an explicit assessment of how effective that process proved to be. The effectiveness assessment is the part most often omitted and the part this control is tested on, so it is written as its own conclusion rather than left implied by a narrative. Record the improvements agreed, each with a named owner, and reference them from the recovery process document they change. Attach the review minutes or report for each disruption.

evidenceHint.en: Post-disruption review minutes or report per disruption, carrying an explicit assessment of the recovery process's effectiveness and the agreed improvements with named owners

title.en: Track actual restoration time against the documented expected timeline for every disruption

description.en: Build one line per disruption comparing the restoration time actually achieved with the expected timeline recorded in the applicable recovery process, and show the difference. Where the actual time exceeded the expectation, write the reason it did and the evidence behind that reason; where restoration beat the expectation materially, note whether the documented expectation is now wrong and should be revised. A deviation left with a blank reason is the finding this task produces, not an accepted result. Attach the completed tracking spreadsheet, including the disruptions whose applicable process carried no expected timeline at all.

evidenceHint.en: Restoration timeline spreadsheet with one line per disruption showing the expected time, the actual time, the difference, and a written reason against every deviation

title.en: Assess each disruption's handling against the documented recovery process and report adherence

description.en: Take the register row by row and cross-check what was actually done during each disruption — from the response records, the temporary measures report and the review minutes — against the steps the applicable recovery process sets out. Record per disruption whether the process was followed, partially followed or bypassed, naming the specific steps missed and whether the omission changed the outcome. Where a disruption had no recovery documentation at all, record that as its result rather than excluding the row. The output is the analysis report the control calls for, and its conclusions feed the next revision of the recovery processes. Attach the report with the records each conclusion was drawn from.

evidenceHint.en: Adherence analysis report covering every disruption on the register, giving a followed, partially followed or bypassed verdict per disruption and naming the steps missed

controls.title: DNS Query Audit Logging
controls.objective: Ensure the collection and storage of DNS query audit logs on all enterprise assets where appropriate and supported, to monitor and analyze network traffic for security and operational efficiency.
controls.successCriteria:
All enterprise assets that support DNS query logging have it enabled and properly configured.
DNS query audit logs are regularly reviewed and stored in accordance with organizational policies and standards.
Any irregularities or security concerns identified in the DNS query logs are addressed and documented.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Retrieve a list of all enterprise assets capable of DNS query logging.
Obtain DNS query audit logs from a representative sample of these assets.
Acquire documentation on the configuration settings for DNS query logging on these assets.

Analysis:
Verify that all listed enterprise assets have DNS query logging enabled and are appropriately configured.
Examine the DNS query audit logs for signs of irregular activity or patterns that might indicate security concerns.
Cross-reference the DNS query logs with other network activity logs for comprehensive analysis.

Output:
A comprehensive list of enterprise assets with their DNS query logging status.
Copies of DNS query audit logs.
A report detailing the analysis of the DNS query logs and any findings or recommendations.

title.en: List every enterprise asset capable of DNS query logging with its current status

description.en: Enumerate the assets that can record DNS queries — internal resolvers, domain controllers running DNS, firewalls performing DNS inspection, endpoint agents and any cloud or managed resolver the organisation uses — and give each a row carrying whether query logging is enabled, disabled or unsupported on that platform. Mark unsupported explicitly rather than omitting the asset, since 'where appropriate and supported' is a judgement that has to be visible. Attach the list; it is the population the configuration record, the sampling and the reconciliation all draw from.

evidenceHint.en: List of enterprise assets capable of DNS query logging, each row giving the platform, the enabled, disabled or unsupported status and the owner

title.en: Record the DNS query logging configuration in force on each capable asset

description.en: For every asset the list marks capable, export the logging configuration as it actually reads: which fields are recorded (querying client, query name, query type, response and timestamp), where the records are sent, and the retention applied there. Note where a resolver logs only aggregate counts or drops the client address, because that determines whether the later analysis can attribute a query to a machine at all. Attach the configuration documentation per asset against the list row it belongs to.

evidenceHint.en: Configuration exports or documented settings per capable asset showing the DNS query fields recorded, the log destination and the retention applied

title.en: Review the sampled DNS query logs for irregular query patterns and record each finding

description.en: Pull DNS query logs from a representative sample of the capable assets for the period under test and work through them for the patterns that indicate a security concern: sustained NXDOMAIN volume from one client, query names carrying encoded payloads, clients resolving through anything but the resolver their network is configured to use, and lookups of newly registered or known-bad domains. Each hit gets a row naming the client, the query, the time and its disposition — benign with a reason, or referred for investigation and to whom. Attach the log extract together with the dispositioned findings list; the extract is what shows the logs were read rather than merely held.

evidenceHint.en: DNS query log extracts for the sampled assets plus a findings list giving client, query, time and a benign or referred disposition per hit

text.en: Select the sample so every resolver platform contributes at least one asset.
Pull DNS query logs covering the whole period under test for those assets.
Search for NXDOMAIN bursts and query names carrying encoded payloads.
Flag clients resolving through anything but the resolver their network is configured to use.
Disposition every hit as benign with a reason or refer it for investigation.

title.en: Cross-reference each DNS finding against the corresponding network activity logs

description.en: For every finding raised, look for the same client in the same time window in the other network records — firewall sessions, proxy or URL request logs and endpoint telemetry — and record whether the DNS activity is corroborated by a connection that followed, contradicted, or has no counterpart at all. A resolved name with no subsequent session and a session with no preceding lookup are both reportable, the second usually meaning a client is bypassing the logged resolver. Attach the cross-reference working paper listing, per finding, the sources consulted and the outcome.

evidenceHint.en: Cross-reference working paper giving, per DNS finding, the other network log sources consulted and whether the activity was corroborated, contradicted or absent

title.en: Reconcile the asset list against the assets actually delivering DNS logs

description.en: Take the assets the list marks as enabled and query the log store for the most recent DNS event received from each one. An asset whose configuration says logging is on but which has sent nothing for days is the silent failure this task exists to catch, and it is invisible to a configuration review. Record per asset the last event timestamp, a delivering or not-delivering verdict, and for every gap the cause and an accountable owner. Attach the reconciliation with the log-store query output behind it.

evidenceHint.en: Reconciliation listing every asset marked enabled with its last received DNS event timestamp, a delivering or not-delivering verdict, and a cause and owner for each gap

controls.title: Information Classification and Labeling Compliance
