controls.objective: To ensure that information within the organization is classified and labeled correctly according to the defined categories of confidential, sensitive, and public, in compliance with the organization's information classification and labeling policies.
controls.successCriteria:
All examined information is classified and labeled correctly in accordance with the organization's information classification and labeling policies.
Documentation of classification decisions and labeling practices is complete and demonstrates adherence to the policies.
Any identified misclassifications, mislabeling, or process gaps are addressed promptly to maintain the integrity of the information classification and labeling system.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the latest version of the organization's information classification policy and labeling procedures.
Gather a representative sample of documents, records, and digital files from various departments.
Retrieve logs or records of information classification decisions made by information owners.
Collect metadata information from a sample of digital documents and files.
Request evidence of training materials or communication regarding labeling procedures.

Analysis:
Review the sampled documents, records, and digital files to verify their classification and labeling against the criteria outlined in the information classification and labeling policies.
Assess whether the classification (confidential, sensitive, public) and labeling (physical labels, headers, footers, metadata, watermarking) are appropriate based on content and policy criteria.
Examine logs or records of classification decisions and labeling practices to ensure adherence to the policies.
Evaluate the metadata of digital documents for alignment with classification labels and efficient information management.
Review training and communication materials for adequacy in informing personnel about classification and labeling processes.

Output:
A report detailing the classification and labeling review of each sampled document, record, and digital file.
A summary of compliance or non-compliance with the classification and labeling policies for each examined item.
Recommendations for any reclassification, relabeling, or process improvements where necessary.

title.en: Record the information types each department holds and the owner who classifies them

description.en: List, department by department, the kinds of information held — documents, records and digital files, and the systems or locations they live in — and name the information owner who decides the classification for each. Take it from the departments themselves rather than from a register drawn up centrally, because the sample the review later draws has to come from this same population. Where two departments hold the same information type, record which owner is accountable for classifying it, so the decision cannot fall between them. Attach the list with an owner named against every information type.

evidenceHint.en: List of information types per department with the holding system or location and the named information owner responsible for classifying each

title.en: Publish the classification categories and the labeling method required for each medium

description.en: Issue the classification policy and the labeling procedure together, so the categories — confidential, sensitive and public — are defined by the criteria that decide between them, and each category carries the label it must bear on every medium it appears on: physical labels on paper, headers and footers in documents, metadata fields in digital files, and watermarking where the policy requires it. Written that way the procedure can be applied by the person holding the document rather than interpreted by them. Attach the issued and dated policy and labeling procedure versions.

evidenceHint.en: Issued and dated information classification policy and labeling procedure, giving the criteria for each category and the label required on each medium

text.en: State the criteria that place information in the confidential, sensitive or public category.
Set the label each category carries on paper, including cover markings and physical labels.
Set the label each category carries inside documents: headers, footers and watermarking.
Set the metadata field and the value digital files must carry for each category.
Name who decides an item's category and how each decision is recorded.

title.en: Log each classification decision the information owners make, with the criterion applied

description.en: As information owners classify what they hold, record the decision: the item or information type, the category assigned, the criterion from the policy that decided it, the owner who decided and the date. Reclassifications carry the same record plus the reason for the change, because a category that moved without a stated reason is indistinguishable from a mislabel. This log is what the review examines to judge whether the policy is being applied rather than merely known. Attach the classification decision log for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Classification decision log for the period showing the item, the category assigned, the policy criterion applied, the deciding owner and the date, with reasons recorded against reclassifications

title.en: Train the staff who apply the labels and record their acknowledgement

description.en: Get the labeling procedure in front of the people who create and handle information in the departments on the scope list, through training or a communication that shows what each label looks like on each medium and when it has to be applied. Keep the material used, its date, the audience it went to and the record of who received or completed it. Where a department has had no such communication in the period, record that gap, since the review would otherwise read its mislabelling as carelessness rather than as never having been told. Attach the material with the acknowledgement record.

evidenceHint.en: Labeling training or communication material with its date, the departments it reached, and the record of who acknowledged or completed it

title.en: Score a sample of documents, records and digital files against the classification and labeling policy

description.en: Draw a sample across the departments on the scope list covering paper records, documents and digital files alike, and test each item twice: is the category it carries the right one for its content under the policy criteria, and does it bear the label that category requires on the medium it is held on. Score each item pass or fail with the specific defect named — misclassified, correctly classified but unlabelled, labelled to the wrong category — and write a reclassification or relabelling action with an owner against every fail. Attach the completed scoring sheet with the exceptions and their owners.

evidenceHint.en: Scoring sheet with one row per sampled item giving its department, assigned category, observed label, a pass or fail verdict, and the reclassification or relabelling action for each fail

text.en: Draw the sample so every department on the scope list and every medium is represented.
Judge each item's content against the policy criteria for confidential, sensitive and public.
Check the label it actually bears against the label its category requires on that medium.
Name the specific defect against each fail rather than recording it as non-compliant.
Assign a reclassification or relabelling action with an owner to every failed item.

title.en: Check the metadata of the sampled digital files against the classification they carry

description.en: For the digital files in the sample, read the classification metadata the file actually holds — the stored property values, not the marking printed on the page — and set it against the category recorded in the decision log and the label shown in the document. Record per file whether the metadata is present, absent or inconsistent with the visible label, because it is the metadata that downstream tooling reads when it decides how a file may be handled. Where a file format or repository cannot carry the field at all, record that as a finding against the repository. Attach the metadata comparison with those findings.

evidenceHint.en: Metadata comparison for the sampled digital files showing the classification metadata held, the visible label and the decision-log category, with every absence or inconsistency recorded

controls.title: Privacy Notice Communication Control
controls.objective: To ensure that privacy notices are effectively communicated to data subjects, are up-to-date, and reflect current privacy practices, including changes in the use of personal information.
controls.successCriteria:
The privacy notice includes all required elements and accurately reflects current privacy practices.
Evidence of timely communication of the privacy notice and any updates to data subjects.
Changes in privacy practices are consistently and accurately updated in the privacy notice and communicated to data subjects.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the latest version of the privacy notice documentation.
Collect records of privacy notice communications to data subjects (e.g., email notifications, website updates).
Acquire documentation of any recent changes to privacy practices or use of personal information.

Analysis:
Review the privacy notice to verify it includes all necessary information such as purpose of data collection, consent mechanisms, types of data collected, data use, retention, disposal, etc.
Examine communication records to ensure timely notification of privacy notice updates to data subjects.
Analyze change documentation to confirm that updates to privacy practices are accurately reflected in the latest privacy notice.

Output:
A report summarizing the findings of the privacy notice content and its communication.
A compliance checklist verifying each required element of the privacy notice.
Documentation of the analysis of privacy notice change communications.

title.en: Identify the data-subject populations the privacy notice must reach and the channel that reaches each

description.en: List each population the entity holds personal information about — customers, prospects, employees, applicants, website visitors — and for each one the channel through which the privacy notice and its updates actually reach them: the page it is published on, the email list, the in-product prompt, the paper form. Name the system that holds the addressing data for each channel, because that is what has to produce the communication records later, and name a population's contactability where no channel exists rather than leaving it implied. This register is the denominator the communication log is read against: a population with no channel cannot be shown to have been told anything. Attach the register with a channel or an explicit gap recorded on every row.

evidenceHint.en: Register of data-subject populations with the publication or notification channel for each, the system holding the addressing data, and an explicit gap marked where no channel exists

title.en: Record the collection purpose, consent mechanism, data types, use, retention and disposal in the notice

description.en: Work through the current privacy notice and make it state each of these explicitly rather than by reference: why personal information is collected, how consent is obtained where it is relied on, what categories of data are collected, what they are used for, how long they are kept, and how they are disposed of at the end of that period. Where the notice points at another document for any of these, either bring the substance into the notice or make the pointer specific enough that a data subject can follow it. Legal/DPO owns the wording; the business owner of each processing activity confirms the description matches what actually happens, since a notice that is complete but inaccurate fails this control in the same way as one that is silent. Attach the issued notice version.

evidenceHint.en: Issued privacy notice version showing the collection purpose, consent mechanism, data categories, uses, retention periods and disposal treatment stated in the notice itself

title.en: Log each issue and update of the privacy notice with its date, channel and audience

description.en: Every time the notice is published or updated, record the notice version, the date that version was issued, the date it went out, the channel it went out on and the population it addressed — the send report, the page publication timestamp, the screenshot of the in-product prompt. Keep the underlying artefact rather than a note that it happened, since a line in a spreadsheet saying 'notified customers' is not a communication record. Where a population from the register received nothing, record the nil against it explicitly. Attach the communication log with the send reports and publication evidence it references.

evidenceHint.en: Privacy notice communication log with the send reports, publication timestamps or screenshots behind each entry, showing the notice version, its issue date, the date it went out, the channel and the population addressed

text.en: Record the notice version and the date each publication or update went out.
Record the channel used and the data-subject population it addressed.
Attach the send report, publication timestamp or screenshot as the underlying record.
Record the date the notice version was issued beside the date it went out.
Record an explicit nil against any register population that received nothing.

title.en: Record each change in privacy practice against the notice version and the communication that carried it

description.en: When a use of personal information changes — a new purpose, a new recipient, a changed retention period, a new processor — record the change, the date it took effect in the business, the notice version that reflects it, and the communication log entry that told data subjects. Read the effective date against the notice date: a practice that changed before the notice was updated is the gap this task exists to surface, and it is recorded as a finding with a remediation owner rather than quietly backdated. Where a change was judged not to require a notice update, record that judgement and who made it. Attach the change record set with its cross-references to notice versions and communications.

evidenceHint.en: Privacy practice change record listing each change with its effective date, the notice version reflecting it, the communication entry that carried it, and any judgement that no update was required

title.en: Verify the issued notice against the required-element checklist and record a verdict per element

description.en: Take the current notice and mark each required element present, partial or absent — purpose of collection, consent mechanism, data types collected, use, retention, disposal — quoting the passage of the notice that satisfies it, so the verdict can be re-checked without re-reading the whole document. Then read the notice against the change record: an element that is present but describes a practice that has since changed is scored as inaccurate, not present. Produce the checklist and the summary report the control calls for, with a remediation owner and a target notice version against every element scored partial, absent or inaccurate. Attach both.

evidenceHint.en: Completed privacy notice compliance checklist quoting the satisfying passage per required element, plus the findings report with a remediation owner for each element scored partial, absent or inaccurate

controls.title: Data Subject Consent Management
controls.objective: To ensure that explicit consent for the collection, use, retention, disclosure, and disposal of personal information is obtained from data subjects, and the entity's processes align with privacy objectives.
controls.successCriteria:
All instances of personal data collection and use have documented explicit consent from data subjects.
The consent process is clear, transparent, and aligns with the stated privacy objectives.
Sensitive information is handled with explicit consent, and any changes in data use are communicated and consented to by data subjects.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain a sample of consent forms or digital consent logs.
Gather documentation on the entity's privacy notices and consent procedures.
Collect records of any instances where consent was required, especially for sensitive information.

Analysis:
Review the consent forms/logs to ensure they cover all aspects of data use as per the privacy notice.
Verify that the consent process includes clear communication about the consequences of consent denial or withdrawal.
Assess the documentation to confirm that explicit consent is obtained before personal information is used for new purposes.

Output:
A report detailing the analysis of consent forms and processes.
A compliance checklist verifying adherence to consent procedures for data collection and use.
Documentation of instances where consent was required and obtained.

title.en: Identify every collection and use of personal information that requires explicit consent

description.en: Build the register of processing activities where consent is the basis relied on: what is collected, from whom, for what purpose, and whether the data is sensitive — the sensitive flag decides which rows carry the higher bar the control sets and it must be populated on every row, not only where somebody thought to add it. Cover collection, use, retention, disclosure and disposal, since consent is required across that whole lifecycle and a row that records only the collection consent hides a disclosure nobody agreed to. Legal/DPO owns the register; the product owner confirms each row against what the system actually does. Attach the register; it is the population every later task in this control is measured against.

evidenceHint.en: Register of consent-dependent processing activities covering collection, use, retention, disclosure and disposal, with the sensitive-data flag populated on every row

text.en: List each processing activity that relies on the data subject's consent.
Cover disclosure and disposal, not only the initial collection of the data.
Record the personal information collected and the purpose consent is sought for.
Mark every row as sensitive or non-sensitive so the higher bar has a population.
Confirm each row against what the system does, not what the design document says.

title.en: Record the consequences of refusing or withdrawing consent in every consent form and capture screen

description.en: For each consent point in the register, put in front of the data subject what happens if they decline and what happens if they later withdraw: which service or feature becomes unavailable, what the entity does with information already held, and how withdrawal is exercised. Write it at the point of consent rather than in the privacy notice alone, since this control tests the consent process for clarity and transparency and a consequence a data subject has to go looking for was not communicated. Engineering lead implements the wording in the capture screens; Legal/DPO owns what it says. Attach the current form and screen versions showing the consequence wording in place at each consent point in the register.

evidenceHint.en: Current consent form and capture-screen versions for every register row, each showing the wording that states the consequences of refusing and of withdrawing consent

title.en: Map each consent form to the data uses in the privacy notice it must cover

description.en: Set the consent forms and digital consent flows side by side with the privacy notice and produce the mapping: which notice-stated use each form obtains consent for, and which uses are covered by no form at all. A use described in the notice but absent from every consent point is processing without the consent this control requires, and it is the finding the mapping exists to produce. Read it in the other direction too — a form seeking consent for a use the notice does not describe is equally a mismatch. Attach the mapping with the unmatched entries listed in both directions and a named owner against each.

evidenceHint.en: Consent-to-notice mapping showing the notice uses each consent form covers, the uses covered by no form, the forms seeking consent beyond the notice, and an owner for each mismatch

title.en: Log every consent, refusal and withdrawal with the data subject, purpose, timestamp and form version

description.en: Each consent event is written to the consent log carrying the data subject identifier, the purpose consented to or refused, the timestamp, the channel, and the version of the form or screen that was shown — the version is what lets a consent obtained two years ago be read against the wording actually presented then. Log refusals and withdrawals to the same standard as grants: a log holding only grants cannot evidence that a withdrawal was honoured. Engineering lead owns the capture; where consent is taken on paper or by phone, record how those events reach the same log. Attach the consent log extract for the period under test.

evidenceHint.en: Consent log extract for the period showing, per event, the data subject, purpose, grant or refusal or withdrawal, timestamp, channel and the form or screen version presented

title.en: Collect explicit consent before personal information is used for a new purpose

description.en: When a new purpose for existing personal information is proposed, obtain and record explicit consent from the affected data subjects before the processing starts, and hold the record that shows the sequence: what they were told, when they were told it, when consent was given, and the date processing began. Where consent is not given, record how those data subjects were excluded from the new processing. A consent obtained after the processing started is recorded as an exception with a remediation owner rather than filed as compliant, and sensitive information carries this bar without exception. Attach the new-purpose consent records with the communication that preceded them.

evidenceHint.en: New-purpose consent records showing the communication sent to data subjects, the consents and refusals returned, the processing start date, and how refusers were excluded

title.en: Test a sample of consent records against the uses they authorise

description.en: Draw a sample of consent records across the register, weighted towards sensitive rows, and for each one check that the purpose actually being processed against that data subject is covered by the consent held, that the consent is current rather than withdrawn, and that the form version shown carried the consequence wording. Then check the reverse for the same subjects: personal information being used for a purpose no consent covers. Produce the report and compliance checklist the control calls for, with each exception dispositioned — corrected, consent re-obtained, or processing stopped — and an owner named. Attach both with the sampled records behind them.

evidenceHint.en: Consent sampling report and compliance checklist covering the sampled records, each exception dispositioned with an owner, and the sampled consent records themselves

controls.title: Unauthorized Extension Restriction
controls.objective: To ensure that all browser and email client extensions installed on company devices are authorized and necessary for business operations.
controls.successCriteria:
All installed browser and email client extensions are verified and authorized as per company policy.
There are no unauthorized or unnecessary extensions installed on company devices.
All extension installations have appropriate request and approval documentation.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain a list of all installed browser and email client extensions on company devices. This can be done through IT inventory management tools or direct inspection.
Secure screenshots or reports showing the details of these extensions.
Gather records of any extension installation requests and approvals since the last audit.

Analysis:
For each installed extension, verify against an approved list of extensions to ensure it is authorized for use.
Examine the extension installation request and approval records to confirm that each extension has undergone the necessary approval process.
Identify any unauthorized or unnecessary extensions that are installed without following the approval process.

Output:
A comprehensive list of all installed extensions with annotations on their authorization status.
Documentation or screenshots evidencing the installation and approval of extensions.
A summary report identifying any unauthorized or unnecessary extensions found during the audit.

title.en: Collect the browser and email client extensions installed across every company device

description.en: Produce the list the audit starts from: one row per device and extension, giving the device, its user, the browser or email client, the extension name, its identifier, its version and its publisher. Pull it from the IT inventory management tooling where that tooling reports extensions, and inspect the remaining devices directly rather than assuming they carry none — a device the tooling does not cover is a device whose extensions are unknown, and it is recorded as such with an owner. Keep the console reports or screenshots the collection was taken from, since the auditor asks for them alongside the list. Attach the inventory with its collection date.

evidenceHint.en: Dated extension inventory listing each device, user, browser or email client, extension name, identifier, version and publisher, backed by the tool reports or screenshots it was collected from, with uncovered devices flagged

text.en: Export installed browser and email client extensions from the inventory management tooling.
Identify the devices that tooling does not report on and inspect each of those directly.
Record the extension identifier, version and publisher for every row, not just the display name.
Keep the console report or screenshot each row was collected from as the backing evidence.
Flag the devices whose extensions could not be collected and name an owner for each.

title.en: Record the approved extension list with the business need each entry serves

description.en: Write down which extensions are permitted, because without that list every later comparison is an opinion: name each approved extension by its identifier rather than its display name — display names are duplicated by imitations — with the browser or client it applies to, the business need it serves, the user group it is approved for, and the date and approver of that decision. An extension nobody can state a business need for does not belong on the list. Attach the approved list with its version and approval date.

evidenceHint.en: Approved extension list naming each permitted extension by identifier with its client, business need, approved user group, approver and approval date

title.en: Record the request, justification and approver for each extension installed since the last review

description.en: For every extension that has appeared since the previous review, keep the request and approval documentation the control requires: who asked for it, the business justification given, the review of what the extension can access, the approver, the date, and whether the approval covered that user alone or added the extension to the approved list. Where an extension appeared with no request behind it, record it as installed without approval — that absence is itself the record, and leaving the row blank hides it. Attach the request and approval records for the period alongside the list of installations carrying none.

evidenceHint.en: Extension installation request and approval records for the period, giving the requester, justification, approver and date per extension, plus the list of extensions installed with no request behind them

title.en: Annotate every installed extension against the approved list and report the unauthorised ones

description.en: Match the extension inventory against the approved list by identifier and annotate each row: approved and within its user group, approved but installed for a group it was not approved for, or not on the list at all. Split the last group into extensions that are unauthorised outright and extensions authorised elsewhere but no longer necessary for that user, because the two are remediated differently. Produce the summary report the control calls for, naming per entry the devices carrying it, its publisher, and the owner who will remove it. Attach the annotated list together with the summary.

evidenceHint.en: Annotated extension list marking every installed extension approved, out-of-group or unauthorised, plus a summary report naming each unauthorised or unnecessary extension, the devices carrying it and its removal owner

title.en: Remove the extensions the review found unauthorised and record the outcome per device

description.en: Work the summary report's removal list device by device and record what happened to each entry: the device, the extension, the date it was removed, who removed it, and confirmation from a re-read of that device that it is gone. Where an extension turned out to be genuinely needed, record the approval obtained instead and add it to the approved list rather than leaving it standing as an unresolved exception. A device that could not be reached within the period is carried forward with a named owner and a date rather than closed. Attach the removal record showing every entry resolved as removed, approved, or carried forward.

evidenceHint.en: Extension removal record showing per device and extension the removal date and operator with post-removal confirmation, plus any entry resolved by approval or carried forward with a named owner and date

controls.title: Output Delivery Management
controls.objective: Ensure the availability and delivery of outputs in a complete, accurate, and timely manner in accordance with specifications.
controls.successCriteria:
Outputs are distributed in line with defined specifications, including completeness, accuracy, and timeliness.
Outputs are protected against unauthorized access, corruption, or loss.
Distribution and access of outputs are restricted to intended recipients.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Collect specifications and requirements for outputs related to services and products.
Obtain records of output delivery, including storage and distribution logs.
Retrieve documentation of security measures for protecting outputs.

Analysis:
Compare output specifications with delivery records to verify completeness, accuracy, and timeliness.
Review security measures to ensure output protection during storage and delivery.
Analyze distribution records to confirm outputs are delivered only to intended parties.

Output:
Report comparing output specifications with actual delivery records.
Assessment of output protection measures.
Review summary of output distribution and access controls.

title.en: Catalogue every output the services and products deliver, with its recipients and delivery route

description.en: One row per output the entity produces for a customer or another party — report, file, feed, statement, extract — carrying what it contains, who is entitled to receive it, the route it travels to them (portal download, email, SFTP, API, post) and the system that generates it. Build it from what the systems actually emit rather than from the service catalogue, so an output that grew up outside the documented set appears rather than being assumed away. The recipient column is the one the distribution test reads, so an output addressed to a group must name the group and where its membership is maintained. Attach the catalogue; a row with a blank recipient or route is not done.

evidenceHint.en: Output catalogue listing every delivered output with its contents, entitled recipients or recipient group, delivery route and generating system

title.en: Record the completeness, accuracy and timeliness specification for each output

description.en: For every catalogued output, state what a correct delivery is: the records or sections it must contain to be complete, the checks that establish its values are accurate, and the deadline or frequency by which it must reach the recipient. Take each value from the stated requirement for that output and cite that requirement beside the specification, so the specification can be defended as the requirement rather than as an internal preference. Where no requirement has been stated for an output, record the specification as unset and name the owner who will agree one — the comparison test reports those rows as untestable rather than passing them. Attach the issued output specification.

evidenceHint.en: Output specification stating, per output, the completeness criteria, accuracy checks and delivery deadline or frequency, each citing the stated requirement it was taken from

title.en: Document the storage and transmission protection applied to each output

description.en: Record for every catalogued output how it is protected while it is held and while it is delivered: where generated copies are stored and who can reach them, the encryption or transport protection on the delivery route, the integrity check that would reveal corruption, and the measure that protects a stored copy against loss. Name the control actually in force per output rather than the platform standard, since an output emailed as an attachment and one collected from an authenticated portal are protected very differently. Security engineering assesses each row against the protection expected for the data it carries and flags the shortfalls. Attach the protection record with those flags and a named owner against each.

evidenceHint.en: Output protection record giving, per output, the storage location and its access restriction, the transport protection, the integrity check that would reveal corruption and the measure protecting a stored copy against loss, with shortfalls flagged and owned

text.en: Record where each generated output is stored and which accounts can reach it.
Record the transport protection in force on each delivery route in the catalogue.
Record the integrity check that would reveal an output corrupted in storage or transit.
Record what protects a stored copy against loss and how it would be restored.
Flag every output whose protection falls short of the data it carries and name an owner.

title.en: Log every output delivery with its dispatch time, recipient and completeness check

description.en: Each delivery is recorded with the output, the recipient it went to, the time it was dispatched and made available, the result of the completeness and accuracy checks that ran before dispatch, and any failure or retry. Where the route emits its own transfer log, export that rather than re-keying it, and record separately the deliveries made by hand, since a manual send is the one the export will not contain and the one most likely to reach the wrong party. A failed or missed delivery is logged as such with the recovery action taken. Attach the delivery and distribution log for the period under test.

evidenceHint.en: Output delivery and distribution log for the period showing, per delivery, the output, recipient, dispatch and availability time, pre-dispatch check result, and any failure with its recovery action

title.en: Test the period's delivery records against each output's specification

description.en: Take the catalogue row by row and read the delivery log for the period against the specification: was every scheduled delivery made, was each complete against the stated criteria, did the accuracy checks pass, and did it arrive inside the stated deadline. Count the deliveries that should have occurred from the schedule rather than from the log, because a delivery that never ran leaves no row to inspect and is the failure most easily missed. Produce the comparison report with a per-output verdict and, for each deviation, the recipient affected, the impact and the remediation owner. Attach the report with the log extracts it was built from.

evidenceHint.en: Comparison report of specification against actual delivery for every catalogued output, giving completeness, accuracy and timeliness verdicts and an owner plus remediation for each deviation

text.en: Derive the deliveries that should have occurred from each output's schedule.
Match the delivery log against that expected set and list the deliveries never made.
Check each completed delivery against the output's stated completeness criteria.
Check dispatch and availability times against the stated deadline or frequency.
Record a verdict per output and name an owner and remediation for each deviation.

title.en: Verify the distribution records show no output reaching a party outside its recipient list

description.en: Read the period's distribution and access records against the catalogue's entitled recipients and produce the exception list: deliveries addressed outside the entitled set, portal or share access by accounts not on it, and recipient-group memberships that have drifted from what the catalogue says. Check the group memberships themselves rather than only the delivery addresses, since a stale group is how an unentitled party keeps receiving an output that looks correctly addressed. Disposition every exception as authorised — naming the approval that covers it — or as an incident referred for investigation. Attach the access and distribution review with its dispositioned exception list.

evidenceHint.en: Distribution and access review for the period listing deliveries and accesses outside the entitled recipient set, drifted recipient-group memberships, and each exception dispositioned as authorised or referred

controls.title: Organizational Structure Compliance
controls.objective: To ensure that the organization's structures, reporting lines, authorities, and responsibilities are clearly established and documented
controls.successCriteria:
The organizational chart accurately reflects the entity's structures.
Reporting lines are clearly established and facilitate effective communication and execution of responsibilities.
Authorities and responsibilities are properly defined, assigned, and limited, with specific attention to security and compliance requirements.
Effective mechanisms are in place for interaction and monitoring of activities with external parties.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the organizational chart detailing all structures of the entity, including operating units, legal entities, and geographic distributions.
Acquire documentation of established reporting lines for each entity structure.
Gather records of delegated authorities and responsibilities at various levels of the organization, particularly relating to security, availability, processing integrity, confidentiality, and privacy.
Collect evidence of interactions and monitoring mechanisms with external parties relevant to the organizational structure.

Analysis:
Review the organizational chart to verify the clarity and comprehensiveness of the entity's structures.
Analyze the reporting lines documentation to confirm that they facilitate effective execution of authorities and responsibilities.
Examine the delegation records to ensure that roles, responsibilities, and segregation of duties are clearly defined and assigned as per the organizational needs.
Assess the documented interactions with external parties for completeness and relevance to the organizational structure and responsibilities.

Output:
A report detailing the findings from the organizational chart, reporting lines, delegated authorities, and external interactions analyses.

title.en: Document the organisational chart covering every operating unit, legal entity and geography

description.en: Produce a current chart that shows the whole entity rather than the head-office view: each operating unit, each legal entity, and the geographic locations the organisation operates from, with the relationships between them. Date it and name the person who prepared it, because the later verification reads it as a statement made on a particular day rather than as a standing truth. Where an entity is dormant, jointly held, or being wound up, mark it as such rather than omitting it — an entity missing from the chart carries responsibilities nobody has been assigned. Attach the chart together with the source the organisation treats as authoritative for its list of legal entities.

evidenceHint.en: Dated organisational chart showing every operating unit, legal entity and geographic location with the relationships between them, and the entity source it was reconciled against

title.en: Record the reporting line for every structure shown on the chart

description.en: For each unit and entity on the chart, document who it reports to, the role that reporting line runs through, the frequency and form of the reporting, and the decisions the receiving role is able to take on it. A line drawn on a chart is not a reporting line until the reporting it carries is described, and this control tests whether these lines actually let responsibilities be executed. Record dotted-line and matrix relationships explicitly, since those are where accountability is most often assumed rather than assigned. Attach the reporting line documentation covering every structure the chart shows.

evidenceHint.en: Reporting line documentation covering every structure on the chart, naming the receiving role, the frequency and form of reporting and the decisions that role can take, with matrix and dotted lines marked

title.en: Record the delegated authorities for security, availability, processing integrity, confidentiality and privacy

description.en: Build the delegation record the control asks for: for each of those five areas, at each level of the organisation, the role holding the authority, the named person in it, the limits on what they may decide alone, and the instrument that delegated it — a board resolution, a job description, a signed delegation of authority. Record the limit as well as the grant: an authority recorded with no boundary is precisely what the control means by an authority that is not properly limited. Where an area has no named holder at a level that needs one, record the gap rather than assigning it here. Attach the delegation records with the instruments behind them.

evidenceHint.en: Delegation records covering security, availability, processing integrity, confidentiality and privacy at each organisational level, naming role, holder, decision limits and the delegating instrument, with unfilled areas listed

text.en: Take each of the five areas the control names in turn.
Record the role and named person holding the authority at each level.
Record the limits on what each holder may decide without escalation.
Cite the resolution, job description or instrument that delegated it.
List the areas and levels where no holder is named as a gap to close.

title.en: Log the interactions and monitoring carried out with external parties

description.en: Record, for the period, the external parties whose activities fall inside the organisational structure's responsibilities — outsourced functions, service providers, joint arrangements — and against each one the interactions held and the monitoring performed: meetings, reports received, reviews conducted, and the internal role that owns the relationship. That internal owner is the field that ties the external party back to the chart, so a party with no named internal owner is the finding this log exists to surface. Attach the log with the reports and meeting records it references.

evidenceHint.en: External party interaction and monitoring log for the period listing each party, the interactions and monitoring performed with dates, the internal role owning the relationship, and any party with no named owner

title.en: Verify the chart and reporting lines against the entities and roles that actually exist

description.en: Test the chart rather than reading it: reconcile the entities it shows against the organisation's authoritative record of its legal entities, sample roles from it and confirm the named holder is in post and reports where the chart says they do, and check that each structure's reporting line has actually produced the reporting it describes over the period. Record each discrepancy — an entity absent from the chart, a vacant role shown as filled, a reporting line that produced nothing — with the accountable owner and the correction agreed. Attach the verification with the samples drawn and the register extract it was reconciled against.

evidenceHint.en: Chart and reporting line verification showing the entity reconciliation, the roles sampled with post-holder confirmation, the reporting actually produced, and each discrepancy with its owner and correction

title.en: Assess the delegations and external-party monitoring, and issue the findings report

description.en: Read the delegation records for incompatible duties resting on one role — approving and executing the same transaction, granting and reviewing the same access — and for authorities left with no holder or no stated limit, then read the external party log for parties monitored inconsistently or not at all. Draw those findings together with the chart and reporting line verification into the single report this control outputs, giving each finding an accountable owner and the correction agreed. Attach the issued report with the delegation records and external party log it draws on.

evidenceHint.en: Organisational structure findings report covering the chart, reporting lines, delegations and external-party monitoring, each finding carrying an accountable owner and the correction agreed

text.en: Pair each role against the duties it holds and mark incompatible pairs.
List authorities with no named holder or no stated decision limit.
Check each external party for monitoring actually performed in the period.
Give each finding an accountable owner and the correction agreed.

controls.title: Network Architecture Documentation Control
controls.objective: To ensure that the organization's network architecture diagrams and system documentation are accurately maintained, updated annually, and revised with significant enterprise changes to reflect the current network structure and connections.
controls.successCriteria:
The network architecture diagrams and system documentation are complete, up-to-date, and accurately reflect the current network structure and any significant changes.
Documentation has been reviewed and updated at least annually or after significant enterprise changes.
All modifications to the network are properly documented and integrated into the architecture diagrams and system documentation.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the latest network architecture diagrams and system documentation.
Collect evidence of the last update or review date of these documents.
Gather documentation of significant enterprise changes since the last update (e.g., major system overhauls, network expansions).

Analysis:
Verify that the network architecture diagrams and system documentation are comprehensive and reflect the current state of the network.
Confirm that these documents have been reviewed and updated at least annually.
Assess whether any significant enterprise changes have been properly documented and reflected in the latest versions of the network diagrams and documentation.

Output:
A report detailing the findings of the network architecture and system documentation review.
A list of discrepancies or outdated information found in the documents.
Recommendations for updates or revisions to the documentation, if necessary.

title.en: List the diagrams and system documents that make up the network documentation set

description.en: Name every artefact the control covers — architecture diagrams, connection and interface documents, address plans, system descriptions — with where each is stored, who owns it, and the date it was last reviewed or updated. Take the last-updated date from the document control record rather than a file timestamp that a copy operation can reset, because that single field is what the annual check depends on. Attach the documentation register with an owner and a date on every row.

evidenceHint.en: Network documentation register listing each diagram and system document with its storage location, owner and last review or update date taken from document control

title.en: Record which enterprise changes are significant enough to trigger a documentation revision

description.en: The control requires revision on significant enterprise change as well as annually, so write down what counts: the change types that force an update — major system overhauls, network expansions, new sites or connections, decommissioning — and for each, which documents in the register have to be revised and who raises it. Attach the trigger definition and show where the change process references it, so a qualifying change picks up the documentation step without anyone having to remember.

evidenceHint.en: Documentation revision trigger definition listing the qualifying change types, the documents each affects and the owner who raises the revision, with the change-process reference to it

title.en: Record each significant enterprise change against the documentation revision that followed it

description.en: Keep one row per qualifying change: what changed, when it went live, which documents were revised in response, the version each moved to and the date of that revision. The gap between the change date and the revision date is the number this record exists to expose, so both dates are recorded even — especially — when they are far apart. Changes still awaiting a revision stay open in the record with an owner rather than being left out of it. Attach the change-to-revision record for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Change-to-revision record for the period showing each significant enterprise change, its live date, the documents revised, their new versions and the revision date, with outstanding revisions left open

title.en: Walk the current network against the diagrams and record every discrepancy

description.en: Take the live network — the devices, links, third-party connections and cloud environments actually in place — and read the diagrams against it item by item. Record everything that does not match in three buckets: present in the network but absent from the documentation, present in the documentation but no longer in the network, and present in both but described wrongly. Each entry carries the document it belongs to and the correction needed, so the list doubles as the work order for the next revision. Attach the review findings report with the discrepancy list.

evidenceHint.en: Documentation review findings report with a discrepancy list classifying each item as undocumented, obsolete or wrongly described, naming the affected document and the correction required

text.en: Compare the device and link inventory against every diagram in the register.
Check external and third-party connections appear with their current endpoints.
Check cloud and remote-access environments are represented as they now stand.
Classify each mismatch as undocumented, obsolete or wrongly described.
Record the correction required and the document it belongs to for each entry.

title.en: Check every document in the register was reviewed within the last twelve months

description.en: Read the last review date on each register row against today and list the documents that have passed twelve months without one, together with those whose last revision predates a change the change-to-revision record shows as significant. Both are overdue for different reasons, and both go to the document owner with a date to complete. Attach the currency check showing every document, its last review date, its in-date or overdue status, and the owner and completion date agreed for each overdue item.

evidenceHint.en: Annual currency check listing every registered document with its last review date and an in-date or overdue status, and an owner plus completion date for each overdue document

controls.title: Secure Authentication Control
controls.objective: To ensure that secure authentication measures, including multi-factor authentication and robust log-on procedures, are effectively implemented and maintained across all critical information systems.
controls.successCriteria:
All high-risk and sensitive systems employ authentication methods in compliance with the Secure Authentication standards in the policy.
Log-on procedures across systems effectively protect against unauthorized access and minimize security risks.
Change requests related to authentication settings adhere to the policy and maintain or enhance the security posture.
Measures to protect against brute force attacks and unauthorized access are effectively in place and functioning as intended.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain a list of systems classified as high-risk or containing sensitive information, as identified in the Access Control Matrix.
Gather configuration details and screenshots of the authentication settings from each system.
Collect recent access logs, including successful and unsuccessful log-on attempts.
Acquire documentation on the implementation and management of authentication methods (e.g., multi-factor authentication, biometric data handling).
Retrieve change requests related to authentication settings since the last audit.

Analysis:
For each system, verify that the implemented authentication methods align with the requirements for secure authentication as outlined in the policy.
Examine access logs to ensure that multi-factor authentication is in use and that log-on procedures are minimizing unauthorized access.
Review the handling and invalidation processes for compromised biometric data.
Assess change requests to confirm that any modifications to authentication settings followed the established procedures and did not compromise security.
Check for evidence of measures against brute force attacks and proper handling of sensitive information during log-on.

Output:
Screenshots of system authentication settings.
A report detailing the comparison of current authentication settings against policy requirements.
An analysis spreadsheet of access logs, focusing on authentication success and failure patterns.
A summary of reviewed change requests with an assessment of adherence to the policy.

title.en: List the high-risk and sensitive systems and the authentication method each uses today

description.en: From the Access Control Matrix, extract the systems classified high-risk or holding sensitive information and record, per system, how users authenticate now: the identity source, whether a second factor is required and which factor types are accepted, and whether administrative access takes the same route as ordinary access. Record the observed state rather than the intended one — the gap between the two is what the later comparison reports, and a list built from intent hides it. Attach the system list with an authentication method recorded against every entry.

evidenceHint.en: List of high-risk and sensitive systems from the Access Control Matrix with the identity source, second-factor requirement, accepted factor types and administrative access route recorded per system

title.en: Record the required authentication methods, log-on procedure and lockout thresholds in the standard

description.en: Set out what each class of in-scope system must implement: the permitted authentication methods and accepted second-factor types, the log-on procedure rules — no system or application detail shown before authentication succeeds, no indication of which part of a credential was wrong, no echo of the credential itself — and the attempt limit, lockout duration and throttling that answer brute force. Where biometrics are used, state how templates are held and the route by which a compromised template is invalidated and the user re-enrolled; where they are not, record that as an explicit nil rather than leaving it silent.

evidenceHint.en: Issued secure authentication standard giving, per system class, permitted methods and factor types, the log-on procedure rules, attempt limit and lockout parameters, and the biometric handling and invalidation route or an explicit nil

text.en: State the permitted authentication methods and accepted second-factor types per system class.
Write the log-on procedure rules covering what may be displayed before authentication succeeds.
Set the failed-attempt limit, lockout duration and throttling that apply to each class.
State how biometric templates are stored and how a compromised template is invalidated.
State how the standard applies to administrative access routes on each system.

title.en: Apply the standard's second-factor and lockout settings to each in-scope system

description.en: Configure each system on the list to the values the standard sets, capturing the resulting settings screen or configuration export as you go — the capture is what makes the change evidenced rather than asserted. Systems that cannot enforce a required setting are recorded as deviations with a named owner and the remediation agreed, rather than being quietly left at their previous configuration. Attach the configuration screenshots or exports per system together with the deviation list.

evidenceHint.en: Per-system authentication configuration screenshots or exports showing the second-factor requirement and lockout parameters in force, plus the list of systems unable to enforce a required setting with their owner and remediation

title.en: Analyse the period's successful and failed log-on records for factor coverage and attack patterns

description.en: Take the access logs from the in-scope systems and produce the pattern analysis: how many successful sign-ins completed a second factor and how many did not, which accounts or source addresses generated repeated failures, and whether any lockout threshold fired. A sign-in that succeeded without a second factor is either a bypass route or a system not yet configured, and each one is followed up by name rather than counted. Attach the log analysis for the period with the follow-up items it produced.

evidenceHint.en: Access-log analysis spreadsheet for the period showing successful and failed log-on counts per system, sign-ins completed without a second factor, repeated-failure sources, lockouts fired and the follow-up raised per anomaly

text.en: Collect successful and failed log-on records from every in-scope system for the period.
Split the successful sign-ins by whether a second factor was completed.
List the accounts and source addresses generating repeated failures, and any lockouts fired.
Raise a named follow-up for each sign-in that succeeded without the required second factor.

title.en: Compare each system's live authentication settings against the standard

description.en: Read the settings actually in force on each in-scope system and set them beside the standard's values for its class, item by item — method, factor types, log-on display rules, attempt limit and lockout. Mark a pass or deviation per system and, for each deviation, record the observed value, the required value, the accountable owner and the remediation agreed. A system carrying an open deviation is counted as a deviation and not as a pass, so the report does not overstate coverage. Attach the comparison with the configuration captures it rests on.

evidenceHint.en: Comparison report listing every in-scope system with observed against required authentication settings, a pass or deviation verdict, and an owner plus remediation for each deviation

title.en: Verify each authentication change request in the period followed the change procedure

description.en: Take the change requests that altered authentication settings and read each against the procedure: the authoriser recorded against it, a stated reason, and a record of the setting before and after. Judge each change on whether it left the system at or above the standard — a change that relaxed a lockout threshold or dropped a factor requirement is the one this review exists to find, whether or not its paperwork was complete. Attach the summary with an adherence verdict and a posture assessment per change.

evidenceHint.en: Summary of authentication change requests for the period with authoriser, the setting before and after, an adherence verdict and an assessment of whether each change held or weakened the standard

controls.title: Information Transfer Security Control
controls.objective: To ensure that information transfer within and between the organization and external parties is secure, traceable, and complies with the organization's policies and standards.
controls.successCriteria:
All information transfers adhere to the organization's encryption, authentication, and classification standards.
Third-party transfer agreements are in full compliance with the organization's security policies.
No incidents of information transfer breaches or policy non-compliance are found.
Adequate remedial actions are in place for any identified non-compliance issues.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain a comprehensive list of all information transfer methods used within the organization (e.g., email, file transfer protocols, physical media transfer).
Collect records of information transfer agreements with third parties.
Gather documentation or logs related to recent information transfers, including encryption usage, transfer methods, and recipient authentication.
Acquire evidence of information classification and handling procedures for transferred data.

Analysis:
Review the list of information transfer methods against the company's approved transfer protocols to ensure compliance.
Examine third-party agreements to verify that they align with the company's information security standards.
Analyze transfer logs to check for adherence to encryption standards, proper recipient authentication, and correct information classification.
Inspect incident reports, if any, related to information transfer breaches or non-compliance.

Output:
A report detailing the compliance status of each information transfer method.
An assessment report of third-party transfer agreements.
A compliance matrix aligning transfer logs with company policies.
A summary of any incidents and remedial actions taken.

title.en: Inventory every method used to transfer information inside and outside the organisation

description.en: This control is tested against a comprehensive list of transfer methods, and compiling it is the task: email, managed and ad-hoc file transfer, collaboration and file-sharing services, APIs and system-to-system feeds, and physical media carried by hand or courier. Against each, record the owner, the classifications of information it carries, the parties at each end, and whether it is an approved method or one simply found in use. That last column is the one that matters — the methods people reached for because the approved route was inconvenient are exactly what the compliance assessment needs to see. Attach the register.

evidenceHint.en: Register of information transfer methods covering electronic, system-to-system and physical routes, each with its owner, the classifications carried, the parties at each end and an approved or found-in-use marking

title.en: Record the encryption, recipient-authentication and classification rules for each transfer method

description.en: Turn the organisation's transfer standards into a rule per method: the encryption required in transit and at rest at the far end, how the recipient's identity is established before information leaves, and how the transfer is labelled and handled for the classification it carries. State the highest classification each method may carry and name the alternative route for anything above it, so a sender has somewhere to go rather than only an instruction to stop. Where a method in the register cannot meet the rule for the data it currently carries, record that as a gap with a named owner. Attach the issued handling procedure.

evidenceHint.en: Issued information transfer handling procedure giving, per method, the encryption required, the recipient authentication required, the classification ceiling and the named alternative route above it

text.en: Set the encryption required in transit and at rest for each transfer method.
State how a recipient's identity is established before information is sent.
Set the highest classification each method is permitted to carry.
Name the alternative route for information above that ceiling.
Record any method that cannot meet its rule as a gap with a named owner.

title.en: Record the security terms of every third-party information transfer agreement

description.en: For each external party the register shows information moving to or from, pull the current agreement and set what it commits that party to beside the organisation's own transfer rules: the transfer methods it permits, the encryption it requires, how it requires a recipient to be authenticated, and how it requires transferred information to be classified and handled. Mark each term as meeting the organisation's standard, falling short of it, or silent — an agreement silent on a term is marked silent rather than compliant, and that flag list is the assessment output this control expects. Legal/DPO reads the wording. Attach the register with the contract extracts behind it.

evidenceHint.en: Third-party transfer agreement register giving, per party, the permitted methods and the encryption, recipient-authentication and classification terms the agreement carries, each marked as meeting, falling short of or silent on the organisation's standard, with the contract extracts behind it

title.en: Log each information transfer with its method, classification, encryption and recipient authentication

description.en: Keep the transfer record this control is tested against: per transfer, the method used, the classification of the information, whether it was encrypted and how, how the recipient was authenticated, the party at the far end and the date. Export what the transfer systems record themselves rather than re-keying it, and record physical media movements by hand in the same set, since they are the transfers with no system to export from and the ones a courier can lose. Attach the transfer log for the period under test.

evidenceHint.en: Information transfer log for the period, machine-exported where the method allows and hand-recorded for physical media, showing method, classification, encryption used, recipient authentication, counterparty and date per transfer

title.en: Record each information transfer incident and the remedial action taken

description.en: Where a transfer breaches the rules or information reaches somewhere it should not — a misdirected message, an unencrypted route used for classified data, media lost in transit — record the incident with the method involved, what was disclosed, how it was detected, the remedial action taken and the date it closed. Include near-misses stopped by a control, because they identify the routes under pressure before one gets through. Where the period contains no incidents, record the nil return and how it was established rather than leaving the set empty. Attach the incident record with its remedial actions.

evidenceHint.en: Information transfer incident record for the period showing the method involved, what was disclosed, the detection route, the remedial action and its closure date, or an evidenced nil return

title.en: Test sampled transfers against the encryption, authentication and classification rules

description.en: Draw a sample from the transfer log covering every method in the register, and check each sampled transfer against the rule that applies to its method: whether the required encryption was actually used, whether the recipient was authenticated the way the procedure states, and whether the classification labelling and handling were correct for the information sent. Build the result into a compliance matrix, one row per method, with a pass or fail per sampled transfer and, against each fail, the accountable owner and the remedial action agreed. Attach the matrix with the log extracts it was built from.

evidenceHint.en: Transfer compliance matrix covering every registered method, showing per sampled transfer whether the required encryption, recipient authentication and classification handling were applied, with an owner and remedial action against each fail

text.en: Draw the sample so that every method in the register is represented in it.
Check the encryption actually used against the rule for that method.
Check how the recipient was authenticated against the documented procedure.
Check the classification labelling and handling against the information sent.
Record a pass or fail per transfer with an owner and remedial action for each fail.

controls.title: Third-Party Privacy Compliance
controls.objective: To ensure third-party vendors and partners comply with privacy commitments and notify the entity in case of unauthorized disclosures.
controls.successCriteria:
All third-party agreements include required privacy commitments and compliance clauses.
Third parties demonstrate adherence to privacy standards through regular assessments.
Effective and timely reporting of unauthorized disclosures by third parties.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain and review third-party agreements focused on privacy and data handling.
Access records of third-party privacy compliance assessments.
Review incident logs related to unauthorized disclosures reported by third parties.

Analysis:
Assess third-party agreements for compliance clauses and privacy commitments.
Analyze the results of third-party compliance assessments to ensure adherence to privacy standards.
Review incident logs for timeliness and adequacy of third-party notifications on unauthorized disclosures.

Output:
A report summarizing third-party compliance with privacy commitments.
Analysis of third-party incident notification effectiveness.
Documentation of any non-compliance or deficiencies in third-party reporting.

title.en: Identify every third party that handles personal information on the entity's behalf

description.en: List each vendor and partner that receives, stores, processes or has access to personal information, with the categories of data involved, the purpose it is handled for, and the reference of the agreement in force. Build it from the systems and data flows rather than from the vendor spend list, so a partner with access granted informally appears rather than being absent by definition. Procurement supplies the agreement references; Legal/DPO confirms the data categories. Attach the register with an agreement reference or an explicit 'no agreement in force' marker on every row, because those markers are the first population the clause review acts on.

evidenceHint.en: Third-party register listing each vendor and partner handling personal information with the data categories, the purpose, and the agreement reference or an explicit no-agreement marker

title.en: Record the privacy commitment and disclosure-notification clauses present in each agreement

description.en: For every third party in the register, read the agreement in force and extract into a clause register what it actually commits them to: the privacy and data-handling obligations, the restriction on onward disclosure, the requirement to notify the entity of an unauthorised disclosure, and the term within which that notification must arrive. An agreement silent on any of these is recorded as silent rather than scored as compliant — that list of silences is the deliverable, and it is what the compliance report and any contract remediation are built from. Legal/DPO reads the clause wording. Attach the clause register with the agreement extracts behind it.

evidenceHint.en: Clause register giving, per third party, the privacy commitments, onward-disclosure restriction, breach-notification obligation and notification term, with the agreement extracts behind each and the silences listed

title.en: Assess each third party against its privacy commitments and record the result

description.en: Run the assessment each third party's agreement calls for — questionnaire, evidence review, or an audit report they supply — and record what was asked, what they returned, the date, and a verdict against each commitment in the clause register rather than a single overall score. An assertion accepted without supporting evidence is recorded as unevidenced, since this control asks that third parties demonstrate adherence and a returned questionnaire on its own does not. Where a third party did not respond, record the non-response and escalate it to the relationship owner. Attach the completed assessment records with the evidence each verdict rests on.

evidenceHint.en: Completed third-party privacy assessment records showing the date, what was requested, what was returned, a verdict against each registered commitment, and any non-response or unevidenced assertion

title.en: Log every unauthorised-disclosure notification received from a third party

description.en: When a third party reports an unauthorised disclosure, record it with the third party, what they said happened, the personal information and data subjects affected, the date the incident occurred, the date they became aware, the date they told the entity, and the entity's own response and onward notifications. The three dates are the load-bearing ones: the timeliness measure cannot be produced without them, so an entry missing them is incomplete rather than closed. Record near-miss and 'no impact' reports on the same log, since exclusion decisions belong in the record. Attach the third-party incident log for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Third-party unauthorised-disclosure log for the period showing per incident the third party, data and subjects affected, occurrence, awareness and notification dates, and the entity's response

title.en: Measure each third-party notification against the reporting term in its agreement

description.en: For every incident on the log, set the elapsed time from the third party becoming aware to the entity being told against the notification term the clause register records for that third party, and mark it inside or outside term. Assess the content too: whether what they sent identified the data and data subjects affected and was enough for the entity to meet its own notification obligations, or whether the entity had to go back for it. Where the agreement carries no notification term, the incident is measured against nothing and is reported as such, which is a contract finding rather than a vendor one. Attach the analysis with a remediation owner for each late or inadequate notification.

evidenceHint.en: Notification effectiveness analysis giving per incident the awareness-to-notification elapsed time against the contractual term, an in or out of term verdict, an adequacy assessment of the content, and an owner for each failure

title.en: Publish the third-party privacy compliance report naming each deficiency and its owner

description.en: Consolidate the clause register, the assessment results and the notification analysis into the report this control produces: per third party, whether the agreement carries the required commitments, whether adherence was demonstrated, and whether their incident reporting met the term. Carry the deficiencies forward explicitly — agreements missing clauses, assessments unevidenced or unreturned, notifications late or inadequate — each with a named owner and an agreed action, whether that is a contract amendment, a re-assessment or ending the relationship. Attach the issued report together with the clause register, assessment records and notification analysis it consolidates.

evidenceHint.en: Issued third-party privacy compliance report with a per-vendor status and the consolidated deficiency list, each deficiency carrying a named owner and an agreed action

controls.title: Software Installation Management
controls.objective: To ensure that all software installations on operational systems are authorized, documented, and compliant with the organization's security standards.
controls.successCriteria:
All software installations and updates on operational systems are accounted for in the IT Asset Inventory and have corresponding, approved change records.
Each software installation or update has been subjected to thorough testing as per the organization's standards.
The organization's process for software installation and updates is consistently followed, minimizing security risks.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain a list of all operational systems from the IT Asset Inventory.
Retrieve records of software installations and updates from the Change Management logs since the last audit.
Gather documentation of approval and testing procedures for each software installation or update.

Analysis:
For each recorded software installation or update, verify that it is listed in the IT Asset Inventory and has an associated change record.
Check each change record to confirm that the installation or update was approved by the Information Security Team or management.
Review the testing documentation for each software installation or update to ensure thorough testing in a controlled environment.

Output:
A comprehensive list of all software installations and updates with corresponding change records.
A report detailing the approval status for each software installation or update.
A summary of testing procedures and results for each software installation or update.

title.en: List the operational systems on which software may be installed

description.en: Extract from the IT asset inventory the operational systems in scope — the servers, workstations, appliances and platforms carrying production software — and record against each the owner, the environment it belongs to, and the mechanism by which software reaches it: a package repository, an image build, a deployment pipeline or manual installation. The installation mechanism matters because it determines where the record of an installation can be found, and a system whose mechanism is manual is the one where an unrecorded install is most likely to sit undetected. Attach the list with owner, environment and mechanism populated for every system.

evidenceHint.en: List of operational systems drawn from the IT asset inventory, each with its owner, its environment and the mechanism through which software is installed or updated on it

title.en: Set out the approval and controlled-environment testing required before software reaches production

description.en: Write down what has to happen before software is installed or updated on an operational system: who approves it — the information security team or management, per the organisation's standard — what the request must state, what testing must be performed in a controlled environment that mirrors production, and what test evidence is retained.
