State where the approval and the test evidence are filed against the change record, because the reconciliation has to find both without reconstructing them from memory. Attach the issued procedure.

evidenceHint.en: Issued software installation procedure naming the approver for an installation or update, the controlled-environment testing required, the test evidence retained, and where the approval and that evidence are filed against the change record

title.en: Test each software installation or update in a controlled environment before it is released

description.en: Before software goes onto an operational system, install it in the controlled environment and record what was tested and what happened: the version tested, the environment used and how it differs from production, the functional and security checks performed, the result of each, and any issue found together with its resolution or the decision to accept it. Keep the test output itself rather than a statement that testing occurred, since that statement is what the review would otherwise have to take on trust. Attach the testing documentation for each installation and update in the period.

evidenceHint.en: Testing documentation per software installation or update, giving the version tested, the controlled environment used and its differences from production, the checks performed with their results, and the issues found with their resolution

title.en: Record each installation and update in the asset inventory with its change record and approver

description.en: When software is installed or updated on an operational system, update that system's entry in the IT asset inventory with the product and the version now running, and link the change record that authorised it together with the name of the approver. The inventory and the change record have to agree, because the reconciliation reads them against each other and against the system itself, and a disagreement between them is indistinguishable from an unauthorised install. An installation made without an approved change record is recorded as exactly that rather than back-filled quietly, because it is the exception the reconciliation exists to surface. Attach the inventory extract covering the period's installations.

evidenceHint.en: IT asset inventory extract for the period showing each software installation and update, the version now running, the linked change record and the named approver

title.en: Reconcile the software running on each operational system against the change records

description.en: Read the software actually present on each operational system and compare it against the inventory and the change records for the period, in both directions. Software running with no change record is an unauthorised installation; a change record with no matching software is a change that did not land, or was reversed without being recorded. For each installation reconciled, record whether the required approval is present and who gave it, and whether the controlled-environment test evidence exists. Report the exceptions with an owner and a remediation — removal, retrospective approval or investigation. Attach the reconciliation with the approval and testing status per installation.

evidenceHint.en: Reconciliation of installed software against the IT asset inventory and the change records, listing each installation with its approval status, approver and test evidence, and every unauthorised or unmatched item with an owner and remediation

text.en: Collect the software actually installed on each operational system in scope.
Match each installed product and version against the IT asset inventory entry for that system.
Match each installation against the change record that should have authorised it.
Record the approver and the controlled-environment test evidence for each matched installation.
List software with no change record, and change records with no matching software, as exceptions with owners.

controls.title: Competence Management
controls.objective: To ensure that all personnel involved in business continuity activities possess the necessary competence, through appropriate education, training, and experience, and to document and evaluate the effectiveness of these competencies.
controls.successCriteria:
All employees in business continuity roles meet the documented competence requirements.
There is documented evidence of effective training, mentoring, or other actions taken to address any competence gaps.
All competence-related documentation is complete, up-to-date, and accurately reflects the current competence levels of employees.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence

Competence Requirements Documentation

Obtain the documented competence requirements for each role involved in business continuity.
Get a list of current employees and their roles related to business continuity.
Education, Training, and Experience Records

Collect records of education, training, and experience for each employee in business continuity roles.
Gather evidence of any additional training or mentoring provided to employees to meet competence requirements.
Evaluation of Competence Actions

Obtain documented evaluations of the effectiveness of training and other actions taken to ensure competence.

Analysis

Comparison Against Requirements

Compare the documented competence requirements for each role against the actual qualifications (education, training, experience) of employees in those roles.
Identify any gaps between required and actual competence levels.
Review of Training and Development Actions

Assess the actions taken to acquire necessary competence (e.g., training programs, mentoring) and their documented effectiveness evaluations.
Verify that all actions are appropriately documented and that there is evidence of periodic evaluations.

Output

A report summarizing the comparison of competence requirements vs. actual qualifications for each employee.
A spreadsheet detailing training and development actions taken, along with their effectiveness evaluations.
Screenshots or documents evidencing the competence records and evaluations.

title.en: List the business continuity roles whose competence must be evidenced, with their current holders

description.en: Produce the roster the rest of this control runs against: one row per role carrying a business continuity responsibility — incident lead, recovery team member, communications, damage assessment, plan owner — naming the person who holds it today and their department. Include deputies and alternates, because a competence gap in the person who actually stands in during a disruption is the same gap. Take the role list from the documented business continuity responsibilities and the holders from HR records rather than from a distribution list, so a vacant role appears as a vacancy instead of being absent from the population. Attach the roster with its compilation date; a role with no named holder is a finding to carry, not a row to delete.

evidenceHint.en: Dated roster of business continuity roles naming the current holder and any deputy against each role, with vacancies shown explicitly

title.en: Define the education, training and experience each business continuity role requires

description.en: Against each role on the roster write down what competence it demands, split into the three things this control is tested on: the education or qualification expected, the training that must have been completed, and the practical experience required — exercises led, incidents worked, time in the discipline. Write them so that a third party could decide from the record alone whether a given person meets the requirement, because 'suitable experience' cannot be compared against anything. Where a deputy's requirement differs from the principal's, state it separately. Attach the issued competence requirements document covering every role on the roster, with none left blank.

evidenceHint.en: Issued competence requirements document giving, per business continuity role, the required education, the required training and the required practical experience

text.en: Work down the roster so that every role, deputy roles included, receives a requirement.
State the education or qualification the role expects, or record explicitly that none is required.
Name the courses or internal sessions the role holder must have completed.
Express the practical experience as something checkable rather than as a judgement of suitability.

title.en: Collect and file the education, training and experience record for each role holder

description.en: For every person on the roster, gather and file the evidence of what they have actually done: certificates and qualification records, dated attendance records for the training they have completed, and a record of the exercises and real incidents they have taken part in and in what capacity. Refresh the file when someone completes new training or works an incident, so it reflects competence today rather than competence on the day the role was assigned. Where an item cannot be evidenced, record it as unevidenced rather than assumed — an assumed qualification is exactly what the comparison is meant to expose. Attach the competence record set covering the roster.

evidenceHint.en: Competence record per role holder holding qualification certificates, dated training attendance records, and the exercises and incidents the person took part in

title.en: Record the training or mentoring delivered to close each competence gap

description.en: Where a role holder is short of their role's requirement, record the action taken to close it — a course booked and completed, a mentoring arrangement with a named mentor and its cadence, a shadowing assignment on an exercise — naming the gap it targets, the date it started and the date it completed. An action still running is recorded as open with its expected completion date rather than omitted, because the open list is what shows the gap is being worked rather than noted. Attach the training and development action log with the completion evidence filed against each closed action.

evidenceHint.en: Training and development action log naming, per action, the competence gap it targets, the person, the course or mentor, the start date and the completion evidence

title.en: Assess each role holder's qualifications against their role's requirements and list the gaps

description.en: Set the competence record for each person on the roster beside the requirement written for their role and mark each of the three dimensions — education, training, experience — met or not met, naming in the cell the specific record that satisfies it. The output is a report at person level rather than a headline percentage, because the control is tested on whether each individual meets their own role's requirement. Every 'not met' becomes a gap carried into the action log with a named owner. Attach the comparison report; a row marked met with no supporting record named is not evidence of competence.

evidenceHint.en: Competence comparison report, one row per role holder, showing education, training and experience each marked met or not met, the record satisfying each, and the resulting gap list

text.en: Set each person's filed record beside the requirement written for the role they hold.
Mark education, training and experience separately as met or not met for that person.
Name the certificate, attendance record or exercise that satisfies each met mark.
Carry every not-met mark into the action log with a named owner against it.

title.en: Evaluate whether each competence action actually delivered the competence it targeted

description.en: Completing a course is not evidence that competence was acquired, and this control is explicit that the effectiveness of the actions taken must itself be evaluated. For each completed action in the log, record how effectiveness was judged — an assessment result, performance observed in an exercise or a real activation, a supervisor's structured sign-off — the date that judgement was made, and whether the gap is now closed or still open. Where an action was judged ineffective, record the follow-on action rather than closing the gap. Attach the evaluation spreadsheet covering every completed action, so the periodic evaluation of effectiveness can be evidenced rather than asserted.

evidenceHint.en: Effectiveness evaluation spreadsheet covering each completed competence action, naming how effectiveness was judged, the date judged, and whether the gap is now closed

controls.title: ICS/OT Security Management
controls.objective: To ensure robust security measures are in place for the protection and management of Industrial Control Systems and Operational Technology, addressing network segmentation, monitoring, system isolation, external media restrictions, mobile device connections, system hardening, and vulnerability and patch management.
controls.successCriteria:
Network segmentation and isolation are as per the best practices and company policies.
Continuous monitoring and event logging are effectively implemented and operational.
External storage media and mobile device usage are strictly controlled and monitored.
Systems are regularly reviewed, securely configured, and hardened against vulnerabilities.
Vulnerability and patch management processes are comprehensive, up-to-date, and effective.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the network architecture diagrams detailing ICS/OT and corporate networks.
Collect configuration files and settings for network segmentation and isolation measures.
Gather logs for continuous monitoring systems in ICS/OT environments.
Secure lists of approved external storage media and mobile devices, along with their usage logs.
Acquire documentation on periodic reviews, system hardening, and secure configuration processes.
Retrieve current vulnerability and patch management reports specific to ICS/OT.

Analysis:
Review network diagrams to validate physical and virtual segmentation and isolation of SIS.
Examine configuration files to verify implementation of network segmentation and isolation controls.
Analyze monitoring logs to assess continuous monitoring and event logging effectiveness.
Cross-check lists of external storage media and mobile devices against actual usage logs.
Evaluate documentation on system reviews, hardening, and secure configurations for completeness and adherence to best practices.
Assess vulnerability and patch management reports for comprehensiveness and timeliness.

Output:
Compiled network architecture diagrams.
Configuration files and settings documentation.
Monitoring system logs.
Lists and logs of external storage media and mobile device usage.
System review, hardening, and configuration documentation.
Vulnerability and patch management reports.

title.en: Diagram every crossing point between the ICS/OT network and the corporate network

description.en: Walk the plant network at each site in scope with the OT engineer who runs it and draw, for every ICS/OT segment, the firewalls, ACL'd switches, data diodes, jump hosts, wireless links and remote-access paths that cross into the corporate network — and show the safety instrumented system on its own segment with the physical or virtual means that isolates it from both the process control network and corporate IT. Name the enforcing device at each crossing rather than drawing an unlabelled line. Attach the diagram set covering every site in scope, each sheet dated, version-labelled and carrying the name of whoever walked the network with you.

evidenceHint.en: Dated, version-labelled ICS/OT network architecture diagram set covering every site in scope, showing each corporate-network crossing and the SIS isolation

text.en: List every site that operates an ICS/OT network in scope.
Trace each cabled, VLAN and wireless path that crosses into corporate IT.
Label the enforcing device at each crossing: firewall, diode or jump host.
Draw the safety instrumented system on its own segment and state how it is isolated.
Version and date each sheet and record who walked the plant network with you.

title.en: Export the configuration of every device enforcing an ICS/OT segmentation boundary

description.en: For each crossing point on the architecture diagram, export the running configuration that enforces it — firewall rule base, switch ACLs, VLAN and port assignments, data-diode direction setting, remote-access broker policy — and index each export to the crossing it belongs to, so a reviewer can move from a line on the diagram to the rule that implements it. List separately every rule that permits traffic inbound to the ICS/OT network, so the isolation the diagram claims can be tested against the rule base rather than taken on trust. Attach the exports carrying device identity, software version and capture date.

evidenceHint.en: Configuration exports for each boundary-enforcing device, dated and indexed to its crossing point on the diagram, with the inbound-permitting rules listed separately

title.en: Record the hardened build standard for each ICS/OT system type

description.en: Write down, per system type in the estate (engineering workstation, HMI, historian, controller/PLC, SIS engineering station), the settings that constitute its secure build: services and ports left enabled, local and shared accounts, removable-media handling, and the permitted remote-access method. Draft the removable-media and remote-access positions together with Security engineering, who hold the media and device controls elsewhere in this control. Where the control-system vendor's supported configuration forbids a hardening setting, record the vendor statement and the measure standing in its place — that constraint is the part of this standard a tester will probe. Attach the standard versioned, listing the assets each system type covers.

evidenceHint.en: Versioned secure configuration and hardening standard per ICS/OT system type, with vendor constraints and substitute measures recorded

text.en: List the ICS/OT system types in the estate and the vendor behind each.
Record enabled services, ports and accounts for each system type.
State how removable media and remote access are handled on that type.
Capture in writing the vendor's supported-configuration constraints.
Record the substitute measure wherever a setting cannot be applied.

title.en: Produce the period's ICS/OT monitoring and event log extract

description.en: Pull the reporting period's events from the ICS/OT monitoring systems and present them asset by asset, so the extract shows which assets sent events and which sent none — a silent asset is the finding here, not the absence of alerts. Where the monitoring system records alert handling, carry the alerts raised and how each was closed out into the same extract. Name the source monitoring systems and the exact date range covered, and state for any asset shown on the architecture diagram but missing from the extract why it is not monitored.

evidenceHint.en: ICS/OT monitoring log extract for the period with per-asset event counts, zero-event and unmonitored assets identified, and alert outcomes where the system records them

title.en: Issue the ICS/OT vulnerability and patch status report for the cycle

description.en: Report per ICS/OT asset the open vulnerabilities, the patches applied in this cycle and the maintenance window used, and every patch deferred with its reason (vendor approval outstanding, no maintenance window, unsupported by the control-system vendor) and the measure holding the risk until it lands. Draw the findings from ICS/OT-specific scanning and control-system vendor advisory feeds rather than the corporate IT report; Engineering lead owns the maintenance windows the report cites. State the date the data was taken and the asset population covered, and attach the report as issued.

evidenceHint.en: ICS/OT vulnerability and patch management report for the cycle, listing per-asset findings, patches applied with their windows, and deferred patches with reasons and holding measures

text.en: Collect vendor advisories and scan results covering ICS/OT assets.
Match every finding to an asset and its system type.
Record the patches applied this cycle and the maintenance window used.
Record each deferred patch with its reason and holding measure.

title.en: Cross-check the approved media and mobile device list against the ICS/OT connection logs

description.en: Take the period's connection and usage logs and test every removable-media and mobile-device connection to an ICS/OT asset against the approved list: each should resolve to an approved device and an authorised holder. Record the connections that match no approved entry, and the approved devices that never appear — those are the candidates for removal from the list — then record the explanation obtained and the outcome for each unmatched connection. Attach the reconciliation showing the count on both sides, every exception, and its disposition.

evidenceHint.en: Reconciliation of the approved external storage media and mobile device list against the period's ICS/OT connection logs, with counts on both sides and every exception and its disposition

controls.title: Cryptography Management and Key Control
controls.objective: To ensure effective use of cryptography in protecting sensitive information, and to manage cryptographic keys securely and in accordance with organizational policies and regulatory requirements.
controls.successCriteria:
Cryptographic practices and key management procedures are fully compliant with the organization’s policy.
All cryptographic keys are managed securely and effectively, with proper logs and records maintained.
Agreements with external suppliers meet organizational and regulatory requirements.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the organization’s policy document on cryptography use and key management.
Retrieve a list of all cryptographic systems and applications in use.
Gather documentation on cryptographic key generation, distribution, and management processes.
Collect logs and records of key management activities, including generation, distribution, change, revocation, and destruction of keys.
Acquire service level agreements or contracts with external suppliers of cryptographic services, if any.

Analysis:
Review the policy document to ensure it covers all aspects of cryptography use and key management, including types and strength of algorithms, key generation, protection, recovery, and legal aspects.
For each cryptographic system and application, verify that the cryptographic practices align with the policy.
Examine key management processes to validate that they adhere to the policy and industry best practices.
Analyze logs and records to confirm proper tracking and handling of key management activities.
Assess agreements with external suppliers to ensure they address liability, reliability, and response times.

Output:
A report on the compliance of the cryptographic systems and practices with the organization’s policy.
A detailed analysis of key management processes and activities.
An evaluation of external supplier agreements.

title.en: Inventory every system, application and supplier that uses cryptography

description.en: The auditor's first request is a list of all cryptographic systems and applications in use, and this inventory is the denominator every later task counts against — the policy has to address each row, and the reconciliation reads each row's live configuration. Build it from what is actually running rather than from an architecture diagram or a procurement list. The in-house/supplier custody column is not decoration: it is what produces the population for the supplier register, so a blank there blocks a later task. Attach the inventory carrying the date it was compiled; if no external party holds key material, record that as an explicit nil rather than leaving the column empty.

evidenceHint.en: Dated inventory of cryptographic systems and applications, one row per system, with purpose, owner and an in-house or supplier key-custody value populated for every row

text.en: Enumerate cryptographic use from certificate inventories, disk and database encryption settings, backup tooling, code-signing and VPN/SSH configuration.
Add every third-party service that encrypts, signs or holds key material on the organisation's behalf.
Record the system owner and the purpose the cryptography serves — confidentiality in transit, at rest, signing or authentication.
Mark every row in-house or supplier-held so the supplier register and the key procedure inherit a complete population.
Date the inventory and hold it as the baseline the policy and the reconciliation are both read against.

title.en: Set the approved algorithms, minimum key strengths and legal constraints in the cryptography policy

description.en: The policy is the yardstick every later task is measured against, so it has to name values rather than principles: which algorithms and modes are permitted, the minimum key length for each, and the legal aspects that apply — export restrictions, the jurisdictions in which key material may be held, and any lawful-access obligation. Work down the inventory so no use in scope is left unaddressed, and state explicitly where an algorithm is permitted only for legacy interoperability, since that is where the reconciliation will otherwise report a deviation every cycle. Legal/DPO supplies the legal text; Security engineering owns the issued document. Attach the issued policy version showing the algorithm and minimum-key-length table and the legal section.

evidenceHint.en: Issued cryptography policy version containing the approved-algorithm and minimum-key-length table and the legal-aspects section

title.en: Document generation, distribution, recovery and destruction for each key type

description.en: Separate from the policy, produce the operating document an operator can follow at the keyboard — the key generation, distribution and management processes an auditor asks for as their own artifact. Cover every distinct key type the inventory implies rather than describing one exemplar key, and read each type's stated generation and protection back against the policy's algorithm and minimum-key-length table so the two documents cannot disagree with each other. Attach the issued procedure with the key-type table filled in end to end and no cell left as 'to be determined'.

evidenceHint.en: Issued key management procedure with a completed row per key type covering generation, custody, distribution, recovery and destruction

text.en: List the distinct key types in use across the inventory — TLS, data-at-rest, signing, transport, tokenisation.
For each key type name the generation method and the module or keystore that holds the material.
Record who is authorised to operate each key type and the route the material travels to reach the systems using it.
Record the recovery or escrow arrangement that applies when the custodian is unavailable, and the destruction method.
Check every row's algorithm and key length against the policy table and correct whichever of the two documents is wrong.

title.en: Record the liability, reliability and response-time terms of each cryptographic supplier agreement

description.en: For every external supplier of cryptographic services the inventory names, pull the current contract or service level agreement and extract three things into a register: the liability position if key material is lost or exposed, the reliability or availability commitment for the key service, and the committed response time to a key compromise or revocation request. An agreement silent on any of the three is flagged as silent rather than scored — that flag list is the finding this task produces. Legal/DPO reads the liability wording. Where the inventory names no external custodian, record the nil return against it and attach that. Attach the register with the contract or SLA extracts it was built from.

evidenceHint.en: Cryptographic supplier register giving liability, reliability and response-time terms per supplier, the contract or SLA extracts behind them, and the list of agreements silent on any of the three

title.en: Log every key generation, distribution, change, revocation and destruction

description.en: Each time a key is generated, distributed, changed, revoked or destroyed, write a record carrying the key identifier, the activity type, the system it serves, who requested it, who performed it and the date. Where a keystore or HSM emits its own audit trail, export that rather than re-keying it by hand, and cover separately the manual steps that leave no machine trace — a ceremony done offline is exactly the event the export will not contain. This record set is what demonstrates the procedure is being followed rather than merely written. Attach the key management activity log for the period under test.

evidenceHint.en: Key management activity log or keystore/HSM audit export for the period, showing key identifier, activity, requester, operator and date per event

title.en: Reconcile each system's live cryptographic configuration against the policy

description.en: Take the inventory row by row and read the cryptographic configuration actually in force from the system itself rather than from its documentation — documentation that agrees with the policy while the system does not is precisely the failure this task exists to catch. Compare what each system reports against the approved values in the policy and produce the compliance report the control calls for, carrying a pass or deviation verdict per system and, for every deviation, the accountable owner and the remediation they have agreed. Attach the report together with the raw configuration output it was derived from.

evidenceHint.en: Cryptography compliance report listing every inventoried system with its observed algorithm, key length and mode, a pass or deviation verdict, and an owner plus remediation for each deviation

text.en: Pull the algorithm, key length and mode each inventoried system is actually running.
Compare every observed value against the approved algorithms and minimum key lengths in the policy.
Record each deviation with the affected system, the observed value and the accountable owner.
Agree a remediation per deviation and carry the unresolved ones into the report's conclusion.

controls.title: Business Continuity Plan Documentation and Maintenance
controls.objective: Ensure that the organization has comprehensive, documented, and maintained business continuity plans to guide response and recovery during disruptions.
controls.successCriteria:
All business continuity plans are documented, up-to-date, and include the required elements specified in section 8.4.4.
Plans are reviewed and updated regularly, with documented evidence of the review process.
Roles and responsibilities for BCP implementation are clearly defined and assigned.
BCP activation criteria and procedures are clearly outlined and followed.
Feedback from drills and incidents is incorporated into the BCPs, demonstrating continuous improvement.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:

Obtain the latest version of the business continuity plans (BCPs).
Collect records of the last BCP review and update process.
Retrieve a list of team members responsible for BCP implementation.
Gather communication logs regarding BCP activations and updates.
Collect any feedback or review documents from recent BCP drills or actual incidents.

Analysis:

Review Documentation:

Verify that the BCPs cover all required elements as specified in section 8.4.4 of the standard.
Check that the plans are updated regularly and reflect the latest organizational changes.
Ensure that the plans include clear guidance and information for teams to respond to disruptions.
Review Updates and Reviews:

Ensure that the review and update process of the BCPs follows a predefined schedule and procedure.
Verify that updates consider feedback from drills and actual incidents.
Verify Team Responsibilities:

Confirm that roles and responsibilities for BCP implementation are clearly defined and assigned.
Check if the team members are aware of their roles and have access to the BCPs when needed.
Evaluate Communication and Activation:

Verify the existence of clear activation criteria and procedures.
Review communication logs to ensure that the BCPs were activated according to predefined thresholds.
Assess Drill and Incident Feedback:

Analyze feedback from recent BCP drills or actual incidents to identify areas for improvement.
Ensure that identified improvements have been incorporated into the BCPs.

Output:

Comprehensive review report of the business continuity plans.
Spreadsheet comparing BCP elements with standard requirements.
Records of plan updates and reviews.
List of team members with assigned roles and responsibilities.
Communication logs and feedback analysis from drills and incidents.

title.en: Register every business continuity plan in force with its owner, version and last review date

description.en: Produce one row per business continuity plan the organisation relies on, naming the plan owner, the current version and its issue date, the date it was last reviewed, the interval at which review is due, and the disruption scenarios or business activities it covers. Draw the list from the continuity programme rather than from a document store's folder listing, so a plan held locally by a team appears as a row. This register is the population the element checklist scores and the review schedule is measured against — a plan absent from it is a plan nobody reviews. Attach the register with its compilation date and the location of each plan's current version.

evidenceHint.en: Business continuity plan register listing each plan with its owner, current version and issue date, last review date, review interval, and the scenarios or activities it covers

title.en: Define the activation criteria, thresholds and stand-down procedure in each plan

description.en: Each plan states what has to be true before it is invoked and who invokes it: the thresholds — outage duration, sites or people affected, service impact — that trigger consideration, the person with authority to declare activation, and the steps that follow the declaration, including who is told and through which channel. Written this way, the communication log can later be read against the thresholds to show whether plans were activated when they should have been, rather than taken on trust. Where a plan leaves a threshold to judgement, say whose judgement it is, because an activation criterion nobody owns is the one found afterwards never to have been applied. Attach the plan versions showing the activation section complete.

evidenceHint.en: Plan versions carrying an activation section with the thresholds, the person authorised to declare activation, and the notification steps that follow the declaration

title.en: Assign the plan implementation roles by name and confirm each holder can reach the plan

description.en: Name a person against every responsibility the plans allocate — team lead, deputy, communications, site liaison — rather than a job title alone, and record a deputy for each so that one absence does not stall a response. Then confirm each named person can actually obtain the current plan when they need it, including when the corporate network is unavailable, and record how: an offline copy held at home, a printed copy at the site, an access grant to the document store. Take back their dated acknowledgement that they understand the role. Attach the role assignment list showing the holder, the deputy, the acknowledgement and the access route for each responsibility.

evidenceHint.en: Plan implementation role list naming the holder and deputy for each responsibility, with each person's dated acknowledgement and the route by which they can reach the current plan offline

text.en: Name a person and a deputy against every responsibility the plans allocate.
Record how each person obtains the current plan when the corporate network is unavailable.
Take back a dated acknowledgement from each person that they understand the role.
Record the gaps where a responsibility has no named holder or no reachable copy of the plan.

title.en: Log every plan activation and plan-update communication as it is issued

description.en: Keep one log of the communications this control is tested on: each time a plan is activated, and each time an updated plan is issued to the teams. Record the date and time, what was sent, who sent it, who received it and by which channel, and keep the message itself — the email, the memo, the intranet post — with the entry. For an activation, record the threshold that was met, so the log can be read against the plan's own activation criteria and a plan invoked outside its thresholds, or not invoked when they were met, becomes visible. Attach the communication log for the period with the retained messages.

evidenceHint.en: Communication log covering plan activations and plan reissues, each entry naming the date, sender, recipients, channel and threshold met, with the message retained

title.en: Record the feedback from each drill and incident and the plan change it produced

description.en: After every drill and every real activation, capture the feedback while it is fresh: what the plan said, what actually happened, what was missing or wrong, and what the participants recommend. Turn each recommendation into an entry carrying an accept or reject decision with its reason, a named owner, and — where accepted — the plan section it changes and the plan version in which that change appeared. An improvement accepted but never traced to a plan version is the failure mode this task exists to catch, and it is what makes continuous improvement demonstrable rather than claimed. Attach the feedback records with the change entries they produced.

evidenceHint.en: Drill and incident feedback records, each recommendation carrying an accept or reject decision, an owner, and the plan section and version the accepted change landed in

title.en: Assess each plan against the clause 8.4.4 element checklist at its scheduled review

description.en: Build the checklist by taking the elements clause 8.4.4 requires straight from the standard, one column per element, then score every registered plan row by row: present, partially present or absent, citing the section reference wherever present. Read the plan against the organisation as it stands today in the same pass — the sites, systems, suppliers and people it names — so that a plan complete against the checklist but describing a structure that no longer exists is still found. Record the review date, the reviewer and the plan version the review produced, and give every absent or partial element an owner and a date. Attach the completed comparison spreadsheet with the review record.

evidenceHint.en: Element-by-element comparison spreadsheet scoring each registered plan against the clause 8.4.4 requirements, with the review date, the reviewer, and an owner against every gap

text.en: Derive the checklist columns from the elements clause 8.4.4 itself requires.
Score each registered plan element by element, citing the section reference where present.
Check that the sites, systems, suppliers and people named still match the organisation today.
Record the review date, the reviewer, and the plan version the review produced.
Give every absent or partial element a named owner and a date to close it.

controls.title: Security Event Reporting Control
controls.objective: Ensure timely and accurate reporting of information security events by personnel.
controls.successCriteria:
All information security events are reported in accordance with the defined timelines in the Incident Management Policy.
Complete alignment between reported security events and communication logs or emails.
Incident Management Policy and procedures are effectively guiding and aligning with the actual reporting practices.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Collect records of reported information security events from the designated reporting system or tool.
Obtain communication logs or emails related to the reporting of information security events.
Gather the Incident Management Policy and procedures documentation.

Analysis:
Review the records of reported security events to verify they were reported in a timely manner as defined by the Incident Management Policy.
Cross-reference communication logs or emails with the records to confirm the completeness of reported events.
Assess the Incident Management Policy and procedures to ensure they align with the actual reporting practice.

Output:
A detailed report summarizing the findings from the security events records.
A comparison matrix of reported events versus communication logs to identify any discrepancies.
An assessment report of the Incident Management Policy and procedures.

title.en: Document the designated reporting channel and the deadline that applies to each event type

description.en: State, in the incident management procedure, which tool or channel personnel use to report an information security event, and what the reporting deadline is for each type of event the policy distinguishes. This control is tested by comparing report times against defined timelines, so a procedure asking for prompt reporting without stating a period leaves nothing to test against and every event passes by default. Where the deadline differs by severity or event type, tabulate it rather than describing it in prose. Attach the issued procedure extract showing the channel and the deadline table.

evidenceHint.en: Issued reporting procedure extract naming the designated reporting tool or channel and the reporting timelines the Incident Management Policy defines, tabulated per event type or severity

title.en: Record every reported security event with its detection time, report time and reporter

description.en: Capture each event reported by personnel in the designated reporting system with the time it was detected or noticed, the time it was reported, who reported it, and what was reported. Detection time is the field most often omitted and the one the timeliness test depends on entirely — without it the interval cannot be computed and the record proves only that something was reported eventually. Where an event first surfaced in a conversation or an email and was entered into the system later, record both times so the delay is visible rather than absorbed. Attach the export of reported events for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Export of reported information security events for the period showing per event the reporter, the detection time, the report time and the description given

title.en: Test each reported event's report time against the deadline the procedure sets

description.en: Compute, for every event in the period's export, the interval between detection and report, and compare it against the deadline its event type carries. Mark each event on time or late, and for every late event record the reason given and the owner who follows it up — a pattern of late reports concentrated in one team or one event type is the real finding and it is invisible unless lateness is attributed. Report the on-time proportion for the period alongside the individual results so the trend is readable at the next test. Attach the timeliness report.

evidenceHint.en: Reporting timeliness report listing every event in the period with its detection-to-report interval, the applicable deadline, an on-time or late verdict, and a reason and owner recorded for each late event

title.en: Build the matrix comparing communication logs and emails against the reporting system's records

description.en: Timeliness is only half the test: an event discussed in an email or a chat channel and never entered in the reporting system does not appear in the export at all, and no analysis of the export can find it. Search the period's communication records for discussion of security events and match each one to a record in the reporting system. The unmatched entries are the under-reporting this task exists to surface. Record each with the date it was discussed, who discussed it, and whether it was subsequently reported or remains unreported. Attach the comparison matrix identifying both sources.

evidenceHint.en: Comparison matrix of security events found in communication logs and emails against the reporting system records, listing every discussed event with no corresponding report and its current state

text.en: Search the period's communication logs and mailboxes for discussion of security events.
Match each discussed event to a record in the designated reporting system.
List the events discussed in communications that have no corresponding report record.
Record for each unmatched event whether it was later reported or remains unreported.

title.en: Assess the reporting procedure against the practice observed and record the changes it needs

description.en: Read the timeliness results and the unmatched-event list back against the procedure and decide which failures are people not following a workable procedure and which are the procedure not matching how events actually surface — a deadline nobody can meet, a channel staff do not reach for, or event types the deadline table does not cover. Write the required changes with an owner and a target date, and state explicitly where the procedure was found sound, so a repeated failure next period is not re-diagnosed as a documentation problem when it is a behavioural one. Attach the assessment with its change list.

evidenceHint.en: Assessment of the incident reporting procedure against observed practice, listing the required changes with owners and target dates and naming the areas found sound

controls.title: Business Impact Analysis (BIA)
controls.objective: To determine business continuity priorities and requirements by analyzing the impacts of disruptions on business activities and setting recovery priorities.
controls.successCriteria:
Impact Criteria Relevance:
Impact types and criteria are relevant and comprehensive.
Activity Identification Completeness:
All critical activities supporting products and services are identified.
Impact Assessment Accuracy:
Impact assessments are accurate and consider time-based impacts.
MTPD Alignment:
MTPD is well-defined and aligns with the organization's risk tolerance.
RTO Realism:
RTOs are realistic and fit within the MTPD.
Prioritization Validity:
Prioritized activities are based on thorough impact analysis.
Resource Adequacy:
Resources required for prioritized activities are adequately identified and available.
Dependency and Interdependency Completeness:
Dependencies and interdependencies are accurately identified and documented.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Impact Types and Criteria:
Obtain the documented list of impact types and criteria relevant to the organization’s context.

Activity Identification:
Get a list of all business activities that support the provision of products and services.

Impact Assessment:
Collect assessments of impacts over time for each identified activity.

Maximum Tolerable Period of Disruption (MTPD):
Retrieve documents detailing the maximum tolerable period of disruption for each activity.

Recovery Time Objective (RTO):
Gather the prioritized time frames for resuming disrupted activities at a specified minimum acceptable capacity.

Prioritized Activities:
Obtain the list of prioritized activities identified through the impact analysis.

Resource Requirements:
Collect information on the resources required to support prioritized activities.

Dependencies and Interdependencies:
Get documents identifying dependencies, including partners and suppliers, and interdependencies of prioritized activities.

Analysis:
Impact Types and Criteria:
Verify that the impact types and criteria are comprehensive and relevant to the organization's context.

Activity Identification:
Ensure all critical activities that support product and service provision are identified.

Impact Assessment:
Review the assessments to confirm they consider the impacts over time resulting from activity disruption.

Maximum Tolerable Period of Disruption (MTPD):
Check that the MTPD is defined and aligns with the organization's risk appetite.

Recovery Time Objective (RTO):
Validate that the RTOs are prioritized within the MTPD and are realistic.

Prioritized Activities:
Confirm that the prioritized activities are based on the impact analysis.

Resource Requirements:
Ensure the identified resources are sufficient and available to support the prioritized activities.

Dependencies and Interdependencies:
Review the dependencies and interdependencies for completeness and accuracy.

Output:
Impact Types and Criteria Document:
Documentation confirming the impact types and criteria.

List of Critical Activities:
A list of all identified critical activities.

Impact Assessment Report:
Reports detailing the impacts over time for each activity.

MTPD Documentation:
Documents detailing the MTPD for each activity.

RTO Documentation:
Prioritized time frames for resuming disrupted activities.

Prioritized Activities List:
List of activities prioritized based on impact analysis.

Resource Requirements Documentation:
Documents detailing the resources needed for prioritized activities.

Dependencies and Interdependencies Documentation:
Comprehensive list of dependencies and interdependencies for prioritized activities.

title.en: Identify every business activity that supports the delivery of products and services

description.en: Build the activity list the whole analysis runs on: one row per activity that contributes to delivering a product or service, named as an activity performed rather than as a department or a system, with the product or service it supports and the person accountable for it. Work outwards from the product and service catalogue so that nothing is included because a team is large or excluded because it is quiet — an activity carried out by one person can still be the one that stops delivery. Include the supporting activities that products depend on, such as IT operations, payroll and customer support. Attach the activity list; it is the population every later task in this control assesses, prioritises and resources.

evidenceHint.en: Business activity list, one row per activity, naming the product or service it supports and the accountable owner

text.en: Start from the product and service catalogue and work back to the activities delivering each.
Name each row as an activity that is performed, not as a department or a system.
Add the supporting activities that products depend on, such as IT operations and payroll.
Name an accountable owner on every activity and confirm it with that person.

title.en: Define the impact types and the criteria used to rate them

description.en: Set out the types of impact a disruption can have on this organisation — financial, legal and regulatory, reputational, contractual, health and safety, and any others its context adds — and against each type write the criteria that separate a minor impact from a severe one in units that can be measured: money, customers affected, hours of service lost, a specific regulatory obligation breached. Assessors then read the criteria rather than exercise judgement, so the same disruption rated by two people yields the same answer, which is what makes the impact assessments comparable across activities. Record against each type what makes it relevant to this organisation's context, since a type nobody can tie to the context is the one assessors quietly skip. Attach the impact types and criteria document.

evidenceHint.en: Impact types and criteria document naming each impact type, the measurable thresholds separating its severity levels, and what makes that type relevant to the organisation's context

title.en: Assess the impact over time of each activity's disruption and record the MTPD it implies

description.en: For every activity on the list, work through the agreed impact types and rate the impact of that activity being unavailable at each time horizon — hours, a day, several days, weeks — because an impact that is trivial after two hours and severe after two days is exactly what a single rating hides. From the horizon at which the impact first becomes intolerable against the criteria, derive the maximum tolerable period of disruption for that activity and record it with the reasoning behind it. Record the assessment date and the people who supplied it, since an MTPD with no attributable source cannot be challenged or refreshed. Attach the impact assessment report covering every activity on the list.

evidenceHint.en: Impact assessment report giving, per activity, the rated impact at each time horizon for every impact type and the maximum tolerable period of disruption derived from it

text.en: Rate every activity against each agreed impact type, not only the financial one.
Rate the impact at several time horizons rather than at a single point after the disruption.
Identify the horizon at which the impact first becomes intolerable against the criteria.
Record that horizon as the activity's maximum tolerable period of disruption.
Name the people who supplied the assessment and the date on which it was made.

title.en: Determine the recovery time objective and minimum acceptable capacity for each prioritised activity

description.en: Rank the activities by the impact assessment and record which of them are prioritised for recovery. For each prioritised activity set the recovery time objective — the timeframe within which it must be resumed — and state the minimum acceptable capacity it must be resumed at, since restoring an activity at five per cent of normal throughput is not the same as restoring it. Check every objective sits inside that activity's maximum tolerable period of disruption, and where it cannot realistically be met inside it, record the shortfall as an open item rather than moving the objective to fit. Attach the prioritised activity list with the objective and the capacity recorded against each.

evidenceHint.en: Prioritised activity list giving each activity's recovery time objective, its minimum acceptable capacity, and its maximum tolerable period of disruption side by side

title.en: Record the resources, dependencies and interdependencies each prioritised activity needs

description.en: For every prioritised activity, write down what it takes to run it at the minimum acceptable capacity: people and the skills they hold, premises, systems and data, equipment, and information. Then record what it depends on outside its own control — other internal activities, partners and suppliers, and utilities — and the interdependencies where two prioritised activities each rely on the other, because those pairs determine the sequence in which recovery has to happen. Name the partner or supplier behind each external dependency rather than the service alone, so a dependency can be traced to the organisation that has to deliver it. Attach the resource and dependency documentation, one section per prioritised activity.

evidenceHint.en: Resource and dependency documentation per prioritised activity, naming the people, premises, systems and equipment required and each internal, supplier and utility dependency

title.en: Validate that each recovery time objective fits inside its MTPD and follows the impact analysis

description.en: Read the finished analysis back as a whole and check that it holds together: every activity on the list has been assessed, every recovery time objective falls inside the maximum tolerable period of disruption for its activity, the prioritisation reflects the assessed impacts rather than organisational seniority, and the resources named for each prioritised activity actually exist and are available within the objective. Record each inconsistency found with the activity it affects and the correction agreed, naming who agreed it. Attach the validation report; it is what shows the analysis was checked rather than merely assembled.

evidenceHint.en: BIA validation report listing every activity checked, each recovery time objective set against its MTPD, and each inconsistency found with the correction agreed

controls.title: Redundancy for Information Processing Facilities
controls.objective: To ensure that information processing facilities are implemented with sufficient redundancy to meet availability requirements and maintain security levels consistent with primary systems.
controls.successCriteria:
All critical information processing facilities have appropriate redundancy measures in place as per the availability requirements.
Redundancy implementations are verified to be effective and maintain equivalent security levels to primary systems.
Failover and redundancy mechanisms are tested and proven functional.
Incident responses involving the activation of redundant systems are timely and effective in ensuring continued operations.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain a list of all critical information processing facilities and their redundant components.
Gather documentation on the architecture and implementation of redundancy measures (e.g., mirrored systems, duplicated components).
Collect records of recent tests conducted on redundant systems to validate failover and functionality.
Acquire incident reports or logs that detail activation of redundant systems in emergencies.

Analysis:
Review the list of critical information processing facilities against their redundancy implementations to verify if they meet the defined availability requirements.
Analyze the architecture documentation to ensure that redundancy is appropriately implemented (e.g., geographically separate data centers, redundant power supplies, load balancing).
Evaluate test records to confirm that failover mechanisms work as intended and that redundant systems maintain the same security level as the primary systems.
Assess incident reports to understand the effectiveness and timeliness of the activation of redundant systems during emergencies.

Output:
A comprehensive report detailing the redundancy implementations for each critical information processing facility.
A summary of findings from the analysis of the redundancy architecture and its effectiveness.
A report on the outcomes of redundancy system tests.
A review of incident reports concerning the activation of redundant systems.

title.en: List each critical information processing facility with its availability requirement and redundant components

description.en: Identify the information processing facilities that are critical — the data centres, server rooms, hosted platforms and network cores whose loss stops the business — and against each record the availability requirement it is held to and the redundant components that exist for it today: the mirrored system, the duplicated appliance, the second site, the second power path. A facility whose availability requirement has never been stated is the row to resolve first, because every later task compares against it and cannot reach a verdict without it. Attach the list with the availability requirement and redundancy columns populated for every critical facility.

evidenceHint.en: List of critical information processing facilities, each with its stated availability requirement and the redundant components currently in place for it

title.en: Document the redundancy architecture behind each critical facility

description.en: For every facility on the list, produce the architecture documentation showing how the redundancy is actually built — which components are mirrored or duplicated, whether the redundant capacity sits in a geographically separate location or the same room, how traffic or workload moves between the two, and the redundant power and cooling paths beneath. State the single points of failure the architecture still contains rather than omitting them, since an undocumented shared dependency is what turns a tested failover into an outage. Have the architecture confirmed by whoever operates the facility, not only by whoever designed it. Attach the documentation per facility.

evidenceHint.en: Redundancy architecture documentation per critical facility showing the duplicated or mirrored components, the geographic separation, the failover or load-balancing mechanism, and the single points of failure that remain

text.en: Draw the primary and redundant components for each facility, including power and cooling paths.
Record the physical location of the redundant capacity and its distance from the primary.
Describe how traffic or workload moves between primary and redundant components on failure.
Name the component or dependency that both sides still share, where there is one.
Have the architecture confirmed by whoever operates the facility rather than only by its designer.

title.en: Compare the security controls on each redundant component against those on its primary

description.en: Redundant capacity is frequently built quickly and then left with weaker controls than the system it stands in for, so record for each redundant component the controls it actually carries — patch level, hardening baseline, access model and administrative accounts, encryption, and logging and monitoring coverage — beside the same values for the primary. Mark every line where the redundant side is weaker as a difference with a named owner and an agreed remediation, because those lines become the exposure on the day the failover happens rather than a theoretical gap. Attach the comparison with the configuration evidence behind it.

evidenceHint.en: Security comparison for every redundant component listing patch level, hardening baseline, access model, encryption and logging coverage beside the primary's values, with each weaker line owned and a remediation set

title.en: Test failover to the redundant capacity for each critical facility and record the outcome

description.en: Fail over to the redundant capacity in a planned test rather than reasoning about whether it would work, and record what happened: the time failover was initiated, the time service was restored on the redundant side, whether it carried full load or ran degraded, whether failback succeeded, and every manual step the documented mechanism turned out to require. A test aborted before completion is recorded as an aborted test with its reason, not omitted. Raise an item with a named owner for each failure or undocumented manual dependency found. Attach the test records for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Failover test records per critical facility giving the date, the initiation and restoration timestamps, whether full load was carried, the failback result, and the items raised with owners

title.en: Record every unplanned activation of redundant capacity with the time it took to take over

description.en: When redundant capacity is brought into service in a real incident — automatically or by hand — capture it as its own record: what failed, when the redundancy took over, whether the takeover was automatic or required intervention, how long service was actually degraded or lost, and whether the redundant side sustained operations for the whole duration. These records are the only evidence of redundancy behaving under conditions nobody chose, which is exactly what a planned test cannot give. Attach the incident reports covering activations of redundant systems in the period.

evidenceHint.en: Incident reports for every activation of redundant capacity in the period, each giving the failure, the takeover time, whether it was automatic or manual, and the duration of degraded or lost service

title.en: Assess each facility's redundancy against the availability requirement it is held to

description.en: Bring the test records and the incident records together against the list and judge, per critical facility, whether the redundancy as built and as exercised actually meets the availability requirement stated for it. Use the measured takeover times rather than the design intent, and treat a facility with a requirement but no completed test or activation in the period as unproven rather than compliant — the two are routinely confused and only one of them is evidence. Record a verdict per facility and, against every shortfall, the owner and the design or investment change agreed. Attach the report with the test and incident evidence it draws on.

evidenceHint.en: Redundancy assessment report giving, per critical facility, the availability requirement, the measured takeover times from tests and incidents, a met, unproven or shortfall verdict, and an owner for each shortfall

controls.title: Payment Card Data Retention Control
controls.objective: To ensure that full track data from payment cards is not retained post-authorization and that only necessary data elements (cardholder name, PAN, expiration date, service code) are stored securely.
controls.successCriteria:
All systems involved in payment processing are in compliance with data retention policies, retaining only the necessary data elements.
No evidence of full track data storage post-authorization in transaction records.
System configurations align with the requirements for secure storage and handling of payment card data.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Retrieve a list of all systems involved in payment processing and card data handling.
Collect logs and records of payment transactions and authorization processes.
Obtain configuration settings and data retention policies from these systems.

Analysis:
For each transaction record, verify that only cardholder name, PAN, expiration date, and service code are retained, and full track data is not stored.
Review system configuration settings to ensure compliance with data retention policies.
Examine transaction logs to confirm the deletion or anonymization of full track data post-authorization.

Output:
A report detailing each system's compliance with data retention policies.
Spreadsheet analysis of transaction records to verify stored data elements.
Compliance status report of system configurations with respect to payment card data handling.

title.en: List every system involved in payment processing and the card data elements it stores

description.en: Build the population from the payment flow rather than from the systems that obviously take a card: the authorisation path, the settlement and reconciliation systems, the reporting and warehouse copies, and any export or file transfer that carries card data onward. Record per system which of the permitted elements it stores — cardholder name, primary account number, expiration date, service code — where each is held, and whether the system ever receives full track data in the course of authorisation. That last column is what makes the control testable: a system that never sees track data cannot retain it, and a system that does is where the later searches start. Attach the dated list naming the flow it was derived from.

evidenceHint.en: Dated list of payment processing systems naming, per system, the card data elements stored, the store holding each, and whether the system receives full track data during authorisation

title.en: Set the permitted elements and the retention period for every payment data store

description.en: For each store on the list, record which of the four permitted elements it may hold, how long each is retained, and the step that removes full track data once authorisation completes — deletion, truncation or anonymisation, named specifically rather than described as a principle. Where the primary account number is stored, record how it is protected in that store and where the setting that protects it lives, so a later configuration export can be read against something. Any element held outside the permitted four is recorded here as an exception with the business reason and the owner who accepted it, rather than quietly normalised into the retention record. Attach the retention record with the configuration references it cites.

evidenceHint.en: Retention record per payment data store naming the permitted elements held, the retention period for each, the step that removes full track data, and any retained element outside the permitted four with its owner

title.en: Export each payment system's retention configuration and file it against the requirement

description.en: Pull the live configuration from every system on the list — retention and purge settings, the storage locations card data is written to, log level and masking rules, and the truncation or encryption setting applied to the primary account number — and file it with the date it was read. Configuration taken from a build template or a runbook does not satisfy this: the control compares the settings in force against the retention requirement, so the export has to come from the running system. Where a setting the requirement expects is simply absent from a system, record that absence explicitly rather than omitting the row and leaving it to be read as compliant. Attach the configuration export set for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Dated configuration export per payment system showing the retention and purge settings, card data storage locations, log masking rules and account number protection settings as they were in force

title.en: Sample transaction records from each system and record the data elements actually stored

description.en: Draw a sample of transaction records from every system on the list and inspect what each record actually holds, field by field, rather than what its schema says it may hold. Record per sampled record which of the four permitted elements are present, and flag any additional element found — track data, a card verification code, a PIN block or anything else outside the permitted set — with the store and record identifier so it can be traced. Sample across the stores as well as the systems, so that a reporting copy or an export file is examined and not only the primary database, since those copies are where retention settings are most often never applied. Attach the spreadsheet with one row per sampled record and the flagged rows called out.

evidenceHint.en: Spreadsheet listing each sampled transaction record with the card data elements actually found in it, flagging every element outside cardholder name, account number, expiration date and service code

text.en: Draw the sample so that every system and every store on the list is represented.
Inspect each record's stored values field by field rather than reading the schema.
Record which of the four permitted elements the record actually holds.
Flag any additional element found and note its store and record identifier.

title.en: Trace the authorisation logs to confirm full track data is removed once authorisation completes

description.en: The sampling shows what is held now; this task shows what happened between authorisation and now. Take the transaction and authorisation logs for the period and trace, across a set of transactions on each system, where full track data appears, whether the deletion, truncation or anonymisation step recorded in the retention record actually ran, and when. Record the interval between authorisation and removal for each traced transaction, and treat any transaction where the removal step left no trace as unproven rather than passed, since an absent log line is not evidence the step ran. Attach the log analysis with the traced transaction identifiers it rests on.

evidenceHint.en: Log analysis tracing full track data from authorisation to removal for a set of transactions per system, giving the removal step, its timestamp and the interval, and listing every transaction where removal is unproven

title.en: Report each system's compliance with the retention requirement and assign every exception

description.en: Bring the configuration exports, the record sampling and the log tracing together into the per-system compliance report the control calls for. Each system carries a verdict on three questions separately — is its configuration aligned with the retention requirement, does it hold only the permitted elements, and is full track data demonstrably removed after authorisation — because a system can pass one and fail another, and a single blended verdict hides exactly that. Every exception is recorded with the evidence line that found it, a named owner, the remediation agreed and a date. Attach the report with the three evidence sets it draws on.

evidenceHint.en: Compliance status report giving each payment system a separate verdict on configuration alignment, permitted elements held and full track data removal, with an owner, remediation and date for every exception

controls.title: Information Security Roles Compliance Check
controls.objective: To ensure that information security roles and responsibilities are properly defined, allocated, and complied with according to the organization’s policy and specific needs.
controls.successCriteria:
All roles within the organization have clearly defined and documented information security responsibilities.
Evidence of effective communication and training regarding these roles and responsibilities.
A record of adherence to the information security policy, with appropriate disciplinary actions taken where necessary.
Management reviews reflect active and effective oversight in the allocation of information security roles and responsibilities.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Collect the organizational structure and roles documentation.
Gather records of information security roles and responsibilities assigned to individuals.
Obtain training and awareness session records, including attendance sheets.
Retrieve records of any disciplinary actions related to information security policy violations.
Access the latest management review documents.

Analysis:
Verify that each role in the organization has clearly defined information security responsibilities.
Check that roles and responsibilities are communicated effectively to all staff members, as evidenced by training records and attendance sheets.
Review disciplinary records to assess compliance with the information security policy.
Assess the effectiveness of the management review in ensuring roles and responsibilities are current and relevant.

Output:
A report detailing the allocation and definition of information security roles and responsibilities.
A compliance assessment report based on training records and disciplinary actions.
A review report on the effectiveness of management’s oversight on role allocations.

title.en: Map every role in the organisational structure to the person holding it

description.en: Work from the organisational chart and the roles documentation to produce one row per role, naming the current holder, the business unit and the reporting line. A role with no named holder is exactly where an information security responsibility falls to nobody, so record it as vacant rather than omitting the row. HR supplies the holder and reporting data. This register is the population every later task counts against — the responsibilities record, the training coverage position and the management review each read it row by row. Attach the register carrying the date it was compiled; a row with a blank holder and no vacancy note is not done.

evidenceHint.en: Dated role register listing every role in the organisational structure with its current holder or vacancy note, business unit and reporting line

title.en: Record the information security responsibilities assigned to each role

description.en: Against every row of the role register, write the information security responsibilities that role carries and the individual they are allocated to, in the wording the person will actually be held to rather than a cross-reference to the policy. Where a responsibility is shared, mark one role accountable and list the contributing roles beside it so the allocation cannot be read two ways. A role whose information security duties cannot be stated is a finding to raise with its manager, not a row to leave empty. Attach the allocation record showing full coverage of the register — it is the report on the definition and allocation of roles that this control asks for.

evidenceHint.en: Information security role-and-responsibility allocation record covering every role in the register, naming the accountable individual for each responsibility

title.en: Log attendance at each information security training and awareness session

description.en: For every session run, keep the attendance sheet and post it against the role register so coverage reads per role rather than per headcount. Record the session date, the topics covered and each attendee, and carry the roles that did not attend forward so the next session starts with a named follow-up list instead of a percentage. Where a session was delivered to a specific role group, record which responsibilities it covered — that link is what evidences the responsibilities were communicated rather than merely published. Attach the attendance sheets for the period together with the per-role coverage position they produce.

evidenceHint.en: Training and awareness attendance sheets for the period plus the per-role coverage position showing which roles attended, which topics were covered and which roles are outstanding

title.en: Record every information security policy violation and the disciplinary action taken

description.en: Keep one row per violation carrying the date, the role and individual involved, what the policy required, the action taken and the date the case concluded. Where no disciplinary action followed, record the reason it was not warranted rather than leaving the outcome blank — this control expects action where necessary, and an unexplained blank cannot be told apart from an unhandled case. HR owns the disciplinary record. Attach the violation and disciplinary record for the period under test, or the signed nil return where there were none.

evidenceHint.en: Information security violation and disciplinary record for the period, one row per case with the action taken or the reason none was warranted, or a signed nil return

title.en: Review the allocation of information security roles at the management review

description.en: Put the role register, the allocation record, the training coverage position and the violation record in front of the management review, and take a decision on each role whose allocation is out of date, unfilled or contested. The minutes have to show which roles were discussed and what was decided about them: a minute recording only that the item was noted evidences attendance, not oversight. Reallocations agreed in the meeting are written back into the allocation record before the item closes. Attach the management review minutes carrying the role-allocation item, the decisions taken and the owner of each.

evidenceHint.en: Management review minutes carrying the information security role-allocation item, the roles discussed, the decisions taken and the owner assigned to each

title.en: Assess each role against its responsibilities, training and violation record
