description.en: Produce the compliance assessment this control asks for by reading the three records together, one role at a time: does the role have documented information security responsibilities, has its holder attended the training that covered them, and is any violation attached to it still open. Give each role a pass or a gap verdict and, against every gap, the accountable manager and the remediation agreed with them. Roles that are unfilled or newly created are reported as such rather than scored, so the assessment cannot read as complete when part of the population was skipped. Attach the assessment with the three records it was built from.

evidenceHint.en: Role compliance assessment giving a pass or gap verdict per role across documented responsibilities, training attendance and open violations, with an accountable manager and remediation per gap

text.en: Read each role register row against the responsibilities allocation record.
Check the training coverage position for the role holder and the topics attended.
Check whether any violation recorded against the role is still open.
Give the role a pass or gap verdict and name the accountable manager for each gap.
Report unfilled and newly created roles separately rather than scoring them.

controls.title: Risk Appetite Compliance Check
controls.objective: To ensure the organization's risk tolerance is accurately determined and clearly expressed in alignment with the documented risk appetite.
controls.successCriteria:
The Risk Appetite Statement accurately reflects the organization's risk tolerance and is consistently applied in risk assessments and treatments.
Documentation of decisions in high-risk situations demonstrates adherence to the risk appetite.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Retrieve the organization's Risk Appetite Statement.
Gather recent risk assessment reports and risk treatment plans.
Collect documentation of decisions made in situations involving significant risks.

Analysis:
Review the Risk Appetite Statement to confirm it clearly expresses the organization's risk tolerance.
Examine risk assessment reports and risk treatment plans to ensure they align with the stated risk appetite.
Analyze decisions made in high-risk situations to verify compliance with the risk tolerance levels.

Output:
A summary report comparing the Risk Appetite Statement with actual risk management practices.
A compliance matrix showing alignment between risk assessments, risk treatment plans, and the Risk Appetite Statement.
A decision analysis report highlighting instances of risk-related decision-making.

title.en: Inventory the risk assessments, treatment plans and significant-risk decisions falling in the period under test

description.en: The appetite can only be tested against something, and this list is that something — every risk assessment report issued in the period, every risk treatment plan issued, and every decision taken in a situation involving a significant risk. Record for each its identifier, its date, the risk it concerns and the person or body that owned it, so a later task can sample it and a reader can see the population was not selected to flatter the result. Where a decision on a significant risk was taken without a written record, list it with the record marked absent rather than dropping it — those rows are themselves a finding. Attach the population list carrying the period it covers.

evidenceHint.en: Population list for the period naming every risk assessment report, risk treatment plan and significant-risk decision, with date, risk concerned and accountable owner

title.en: Express each risk category's tolerance in the Risk Appetite Statement as a stated threshold

description.en: The statement has to say where the line is, not that a line exists. For each risk category the organisation runs, record the tolerance in terms somebody can test an assessed risk against: the score, loss value or exposure above which a risk cannot be carried without a decision, and what the statement requires once a risk sits above it. A category expressed only as a sentiment cannot be applied consistently across risk assessments and treatment plans, which is exactly what this control is tested on. Attach the issued Risk Appetite Statement version showing a testable threshold against every category it covers.

evidenceHint.en: Issued Risk Appetite Statement version carrying, per risk category, a tolerance threshold an assessed risk can be tested against and what the statement requires above it

text.en: List the risk categories the statement has to set a tolerance level for.
Express each category's tolerance as a score, loss value or exposure limit.
State what the statement requires when an assessed risk sits above its limit.
Show how a risk assessment records the tolerance level it was judged against.
Issue the statement as a version the assessments and treatment plans can cite.

title.en: Record each significant-risk decision against the tolerance level that applied to it

description.en: Each time a decision is taken in a situation involving a significant risk, write the decision down against the appetite: the risk and its assessed level, the threshold that applies to its category, whether the decision sits inside or outside that threshold, the option chosen and the person or body that took it. A decision taken outside the threshold is not forbidden by this task — it is recorded as such with the reason given at the time, because this control is tested on the documentation of high-risk decisions demonstrating adherence to the appetite, and a record that omits the tolerance it was weighed against demonstrates nothing either way. Attach the decision log for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Significant-risk decision log for the period showing, per decision, the assessed risk level, the applicable appetite threshold, an inside or outside verdict, the option chosen and the person or body that took it

title.en: Map every risk assessment and treatment plan to the appetite threshold it was judged against

description.en: Build the compliance matrix this control calls for: one row per assessed risk carrying its category, its assessed level, the appetite threshold that category sets, the treatment chosen and a verdict of within or outside appetite. Work from the population list rather than from a convenient subset, and leave the verdict blank on no row — a risk whose treatment plan never cites a threshold is recorded as unjudged, which is a distinct and more useful finding than a guess. Attach the matrix with the assessment and treatment-plan references each row was built from.

evidenceHint.en: Compliance matrix with one row per assessed risk giving category, assessed level, applicable appetite threshold, chosen treatment and a within, outside or unjudged verdict

text.en: Take each risk assessment from the population list and record its category and level.
Look up the appetite threshold the statement sets for that risk category.
Record the treatment the plan selected and the residual level it expects.
Mark each row within appetite, outside appetite, or unjudged where no threshold was cited.
Carry the outside and unjudged rows forward as the matrix's exception list.

title.en: Analyse the significant-risk decisions for departures from the stated tolerance levels

description.en: Read the decision log against the statement and produce the decision analysis this control asks for: which decisions accepted risk beyond the tolerance their category sets, and whether the decision record itself shows the tolerance was weighed at the time or the departure only surfaced in this analysis. That distinction is the one that matters, because this control is tested on the documentation of high-risk decisions demonstrating adherence — a departure weighed and written down and a departure found here are different findings about the same decision. Attach the analysis naming each departure and the decision reference it was read from.

evidenceHint.en: Decision analysis report listing each significant-risk decision that departed from the stated tolerance, the decision reference it was read from, and whether the record shows the tolerance was weighed at the time

title.en: Compare the Risk Appetite Statement against observed practice and report where the two diverge

description.en: Draw the matrix and the decision analysis together into the summary comparison this control's output calls for, and state a conclusion the statement's owner can act on: whether the appetite as written still describes the risk the organisation is actually accepting. Where practice consistently sits outside a threshold, say which of the two the divergence indicts — the threshold may be miscalibrated rather than the practice non-compliant — and record that reading against each divergence rather than listing it without one. Attach the summary report with the matrix and decision analysis it draws on.

evidenceHint.en: Summary report comparing the Risk Appetite Statement with observed risk management practice, listing each divergence and whether it indicts the stated threshold or the practice observed

controls.title: Source Code Access Management
controls.objective: To ensure that read and write access to source code, development tools, and software libraries are appropriately managed and restricted based on personnel roles and business needs, in accordance with the organization's security policies.
controls.successCriteria:
All instances of access to source code, development tools, and software libraries align with the permissions defined in the Access Control Matrix.
All change requests related to source code access have been executed following established procedures and with appropriate authorizations.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the Access Control Matrix specifying access rights for source code repositories and development tools.
Collect system logs showing read and write access to source code, development tools, and software libraries.
Gather documentation of change requests related to source code access since the last audit.

Analysis:
Compare the actual access rights (from system logs) against the Access Control Matrix to verify compliance.
Review change request documentation to ensure each request follows established change control procedures and proper authorization was obtained.
Examine system logs for unauthorized or anomalous access patterns, focusing on write access to source code.

Output:
A report detailing compliance with the Access Control Matrix.
A spreadsheet or database cross-referencing each access instance against the Access Control Matrix.
Compiled documentation and analysis of change requests.

title.en: Inventory every source code repository, development tool and software library the access matrix must cover

description.en: The Access Control Matrix is only as good as the population it names, so start by enumerating what it has to cover: each source code repository, each development tool that can read or write code, and each internal or third-party software library the build consumes. Record the hosting platform, the accountable engineering owner, and whether the item is self-hosted or supplied as a service — the access logs for those two come from different places, and a source nobody named is how a repository ends up unlogged. Attach the list carrying the date it was compiled; a repository live on the platform but absent here is the first gap this task closes.

evidenceHint.en: Dated list of source code repositories, development tools and software libraries with hosting platform, accountable engineering owner, and a self-hosted or supplied-as-a-service value on every row

text.en: Enumerate the repositories from the hosting platform's own project listing rather than from a wiki page.
Add the development tools that can read or write code — build servers, package registries, code review services.
Add every internal and third-party software library the build consumes, naming where each is fetched from.
Record the accountable engineering owner and the self-hosted or service custody of each item.
Date the list and hold it as the population the matrix and the log collection are both read against.

title.en: Record the read and write rights each role holds in the Access Control Matrix

description.en: Work the matrix out against the repository and tool list so every item carries, per personnel role, whether that role may read, may write, or holds no access — and the business need justifying write access wherever it is granted. "Developers have access" is not a matrix row: the later reconciliation compares a real account's permission against a named cell, and a cell that does not exist cannot be reconciled against, so an item on the list with no row is an item the audit cannot test. Attach the issued matrix version showing full coverage of the list.

evidenceHint.en: Issued Access Control Matrix version giving read and write rights per role for every repository, development tool and library on the list, with the business need recorded against each write grant

title.en: Export the read and write access logs for the repositories, tools and libraries in scope

description.en: For each item on the list, pull the access log covering the period under test — who read, who wrote, when, and under which account, service accounts and CI identities included. Machine identities are the ones most often left out of an export drawn from the user directory, and a build agent holding write access to a repository is precisely the account the anomaly review needs to see. Where a platform emits no usable access log, record that as a finding against the platform rather than leaving its rows silently empty. Attach the exports with the date range each covers.

evidenceHint.en: Access log exports covering the period for every repository, development tool and library in scope, showing account, access type and timestamp, plus a named finding for any platform that produced no usable log

title.en: Record the authorisation behind every change to source code access

description.en: Each time read or write access to a repository, development tool or library is granted, altered or removed, keep the change request that asked for it and the record of who authorised it, both dated. The audit asks for change requests since the last audit as an artifact in its own right, so the collection has to run continuously rather than be assembled afterwards from memory — an access change with no change request is the finding, and it is only visible when the register covers the whole period rather than the part somebody remembered. Attach the change request set for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Change request records for every source code access grant, modification and revocation in the period, each showing the account and item affected, the requester, the authoriser and both dates

title.en: Reconcile each account's repository and tool access against the Access Control Matrix

description.en: Take every account appearing in the access logs or in a platform's current permission listing and compare the permission it actually holds against the cell the matrix authorises for its role. Produce the cross-reference the audit asks for — one row per account and item, carrying a conforms or exception verdict — and for each exception name the accountable owner and whether the resolution is to correct the access or to amend the matrix. Both are legitimate outcomes; leaving the disagreement unresolved is not. Attach the cross-reference and the compliance report drawn from it.

evidenceHint.en: Cross-reference of every account against the Access Control Matrix for each repository, development tool and library, with a conforms or exception verdict per row, and a compliance report naming the accountable owner and the agreed resolution for every exception

text.en: Pull the current permission listing for every repository and development tool on the list.
Resolve each account to a person or service and to the role the matrix assigns it.
Compare the permission held against that role's matrix cell and mark conforms or exception.
Classify each exception as excess access, an account with no matrix cell, or a holder with no current role.
Name the accountable owner and agree whether the access or the matrix is the thing corrected.

title.en: Examine the source code write-access log for unauthorised or anomalous activity

description.en: Read the write half of the log specifically, because that is where the control's exposure sits: pushes and merges from accounts holding no matrix write cell, writes outside the account's normal hours or from unexpected locations, direct writes to protected branches, and writes by service accounts that no pipeline run explains. Disposition each hit either as explained — naming the change request or pipeline run that accounts for it — or as an exception referred for investigation. Attach the anomaly report naming the extract and date range read, so an empty exception list reads as a result rather than as an absence of looking.

evidenceHint.en: Source code write-access anomaly report naming the log extract and date range examined, each anomalous write found, and its disposition as explained or referred for investigation

controls.title: Access and Identity Security Management
controls.objective: To ensure secure and compliant management of access control, identity lifecycle, authentication information, and access rights in alignment with organizational policies and security requirements.
controls.successCriteria:
All aspects of access control, identity management, authentication information, and access rights are managed securely, efficiently, and in full compliance with organizational policies.
Identities, both human and non-human, are managed with accountability and transparency.
Authentication information is allocated, managed, and protected securely, with user compliance to guidelines.
Access rights are provisioned, reviewed, and modified in accordance with organizational needs and security requirements, with special attention to changes in roles or employment status.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain policy documents for Access Control, Identity Management, Authentication Information Management, and Access Rights.
Collect records of identity assignments, shared identity approvals, access logs, change requests, and identity disablement or removal actions.
Gather logs and records related to authentication information allocation, transmission, receipt, and changes.
Acquire documentation and records for access rights provisioning, review, modification, and revocation.

Analysis:
Review policy adherence in managing access control, identity lifecycle, authentication information, and access rights.
Verify the uniqueness and appropriateness of identity assignments and management, including shared identities and non-human entities.
Assess the security and compliance in allocation, transmission, and management of authentication information.
Analyze access rights management processes, including provisioning, modification, revocation, and regular reviews, especially after changes in roles or employment status.

Output:
A comprehensive report detailing compliance and adherence to policies across all areas.
Summaries of identity management, authentication information practices, and access rights governance.
Analysis of logs and records for irregularities or non-compliance.

title.en: Register every human and non-human identity with its accountable owner

description.en: Build the register the audit's identity-assignment records are read against: one row per identity, human and non-human alike, giving the person or team accountable for it, the systems it can reach, and whether it is unique to a single holder or shared. Service accounts, API identities, machine accounts and integration credentials belong here — they are the population the uniqueness check runs against and the one most often missing from an identity list drawn off the HR roster. Attach the register; a row with no named owner is not finished, because an identity nobody owns is an identity nobody disables.

evidenceHint.en: Identity register listing every human and non-human identity with its accountable owner, the systems it can reach, and a unique or shared marking on every row

text.en: Draw the human identities from the directory rather than the HR roster, so orphaned accounts appear.
Add every service account, API identity, machine account and integration credential in use.
Name the person or team accountable for each identity and the systems it can reach.
Mark each identity as unique to one holder or shared, so the shared population becomes explicit.
Resolve every row left without a named owner before treating the register as complete.

title.en: Record the approval and accountable holder for each shared identity

description.en: For every identity the register marks shared, capture the approval that permitted the sharing, who granted it and when, the named individual accountable for its use, and the compensating record that ties an individual action back to a person. A shared identity without that trail is exactly the accountability gap the control names, and it is reported as an exception rather than quietly scored as acceptable. Where the register marks no identity as shared, record that nil return explicitly rather than leaving the artifact absent — an absent artifact and an unexamined population look the same. Attach the approvals against the register rows they belong to.

evidenceHint.en: Shared identity approval records giving approver, approval date, accountable holder and the attribution method for each shared identity, or an explicit nil return where none is shared

title.en: Document how authentication information is allocated, transmitted and changed

description.en: Write the operating procedure for authentication information as its own artifact: how a credential is generated or allocated to a holder, the channel it travels on to reach them, how receipt is confirmed, the guidance the holder is bound by, and the route for changing or replacing it when compromise is suspected. Cover each credential type distinctly — initial passwords, resets, API keys, certificates, MFA enrolment — because they are allocated and transmitted by different routes, and the types handled manually are the ones that leave no log for the later analysis to read. Attach the issued procedure.

evidenceHint.en: Issued authentication information management procedure covering allocation, transmission channel, receipt confirmation, holder guidance and change route for each credential type in use

title.en: Log every identity disablement and removal against the change that triggered it

description.en: Each time an identity is disabled or removed, record the identity, the date and time of the action, who performed it, and the role change, employment change or service decommissioning that triggered it — with the elapsed time between trigger and action. That elapsed figure is the number the review actually reads: it is what shows access follows employment status rather than lagging behind it by weeks. Non-human identities belong on the same log when the service they serve is retired. Attach the disablement and removal log for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Identity disablement and removal log for the period showing the identity, the triggering event and its date, the action date, the elapsed time between them, and the operator who performed it

title.en: Record each access rights provisioning, modification and revocation with its authorisation

description.en: Keep the change record behind every access right granted, altered or revoked: what was requested, for which identity, on which system, who approved it, and when it took effect. The audit asks for provisioning, modification and revocation records as one set, and a register holding only grants cannot answer whether revocations happened at all — which is the half that carries the risk. Where a right was applied without a request, record it as an unrequested change rather than back-filling a request for it. Attach the change records for the period with the ticket or request references behind them.

evidenceHint.en: Access rights change records for the period covering provisioning, modification and revocation, each naming the identity, system, approver and effective date, with unrequested changes flagged as such

title.en: Review access rights against each holder's current role and employment status

description.en: Run the review the control calls for: put each identity's current rights in front of the accountable owner alongside the holder's present role and employment status, and have them confirm, reduce or revoke each right. Give particular weight to identities whose role or employment changed during the period — that is where a right which was appropriate on the day it was granted becomes standing excess. Record every decision with the reviewer and the date, and carry each revocation raised here into the access rights change record so the two artifacts cannot disagree. Attach the completed review with the irregularities it surfaced.

evidenceHint.en: Completed access rights review showing, per identity, the rights held, the reviewer's confirm, reduce or revoke decision and date, and a list of irregularities with the resolution of each

text.en: Extract the rights currently held per identity from each system, not from the request history.
Route each identity's rights to the owner accountable for that holder's current role.
Have the reviewer mark each right confirm, reduce or revoke, with their name and the date.
Give separate attention to holders whose role or employment changed during the period.
Raise a change record for every reduce or revoke decision and track it through to applied.

controls.title: Trusted DNS Server Configuration
controls.objective: Ensure all enterprise assets are configured to use designated, trusted DNS servers to enhance network security and integrity.
controls.successCriteria:
All audited assets use the designated trusted DNS servers as per the enterprise standards.
Any deviations from the standard DNS configurations are properly justified and documented.
DNS configuration changes have followed the established change management process.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Retrieve a comprehensive list of all enterprise assets.
Collect network configuration details from a representative sample of assets, focusing on DNS server settings.
Gather documentation or configurations that specify the enterprise’s trusted DNS servers (either internal or reputable external servers).

Analysis:
For each asset in the sample, verify that the DNS server settings align with the enterprise’s designated trusted DNS servers.
Assess any deviations to determine if they are justified or require remediation.
Review change management records to confirm that any updates to DNS settings were properly authorized and documented.

Output:
A report detailing DNS configurations for each sampled asset.
A compliance matrix comparing current DNS settings against the enterprise standard.
A summary of change management records related to DNS configuration changes.

title.en: Group the enterprise asset list into the classes the DNS sample will be drawn from

description.en: Start from the comprehensive asset list and group it by how DNS reaches each asset — domain-joined workstations, servers, network devices, cloud instances, containers, mobile and unmanaged devices — recording how many assets sit in each class, who owns it, and the mechanism that sets its resolvers. The grouping is what makes the later sample representative rather than convenient, and it also shows which classes are configured centrally and which are set on the device itself. Attach the grouped population with its per-class counts.

evidenceHint.en: Enterprise asset population grouped by DNS configuration class, with the asset count and owner per class and the mechanism that sets resolvers for it

title.en: Record the designated trusted DNS servers and the asset classes each serves

description.en: Write down the resolvers the enterprise standard designates — their addresses, whether each is internally operated or a named reputable external provider, who runs it, and which of the asset classes is expected to use it. Where a class legitimately uses a different resolver, such as a cloud provider's own service or a segregated environment's forwarder, name that resolver in the standard too, so the compliance test has something to pass against rather than reporting the same deviation every cycle. Attach the issued standard.

evidenceHint.en: Issued DNS standard naming each designated trusted resolver, its address, whether it is internal or a named external provider, its operator and the asset classes expected to use it

title.en: Capture the DNS resolver settings from each sampled asset

description.en: Draw the sample across the grouped classes and read the configured resolvers off each asset directly — the resolver list, its order, and whether it is set locally or handed down by DHCP or configuration policy — recording the command or console used and the date of capture so the reading can be reproduced. Take the value the asset is actually running rather than the value its build template specifies; the difference between those two is the reason for sampling at all. Attach the per-asset DNS configuration report.

evidenceHint.en: Per-asset DNS configuration report for the sample, giving each asset's configured resolvers in order, whether they are set locally or centrally, and the capture method and date

title.en: Compare each sampled asset's resolvers against the designated servers

description.en: Score every sampled asset against the standard for its class: a match, or a deviation naming the resolver actually configured. For each deviation record whether an accepted written justification exists and, where it does not, a remediation owner and date — an undocumented public resolver on a server is a different finding from an approved cloud forwarder, and the matrix has to tell them apart. Attach the compliance matrix with a justification or a remediation recorded against every deviating asset.

evidenceHint.en: DNS compliance matrix with one row per sampled asset showing its configured resolvers, the designated resolvers for its class, a match or deviation verdict and the justification or remediation owner for each deviation

title.en: Trace every DNS configuration change in the period back to its change record

description.en: List the changes made to DNS settings during the period — on the resolvers themselves and on the mechanisms that hand resolvers to assets, such as DHCP scopes and configuration policy — and for each one find the change record that authorised it, with the requester, the approver and the date. Changes with no record are reported by name; they are usually what explains the deviations found in the sample. Attach the change management summary with a compliant or unauthorised status against each change.

evidenceHint.en: Change management summary of DNS configuration changes in the period, each with its change record reference, requester, approver, date and a compliant or unauthorised status

controls.title: Outsourced Development Oversight
controls.objective: To ensure that outsourced system development activities comply with the organization's information security requirements and expectations.
controls.successCriteria:
All outsourced development projects have contracts or agreements that meet the organization's security requirements.
Acceptance testing and assurance reports demonstrate compliance with security and privacy standards.
Intellectual property rights, threat models, and escrow agreements are properly managed and documented.
Supplier development processes have been audited and found compliant with the organization's standards.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain a list of all outsourced development projects and associated suppliers.
Acquire copies of signed contracts or agreements with these suppliers, highlighting security and development requirements.
Collect recent acceptance testing reports, security and privacy assurance reports, and any documentation related to code ownership and intellectual property rights.
Gather evidence of threat models provided to the suppliers and any escrow agreements in place.
Obtain logs or reports of any audits conducted on the supplier's development processes.

Analysis:
Verify that each outsourced project has a corresponding contract or agreement that includes the necessary security and development requirements.
Assess the acceptance testing reports and other assurance reports to ensure they meet the minimum acceptable levels of security and privacy.
Confirm that threat models, intellectual property rights, and escrow agreements are appropriately addressed and documented.
Review the audit logs or reports to validate that the supplier's development processes comply with the contractual requirements.

Output:
A comprehensive report detailing the compliance status of each outsourced development project.
A checklist verifying the presence and adequacy of contracts, testing reports, intellectual property documentation, threat models, and audit logs.

title.en: Register every outsourced development project with its supplier and deliverable

description.en: The control is measured over the outsourced projects, so the list of them is the denominator for everything that follows. Build it from procurement and finance records of what was actually paid for as well as from the engineering plan, since a development contract placed by a business team is the row most likely to be missing. Record for each project the supplier, the system or component being built, the contract or purchase order reference, the delivery dates, and the internal owner accountable for the relationship. Attach the register; a row without a contract reference blocks the clause extraction task, so chase it rather than leaving it blank.

evidenceHint.en: Register of outsourced development projects, each row naming the supplier, the deliverable, the contract or purchase order reference, the delivery dates and the accountable internal owner

text.en: Cross-check the engineering plan against procurement and finance records of development spend.
Record the supplier, the deliverable and the contract or purchase order reference per project.
Record the delivery dates and the internal owner accountable for each supplier relationship.
Chase any row whose contract reference is missing before the register is treated as complete.

title.en: Extract each contract's security, development, code-ownership and escrow terms into a clause register

description.en: Pull the signed contract or agreement behind every row of the project register and extract into one clause register what it actually says on four points: the information security requirements the supplier is bound to, the development requirements including secure coding and testing obligations, who owns the code and the intellectual property in it, and whether source code is held in escrow and under what release conditions. Record the clause reference against each entry so a reader can go back to the contract, and mark an agreement silent on a point as silent rather than scoring it - the list of silent agreements is the finding this task produces and is what the renewal conversation is built on. Legal/DPO reads the ownership and escrow wording; Procurement holds the register. Attach the register with the contract extracts it was built from.

evidenceHint.en: Clause register giving, per outsourced project, the security requirements, development requirements, code-ownership position and escrow arrangement with a contract clause reference each, plus the list of agreements silent on any of the four

text.en: Retrieve the signed contract or agreement behind every row of the project register.
Extract the information security and development requirements with their clause references.
Extract the code ownership and intellectual property position for the delivered work.
Record whether source code is escrowed and the conditions under which it is released.
Mark every agreement silent on one of the four points and list them for renewal.

title.en: Issue the threat model for each outsourced build to its supplier and record the handover

description.en: A supplier cannot design against threats it has not been told about, and the auditor asks for evidence that the threat model was provided rather than merely produced. For each project on the register, issue the threat model covering the system being built - the assets it handles, the trust boundaries it crosses and the threats the supplier is expected to mitigate - and record the date it was sent, the person it went to, and their acknowledgement. Where the model was updated mid-delivery, record the re-issue too, since a supplier working from a superseded model is a real exposure and an easily evidenced one. Attach the threat models issued in the period with their transmittal and acknowledgement records.

evidenceHint.en: Threat models issued to suppliers in the period, each with the date sent, the recipient and the supplier's acknowledgement, including any mid-delivery re-issues

title.en: File the acceptance test result and security assurance report for each delivery with its decision

description.en: Every delivery from an outsourced project is accepted against a test, and the record of that test is the evidence this control turns on. For each delivery record the acceptance testing carried out, the security and privacy assurance report the supplier provided, the defects or vulnerabilities either of them raised, and the decision taken - accepted, accepted with conditions, or rejected - with the person who took it. Where a delivery was accepted with findings still open, record the conditions and the date agreed for clearing them, so an acceptance does not silently close a vulnerability. Engineering lead runs the acceptance; Security engineering reads the assurance report. Attach the acceptance and assurance records for the period's deliveries.

evidenceHint.en: Acceptance test result and supplier security and privacy assurance report per delivery, showing the findings raised, the accept-or-reject decision, who took it and any conditions with their agreed clearance dates

title.en: Audit each supplier's development process against the requirements its contract carries

description.en: The contract's security and development requirements are only worth what the supplier's process actually does, so test the process rather than the promise. Take the security and development clauses recorded in the clause register as the audit scope, and for each of them establish what the supplier's development process does and what record proves it - the supplier's own audit logs and reports are the starting material an auditor asks for. Where the supplier offers an independent report in place of a direct audit, record its scope and date and state which contracted requirements that report does not cover, because the uncovered remainder is where the contract is still untested. Score each requirement in the clause register as evidenced or not evidenced, and raise every gap with the supplier and an internal owner. Attach the audit report, or the accepted independent report, with the scope it covered and the gaps it raised.

evidenceHint.en: Audit report on each supplier's development process, or the independent report accepted in its place with its scope and date, scoring every contracted requirement evidenced or not and listing the gaps raised

text.en: Draw the audit scope from the security and development clauses in the clause register.
Obtain the supplier's own audit logs and reports covering its development process.
Establish for each contracted requirement what the process does and what record proves it.
Record which contracted requirements an accepted independent report leaves uncovered.
Score each contracted requirement evidenced or not and raise every gap with an owner.

title.en: Score every outsourced project on the compliance checklist and report its status

description.en: Close the control by running each project on the register through the checklist the control's output calls for: a contract carrying the security and development requirements, acceptance testing and assurance reports present and adequate, intellectual property and escrow documented, a threat model issued, and the supplier's development process audited. Mark each item present and adequate, present but inadequate, or absent, and wherever it is not present name the accountable owner and the date it will be. The report drawn from the checklist states the compliance status of every outsourced project in one place, which is what Management needs to decide whether a supplier relationship continues. Attach the completed checklist and the status report.

evidenceHint.en: Completed compliance checklist covering contract, acceptance and assurance reports, IP documentation, threat model and process audit for every outsourced project, with the status report drawn from it

controls.title: Endpoint Device Security Compliance
controls.objective: To ensure that all user endpoint devices adhere to the organization's IT security policies and standards for handling and protecting information.
controls.successCriteria:
All user endpoint devices in the sample are registered and comply with physical protection, software, encryption, and security update requirements as per policy.
Users have acknowledged and adhere to the endpoint device security policy.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain an inventory list of all user endpoint devices (laptops, mobile phones, etc.) from the IT department.
Gather configuration reports and security settings for a sample of endpoint devices.
Collect recent logs of security updates, patch management, and antivirus updates for these devices.
Request records of user acknowledgments or compliance attestations regarding the endpoint device security policy.

Analysis:
Cross-check the inventory list against the policy's requirements for device registration, physical protection, software restrictions, encryption, and other specified security measures.
Verify that the security settings on sampled devices comply with the policy (e.g., firewalls, automatic updates, access controls).
Assess the currency of security updates and patch management against policy requirements.
Evaluate user acknowledgments and compliance attestations to ensure understanding and adherence to the policy.

Output:
A compiled inventory and configuration report for the sampled devices.
A compliance matrix showing each device's adherence to the policy's requirements.
A summary of security updates and patch management status for these devices.
Documentation of user acknowledgments or compliance attestations.

title.en: Register every user endpoint device with its holder and registration status

description.en: Build the inventory the compliance matrix is drawn from: one row per laptop, mobile phone and other user endpoint, giving the device identifier, the assigned user, the device type and operating system, and whether it is registered under the endpoint device policy. Hold devices in stock or unassigned in their own section so they are not read as gaps. A device in use but absent from the register is the finding this task produces, so reconcile against the identity and management consoles rather than against the procurement list alone. Attach the dated inventory.

evidenceHint.en: Dated endpoint device inventory giving each device's identifier, assigned user, type and operating system, and its registration status under the endpoint device policy, with unregistered devices in use flagged

title.en: Record the required security settings for each class of endpoint device

description.en: State the baseline the sampled devices will be scored against, in checkable terms rather than principles: for each device class in the inventory, the physical protection expected, the software permitted and prohibited, whether storage encryption is required and to what standard, the firewall and automatic-update settings, the screen lock and access controls, and the maximum age permitted for security patches and antivirus definitions. Every line has to be something an assessor can observe on a device, because a baseline entry that cannot be read off a configuration report cannot be scored. Attach the issued baseline covering every class in the inventory.

evidenceHint.en: Issued endpoint security baseline with a row per device class covering physical protection, permitted software, encryption, firewall, automatic updates, access control, and the maximum permitted patch and definition age

title.en: Collect each device holder's acknowledgement of the endpoint device policy

description.en: Ask every user holding a registered device to acknowledge the endpoint device security policy, and record the acknowledgement against the device register so the artifact shows coverage rather than volume: the user, the device, the policy version acknowledged and the date. The output that matters is the list of holders who have not acknowledged the current version of the policy, including anyone whose acknowledgement is against an earlier one. Attach the acknowledgement register with those outstanding named.

evidenceHint.en: Endpoint policy acknowledgement register giving per holder the device, the policy version acknowledged and the date, with everyone outstanding or holding an acknowledgement of an earlier version named

title.en: Record the patch, operating system and antivirus update status of every endpoint

description.en: Export from the management tooling, for the period under test, what each registered endpoint is actually running: its operating system build, the date it last received security patches, any patches outstanding beyond the baseline's maximum age, and the date its antivirus definitions last updated. Report the devices that have not checked in during the period as their own group with the date each was last seen, because a device missing from an export reads as compliant unless it is called out. Attach the update status summary with the raw management export behind it.

evidenceHint.en: Security update and patch status summary per registered endpoint giving the operating system build, last patch date, patches outstanding beyond the maximum age and antivirus definition date, plus the devices not seen in the period with their last check-in

title.en: Score a sample of endpoints' configuration reports against every baseline requirement

description.en: Draw a sample from the register covering each device class and operating system, pull the configuration report and security settings for each sampled device, and score it line by line into the compliance matrix the control calls for — one row per device, one column per baseline requirement, and a pass, fail or not-applicable in each cell rather than an overall impression. Read encryption state, firewall state, automatic-update setting, screen lock and installed software from the device's own report, not from the build standard it was imaged with. Give every fail an owner and a remediation date in the same matrix. Attach it with the configuration reports it was scored from.

evidenceHint.en: Endpoint compliance matrix with one row per sampled device and one column per baseline requirement, a pass, fail or not-applicable per cell, an owner and remediation date for each fail, backed by the device configuration reports

text.en: Draw the sample so every device class and operating system in the register is represented.
Pull the configuration report and security settings for each sampled device.
Score each baseline requirement against what that report shows, cell by cell.
Read encryption, firewall, update and screen-lock state from the device rather than the build standard.
Assign an owner and a remediation date to every cell scored as a fail.

controls.title: Supplier Security Compliance
controls.objective: To ensure that suppliers adhere to the organization's information security standards and requirements throughout the duration of their engagement.
controls.successCriteria:
All suppliers have clearly documented security requirements in their contracts/agreements.
Suppliers demonstrate compliance with the organization's security standards.
Effective monitoring and management of supplier-related security incidents.
Prompt and appropriate action taken in response to non-compliance or security issues.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the list of current suppliers from the Supplier Management Register.
Gather copies of security clauses or requirements from contracts/agreements with these suppliers.
Collect recent audit reports, security assessments, or compliance certificates from suppliers.
Retrieve incident logs or non-compliance reports related to suppliers.
Gather documentation of supplier monitoring activities, such as regular review meetings or communication records.

Analysis:
Review each supplier’s contract/agreement to confirm the inclusion and clarity of information security requirements.
Cross-examine audit reports, assessments, or certificates against the organization's security standards to verify compliance.
Analyze incident logs for patterns or repeated security issues with specific suppliers.
Evaluate the effectiveness of the monitoring process - frequency, depth, and responsiveness to issues.

Output:
Compiled list of suppliers with associated security requirements from contracts.
Comparison spreadsheet of supplier compliance vs. organization's security standards.
Summary report of incidents and non-compliance issues.
Evaluation report on the supplier monitoring process.

title.en: Record the contract security clause reference for every supplier on the register

description.en: Work through the Supplier Management Register and, for each supplier, open the executed contract or agreement and record where the information security requirements sit — clause number, document title and version — together with whether that clause states the requirements clearly enough to test a supplier against, or only refers to security in general terms. Where a supplier has no security clause at all, record 'no security clause'; where the executed version cannot be located, record 'contract not held' and ask Legal for the signed copy. The task is finished when every row on the register carries one of those three states and none is blank.

evidenceHint.en: Supplier Management Register export showing, against every supplier row, a clause reference with a clarity note, or a 'no security clause' or 'contract not held' state

title.en: Record the assurance artifact expected from each supplier and the expiry of the copy held

description.en: Against each register entry, record which of the three assurance types we will accept from that supplier — an audit report, a security assessment, or a compliance certificate — naming the specific document (for example an ISO 27001 certificate covering the contracted service, or a completed security assessment questionnaire), and the expiry or report-period end date of the copy currently held. Where nothing has ever been received, record 'none held' rather than leaving the field empty, so the chase list can be filtered from the register itself. Security engineering decides which artifact is acceptable for the service being bought and is accountable for this entry; Procurement holds the register and enters the dates.

evidenceHint.en: Register columns showing the expected assurance artifact and the expiry or report-period end date of the copy held, or 'none held', for every supplier

title.en: Send and log the assurance evidence request for every supplier with a lapsed or missing artifact

description.en: Filter the register for suppliers whose assurance artifact is expired or marked 'none held', and send each one's named contact a written request for the artifact recorded against them. This task is finished when the request has been sent and logged for every supplier in that filter — not when the suppliers reply, which is not ours to complete. Against each supplier record the date sent, the contact addressed, and then either the artifact received or the escalation raised with the internal owner of that contract. The resulting log is that supplier's communication record and feeds the monitoring evaluation.

evidenceHint.en: Request log listing supplier, contact addressed, date sent, and response or escalation status for each outstanding artifact

title.en: Log each supplier security incident and non-compliance against the supplier's register entry

description.en: For every security incident or non-compliance involving a supplier — a breach they notified, an outage affecting our data, a control failure found during assessment, or an expired certificate they declined to renew — add a dated entry to the supplier incident log carrying the supplier name, what happened, the action we took, and whether it is open or closed. Link each entry to the supplier's register row so repeat issues with one supplier are visible when the register is read.

evidenceHint.en: Supplier incident and non-compliance log with dated entries, action taken, and open or closed status per supplier

title.en: Compare each assurance artifact held against our security requirements and record the gaps

description.en: Take every certificate, audit report and completed assessment currently held and check it against the organisation's security standards as that supplier's contract clause imposes them. Judge the artifact, not the supplier's assurances: scope statements routinely exclude the service we actually buy, and a report can be in date while carrying exceptions against controls we rely on. Produce a comparison sheet giving each supplier a compliant, gap or expired verdict, naming the specific unmet requirement wherever the verdict is not compliant.

evidenceHint.en: Supplier compliance comparison spreadsheet: supplier, artifact, verdict, and the named unmet requirement behind each gap

text.en: Check the artifact's scope statement names the service or system we actually purchase.
Check the certificate or report period is still current at the date of review.
List every exception, qualified opinion or user-entity control the report places back on us.
Note where the artifact covers a different legal entity, region or subsidiary than the one we contract with.

title.en: Record each supplier's last monitoring contact and the issues still open from it

description.en: For every supplier on the register, record the date and outcome of the most recent review meeting, service report or security correspondence held with them — the logged assurance requests count as correspondence — and whether the issues raised there, and any incident logged against that supplier, are now closed. State at the top of the report the window examined, because the control sets no review frequency: until the report says what period it covered, 'no contact recorded' means nothing. The two lists are the output — suppliers with no monitoring contact in that window, and suppliers with issues or incidents still open — and they are what show whether monitoring is running rather than merely scheduled.

evidenceHint.en: Supplier monitoring evaluation report stating the window examined, the last contact date and outcome per supplier, and the lists of suppliers with no contact recorded and with issues or incidents still open

controls.title: Information Security Continuity Control
controls.objective: To ensure the maintenance of information security at an appropriate level during disruptions and integrate security controls in business continuity processes.
controls.successCriteria:
The BCP and ICT Continuity Plans adequately address information security requirements during disruptions.
The implemented security controls and compensating controls are effective and comply with industry best practices.
Response actions taken during disruptions align with the planned procedures and effectively maintain information security.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the Business Continuity Plan (BCP) and ICT Continuity Plan documents.
Get records of the latest tests and reviews of the BCP.
Acquire a list of information security controls and compensating controls implemented for disruptions.
Obtain logs or records of any recent disruptions and the response actions taken.

Analysis:
Review the BCP and ICT Continuity Plan to ensure they include specific information security requirements and controls for disruptions.
Examine the test and review records of the BCP to check for the effectiveness and relevance of the plans in maintaining information security during disruptions.
Evaluate the list of implemented security controls and compensating controls against industry best practices and specific organizational needs during disruptions.
Analyze the response actions taken during recent disruptions to assess the effectiveness of current security measures and identify any potential gaps.

Output:
A detailed report on the evaluation of the BCP and ICT Continuity Plans.
A compliance matrix comparing current controls with industry best practices.
A gap analysis report from recent disruption responses.

title.en: Register the information security and compensating controls that apply during a disruption

description.en: Produce the list the control calls for: every information security control that must keep operating while the organisation is disrupted, and every compensating control that stands in when a primary one cannot. Against each entry record which control it compensates for, the scenario in which it is invoked, and who operates it under those conditions — a compensating control with no named operator is one nobody will apply on the day. Where a primary control is simply accepted as unavailable during a disruption, record it as accepted with the approver rather than leaving it off the list. Attach the register.

evidenceHint.en: Register of disruption-time information security controls and compensating controls, each showing the control it substitutes for, the scenario that invokes it, its named operator, and any control formally accepted as unavailable with its approver

title.en: Write the disruption-time information security requirements into the BCP and ICT continuity plan

description.en: Both plans have to say what information security looks like while they are being executed rather than assuming normal conditions: which access route is used when the usual one is unavailable and who authorises it, how information is protected at the alternate site or on the alternate service, what logging continues and where it lands, and how data handled on a workaround path is brought back under control afterwards. Cross-reference each requirement to the register entry that implements it, so neither document carries a requirement nothing delivers. Attach both issued plan versions showing their security sections.

evidenceHint.en: Issued BCP and ICT continuity plan versions containing the disruption-time information security sections, each requirement cross-referenced to the control register entry that delivers it

text.en: Record the access route used when normal authentication or network paths are unavailable, and its authoriser.
State how information is protected at each alternate site or alternate service named in the plans.
State which logging and monitoring continues during a disruption, and where the records land.
Describe how data created on a workaround path is reconciled and re-secured once normal service returns.
Cross-reference every requirement to the register entry implementing it and close the ones with no entry.

title.en: Test the BCP and record whether each security requirement held through the exercise

description.en: When the business continuity plan is exercised, judge it against its security requirements as well as its recovery timings: for each requirement in the plan's security section, record whether it held, degraded or was bypassed during the exercise, and what the participants actually did in the moment. Bypasses are the finding this task exists to surface, so record the bypass and the reason rather than the corrected behaviour somebody supplies afterwards. Raise a plan or control item with a named owner for every requirement that did not hold. Attach the test record and the review notes taken during it.

evidenceHint.en: BCP test and review record giving the scenario and, per security requirement, a held, degraded or bypassed outcome with the observed behaviour and any item raised with a named owner

title.en: Record the response actions and the state of each security control for every disruption

description.en: For every real disruption, capture what was done and what it cost in security terms: the actions taken and by whom, which controls from the register were invoked, which primary controls lapsed and for how long, and any access granted or restriction relaxed to keep the business running. Record when each relaxation was reversed — an emergency access that outlives the emergency is precisely the exposure this record is designed to catch, and it is invisible unless the reversal date is captured beside the grant. Attach the disruption response log for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Disruption response log for the period, per event giving the response actions and actors, the compensating controls invoked, the primary controls that lapsed with their duration, and the reversal date of every relaxation granted

title.en: Compare each disruption-time control against the corresponding industry practice

description.en: Build the compliance matrix the control asks for: one row per entry in the disruption-control register, against it the recognised practice for that control under disrupted conditions, and a verdict of meets, partially meets or falls short with the specific difference named. Cite the standard or guidance each comparison is drawn from so a verdict can be re-checked rather than taken on trust, and record an owner against every row that falls short. Attach the matrix with its citations.

evidenceHint.en: Compliance matrix comparing every registered disruption control against the cited industry practice, with a meets, partially-meets or falls-short verdict, the named difference, and an owner for each shortfall

title.en: Produce a gap analysis from the disruption responses of the period

description.en: Read the disruption response log and the BCP test record together and identify where the security response fell short of the plan: requirements bypassed under pressure, compensating controls never invoked because nobody knew of them, relaxations that were not reversed, and controls that failed without anyone noticing at the time. For each gap record whether the fix belongs in the plan, in the control register or in training, and name the owner and target date. Feed the accepted changes back into the plans, so the analysis alters something rather than describing it. Attach the gap analysis report.

evidenceHint.en: Gap analysis report drawn from the period's disruption responses and BCP test, listing each gap, the event that revealed it, whether it is a plan, control or training fix, and the owner and target date

controls.title: POS SSL/TLS Security Assurance
controls.objective: Ensure all POS POI terminals are not susceptible to any known exploits for SSL/early TLS and maintain verified documentation to prove compliance.
controls.successCriteria:
All POS POI terminals must have up-to-date and complete documentation verifying their security against known exploits for SSL/early TLS.
Patch and update logs must show that terminals were updated promptly in response to new vulnerabilities.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain a list of all POS POI terminals in use from the Asset Inventory.
Collect documentation proving each terminal's compliance with SSL/early TLS security, including vendor attestations, system/network configuration details.
Gather a list of all security patches and updates applied to the POS POI terminals since the last audit.

Analysis:
Cross-reference each POS POI terminal against the latest known vulnerabilities for SSL/early TLS to confirm there is no susceptibility.
Verify the documentation for its completeness and relevance to each POS POI terminal.
Review the patch and update history to ensure immediate action has been taken for any new vulnerabilities discovered since the last audit.

Output:
A report detailing each POS POI terminal and its compliance status with SSL/early TLS security requirements.
Documentation verification logs for each POS POI terminal.
A history log of patches and updates applied to POS POI terminals.

title.en: Extract every POS POI terminal in service from the asset inventory into a terminal register

description.en: The auditor's first request is the list of POS POI terminals in use, and it is the denominator every later task counts against — one documentation pack per row, one patch history per row, one compliance verdict per row. Build it from the asset inventory rather than from a procurement or shipment record, and give each terminal its own row carrying the make and model, the firmware or software version currently installed, the site it stands on, and the named owner who can produce it for inspection. A terminal held in a stockroom or awaiting return is still in the population until it is recorded as decommissioned. Attach the register with the date it was compiled and no blank firmware version.

evidenceHint.en: Dated POS POI terminal register drawn from the asset inventory: make, model, installed firmware version, site and named owner for every terminal

title.en: Assemble the documentation proving each terminal is not susceptible to SSL and early TLS exploits

description.en: Against every row of the register, file the evidence that the terminal does not offer SSL or early TLS: the vendor attestation naming that make, model and firmware, and the system and network configuration detail showing which protocol versions and cipher suites the terminal and the endpoint it connects to will actually negotiate. Vendor marketing material naming no protocol version is not an attestation — record that row as undocumented instead, because the gap list is the finding this task produces and it is what the later verdict rests on. Attach the documentation pack indexed by terminal, with the undocumented rows listed at the front.

evidenceHint.en: Documentation pack indexed by terminal — vendor attestation naming model and firmware, plus system and network configuration showing the protocol versions negotiated — with the list of terminals holding no attestation

text.en: Request from each terminal vendor an attestation naming the model and firmware version in service.
Capture the protocol versions and cipher suites each terminal is configured to negotiate.
Capture the same detail for the endpoint the terminal connects to, so both ends are evidenced.
List every terminal for which no attestation or configuration evidence could be obtained.

title.en: Log every security patch and firmware update applied to the POS POI terminals

description.en: Each time a terminal is patched or its firmware updated, write a row carrying the terminal identifier, the version before and after, the advisory or vulnerability the update answers where one prompted it, the date that advisory was published, the date the update reached that terminal, and who applied it. Where the vendor pushes updates without the entity's involvement, export their update report and file it in the same log rather than leaving those terminals blank. This log is what shows terminals were updated promptly rather than merely that a patching process exists. Attach the log covering the period since the last audit.

evidenceHint.en: Patch and update history log for POS POI terminals since the last audit: terminal, version before and after, advisory answered, publication date, applied date and operator

title.en: Cross-reference every terminal against the current SSL and early TLS advisories and record a susceptibility verdict

description.en: Take the currently published exploits and advisories for SSL and early TLS and read them against each register row's model, firmware version and negotiated protocol configuration, producing a susceptible or not-susceptible verdict per terminal with the advisory reference that decided it. A not-susceptible verdict must cite the attestation or the configuration output it rests on; a terminal with no documentation is reported as unverified, never as compliant. For every susceptible or unverified terminal name the accountable owner and the remediation agreed. Attach the report together with the raw configuration output it was derived from.

evidenceHint.en: POS POI compliance report giving each terminal a susceptibility verdict against named SSL and early TLS advisories, the evidence each verdict rests on, and an owner plus remediation for every susceptible or unverified terminal

title.en: Verify each terminal's documentation is complete and still matches its installed firmware

description.en: Documentation goes stale the moment a terminal is updated, so read every attestation and configuration record against the firmware version the register shows installed today. Record per terminal whether documentation exists, whether it names the version actually running, and the date it was issued, marking as expired anything describing a superseded version. The output is the documentation verification log the control calls for, and it is what distinguishes a documented estate from one holding a folder of old paper. Attach the log with a re-documentation item raised against every expired or missing row.

evidenceHint.en: Documentation verification log listing, per terminal, whether documentation exists, the firmware version it covers, its issue date, and a current, expired or missing verdict

title.en: Measure the interval between each SSL and early TLS advisory and the patch reaching every terminal

description.en: For each advisory published since the last audit, read the patch log and calculate how long the fix took to reach each affected terminal, listing separately those still unpatched at the end of the period. Where the delay was caused by the vendor rather than the entity, say so and give the date the update was made available, so the finding sits with whoever can act on it. Attach the timeliness analysis; it is the evidence that action was taken promptly rather than eventually.

evidenceHint.en: Patch timeliness analysis: per advisory and terminal, the publication date, the applied date, the elapsed interval, and the list of terminals still unpatched at period end

controls.title: Application Security Compliance
controls.objective: Ensure that all applications, whether developed in-house or acquired, meet established information security requirements.
controls.successCriteria:
All applications have documented security requirements aligned with the organization's application security policy.
Security testing and code reviews have been conducted for all applications, with documented resolution of identified vulnerabilities.
No critical security vulnerabilities remain unaddressed in the reviewed applications.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain a list of all applications developed or acquired during the audit period.
Gather documentation of security requirements for each application, including risk assessments, design documents, and security testing reports.
Collect records of security code reviews and penetration test results for each application.

Analysis:
For each application, verify that security requirements were identified and documented during the development or acquisition phase.
Assess the completeness and adequacy of the security requirements against the organization’s application security policy.
Review security testing reports and code review records to ensure that all identified vulnerabilities were addressed and mitigated.
Compare penetration test results with initial security requirements to ensure that applications meet the desired security standards.

Output:
A report detailing the security requirements documentation for each application.
A comparison matrix of identified vs. implemented security measures for each application.
A summary of security testing outcomes and any outstanding vulnerabilities or issues.

title.en: List every application developed or acquired during the period, marking in-house or acquired

description.en: The control covers applications however they arrived, so the list has to include software bought, subscribed to or inherited as well as what was built in-house - an acquired application is the row most often missing, and it is the one whose security requirements are least likely to have been written down. Compile it from release records, procurement records and the software asset inventory, and record for each application its owner, whether it was developed or acquired, the date it entered service, and the data it handles. Attach the dated list with the in-house or acquired value populated on every row: it is the population the requirements, code review, testing and matrix tasks all run against.

evidenceHint.en: Dated list of applications developed or acquired in the period, each with its owner, an in-house or acquired marker, its entry-into-service date and the data it handles

text.en: Compile the list from release records, procurement records and the software asset inventory.
Include applications acquired, subscribed to or inherited, not only those built in-house.
Record the owner and the data each application handles against its row.
Populate the in-house or acquired marker on every row before treating the list as complete.

title.en: Document the security requirements and risk assessment for each application on the list

description.en: For every application on the list, record the security requirements set for it and the risk assessment behind them: what the application must protect, the controls it must carry - authentication, authorisation, encryption, logging - and the risks the assessment identified with the requirement each one raised. The point of the record is that the requirements were set during development or acquisition, so date each set and cite the design document or procurement record it came from; a requirement written after the fact is recorded as such rather than presented as original. Read every set back against the application security policy and close the gaps that comparison exposes. Attach the requirements and the risk assessment for each application.

evidenceHint.en: Security requirements document and risk assessment per application, dated to the development or acquisition stage and cross-referenced to the application security policy

title.en: Record the security code review for each application with the disposition of every finding

description.en: Run or obtain a security code review for each application on the list - for an acquired application that is the supplier's review, or the review of whatever code the organisation holds and configures - and record who reviewed it, when, what was covered, and each finding with its severity and disposition. A finding is dispositioned as fixed with the change reference, accepted with the reason and the approver, or open with an owner and a target date; a review whose findings carry no disposition evidences nothing about resolution. Where an application received no review at all, record that against its row as the gap it is. Attach the code review records for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Security code review record per application showing the reviewer, date and scope, and every finding with its severity and disposition - fixed with change reference, accepted with approver, or open with owner and date

title.en: Record the penetration test result for each application and track each vulnerability to closure

description.en: For each application on the list, hold the security testing and penetration test results together with a remediation tracker that carries every vulnerability they raised through to a closed state. The tracker records the vulnerability, its severity, the application it affects, the owner, the fix or accepted-risk decision, and the date the state changed, so that 'was it addressed?' has an answer per vulnerability rather than per report. A vulnerability marked fixed carries the change reference or verification record behind that verdict, since the claim being evidenced is that it was addressed and mitigated rather than merely triaged. Attach the test reports for the period together with the tracker extract showing the state of every vulnerability raised.

evidenceHint.en: Penetration test and security testing reports per application, plus the remediation tracker extract showing each vulnerability's severity, owner and current state and the change reference or verification record behind any fix

text.en: Hold the test report for each application and the date the testing was carried out.
Enter every vulnerability raised into the tracker with its severity and affected application.
Record the fix or the accepted-risk decision, with its approver, against each vulnerability.
Record the change reference or verification record behind every vulnerability marked fixed.
Report the vulnerabilities still open at period end with their owners and target dates.

title.en: Build the comparison matrix of required against implemented security measures per application

description.en: Take each application's documented security requirements and record, measure by measure, whether it was implemented, partly implemented or absent, citing the design document, configuration or test result that evidences the verdict - that matrix is the artifact the control's output calls for. Reading the penetration test results back against the original requirements is what makes it more than a self-assessment: a requirement stated and then contradicted by a test finding is scored on the test. Every measure scored partly implemented or absent carries an owner and a remediation date. Attach the matrix with the evidence references and the remediation entries filled in.

evidenceHint.en: Comparison matrix of identified against implemented security measures per application, each verdict citing the evidence behind it and each shortfall carrying an owner and remediation date

title.en: Report the vulnerabilities outstanding at period end and account for every critical one

description.en: Close the control with a statement over the whole population: list every vulnerability still open across the applications on the list, ordered by severity, with the application it affects, its age, its owner and the date it is due to be cleared. The critical ones are what the control turns on - for each, state either the fix in flight with its date or the compensating control and the manager who accepted the risk, because an unaddressed critical with neither is a control failure rather than a backlog item. Attach the outstanding-vulnerability report together with the summary of the period's testing outcomes it was drawn from.
