evidenceHint.en: Outstanding-vulnerability report at period end listing every open vulnerability by severity with its application, age, owner and due date, and for each critical the fix in flight or the accepted-risk record and its approver

controls.title: Data Specification Management
controls.objective: Ensure the identification and definition of data specifications required to support the use of products and services.
controls.successCriteria:
All data specifications are accurately defined, including detailed descriptions of population, elements, sources, and measurements.
Metadata accurately and completely describes each data element and the data population.
Effective communication of data definitions and specifications to all relevant stakeholders.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the documentation outlining data specifications for all key products and services.
Collect metadata descriptions and usage guidelines for the data sets used.
Gather records showing communication of data definitions and purposes to relevant stakeholders.

Analysis:
Review the documentation to verify that it includes comprehensive data specifications (e.g., population, nature of elements, sources, units of measurement).
Assess the metadata for completeness and accuracy.
Evaluate communication records to ensure proper dissemination of data specifications and definitions.

Output:
Compiled documentation of data specifications.
Analysis report on metadata completeness and accuracy.
Log of communications pertaining to data definitions and specifications.

title.en: Identify the data sets each key product and service depends on

description.en: List the products and services in scope and, against each, the data sets it consumes or produces, the system of record for each, and the owner accountable for that data set's definition. Where two products use what is called the same data set, record whether it is genuinely one set or two with a shared name — that distinction is the one that later makes two teams read the same specification differently. Build the list from the data actually flowing into each product rather than from an architecture diagram, so a set assembled informally still appears. Attach the register; it is the population the specification, the metadata and the communication log are all measured against.

evidenceHint.en: Register of key products and services with the data sets each depends on, the system of record for each set, and the accountable data owner

title.en: Define the population, elements, sources and units of measurement for each data set

description.en: Write the specification for every data set in the register so it states what the data actually is: the population it covers and the rule that decides membership of it, the elements it contains, the source each element comes from, and the unit of measurement or currency where a value is quantitative. Be explicit about the population boundary and the exclusions, since two consumers disagreeing about who is in the set is the failure this specification exists to prevent. Where an element's source cannot be established, record it as unsourced and name the owner who will trace it rather than writing a plausible origin. Attach the issued specifications covering every register row.

evidenceHint.en: Issued data specification per registered data set, stating population and membership rule, elements, the source of each element and the units of measurement used

text.en: State the population each data set covers and the rule for membership of it.
Record the exclusions from that population and the reason each is excluded.
List the elements the data set contains and the source system each comes from.
Record the unit of measurement, currency or scale for every quantitative element.
Mark any element whose source cannot be established and name an owner to trace it.

title.en: Record metadata for every data element: definition, type, permitted values and usage guideline

description.en: Populate the metadata for each element named in the specifications: a definition written so a consumer who did not build the system can read it, the data type, the permitted values or range, the treatment of nulls and unknowns, and the guideline for what the element may and may not be used for. Hold it where consumers actually look — the catalogue, the schema, the data dictionary — rather than in a document beside the specification, and record where that is. An element carrying a name and a type but no definition is not described, and it is the row the completeness test will report. Attach the metadata export showing full coverage of the specified elements.

evidenceHint.en: Metadata export covering every specified data element with its definition, type, permitted values, null treatment and usage guideline, and the catalogue or dictionary it is published in

title.en: Publish each new or changed data definition to the stakeholders that use it

description.en: When a data set or element definition is created or changed, send it to the consumers the register identifies and record the communication: what the definition now says, the purpose the data serves, the effective date, who it went to and by what route. Keep the artefact — the notice, the release note, the catalogue change entry — rather than a note that it was announced, because this control asks for records showing communication of data definitions and purposes to relevant stakeholders. Where a change alters the meaning of an element already in use, say so explicitly in the communication rather than relying on the reader to notice. Attach the communication log for the period with the underlying notices.

evidenceHint.en: Data definition communication log for the period, each entry giving the definition or change communicated, the purpose the data serves, the effective date, the recipients and the route, with the notice or release note that carried it attached

title.en: Test the recorded metadata against the live data sets for completeness and accuracy

description.en: Take a sample of elements across the register and compare the metadata against the data actually held: does the live population match the stated membership rule, do observed values fall inside the permitted range, does the type hold, and are nulls behaving as the metadata says. Then check coverage in the other direction — elements present in the live data set with no metadata at all, and metadata for elements that no longer exist. Produce the analysis report with a per-element result and, for each discrepancy, whether the metadata or the data is wrong and who owns the correction. Attach the report with the extracts the comparison was run on.

evidenceHint.en: Metadata completeness and accuracy analysis giving a per-element result against the live data, the undocumented and orphaned elements found, and an owner for each correction

controls.title: Employment Agreement Compliance
controls.objective: Ensure all employees, contractors, and third parties adhere to the information security responsibilities and legal obligations outlined in their employment contractual agreements.
controls.successCriteria:
All employment contracts and confidentiality agreements include comprehensive information security responsibilities and legal obligations.
Actual practices of handling information security and legal responsibilities are in full compliance with the terms stated in the agreements.
Disciplinary actions for non-compliance are consistently applied in accordance with the terms of employment.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain copies of employment contracts, confidentiality agreements, and other relevant documents for all employees, contractors, and third parties.
Gather documentation detailing information classification responsibilities, legal rights and responsibilities, and procedures for handling information from interested parties.
Collect records of disciplinary actions taken for non-compliance with information security requirements.

Analysis:
Review employment contracts and confidentiality agreements to verify the inclusion of information security responsibilities and legal obligations.
Compare the documented responsibilities with actual practices to assess adherence.
Examine records of disciplinary actions to ensure they align with the terms stated in the employment agreements.

Output:
A report summarizing the review of employment contracts and confidentiality agreements.
A compliance matrix comparing stated responsibilities in agreements with actual practices.
A summary of disciplinary actions taken, correlated with the respective breaches of employment terms.

title.en: Assemble the employment or engagement agreement held for every employee, contractor and third party

description.en: Build the inventory the review runs against: one row per person or party, the type of agreement they hold — employment contract, contractor agreement, third-party engagement — the version or date it was executed, and where the document is held. Carry the confidentiality agreement and any supplementary information security undertaking as separate columns, because the control's requirements may be split across more than one document and an obligation found in none of them is the gap this control looks for. Attach the inventory with the date it was compiled and no row lacking a document reference.

evidenceHint.en: Agreement inventory listing each employee, contractor and third party, the agreement type and version they hold, any supplementary undertaking, and where each document is held

title.en: Record the information security and legal clauses each agreement type must carry

description.en: Write the clause checklist the agreements are scored against, taking it from what the entity needs people bound to: the information classification responsibilities they hold, their legal rights and responsibilities over information they create or receive, and their obligation to follow the entity's procedures for handling information received from interested parties. Set the checklist separately for employees, contractors and third parties wherever the obligations differ. Legal/DPO approves the wording and confirms enforceability. Attach the checklist and the currently issued templates that satisfy it.

evidenceHint.en: Approved clause checklist per agreement type covering information classification responsibilities, legal rights and responsibilities, and handling of information received from interested parties, with the issued templates that satisfy it

text.en: List the information classification responsibilities each engagement type must accept.
State the legal rights and responsibilities over information created or received.
Reference the procedure for handling information received from interested parties.

title.en: Publish the procedure for handling information received from interested parties that the agreements bind people to

description.en: An agreement clause pointing at a procedure is only as good as the procedure, so issue the document it refers to: how information received from customers, suppliers, regulators and other interested parties is classified on receipt, who may handle it, and what restrictions the receiving agreement places on its use. Name in it the classification responsibilities the agreement clause assigns, so the two documents cannot read differently. Attach the issued procedure with its version and the date it was made available to staff and contractors.

evidenceHint.en: Issued procedure for handling information received from interested parties, versioned and dated, showing classification on receipt, who may handle it, and the restrictions placed on its use

title.en: Record every disciplinary action taken for a breach of the information security terms of employment

description.en: For each case where a person breached an information security responsibility their agreement binds them to, record the clause breached, what happened, who investigated, the action taken, the date, and the term of employment the action rests on. Where a case closed with no action, record why. HR holds the record and Security engineering supplies the technical account of the breach. Attach the disciplinary record for the period; it is what shows the agreement's terms are enforced rather than merely stated.

evidenceHint.en: Record of disciplinary actions for information security breaches in the period, each naming the agreement clause breached, the action taken, the date and the term of employment relied on

title.en: Score every agreement against the clause checklist and report the contracts missing a required clause

description.en: Read each agreement in the inventory against the checklist for its type and mark every required clause present, absent, or expressed in superseded terms. Report by clause as well as by person, so a clause missing from an entire generation of contracts appears as one finding rather than fifty. Before calling an absence a gap, check whether the obligation is picked up by a separate undertaking on the same row. Attach the review report with the list of agreements requiring amendment or re-signature.

evidenceHint.en: Contract review report scoring every agreement against its clause checklist, reported by clause and by signatory, with the list of agreements requiring amendment or re-signature

title.en: Compare the responsibilities stated in the agreements against observed practice in a compliance matrix

description.en: An agreement clause is a claim about behaviour, so test a sample of them: for each responsibility the agreements impose — classifying information, handling material received from interested parties, observing the legal rights and responsibilities the agreement states — find what people actually did and record the evidence beside the clause. Draw the sample across employees, contractors and third parties so no engagement type is assumed compliant. Mark each responsibility met, partially met or not met, and name an accountable owner and a date against every not-met row. Attach the matrix with the evidence it cites.

evidenceHint.en: Compliance matrix setting each agreement responsibility against the practice observed, with the evidence cited, a met, partially met or not met verdict, and a named owner and date for every gap

controls.title: BCMS Awareness and Training
controls.objective: Ensure that all personnel are aware of the business continuity policy, their roles and responsibilities, and the importance of adhering to BCMS requirements.
controls.successCriteria:
All employees have completed mandatory BCMS training.
Training materials comprehensively cover required topics.
Regular and clear communication of BCMS information.
100% of employees have signed acknowledgements.
High pass rate on assessments/quizzes indicating sufficient understanding of BCMS.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:

Training Records:

Obtain a list of all employees and contractors.
Get copies of attendance records for BCMS training sessions.
Obtain training materials (slides, handouts, etc.) used in the sessions.

Communication Logs:

Retrieve records of communications sent regarding BCMS policy and procedures (emails, memos, intranet posts).
Get screenshots or copies of announcements related to business continuity.

Employee Acknowledgements:

Obtain signed acknowledgements from employees confirming their understanding of the BCMS policy and their roles.
Collect records of any assessments or quizzes conducted to test understanding of BCMS topics.

Analysis:

Training Participation:

Verify that all employees have participated in mandatory BCMS training sessions.
Ensure that training materials cover all required topics (business continuity policy, roles and responsibilities, implications of non-conformance).

Communication Effectiveness:

Review communication logs to confirm that information about BCMS is regularly and effectively disseminated.
Ensure that key messages about roles and responsibilities before, during, and after disruptions are clearly communicated.

Acknowledgements and Understanding:

Check that all employees have signed acknowledgements.
Review assessment results to ensure employees have a sufficient understanding of the BCMS.

Output:

Attendance records and training materials.
Communication logs and copies of announcements.
Signed employee acknowledgements and assessment results.
A report summarizing compliance with the awareness requirements and any identified gaps.

title.en: Register every employee and contractor required to complete BCMS training

description.en: This control is tested on completion against a population, so the population is written down first: every employee and every contractor working under the organisation's control, with their department, start date, and the manager responsible for chasing their completion. Take it from HR and contractor records on a stated date rather than from a mailing list, because a mailing list is precisely the artefact that omits recent joiners. Mark each row employee or contractor, since both are in scope and completion has to be reported across the whole population rather than the payroll alone. Attach the dated roster; every completion and acknowledgement figure in this control is measured against it.

evidenceHint.en: Dated roster of employees and contractors in scope for BCMS training, showing department, start date, and whether the person is an employee or a contractor

text.en: Take the population from HR and contractor records rather than from an existing mailing list.
Include contractors and temporary staff working under the organisation's control.
Mark each row employee or contractor so completion is reported across the whole population.
Date the roster and name the manager accountable for chasing each person's completion.

title.en: Build the BCMS training material so it covers the policy, the roles and the consequences of non-conformance

description.en: Produce the material actually delivered in the session — slides, handouts, the e-learning module — and make sure it covers the three topics this control is tested on: the business continuity policy and why the organisation holds one, what each person is expected to do before, during and after a disruption, and the implications of not conforming to BCMS requirements. Say concretely what before, during and after means for the audience being trained: where the plan lives, how they will be contacted, where they report, what they must not do. Version and date the material so the attendance records tie to what was actually taught. Attach the training material as issued.

evidenceHint.en: Versioned BCMS training material covering the business continuity policy, the individual's role before, during and after a disruption, and the implications of non-conformance

text.en: Cover the business continuity policy and the reason the organisation holds one.
State in concrete terms what each person does before, during and after a disruption.
State the implications of not conforming to BCMS requirements.
Version and date the material so attendance records tie to what was taught.

title.en: Train every person on the roster and record attendance and assessment results

description.en: Deliver the training and, for each session, keep the attendance record naming who attended, the date, the version of the material used and who delivered it. Where the session ends in an assessment or quiz, record each person's result and whether it reached the mark that counts as a pass, and record the follow-up given to anyone who did not reach it. Reconcile attendance back to the roster at the end of each cycle so that what is outstanding is a list of named people rather than a completion percentage. Attach the attendance records and the assessment results for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Attendance records per session naming the attendees, the date, the material version and the trainer, together with each attendee's assessment result and pass or fail outcome

title.en: Collect a signed acknowledgement from every person on the roster

description.en: Each person confirms in writing that they have received the training, understand the business continuity policy, and know what their own role requires of them. Keep the signed acknowledgement — wet signature, e-signature or a recorded system acceptance — with the date it was given and the version of the policy it refers to, so an acknowledgement given against a superseded policy version can be identified rather than counted as current. Chase the outstanding names against the roster rather than reporting a coverage figure. Attach the acknowledgement set together with the list of people still outstanding and the date each was last chased.

evidenceHint.en: Signed BCMS acknowledgements showing the date and the policy version each refers to, plus the named list of roster members still outstanding

title.en: Log every BCMS communication issued, with a copy of what was sent

description.en: Keep a running log of the communications that hold business continuity in front of people between training cycles — policy announcements, plan updates, drill notices, post-incident messages. Record for each the date, the channel (email, memo, intranet post), the audience it reached and who issued it, and keep the message itself or a screenshot of it with the entry. The log is what evidences regular and clear communication, and a channel that carried nothing for a whole period shows up in it as a gap rather than passing unnoticed. Attach the communication log for the period with the retained copies.

evidenceHint.en: BCMS communication log for the period recording the date, channel, audience and issuer of each communication, with a copy or screenshot of each message retained

title.en: Measure training, assessment and acknowledgement coverage against the roster and name the gaps

description.en: Set the attendance records, the assessment results and the signed acknowledgements against the roster and produce the awareness compliance report: how much of the population has completed each, and — more usefully — exactly who has not. Report the assessment outcomes as the distribution of results rather than an average, since a small group failing is the finding an average hides. Give every gap a named owner and a date by which it will be closed, and note any topic the assessment results suggest the material covers poorly, so the next revision of the material is driven by evidence. Attach the report with the underlying records it was compiled from.

evidenceHint.en: Awareness compliance report setting the training, assessment and acknowledgement records against the roster, naming every person outstanding and the owner and date for each gap

controls.title: BCMS Documentation and Capability Evaluation
controls.objective: Ensure the continuous evaluation and improvement of business continuity documentation and capabilities to maintain organizational resilience and compliance with legal, regulatory, and industry standards.
controls.successCriteria:
All BIA, RA, strategies, solutions, plans, and procedures are current and have undergone regular reviews as per the planned intervals.
Evaluations comprehensively cover all required aspects, including partners' and suppliers' capabilities.
Compliance with all applicable legal and regulatory requirements, industry best practices, and internal business continuity policies and objectives is demonstrated.
Documentation and procedures are promptly updated following evaluations, incidents, activations, and significant changes.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:

Obtain the latest versions of the Business Impact Analysis (BIA), Risk Assessment (RA), strategies, solutions, plans, and procedures.
Collect records of evaluations conducted, including reviews, analysis reports, exercise results, test outcomes, post-incident reports, and performance evaluations.
Retrieve documentation of evaluations conducted on the business continuity capabilities of relevant partners and suppliers.
Gather evidence of compliance checks against legal and regulatory requirements, industry best practices, and internal business continuity policies and objectives.
Collect records of updates made to documentation and procedures following evaluations, incidents, activations, and significant changes.

Analysis:

Verify that the BIA, RA, strategies, solutions, plans, and procedures are up-to-date and have been reviewed at the planned intervals.
Analyze evaluation records to ensure they cover reviews, analyses, exercises, tests, post-incident reports, and performance evaluations.
Check that evaluations include assessments of partners' and suppliers' business continuity capabilities.
Compare compliance documentation against legal and regulatory requirements, industry best practices, and internal policies and objectives to ensure adherence.
Confirm that documentation and procedures have been updated in a timely manner following evaluations, incidents, activations, and significant changes.

Output:

Compilation of the latest versions of BIA, RA, strategies, solutions, plans, and procedures.
Detailed report summarizing the findings of reviews, analyses, exercises, tests, post-incident reports, and performance evaluations.
Evaluation summary of partners' and suppliers' business continuity capabilities.
Compliance checklist against legal and regulatory requirements, industry best practices, and internal policies and objectives.
Log of updates made to documentation and procedures.

title.en: Register every BCMS document with its version, owner and planned review interval

description.en: Produce one row per document the BCMS depends on — the business impact analysis, the risk assessment, the continuity strategies and solutions, the plans and the procedures — carrying the current version and issue date, the owner, the date it was last reviewed, and the interval at which review is planned. The register is what turns 'reviewed at planned intervals' into a checkable statement: without the planned interval written against each document, currency can only be asserted. Include documents held by teams outside the continuity function, since those are the ones that quietly go stale. Attach the register with the location of each current version.

evidenceHint.en: BCMS document register listing the BIA, risk assessment, strategies, solutions, plans and procedures with version, owner, last review date and planned review interval

title.en: Evaluate the BCMS on the planned schedule and file the record each review, exercise and test produces

description.en: Work through the evaluation activities the BCMS relies on — document reviews, analyses, exercises, tests, post-incident reports and performance evaluations — and file the record each one produces: what was evaluated, when, by whom, what was found and what was recommended. Index them by the document or capability they evaluated, so the register can be read against them and it becomes visible which documents have actually been evaluated and which have only been scheduled. An exercise or test that produced no written outcome is recorded as such rather than counted as done. Attach the evaluation records for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Evaluation record set for the period covering reviews, analyses, exercises, tests, post-incident reports and performance evaluations, each naming the evaluator, the date, the findings and the recommendations

title.en: Assess each relevant partner's and supplier's business continuity capability

description.en: For every partner and supplier the business impact analysis names as a dependency, obtain and assess evidence of their own continuity capability — their plan or a summary of it, their recovery objectives, and the outcome of their most recent test or exercise. Compare each against the recovery objective the business impact analysis sets for the activity that depends on them and record whether the supplier can support it. Where a supplier will not or cannot provide evidence, record that refusal as the outcome, because an unassessed dependency is a risk position to be accepted by someone rather than an empty row. Procurement holds the supplier relationship; the continuity owner makes the assessment. Attach the evaluation summary covering every dependency the analysis names.

evidenceHint.en: Partner and supplier continuity capability evaluation summary, one row per dependency, giving the evidence obtained, the supplier's recovery objectives, and whether they support the dependent activity

text.en: Take the population from the dependencies the business impact analysis records.
Obtain each supplier's continuity plan, recovery objectives and most recent test outcome.
Compare the supplier's objectives against the recovery objective set for the dependent activity.
Record a refusal or a non-response as the outcome rather than leaving the row blank.

title.en: Log every update to BCMS documentation with the trigger that caused it

description.en: Each time a BCMS document changes, add an entry naming the document, the version before and after, the date the update was issued, what changed, and — the part this control is tested on — the trigger: the evaluation, the incident, the plan activation or the significant organisational change that made the update necessary. Where an evaluation or an incident produced a recommendation and no document changed, record that decision and its reason in the same log, so a recommendation cannot simply disappear between the review and the next version. Attach the update log for the period.

evidenceHint.en: BCMS documentation update log naming, per update, the document, the version change, the issue date, what changed, and the evaluation, incident, activation or change that triggered it

title.en: Verify each registered document against its planned review interval and list those overdue

description.en: Read the register against the calendar: for every document compare the last review date and the planned interval against today, and mark it current or overdue with the number of days by which it has slipped. Confirm the review actually happened wherever one is claimed by naming the evaluation record that evidences it, since a last-review date with nothing behind it is a date somebody typed. Give every overdue document a named owner and a date for its review. Attach the currency check naming the version of the register it was run against.

evidenceHint.en: Document currency check listing every registered document as current or overdue, the evaluation record evidencing its last review, and an owner and date against each overdue item

title.en: Map each legal, regulatory, industry and internal continuity requirement to the evidence that satisfies it

description.en: Build the checklist from the obligations that actually bind this organisation's continuity arrangements — the legal and regulatory requirements it is subject to, the industry standards or best practice it has committed to, and its own business continuity policy and objectives — then score the BCMS against each line as met, partially met or not met, naming the document or record that satisfies it. A line marked met with nothing named against it is not evidence, and a line whose obligation nobody could confirm is recorded as unverified rather than passed. Every gap takes a named owner and a date. Attach the completed checklist with its evidence references.

evidenceHint.en: Completed compliance checklist scoring the BCMS against each legal, regulatory, industry and internal continuity requirement, naming the evidence behind every met line and an owner for each gap

text.en: List the legal and regulatory obligations that bind the organisation's continuity arrangements.
Add the industry standards or best practice the organisation has committed to follow.
Add the internal business continuity policy commitments and the stated objectives.
Score each line met, partially met or not met and name the evidence behind every met line.

controls.title: Information Backup Verification
controls.objective: To ensure that backups of information, software, and systems are conducted accurately and regularly, in alignment with the organization's backup policy.
controls.successCriteria:
All backups are conducted in accordance with the set schedule and backup policy.
Backup logs confirm the completion of scheduled backups without significant failures.
Backup testing exercises demonstrate the reliability and effectiveness of the backups in data restoration scenarios.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the latest backup schedule documentation.
Retrieve logs of recent backup activities.
Gather a list of critical systems and data requiring backup as per the backup policy.
Secure screenshots or reports demonstrating successful backup completions.
Acquire documentation of the last few backup testing exercises, including dates and outcomes.

Analysis:
Review the backup schedule against the backup policy to confirm adherence to prescribed frequency and types (full, incremental, differential).
For each logged backup activity, verify that it corresponds with the scheduled backups and includes all critical systems and data.
Assess the results of backup testing exercises to confirm the reliability and effectiveness of the backups in various scenarios, including potential data restoration.

Output:
A comprehensive report summarizing the findings from the backup schedule, logs, and testing exercises.
A spreadsheet or checklist comparing scheduled backups with actual backup logs.
A summary of backup testing exercises, indicating successes and areas for improvement.

title.en: List the critical systems and data the backup policy requires to be backed up

description.en: The comparison this control turns on is between what should have been backed up and what was, and this list is the first half of it. Work from the backup policy's own criteria for criticality and record one row per system and data set in scope, naming the system, the data it holds, the policy clause that puts it in scope and the owner. Include data sets that live outside the systems that generate them — file shares, hosted platforms and configuration repositories are the ones habitually missed, and a data set nobody claims is exactly what the analysis is meant to surface rather than what it should quietly omit. Attach the list with the version of the policy it was derived from.

evidenceHint.en: List of critical systems and data requiring backup, one row per system and data set, naming the policy clause that puts it in scope and its owner, with the policy version it was derived from

title.en: Record the backup type and frequency scheduled against each critical system

description.en: Extend the backup schedule so every row of the critical list carries the backup type in use — full, incremental or differential — and the frequency it runs at. Read each row back against what the backup policy requires for that class of system, and where the schedule falls short, record the shortfall on the schedule with a named owner rather than adjusting the policy to fit what is currently scheduled. A critical system with no schedule row at all is the gap this task exists to close, and it is closed by scheduling it, not by removing it from the list. Attach the schedule showing full coverage of the critical list.

evidenceHint.en: Backup schedule with one row per critical system giving the backup type and the frequency it runs at, cross-referenced to the critical list, with every shortfall against the policy's required type and frequency recorded and owned

text.en: Match every entry on the critical list to a schedule row and list the ones with none.
Record the backup type and the frequency it runs at on each schedule row.
Compare each row against the frequency and type the backup policy requires for it.
Record any shortfall against policy on the schedule itself with a named owner.

title.en: File the backup completion logs and success reports for every scheduled run in the period

description.en: Export the backup tool's activity log for the period and file it together with the completion reports or screenshots that show jobs finishing, so the record carries both the tool's own account and the confirmation an operator can read. Each entry needs the system, the job, the start and end time, the volume written and the outcome; where a job completed only partially, record it as partial rather than as a success, because a partial backup is the failure most likely to be discovered for the first time during a restore. Attach the activity log and the completion reports for the same period so the two can be read against each other.

evidenceHint.en: Backup activity log export for the period with the completion reports or screenshots, showing per job the system, start and end time, volume written and a success, partial or failure outcome

title.en: Restore data from backup in a test exercise and record the date, scope and outcome

description.en: Restore real data from a backup copy into an isolated location and confirm it is complete and usable: that the files or records open, that the volume matches what was backed up, and that the application which owns the data can read what came back. Record the exercise date, the system and data set restored, the backup copy used, how long the restore took, who performed it and the outcome, including whatever went wrong along the way, since the difficulties are the part that improves the next restore. Cover different backup types across successive exercises rather than repeating the easiest restore, because an incremental chain fails differently from a full copy. Attach the exercise record with evidence of what was restored.

evidenceHint.en: Backup test exercise record giving the date, the system and data restored, the backup copy used, the restore duration, the tester, and whether the restored data was complete and usable

text.en: Choose the system and backup copy to restore, varying the backup type across exercises.
Restore into an isolated location where the test cannot overwrite live data.
Confirm the restored data opens, is complete, and is readable by the owning application.
Record the restore duration and everything that went wrong during the exercise.
File the record with the date, the tester and the outcome stated plainly.

title.en: Compare the backup logs against the schedule and mark every missed or failed run

description.en: Build the checklist the control asks for: one row per scheduled backup for the period, the log entry that matches it, and a verdict of ran, missed, failed or partial. A run present in the log but absent from the schedule is recorded too, because an unscheduled backup is as much a schedule accuracy problem as a missing one. Every missed, failed or partial run carries its cause, the rerun that succeeded if one did, and the owner. State the coverage of the critical list explicitly, so that a system quietly dropped from the schedule appears as an uncovered system rather than as a clean sheet with nothing to report. Attach the completed checklist.

evidenceHint.en: Checklist comparing every scheduled backup for the period against the activity log, with a ran, missed, failed or partial verdict per run, the cause and owner of each exception, and the critical-list coverage stated

title.en: Summarise the restore exercises and raise an improvement item for every shortfall

description.en: Read the recent exercise records together rather than one at a time and produce the summary the control calls for: which systems have been restore-tested and which have not, what succeeded, and what the failures and the slow restores have in common. Record each restore duration and read the durations against one another, so that a restore which completed but took far longer than comparable ones is reported as a shortfall rather than filed as a success. Every shortfall becomes an improvement item with a named owner and a date, and the items still open from previous exercises are carried into the same summary. Attach the summary with the exercise records behind it.

evidenceHint.en: Summary of the recent backup test exercises naming the systems tested and untested, the outcome and duration of each exercise, and an improvement item with an owner for every shortfall

controls.title: Remote Work Security Compliance
controls.objective: To ensure that all aspects of remote working adhere to the organization’s security standards and policies.
controls.successCriteria:
All remote workers comply with the organization’s remote working policies and guidelines.
Remote devices are configured and secured as per the IT Security Policy standards.
Remote workers have completed necessary training and are aware of secure working practices.
Adequate physical security measures are in place at remote work locations.
Effective backup and emergency procedures are established and followed in remote working environments.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Collect remote working policies and guidelines issued by the organization.
Obtain a list of all employees engaged in remote work.
Gather records of remote access logs and usage data.
Acquire security configuration details of remote devices (laptops, mobile phones, etc.).
Retrieve documentation on training and awareness programs conducted for remote working.

Analysis:
Cross-reference the list of remote workers with the remote access logs to verify authorized access.
Review security configurations of remote devices against the IT Security Policy standards.
Assess whether remote workers have completed the required training for secure remote working.
Evaluate the physical security measures implemented at remote work locations.
Inspect procedures and practices for data backup and emergency responses in remote working settings.

Output:
A report summarizing the compliance status of each remote worker.
A spreadsheet detailing the security configuration of each remote device.
Documentation on training completion and awareness levels among remote workers.
An assessment of physical security measures at remote locations.
An analysis of backup and emergency procedures in place for remote work.

title.en: Register every remote worker with the devices they work from

description.en: Build one row per person engaged in remote work carrying their role, their manager, the type of location they work from, and every device they use to reach organisational systems — issued or personal, laptop, mobile or tablet. IT Operations supplies the device identifiers so each machine is recorded once under one serial or asset tag rather than twice under two descriptions of it. This is the denominator everything downstream counts against: the access-log reconciliation matches sessions to it, the configuration spreadsheet carries one row per device it names, and training completion is measured over its population. Attach the dated register; a worker with no device row, or a device with no named owner, is not done.

evidenceHint.en: Dated remote-worker register listing each remote worker with role, manager, location type and every device identifier they use for organisational access

text.en: Take the list of all employees engaged in remote work and the role each of them holds.
Add every device each worker uses to reach organisational systems, whether issued or personally owned.
Record the serial or asset tag for each device so every row names one identifiable machine.
Record the location type each worker operates from — home, co-working space or client site.
Date the register and hold it as the population every later task in this control is measured over.

title.en: Document the remote working guidelines covering physical security, backup and emergency response

description.en: Extend the issued remote-working guidelines so they state what a remote worker must actually do rather than what they should generally observe: the physical security expected where they work, covering device storage, screen visibility and who else has access to the space; the backup arrangement that covers work produced away from the office; and the emergency procedure to follow when a device is lost, stolen or compromised while remote. Each of those three is separately assessed later, so guidelines that cover only device configuration leave two of the assessments with nothing to measure against. Attach the issued version showing all three sections.

evidenceHint.en: Issued remote-working guidelines carrying distinct sections on physical security at remote locations, backup of remotely produced work, and emergency response to a lost or compromised remote device

title.en: Record each registered device's security configuration against the IT Security Policy standard

description.en: For every device the register names, capture the configuration actually in force — disk encryption state, screen lock and timeout, patch level, endpoint protection status, firewall state and remote-access client version — and set each observed value beside the value the IT Security Policy requires, marking the device compliant or deviating. Read the values from the device or its management console rather than from the worker's assurance. A device the management console has not reported on during the period is recorded as unverified rather than compliant, because an absent report and a passing report are not the same answer. Attach the spreadsheet with one row per device and a named owner against every deviation.

evidenceHint.en: Remote device configuration spreadsheet with one row per registered device showing observed values against the IT Security Policy standard, a compliant, deviating or unverified verdict, and an owner for each deviation

text.en: Export the current configuration for every device the remote-worker register names.
Record encryption state, screen lock, patch level and endpoint protection status per device.
Set each observed value beside the value the IT Security Policy requires for that device class.
Mark devices the management console has not reported on in the period as unverified, not compliant.
Name a remediation owner against every deviating device and every unverified device.

title.en: Reconcile the remote access logs against the remote-worker register

description.en: Take the remote access and usage logs for the period and match every authenticated remote session to a person on the register. Two residues matter and both are recorded: sessions from accounts that are not registered remote workers, and registered workers with no sessions at all. The first is unauthorised remote access until it is explained; the second usually means the register has gone stale. Disposition each unmatched session by naming the approval that covers it or referring it as an exception with an owner. Attach the log extract alongside the matched and unmatched lists, since an empty exception list evidences nothing unless the extract shows the logs were actually read.

evidenceHint.en: Remote access log extract for the period with the matched-session list and the dispositioned list of sessions with no registered worker and registered workers with no sessions

title.en: Track secure remote working training completion for every worker on the register

description.en: For each person on the remote-worker register, record whether they have completed the organisation's remote working training and awareness programme, the date they completed it, and which version of the material they took. Workers who joined the register after the last delivery are the population this task exists to surface, so record them as outstanding with a scheduled date rather than omitting them from the denominator. Where the training is delivered through a platform, export the completion data rather than re-keying it, and reconcile the export against the register so the two populations agree. HR supplies joiner dates so the outstanding list can be aged. Attach the completion record covering the full register.

evidenceHint.en: Training completion record covering every worker on the remote-worker register, showing completion date and material version, with the outstanding workers named and their scheduled dates

title.en: Assess remote locations' physical security, backup and emergency arrangements and report compliance per worker

description.en: Work down the register and evaluate, per worker, the physical security in place where they work, whether the work they produce away from the office is covered by a backup arrangement they actually follow, and whether they can state the emergency procedure for a lost or compromised device. A self-attestation questionnaire is an acceptable collection method provided the answers are held per worker and a subset is corroborated rather than every answer taken at face value. Roll this together with the configuration, access-log and training findings into one compliance status per remote worker, so the control's verdict is readable in a single place. Attach the assessment and the per-worker compliance report.

evidenceHint.en: Remote working compliance report giving a status per remote worker, backed by the per-location assessment of physical security, backup arrangements and emergency procedure awareness

text.en: Collect a per-worker account of device storage, screen visibility and who else can access the space.
Record the backup arrangement covering each worker's output and whether it is being followed.
Ask each worker to state the procedure for a lost, stolen or compromised device and record the answer.
Corroborate a sample of the attestations rather than accepting every answer at face value.
Combine configuration, access-log, training and location findings into one status per remote worker.

controls.title: Asset Inventory Management
controls.objective: Ensure a comprehensive and up-to-date inventory of all organizational assets, including detailed information on network and hardware addresses, machine names, data asset owners, departments, and network connection approvals.
controls.successCriteria:
The asset inventory is complete, accurate, and includes all required details such as network and hardware addresses, machine names, data asset owners, departments, and network approval status.
Ownership is correctly assigned and documented for all listed assets, with additional details accurately recorded.
Asset return forms are complete and comply with policy requirements.
Asset tracking logs confirm timely and proper return of assets, with all additional asset details appropriately documented.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the current Inventory of Information and Associated Assets document.
Gather ownership assignment records for each listed asset and signed asset return forms for terminated or changed employment cases.
Acquire logs of recent updates or changes made to the asset inventory and records of asset tracking upon employee exit.

Analysis:
Review the inventory document for completeness and accuracy, ensuring all assets are listed with appropriate details.
Cross-check ownership records against each asset and returned assets against the Asset Registry.
Analyze change logs and asset tracking logs to verify that inventory updates and asset returns are consistent, timely, and comply with policy.

Output:
A comprehensive report detailing findings from the inventory and asset return review.
A spreadsheet or database capturing the alignment of ownership records with the asset inventory and returned assets.
Summary of discrepancies or gaps identified during the analysis.

title.en: Populate machine name, network address, hardware address and department for every asset

description.en: The control names the fields the Inventory of Information and Associated Assets has to carry, and the inventory counts as complete only when every asset row holds them. Work through the register filling in the machine name, the network address, the hardware address and the owning department for each asset, taking the network and hardware addresses from the systems themselves or from the directory rather than from the original procurement record, which goes stale as hardware is replaced. Where an asset legitimately has no network address because it never connects, record that explicitly, so that a blank always means unfinished work rather than a judgement somebody already made. Attach the inventory export showing every row's fields populated together with the list of rows still incomplete.

evidenceHint.en: Inventory of Information and Associated Assets export with machine name, network address, hardware address and department populated on every asset row, plus the list of rows still carrying a blank

text.en: Read network and hardware addresses from the live systems or the directory, not from procurement records.
Record the owning department against each asset from the current organisational structure.
Record an explicit nil where an asset genuinely has no network or hardware address.
Run a completeness check over the export and list every row still carrying a blank field.

title.en: Assign a named data asset owner to every asset and file that owner's acceptance

description.en: The inventory is judged on ownership being correctly assigned and documented for every listed asset, which means a record naming an individual rather than a team mailbox or a department. Work down the inventory and, for each asset, identify the person accountable for the information it holds, put the assignment to them in writing stating what they are accepting — the assets listed against them and their return when employment or the role ends — and file their acceptance with the date they gave it. Assets whose proposed owner declines or does not respond are escalated to the department recorded against them rather than left assigned by default, since an unacknowledged assignment is the one nobody acts on. Attach the ownership assignment records covering every asset in the inventory.

evidenceHint.en: Ownership assignment records covering every asset in the inventory, each naming the individual data asset owner, what they accepted and the date they accepted it

title.en: Record the network connection approval status and approver against each asset

description.en: The inventory is required to carry whether an asset is approved to connect to the network and who approved it, so for every asset holding a network address record the approval state, the person who granted it and the date. An asset found connected with no recorded approval is marked unapproved and raised to its department owner for a decision rather than left with an empty field, because empty and unapproved are the two states most easily confused here. Where an asset no longer needs network access, the approval is withdrawn and the withdrawal dated in the same field, so the column reads as a current state rather than a historical grant. Attach the inventory export with the approval column populated and the unapproved assets listed separately.

evidenceHint.en: Inventory export carrying the network connection approval status, approver and approval date on every networked asset, with the list of assets connected without a recorded approval

title.en: Complete a signed asset return form at every exit and role change and log what came back

description.en: Whenever employment ends or a role changes, the assets the inventory shows assigned to that person are collected against that list, and the return form is signed both by the person returning and by the person receiving. Log each returned asset with its identifier, the date it came back and its disposition — returned to stock, reissued or destroyed — and record explicitly any asset the inventory expected that did not come back, because that outstanding item is the finding this task exists to surface. HR triggers the process at exit and IT Operations receives the hardware; the form is not closed while an expected asset is unaccounted for. Attach the signed forms for the period together with the asset tracking log they were recorded in.

evidenceHint.en: Signed asset return forms for every exit and role change in the period, with the asset tracking log showing return date, disposition and every asset still outstanding

text.en: Draw the leaver's assigned assets from the inventory before the return meeting takes place.
Record each asset returned with its identifier, return date and condition on the form.
Have both the returning person and the receiving person sign the completed form.
List every expected asset that did not come back and pass it to the department owner.
Update the inventory so the returned assets are no longer assigned to the leaver.

title.en: Record every asset addition, reassignment and retirement in the inventory change log

description.en: Each change to the inventory is written to its change log as it is made, carrying the asset identifier, what changed, who made the change and the date, so that the inventory's currency can be demonstrated rather than asserted. Retirements are logged with the disposal or return route the asset took rather than simply removed from the register, because a row that disappears cannot afterwards be distinguished from one deleted in error. Where the inventory tool keeps its own history, export that instead of maintaining a parallel manual log, and record separately any change made directly in the underlying store, since those are exactly the changes the tool's history will not contain. Attach the change log covering the period.

evidenceHint.en: Inventory change log for the period, one entry per addition, reassignment or retirement showing the asset, what changed, who made the change and the date

title.en: Reconcile the returned assets and the ownership records against the Asset Registry

description.en: Bring the three records together in one sheet: what the Asset Registry says exists and to whom it is issued, what the ownership assignment records say, and what the return log says came back. Every asset on which the three disagree is a discrepancy — an asset still issued to someone who has already left, an asset logged as returned but showing as issued, an asset with no ownership record at all — and each is recorded with the sources that conflict, a named owner and a date to clear it. Report the unresolved discrepancies as the summary of gaps the control calls for rather than folding them into a total. Attach the reconciliation sheet with that summary.

evidenceHint.en: Reconciliation spreadsheet aligning the Asset Registry, the ownership assignment records and the asset return log, with each discrepancy, the sources that conflict, its owner and a clearance date

text.en: Join the Asset Registry, the ownership records and the return log on the asset identifier.
Flag each asset the three sources disagree on and state which of them conflict.
Check that every asset issued to a departed employee appears in the return log.
Name an owner and a clearance date against every discrepancy in the sheet.

controls.title: Control Activities Implementation and Management
controls.objective: Ensure that control activities are effectively integrated into business processes, executed responsibly and timely, and periodically reassessed for relevance and effectiveness.
controls.successCriteria:
All control activities are clearly defined and aligned with business processes.
Clear responsibility and accountability for executing control activities are established and adhered to.
Control activities are performed within the specified timelines.
Corrective actions are appropriately and timely taken in response to issues identified.
Periodic reassessment and updating of control activities are conducted to ensure their continued relevance and effectiveness.
controls.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the documentation of established policies and procedures that detail control activities across various business units or functions.
Collect records of responsibility assignments for executing these policies and procedures.
Gather evidence of timely performance of control activities, such as logs, reports, or compliance tracking tools.
Secure documentation of any corrective actions taken in response to issues identified through control activities.
Access records of the latest reviews and updates made to the control activities.

Analysis:
Review the policies and procedures to verify they clearly define control activities and align with business processes.
Analyze responsibility assignment records to ensure clear accountability for the execution of control activities.
Examine evidence of control activities' performance to assess if they are conducted within defined timelines.
Evaluate corrective action documents to check for appropriate and timely responses to issues identified.
Assess the records of reviews and updates to control activities for evidence of periodic reassessment and relevance.

Output:
A report outlining the compliance of each business unit or function with the established control activities.
A spreadsheet or document detailing the responsibility assignments for control activities.
A timeline analysis showing the timeliness of control activities execution and corrective actions taken.
A summary report of the most recent reassessment and updating of control activities.

title.en: Catalogue the control activities each business unit performs and the process each supports

description.en: Work through the documented policies and procedures of every business unit or function and record one row per control activity: the activity, the unit that performs it, the business process it sits inside and the risk or requirement it addresses. An activity described in a procedure but performed by nobody, and an activity performed but written down nowhere, are both entries this catalogue exists to surface — record them and flag which of the two applies. The catalogue is the population that the responsibility assignment, the timeliness analysis and the reassessment all run against. Attach it with the source procedure reference behind each row.

evidenceHint.en: Control activity catalogue with one row per activity giving the performing business unit, the business process it supports and the source procedure reference

title.en: Record the accountable owner and the required frequency for every control activity

description.en: Against each catalogue row, name the individual accountable for the activity being performed, the person who performs it where that differs, and the frequency or deadline the activity must meet. The frequency has to be a value somebody can be late against — a stated interval, or a fixed count of days from a named trigger — and not a word like periodic, because the timeliness analysis later in this control cannot compute against an adjective. Where accountability is vacant or disputed, record it as unassigned and escalate rather than defaulting it to the unit head. Attach the responsibility assignment spreadsheet covering every row of the catalogue.

evidenceHint.en: Responsibility assignment spreadsheet naming the accountable owner, the performer and the required frequency or deadline for every catalogued control activity

text.en: Name the accountable owner for every activity in the control activity catalogue.
Name the performer separately wherever that is not the accountable owner.
State each activity's frequency or deadline as a value that can be measured against.
Mark activities whose ownership is vacant or disputed as unassigned and escalate them.
Confirm the spreadsheet covers every catalogue row before the assignment is issued.

title.en: Log each performance of a control activity with its due date and completion date

description.en: Every time a control activity runs, record the activity, the period it covers, the date it was due under its assigned frequency, the date it was actually completed and who performed it. Where a compliance tracking tool already holds this, export from the tool rather than re-keying it, and cover separately the activities performed outside that tool — those are the ones with no machine trace, and a timeliness analysis will otherwise report them as never performed at all. Attach the performance log or tracker export for the period under test.

evidenceHint.en: Control activity performance log or compliance tracker export for the period showing activity, period covered, due date, completion date and performer per occurrence

title.en: Record each issue a control activity identified and the corrective action taken

description.en: When a control activity finds an exception, open a row carrying the activity that found it, what was found, the date it was raised, the corrective action agreed, its owner and the date it closed. Actions still open at period end stay on the register with their target date rather than being carried quietly into a new one, so an ageing action stays visible. This register is what evidences that identified issues are responded to rather than merely detected, and it is the input the timeliness analysis reads for corrective-action turnaround. Attach the corrective action register for the period, including the still-open rows.

evidenceHint.en: Corrective action register for the period giving the identifying control activity, the issue found, the action agreed, its owner and the raised and closed dates

title.en: Measure how many control activities and corrective actions completed within their timeline

description.en: Take the performance log and the corrective action register and compute, per business unit, how many occurrences met their due date and how many did not, and the same for corrective actions against their target dates. Report the late ones individually with the activity, the owner and the delay, because a unit-level percentage hides the single control that is always late. Activities with no logged occurrence at all are reported separately from late ones — the two have different causes and different fixes, and merging them understates both. Attach the timeline analysis with the log extract it was computed from.

evidenceHint.en: Timeliness analysis by business unit showing on-time and late counts, each late activity or corrective action with its owner and delay, and the activities with no logged occurrence

title.en: Review each control activity for continued relevance and record the changes made

description.en: Reassess the catalogue against how the business actually runs today: activities covering a process that has changed or ended, activities the timeliness analysis shows are never performed, and processes that have appeared since the catalogue was built and carry no activity at all. Record a keep, amend or retire decision per activity with the reason behind it, and write every amendment back into the underlying procedure and the responsibility assignment in the same pass so the three documents cannot drift apart between reassessments. Attach the reassessment summary with the dated document updates it produced.

evidenceHint.en: Reassessment summary giving a keep, amend or retire decision with its reason for every catalogued control activity, and the dated procedure and assignment updates it produced
